Fix: `pointsDistinct` takes an `allowed` list (the figure's `coincidences`), so a FORCED coincidence is not an avoidable near-collision; `meetsRequirements` and `resample` pass `fig.coincidences`. Now `meetsRequirements` is true → `autoResolve` early-returns, no loop. Locked by `src/store/__tests__/coincidence.test.ts` (the `pointsDistinct` allow-list unit test + the operator's figure asserts `meetsRequirements === true`). **1378 tests green, build clean.** *Known perf follow-up (NOT the freeze): a single `replay` of this figure is ~1.5 s because the area-ratio recruits many DOFs (incl. the gauge centre/radius) into an expensive multi-start solve — bounded and usable now, but a leaner recruitment (or the similarity→side-ratio reduction) would speed it up; "show another configuration" iterates seeds so it is correspondingly slow on this figure.*

## ADR-124 — `extend-onto-circle` onto an EXISTING target point is a CONSTRAINT, never a silent no-op

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-25, work PC). Operator-reported ("check why C-A-D was not respected in the last test"), diagnosed from the debug log (session `v7veg7sc`). The engine fix is already committed in `8b098fa` (a concurrent session committed the working-tree change verbatim — the commit message notes "ADR-124 doc entry to follow"); this is that entry. *Single file: `src/engine/apply.ts`.*

**Context.** The operator's bagrut figure (two circles O, P meeting at A, B): `המיתר AD במעגל P משיק למעגל O בנקודה A` ("chord AD tangent to O at A" — the LLM created **D** as a free on-circle point of P plus the tangency `OA ⟂ AD`), then later `המשך CA חותך את מעגל P בנקודה D` ("extend CA onto circle P at D"). The extension was **silently ignored**: the final figure satisfied the two tangencies but D sat wherever the tangent-chord step left it — replaying the operator's exact facts gives a C-A-D collinearity residual of **0.38** (nowhere near a straight line). Root cause: `extend-onto-circle` was written assuming its target point is **new**. Both code paths re-create the point with `addObj`, which **keeps the first definition** when the id already exists (the deterministic-id idempotency rule, `apply.ts:143`). The shared-endpoint path (case 1, taken here because A is an O∩P crossing → already on circle P) pushes **no constraints**, so when D pre-exists the whole directional coupling (collinear + beyond-the-2nd-letter order) is dropped to **nothing** — a complete no-op.

**Decision.** When the `extend-onto-circle` target **already exists**, treat the extension as a **constraint on that existing point**, never a re-build (a new case (0) before the existing case 1/2). Push `collinear(a, b, id)` + `collinear-order([a, b, id])` (id beyond the 2nd letter). If the existing point is a **free on-circle point of the same circle** (the chord-AD case), attach the order-aware far-crossing `solve` to its carrier — the very mechanism the fresh case-2 path uses — so its θ is driven onto line AB on the **far** side; for any other carrier the constraints alone flex the figure (the global solver / recruiter owns the DOF). Always draws the secant A→D. New targets keep the prior behaviour (case 1 deterministic shared-endpoint second-crossing, case 2 driven on-circle).

**Result.** Verified on a buildable variant (D pre-exists as a plain on-circle point, **no** conflicting tangency): the extension now lands D exactly on line CA, **beyond A** — collinear residual `0`, projection `1.955` → C-A-D order respected. Locked by a unit test in `src/engine/__tests__/extend-onto-circle.test.ts`. **1378 tests green, build clean.**

**The operator's *exact* figure is over-determined — now surfaced honestly, not hidden.** Proven two ways (the tangent-chord-angle algebra, and an independent 15,000-sample brute-force sweep importing **no** engine code): with **AD tangent to O at A** *and* **CB tangent to P at B**, the points **C, A, D can never be collinear** for any non-degenerate pair of circles (only the degenerate coincident-circles case, residual ~1e-10 at centre-gap ≈ 0). The algebra: tangent-chord at A ⟹ ∠DAB = ∠ACB; triangle ABC ⟹ ∠BAC = 180° − ∠ACB − ∠CBA; C-A-D collinear needs ∠BAC + ∠BAD = 180°, i.e. ∠BAD = ∠ACB + ∠CBA — but tangent-chord already fixed ∠BAD = ∠ACB, forcing ∠CBA = 0 (degenerate). So the explicit "AD tangent at A" pins D to a spot incompatible with the CA-extension. **Before this fix the tool hid the conflict** (a clean-looking figure that quietly violated C-A-D); **after it, the step reports `over-constrained: OA ⟂ AD cannot hold`** and keeps the prior figure — the correct, honest behaviour. Most likely the real problem gives "AD tangent to O at A" as the **conclusion to prove**, not a construction given; dropping it lets "extend CA onto P at D" build with C-A-D respected.

**Parked (pending operator review of the bagrut source).** Whether the operator's *exact* (contradictory) sequence should (a) keep the honest over-constrained error or (b) be modelled with the tangency dropped is a problem-statement question the operator is checking ("let me look first"). The end-to-end regression scenario in `scenarios.test.ts` is **held** until that is decided; the engine behaviour itself is already locked by the `extend-onto-circle.test.ts` unit test above. *General principle reaffirmed: a derived/extension point that already exists is **re-constrained, not re-created** — the same lesson as `point-on-line`'s ADR-036 loose-point upgrade.*

**UNPARKED (2026-07-11, issue #6 — operator ruling: "we agreed that it was given and not the question").** "AD tangent to O at A" **is a construction given** in the bagrut source. With both tangencies given, the over-determinacy proof stands — the operator's exact sequence (re-using the chord endpoint **D** as the extension target, i.e. asserting C-A-D collinear) is genuinely contradictory, and option **(a) — the honest over-constrained refusal — is final.** The book's actual figure names a NEW point for that crossing (C-A-**E**), which builds clean and is locked by scenario `shared-endpoint-extension-either-side-default` (ADR-267/issue #19). The held scenario is now added as `adr-124-contradictory-extension-refused-honestly`: the exact 4-step sequence, asserting the last step is refused with the prior figure kept and both stated tangencies genuinely holding.

## ADR-125 — A subject-named incentre ("M is the centre of the incircle") is honoured, not dropped

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-25). Operator-reported, diagnosed from the debug log (session `djvbb7`): `M מרכז המעגל החסום במשולש BDC` ("M is the centre of the circle inscribed in triangle BDC") drew the centre at **O**, not M, and the tangency point on side BD showed as **G** and flipped to **F** when hidden. *Single file: `src/parser/parse.ts`.*

**Context.** The `incircle` rule named the incentre with `circleCenter(s)`, which only catches a centre phrased **"circle M" / "centred at M" / "מעגל M" / "שמרכזו M"** — a label that *follows* the centre word. The operator's phrasing puts the label as the **subject** ("**M** [is the] centre of …"), *before* the centre word, so `circleCenter` returned null → the incentre fell to the auto label `I` and **M was left unreferenced**. App.submit's dropped-label gate ([ADR-089](#adr-089)) then flagged the parse `weak:dropped:M` and escalated to the LLM, which built a **second, complete incircle** (centre O, foot G, `circle-O`) stacked on the parser's (centre I, foot F, `circle-I`). Hence all three symptoms from **one** cause — the wrong centre (the LLM's O won the display), and two duplicated tangency feet (G over F) that flip when one is hidden.

**Decision.** Add `incenterLabel(s)` — captures an incentre named as the **subject** of an incircle phrasing ("M מרכז…", "M is the [in]centre…", trailing "incentre M"). The `incircle` rule prefers `circleCenter` then `incenterLabel` (each guarded so it can't grab one of the triangle's own vertices), names the incentre and `circle-<that letter>`, and only sets `autoCenter` when the incentre is **un-named**. With the label honoured, nothing is dropped → no LLM escalation → exactly **one** incircle. (A symptom-level alternative — suppress the duplicate after the fact — was rejected per the no-patch rule; the root defect is the parser not reading the natural phrasing.)

**Also (same report, the hidden-circle half).** A hidden circle was drawn as a faint **dashed ghost** so it stayed clickable — the operator read it as "still there, just dashed". Since the circle group already carries an always-present transparent **hit-ring**, a hidden circle now draws **nothing** (truly invisible) while staying clickable on its former outline to un-hide (`src/render/Figure.tsx`). The incircle's tangency foot stays a normal, hideable point (operator: "ok to show it, but I need to hide it" — which works now that there's no duplicate underneath).

**Result.** `M מרכז המעגל החסום במשולש BDC` → incentre **M**, `circle-M`, a single foot, no escalation; M equidistant from the three sides. Locked by scenario `named-incenter-of-incircle` (the operator's exact `מלבן DCBA` / `BD` / `M מרכז…` sequence). **1380 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-126 — "Two tangents from a point" works without naming the touch points

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-25). Operator-reported, diagnosed from the debug log (session `gd0kkj`): `מנקודה A יוצאים שני משיקים למעגל O` ("from A, two tangents go out to circle O") fell to the LLM and built nothing — yet "a previous question worked nice". *Single file: `src/parser/parse.ts`.*

**Context.** The `tangentsFromExternal` rule (FR-EN-18) built the two tangents from an external point only when the **touch points were named** — `const abM = s.match(…"A and B"…); if (!abM) return null;`. The operator's previous, working question named them ("…בנקודות B ו C"); the natural phrasing that just says "two tangents from A to circle O" does **not**, so the rule bailed and the input escalated to the LLM (which produced nothing). Naming the touch points is incidental — the student wants the two tangent *lines* drawn, not to label where they touch.

**Decision.** When the touch points are not named, **auto-name two fresh ones** (dodging the figure's labels) and build the same Thales construction (the touch points lie on circle O ∩ the circle on diameter O-E, so each radius ⟂ its tangent). A named pair is still honoured (distinct from the apex, not the centre); only a genuinely absent/invalid pair triggers auto-naming. The rule was already correctly gated (tangent word + plural + "from <point>" + a resolvable circle), so reaching this point means it really is "two tangents from a point" — building is right, failing was the bug.

**Result.** `circle O radius 5` → `מנקודה A יוצאים שני משיקים למעגל O` now builds deterministically: two touch points on circle O and the two tangent segments from A, no LLM. The named form (and all existing tangent tests) are unchanged. Locked by scenario `two-tangents-from-point-unnamed-touch`. **1381 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-127 — "The circumcircle cuts CE at D" keeps D ON the segment, in every configuration

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-25). Operator-reported during manual testing ("all worked well but the last view violates the rule that D is on CE"). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts`, `src/engine/apply.ts`, `src/engine/types.ts`.*

**Context.** `circumcircleMeetsSegment` ("המעגל החוסם את משולש ABC חותך את CE בנקודה D") built D as a `line-circle-intersection` of the **infinite** line through C,E with the circumcircle, **avoiding the shared vertex** — but with **no order constraint**. So the default seed happened to land D on the chord, while "show another configuration" (a re-sampled config) slid D onto the *extension* of CE (projection parameter t up to ~4.3). This violates the segment-reference principle (CLAUDE.md / ADR-077: "a segment reference means the segment between its endpoints, not the continuation, unless the student says המשך").

**Two-step diagnosis.** The first fix — appending `set-line [C,D,E]` — **failed at apply**: `set-line` runs `addCollinear`, which searches its three points for a free on-circle carrier to drive and mis-picks the chord endpoint **C** (a free on-circle point), then tries the second-intersection conversion on it → "unresolved dependencies for E, D, line-CE, line-CD" (a dependency cycle). The real insight: D is **already collinear** with C,E (it's a point *on* line CE), so it needs **only the side/order**, never `addCollinear`.

**Decision.** Give `line-circle-intersection` an optional `order` field (e.g. `[C, D, E]`). When present, apply pushes a single `collinear-order` constraint and nothing else (no `addCollinear`, no carrier re-marking). The order residual is folded into the joint minimisation (like every order/inequality constraint, ADR-039), so the solver/sampler flexes the figure's free DOFs (here the chord endpoints on circle O) to keep D between C and E **in every configuration**, not just the default seed. `circumcircleMeetsSegment` now emits `order: [shared, D, other]` on the intersection instead of a separate `set-line`.

**Result.** D lands on segment CE (t ∈ [0.12, 0.88]) across all sampled seeds (was -2.1 … +4.3); collinear residual 0, no error, no violation. Locked by scenario `circumcircle-cuts-segment-d-on-side`. **1381 tests green, build clean.** *Note: the operator's actual run had a typo ("חותרך") that escalated to the LLM (which produced the un-ordered decomposition); the deterministic rule — where this fix lives — fires on the correct spelling. A future catalog/LLM-prompt note could teach the `order` field to the fallback.*

## ADR-128 — Production LLM proxy: a shared handler hosted by one standalone Node server, deployed at the `/geo-builder/` subpath

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-26). Phase A of the long-parked "production proxy deploy" thread (the only remaining gate before go-live; the static SPA was always trivial to serve). Operator decisions: live at **`themathbible.com/geo-builder/`** (a subpath under `httpdocs`, not a subdomain) and run the proxy as a **Node systemd service on the existing server** (mirroring the Flask apps). *Files: `server/parseHandler.ts` (new), `server/standalone.ts` (new), `server/build.mjs` (new), `server/llmProxy.ts` (refactor), `server/__tests__/parseHandler.test.ts` (new), `vite.config.ts`, `src/parser/llm.ts`, `package.json`, `.gitignore`.*

**Context.** The Phase-7 LLM fallback (ADR-023) existed **only as a Vite dev-server plugin** (`server/llmProxy.ts`, `POST /api/parse`) — there was no production entry point for the `/api/parse` proxy, and the comment "extractable to a serverless function" was never realised. The proxy holds `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, which must never reach the browser. Both a Vite middleware and a bare `http.createServer` callback receive Node's `IncomingMessage`/`ServerResponse` — that **shared shape** means one handler can serve both hosts, so dev and prod stay byte-identical (no drift between "what we tested locally" and "what runs live").

**Decision.**
1. **One shared handler** — `server/parseHandler.ts` `handleParse(req, res, { apiKey, logError })` holds all the logic (method guard, missing-key 503, per-IP rate limit, 4 KB body cap, dynamic Anthropic import, Haiku call via the pure `llmShared`). The dev plugin and the production server both call it; neither owns request logic.
2. **Standalone production server** — `server/standalone.ts`, a bare-`http` listener on `127.0.0.1:8788` (loopback only; reachable solely through the reverse proxy). It reads the key from `process.env` (a root-only systemd `EnvironmentFile`), serves `GET /healthz`, and matches **any path ending in `/api/parse`** so it works whether nginx strips the `/geo-builder` prefix or forwards it intact.
3. **Single-file deploy artifact** — `server/build.mjs` (esbuild, new `build:proxy` script) bundles the server **and the Anthropic SDK** into one self-contained `dist-server/proxy.mjs` (~504 KB). The server needs only Node + the env var — **no `npm install` on the box**. `dist-server` is gitignored.
4. **Subpath wiring** — `vite.config.ts` sets `base: '/geo-builder/'` for `command === 'build'` only (dev stays at root), and the client's fetch becomes base-relative (`` `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}api/parse` ``) so it resolves to `/api/parse` in dev and `/geo-builder/api/parse` in prod with no per-environment branching. `sessionLog`'s `/api/log` is fully `import.meta.env.DEV`-gated, so it no-ops in production untouched.

**Why a standalone bundle over serverless / over keeping node_modules.** The operator wants everything on `themathbible.com` (no second provider), and the box already runs persistent services via systemd — so the Flask pattern applies, just `node` instead of `gunicorn`. Bundling the SDK in makes the deploy a two-file `scp` (`dist/` + `proxy.mjs`) with zero server-side dependency management, and keeps the key in a root-only env file (never in the bundle, never in git — the standing rule).

**Result.** `npm run build` clean (subpath confirmed in `dist/index.html`); `npm run build:proxy` produces the bundle; smoke test of the running bundle **with no key**: `/healthz` → 200, `POST /api/parse` → 503 `no-api-key` (proving it never fires a live call), the `/geo-builder/api/parse` prefix form → matched, `GET` → 405. Handler guards locked by `server/__tests__/parseHandler.test.ts` (method / 503 / 413 / empty / 429 rate-limit — all short-circuiting before the SDK, no autonomous API calls). **1387 tests green, build clean.**

**Deployed 2026-06-26 (Phases B + C, live at `https://themathbible.com/geo-builder/`).** Server reality differed from the plan in one way that matters for any future deploy to this box: **nginx is disabled/off** (failed since 2026-04) — themathbible.com serves over **HTTPS via Apache directly**, and all the existing app reverse-proxies (`/hw/`→8000, `/akinator`→5000, `/bagrut`→3000, `/akinator2`→5001) live in the **HTTPS Apache include** `vhost_ssl.conf`. So the `vhost_nginx.conf` route was a no-op (reverted to byte-identical original); the proxy is instead two `ProxyPass`/`ProxyPassReverse` lines appended to `vhost_ssl.conf` (backup → `apache2ctl -t` → `systemctl reload apache2`). The proxy runs as `geo-proxy.service` (User=www-data, loopback `127.0.0.1:8788`) from `/var/www/geo-proxy/` (outside the Plesk vhost, like the box's `math-evaluator`); the key is `/var/www/geo-proxy/geo-proxy.env` (root:root 600 — systemd reads it as root, www-data never sees it). Static SPA at `httpdocs/geo-builder/` (root:root 755/644, like the other static subdirs — served by Apache default, no directive). `mod_proxy_http` sets `X-Forwarded-For` automatically, so the per-client rate-limit works. Public verification (no live API call): static root 200, assets 200, `POST …/api/parse` empty body → 400 `empty` (Apache→node chain proven, key loaded), existing sites unaffected (`/akinator` 200, `/bagrut` 308). Deploy artifacts updated to match: `deploy/apache-geo-builder.conf` (replaces the nginx snippet), `deploy/README.md`. **Live LLM path CONFIRMED 2026-06-26** by the operator in-browser: the conversational `תצייר לי ריבוע עם שני אלכסונים` (out-of-grammar) escalated through the proxy and built a correct figure — so the full chain (Apache → Node → Haiku → canonical steps → deterministic re-parse → build) works in production. Only follow-up: set the Console spend cap. **Persistence caveat:** the `vhost_ssl.conf` lines are direct edits — a Plesk domain reconfigure could drop them (static app keeps working; LLM fallback degrades gracefully); re-append or add via the Plesk GUI.

## ADR-129 — A tangency's radius ⟂ tangent line is an `implicit` perpendicular: it constrains the figure but draws NO right-angle mark

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-26). Operator: "when I add משיקים, I don't want the 90° sign to show." *Files: `src/engine/types.ts`, `src/parser/parse.ts`, `src/store/geoStore.ts`, `src/engine/__tests__/tangent-points.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`.*

**Context.** A tangency is lowered to a perpendicularity constraint — radius `O–T` ⟂ the tangent line at the touch point `T` (ADR-075/081/093/115). Every tangent emitter pushes `set-perpendicular(O, T, vertex, T)` (the touch point `T` shared in both segment positions). `angleMarkFor` (the store's fact → `AngleMark` map) drew a right-angle square at any `set-perpendicular` with a shared named vertex, so **every tangent rendered a 90° mark at its touch point.** But the documented angle-mark rule (`angle-marks.test.ts`) is: *mark an angle only when the student STATED it — never a merely computed 90°* (a rectangle's corners, a rhombus). A tangency's right angle is exactly such a computed one: the student wrote "tangent," not "the radius is perpendicular here." So the mark was a rule violation, surfaced only now because tangency is the one place a `set-perpendicular` is emitted by the engine rather than typed by the student.

**Decision.** Add an optional `implicit?: boolean` to the `set-perpendicular` command. The **emitter** (the tangent rules — the layer that knows the perpendicularity is structural, not stated) tags every tangency-derived `set-perpendicular` with `implicit: true`; `angleMarkFor` returns `null` for an `implicit` perpendicular. A student-typed `AB ⟂ CD` (the one non-tangent emitter) stays unflagged and still marks. The flag is render-only — the constraint is solved and verified identically (the radius really is ⟂ the line); only the 90° glyph is suppressed.

**Why a flag on the command, not a structural sniff in `angleMarkFor`.** The mark map sees one command in isolation; it can't tell a tangency `(O,T,vertex,T)` from a student's `(C,F,D,F)` "CF ⟂ DF" — both share a vertex in the `b/d` slots. The "is this stated or computed?" knowledge lives only at the emitter, so the flag is set where the intent is known (root cause: the engine was emitting a *stated*-shaped command for a *computed* fact). Consequence honestly absorbed: the four tangent emitters' command shape changed, so their unit-test expectations gained `implicit: true`.

**Result.** Regression locked in scenario `segment-tangent-no-explicit-touch-point` (`fig.angleMarks.filter(m => m.right)` is empty after a tangent); `angle-marks.test.ts` (stated right angles still mark) and `tangent-points.test.ts` (updated emitter expectations) green. **1388 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-130 — A redundant constraint may LEND its hoarded carrier: case (E) in `recruitFreeDofs` resolves figures the greedy one-carrier-per-constraint model falsely calls over-constrained

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-26). Operator session `rw2ypbgq`, reported as a wrong/misleading error. Prototyped, full suite validated, then committed (operator: "investigate deeper first… you decide based on results" → "finalize it"). *Files: `src/engine/step.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`.*

**Context.** The solver satisfies each constraint by assigning it one private free-DOF **carrier** (a free vertex / parametric `t`,θ / shape scalar / free radius) and running a driven solve; when a new constraint's direct carrier can't satisfy it, `recruitFreeDofs` recruits more free ancestors and joint-solves. The operator's figure — kite `ABCD`, circumcircle `O` of `BCD`, `AD`&`AB` tangent to `O`, `E` on arc `BC` with `arc BE = 2·arc EC`, then **`E על המשך DO`** (E on the extension of DO ⇒ `D,O,E` collinear) — is fully determined and **solvable**: since `D` and `E` both lie on `O`, "D, O, E collinear" makes **E the antipode of D**, and a valid kite exists (verified independently and end-to-end). Yet the step failed `over-constrained: E, D, O collinear cannot hold`, and — because `set-line` is a deferrable constraint whose residual flexes across seeds — it was misclassified **pending**, showing the under-determined "recorded but doesn't affect yet — add givens" message with a red input. Both were wrong: nothing was missing.

**Root cause.** Every free DOF was already claimed: the two tangencies drove `A` and `B`, the kite's `AB=AD`/`CB=CD` drove `C` and `D`, the arc-ratio drove `E`. The collinear arrived with **no free DOF reachable** (`cand=[]`), and the recruiter's existing "steal" only fires for an **over-subscribed** constraint (≥2 carriers = slack) — here every constraint had exactly one carrier. But the system is solvable precisely because the kite's `AB=AD` is **REDUNDANT** — implied by the two equal tangent lengths from the external point `A` — so one carrier is genuinely free; the greedy assignment just couldn't see it. Confirmed differentially: deleting the two tangents (freeing `A`,`B`) makes the identical `set-line` solve immediately.

**Decision.** Add a final fallback **case (E)** to `recruitFreeDofs` (failure-path only): when no free DOF and no over-subscribed carrier exist, **LEND** the new constraint `K` a reachable already-claimed carrier (most-recently-added first, to keep base geometry stable) and accept the **first lend under which the ENTIRE system — every constraint, `K` and the lender's `K1` included — evaluates valid**. The lender's `K1` stays a check, so it is re-verified after the joint solve.

**Why it is safe (self-verifying), not a global-solver rewrite.** A lend that actually breaks `K1` fails `evaluate` and is rejected inside the recruiter, so case (E) can **only ever return a fully-valid figure** — it never produces a wrong drawing, it only recovers a real configuration the carrier heuristic missed. This sidesteps the reverted heavy global multi-start (which didn't converge at 8-DOF): we keep the per-carrier joint solver and add a bounded, verified search over which claimed DOF to borrow. It runs only after `evaluate` already failed, so eagerly-satisfied figures never reach it.

**Result.** The operator's figure builds (E = antipode of D; `D,O,E` collinear to ~1e-7; `B,C,D,E` all on `O`; `arc BE = 2·arc EC` holds) and the misleading pending/red message is gone (the step now succeeds). Locked by scenario `collinear-flexes-redundant-carrier-kite-tangents`. **Full suite 1388→1389 green, build clean, no perf regression** (suite 62.9s vs 63.0s baseline — case (E) is failure-path only).

## ADR-131 — An inscribed trapezoid carries `AB ∥ CD` as a CONSTRAINT (free vertices), not just fixed starting angles

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-26). Operator session `su2xwopc`: "in the third step, the engine forgets that this is a trapezoid." *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`.*

**Context.** `טרפז ABCD חסום במעגל` (trapezoid inscribed in a circle) builds the circle + four on-circle vertices + a `quadrilateral`. Its trapezoid shape — `AB ∥ CD`, isosceles by cyclicity — was encoded **only** as the fixed starting angles `INSCRIBED_ANGLES.trapezoid = [215,325,60,120]`, with the vertices NON-free and **no `set-parallel` constraint**. The operator then built a tangent-meets-line point `E` and added `BE=BC`; that `set-equal` recruited an on-circle vertex (`driveOrCheck`'s on-circle case doesn't check the `free` flag) and slid it off its trapezoid angle, so by step 3 `AB ∥ CD` no longer held — the figure had silently stopped being a trapezoid. Same class as ADR-117 (an inscribed triangle's equilateral/isosceles qualifier was dropped because the shape lived only in placement, not in a persistent relation).

**Decision.** The inscribed trapezoid now emits a persistent **`set-parallel(A,B,C,D)`** (via `shapeCmds`, alongside the triangle equal-side relations), and its vertices are **FREE** (`freeAngles` now includes `trapezoid`). A trapezoid is not rigid — its base ratio and height are unstated DOFs (ADR-052) — so the isosceles angles are a *starting* placement the figure may flex away from, while `set-parallel` keeps `AB ∥ CD` no matter what later givens move. Cyclic + `AB ∥ CD` ⇒ isosceles automatically, so no separate equal-legs constraint is needed. Applied in every quad-building branch (fresh vertices, and the existing-points `concyclic` branch).

**Why a constraint, not "freeze the vertices."** Freezing all four (the old behaviour) makes the trapezoid rigid, so a satisfiable later given (`BE=BC`) is met only by silently corrupting the shape or by failing — neither is right. A persistent relation + free vertices lets the figure legitimately flex to satisfy the new given *while staying a trapezoid* (root cause: the shape's defining property must be a relation, not a one-time placement). Square/rectangle/rhombus stay angle-fixed (a cyclic square IS rigid up to similarity) — scoped to the trapezoid, the one non-rigid cyclic shape.

**Result.** The operator's sequence keeps `AB ∥ CD` (residual ~1e-6) through the tangent + `BE=BC` steps, all four vertices on the circle, `BE=BC` satisfied. The lone-inscribed-trapezoid corpus test (`AB ∥ DC`, equal legs, on the circle) still passes. Locked by scenario `inscribed-trapezoid-stays-a-trapezoid-when-flexed`. **1390 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-132 — An unlabeled polygon auto-names its vertices (A,B,C,…) instead of escalating to the LLM

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-26). Operator session `lag0hgpa`: "מרובע חסום במעגל doesn't work." Operator chose the broadest scope ("all polygons, everywhere"). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts`, `src/parser/__tests__/auto-label.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`.*

**Context.** Every polygon rule required an explicit vertex-label run (`labelRun` → null ⇒ rule returns null). So `מרובע חסום במעגל` / `quadrilateral inscribed in a circle` — and bare `מרובע` / `square` / `משולש` / `דלתון` / `regular pentagon` — fell through the deterministic grammar to the LLM (or, with no live LLM, built nothing). Only `circle`/`מעגל` worked bare, because it has no vertices to name. But an unlabeled shape is a *common, simple* input — exactly what the offline parser is meant to own (CLAUDE.md: "the deterministic parser handles the common simple inputs; only ambiguous phrasings escalate"). Escalating it is wasteful and, in production, unreliable.

**Decision.** When a shape rule finds **no labels at all** and **nothing else geometry-significant left over**, it **auto-names** the vertices `A, B, C, …` (skipping any already in the figure), via a shared `autoVertexLabels(n, used)` + `shapeLabels(bare, n, ctx, hasLeftover)`. Wired into all the polygon families — the `quadShape`/`triShape` factories, the `shapeMacro` named shapes (kite/isosceles/equilateral/…), `inscribedPolygon`, and `regularPolygon`. The labels are shown on the canvas, so later references (`AB`, `∠ABC`) work normally. A circle stays bare (no vertices); a *generic* "regular polygon" with no labels still escalates (its `n` is unknown without a label run).

**Two guards keep it from over-firing.** (1) **Partial/typo'd labels escalate, not auto-complete** — `מרובע ABC` (three labels for a quad) is NOT auto-finished to `ABCD`; it returns `not-handled`. (2) **A leftover defers** — a shape word plus a circle/constraint with no labels (`מרובע חסום במעגל`) is left to the right rule (`inscribedPolygon`, which auto-names there), and the bare `quadShape` does not claim it. The "did the student name vertices?" test is `namesVertices = /[A-Z]/` — vertex labels are uppercase Latin by convention, which cleanly separates a named vertex from lowercase English prose remnants (`inscribed in a circle` → `in a`, no uppercase ⇒ unnamed) and from a multi-letter run that `labelRun(…,1)` mis-reads (`ABC` is not a single bounded token).

**Result.** All unlabeled forms build deterministically (He + En): inscribed quad/triangle/trapezoid (the last keeps its ADR-131 `set-parallel`), standalone shapes, named macros, regular n-gons — vertices `A,B,C,…`, skipping existing points. Labeled and partial-label inputs are unchanged. Locked by `auto-label.test.ts` (7 cases) + scenario `unlabeled-inscribed-quad-auto-names-vertices`. **1398 tests green, build clean.**

**Amendment (2026-06-26).** Extended the same principle to **two intersecting circles**: `שני מעגלים נחתכים` / `two circles intersect` (no crossing points named) now auto-names the two intersection points `A, B` (`twoCirclesMeet`, avoiding the centres + existing points) instead of returning `not-handled`. The named forms (`…בנקודות A ו-B`, `circles O and P meet at A and B`) are unchanged. This also fixed a first-page example chip: the empty-canvas CTA examples must each BUILD a figure (operator: "1 doesn't and 1 breaks"), so the chips were reset to self-contained shape builders — `טרפז ABCD חסום במעגל`, `מקבילית ABCD`, `שני מעגלים נחתכים` (+ `ריבוע ABCD`, `משולש ABC`, `מעגל O ברדיוס 5`) — and a guard (`examples-build.test.ts`) now replays EVERY `examples.items` entry in both locales and asserts it builds with no error, so a broken example can't ship again. **1402 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-133 — Textbook-statement export ("decompiler"): planned, LLM-backed, premium feature-flag-gated

**Status.** Proposed / planned (2026-06-26) — **requirement captured, not built** (operator: "for now, just add this as a requirement… let's plan it"). Tracks FR-HS-9 + NFR-FG-1–3. *No code yet.*

**Context.** Israeli geometry problems ship as **verbal statement + figure**. The app already turns a description into a figure (the construction pipeline) and exports the figure as an **image** (FR-HS-5). Teachers/authors composing an exam want the **other half**: from a figure they built, get the **verbal givens** to paste next to the diagram. A raw transcript of the steps is wrong for this — it leaks the construction order, the user's exact wording, and scaffolding (helper points, the path used to place a point). A textbook poses the *givens* in a normalised register ("ABCD is a trapezoid inscribed in a circle; the tangent at C meets the extension of AB at E; BE = BC"), independent of how the figure was drawn.

**Decision (the plan).**
1. **A reverse stage — the "decompiler."** This is the inverse of the input pipeline ([11-architecture-as-compiler.md](11-architecture-as-compiler.md)): instead of `utterance → command[] → figure`, it is `figure/relations → verbal statement`. The source of truth is the **engine model** (objects + constraints + the *verified* relations from `verify.ts`), NOT the raw fact/utterance list — so the prose describes what the figure IS, not how it was typed. Construction order, helper scaffolding, and synonymous phrasings are normalised away before/within generation.
2. **LLM-backed phrasing.** A deterministic pass first serialises the model into a neutral relation list (shapes, memberships, tangencies, equalities, angles, the givens the verifier confirmed); the LLM then renders that list as fluent textbook prose in the target language (He/En), in the "נתון…" register. The LLM does *style*, not geometry — the relations are fixed by the engine, so it cannot invent or drop a given. (Model: the cheapest sufficient one, per NFR-CT-3; routed through the same server-side proxy as the parser fallback, NFR-SE-1.)
3. **Output is editable text.** Presented as a third export beside "image" and "copy construction"; the author can edit before pasting. He/En per the UI locale.
4. **Premium, flag-gated (NFR-FG).** Costs extra LLM spend and is a **paid-tier candidate**, so it sits behind a single feature flag: **on for local development**, **off in the default production build**, where the UI shows it as a **paid option** (a labelled, disabled affordance — never hidden, never an error) and the endpoint does nothing / is unreachable (no API call, no cost, no leak when off).

**Why defer / flag rather than build now.** The operator wants the *capability designed* but **not shipped on**: it needs a billing/licensing story first, and it adds recurring API cost. A flag lets the code live in the repo and be developed/tested locally without exposing a paid feature or spending on the public deployment. The standing test rule still applies when it is built (the relation-serialiser is deterministic and unit-testable; the LLM styling is mocked — and per repo policy the operator authorises any live call, with Opus-as-oracle for dev).

**Open questions (for when it's built).** Granularity (whole figure vs only the *given* facts vs include derived/"prove that" conclusions); how much the author wants to steer register/length; whether a deterministic template fallback (no LLM) is worth it for the common shapes so the feature degrades to a basic statement when the flag/API is off; how the flag is surfaced to a licensed deployment (build-time env vs a per-account entitlement).

## ADR-134 — The ground-truth relations layer ("view relations"): sample-and-check-invariance over the figure, ground truths only

**Status.** Proposed / planned (2026-06-26) — **requirement captured + decided, not built** (operator: "review this requirement… then we can plan it"). Realises and sharpens the long-deferred **Reveal** feature (FR-RV-1–6); part of Plan Phase 9. *No code yet.*

**Context.** The tool is for **exploration**: a student (or teacher) who wants to know *what the figure forces* — which sides are equal, which angles, which triangles are similar, what values/area relations are fixed — should be able to ask for that layer on demand. This was always envisioned as "Reveal" (FR-RV) but left vague. The operator's request pins it down, including the critical rule: **show a size only if it is definitive (has no other option)**.

**Decision — the method.** A relation is a **ground truth iff it holds in EVERY valid drawing of the figure**, not just the one on screen. So the layer **samples the figure many times across its free DOFs and branches** (reusing the FR-ALT-2 sampler / the validation-campaign sweep) and keeps **only the relations invariant across all samples** (to display precision). Holds-always → shown; holds-now-but-breaks-on-resample → a drawing coincidence, discarded. This is the same "check invariance across samples" pattern the verifier and validation campaign already use, and it is a **read-only consumer of the engine** (zero engine edits, additive, can't regress existing behaviour — like the verifier and the coord-validation campaign).

**The unifying principle (and why it answers "definitive only" and the areas twist for free).** A figure is rigid only **up to similarity** ([ADR-101](#adr-101)). So:
- **Scale-invariant** relations — equal sides, equal angles, angle *values*, side/area *ratios*, similarity/congruence, ⟂, ∥ — are detectable as ground truths and shown whenever forced.
- **Absolute** magnitudes — a length = 5, an area = 13 — are shown **only when the figure is scale-anchored** (the givens fixed an absolute size). On a typical (scale-free) figure the layer correctly shows angles/ratios/equalities and **no absolute sizes** — which *is* the operator's "definitive only" rule, falling straight out of the gauge. **Areas:** ratios ("S, 0.4S") are scale-invariant → shown; absolute areas only when anchored — same rule as lengths.

**Decided product shape (operator).**
- **Object universe:** only objects that **appear** — drawn/edge segments, angles at real vertices between real edges, triangles bounded by drawn segments — pairwise over that universe (not all point-pairs/triples), runtime-conscious.
- **Given + derived:** show **both** (a stated relation faint, a derived one emphasised) — omitting givens would make the picture incomplete.
- **On-figure encoding:** **tick marks** (equal segments, one class per group) and **arc marks** (equal angles) + right-angle squares — standard textbook notation, reusing the renderer's existing mark layer.
- **Similar triangles:** in a **list beside the canvas, not on the diagram** (clutter), with vertex correspondence + similar-vs-congruent, click-to-highlight (traceable, FR-TH-4).
- **Trigger/lifecycle:** a **button** (not a live toggle) → ~2–3 s analysis (acceptable) → annotated; a **dismiss** control; **auto-clear on new input** (truths may have changed — recompute on demand, never stale).

**Why a button + on-demand, not live.** Sampling N full configurations (each a replay+evaluate) × pairwise comparison is too costly to run per step; computing only when pressed bounds the cost to a moment the user chose to wait, and auto-clearing on the next fact keeps it honest without re-paying continuously.

**Risk / synergy.** Correctness is **coupled to the sampler genuinely exercising every free DOF**: if a DOF is secretly pinned to a default ([ADR-052](#adr-052) smell), the layer would report a **false** "equal"/"value". So this feature is also a strong **audit of ADR-052** — but the sampler may need hardening before the layer is fully trustworthy. This is the most likely place the work stretches.

**Complexity (for planning).** ~80% of the relation plumbing exists (the sampler, `freeDofs` + similarity gauge, the validation sweep, `verify.ts`'s relation list). The work: a comparison/classification pass over the bounded universe (equal-classes, angle-classes, triangle-similarity with correspondence, ratio/area detection), the on-figure tick/arc layer + the similar-triangles list, and the button/lifecycle. Estimated a **few weeks** for a solid v1; the variable is sampler-completeness (the risk above) and the visual-clutter tuning. Suggested first slice: equal-sides + equal-angles ticks/arcs over the appears-only universe (proves the sample-and-check engine), then values/ratios + area relations, then the similar-triangles list.

**Open questions (for when it's built).** Sample count / tolerance to call a relation "definitive" (false-positive vs false-negative trade-off); whether to also flag *near*-relations a hair outside tolerance (probably not — keep it exact); how aggressively to bound the triangle universe on busy figures; whether area-ratio labels live on the figure or only in the list.

## ADR-135 — "Tangent ∩ the extension of AB" carries an `order` so E lands on the named side (ADR-127 mechanism, applied to `line-intersection`)

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-27). Operator session `efm2i69l`: "E was not on the continuation of AB as I asked — it was on the BA side." *Files: `src/engine/types.ts`, `src/engine/apply.ts`, `src/parser/parse.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`.*

**Context.** `המשיק למעגל בנקודה D והמשך AB נפגשים בנקודה E` ("the tangent at D and the **extension of AB** meet at E"). `tangentLineIntersection` built E as a `line-intersection` of the tangent with the **infinite** line A–B, with **no order** — so the single crossing fell wherever the figure's free DOFs happened to put it (here beyond A, the wrong side). The directional **"המשך AB"** (E beyond the 2nd letter, order A→B→E) was silently dropped. E-beyond-B was reachable (8/40 sampled configs), so this was config selection, not impossible geometry.

**The wrong first attempt (recorded so it isn't retried).** Emitting a `set-line [A,B,E]` and enforcing **every** `set-line` order through the sampler (`firstSatisfyingSeed`/`meetsRequirements`): it fixed the case but **broke 4 tests and blew up to ~300 s** on a heavy figure (the seed loop ran 120 full re-solves). Enforcing all `set-line` orders is too broad, and a 120-seed search over an expensive replay is unacceptable. Reverted.

**Decision.** Reuse the **proven ADR-127 order mechanism** (already used by `circumcircleMeetsSegment` via `line-circle-intersection.order`): add an optional **`order` field to the `line-intersection` command**. When set, `applyCommand` pushes a single `collinear-order` constraint (E is *already* collinear, being the crossing — so only the side/order is added, never `addCollinear`, per the ADR-127 note). The parser sets `order:[a,b,e]` only when "המשך"/"extension" is present. The order's residual **folds into the joint solve**, so the figure flexes its free DOFs to keep E on the named extension **in the default config** — no sampler search, no perf cost, no broad `set-line`.

**Why this is the small fix the operator expected.** The rule never *guaranteed* the side before — the existing tangent-extension scenarios only assert collinearity/on-tangent, not which side — so a default that happened to be right (or unchecked) looked like "it worked." The `order` field makes the side a first-class, solver-honoured constraint, exactly as ADR-127 did for the circle-cuts-segment sibling.

**Result.** E now lands beyond B at seed 0 (t = 3.35), no search. **1424 tests green, build clean, suite back to ~67 s** (no perf regression). Locked by scenario `tangent-meets-extension-lands-on-named-side`.

## ADR-136 — The relations layer's false positives: a frozen inscribed triangle (ADR-052) + degenerate/duplicate angles

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-27). Operator (testing the relations layer): "these angles should not have shown — they're not necessarily those." *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts`, `src/engine/relations.ts`, `src/engine/__tests__/relations.test.ts`.*

**Context.** On a free figure — `משולש ABD חסום במעגל` + a tangent meeting AB's extension at E — the layer wrongly reported many angles as forced (definite values, equal pairs). Two independent bugs.

**Bug 1 — the inscribed triangle's shape was FROZEN (an ADR-052 violation).** `inscribedPolygon` built a general triangle's vertices as plain `point-on-circle` with **no `theta`** (the angle was assigned at evaluate-time by an even spread). `applySeed` perturbs an on-circle point's `theta`; with `theta` undefined the perturbation was `undefined + jitter = NaN`, so evaluate fell back to the same even spread **every** seed — ∠BAD was 44.5° in all 16 samples. The detector samples via `applySeed`, so a frozen shape makes EVERY angle look invariant ⇒ a ground truth. This is exactly the ADR-052 smell ADR-134 flagged: a DOF counted as movable but never actually sampled. **Fix:** give the general inscribed triangle an explicit **scalene** default theta (`INSCRIBED_ANGLES.triangle = [70,175,300]`, uneven gaps) and mark its vertices **`free`** (`freeAngles` now includes `triangle`) — like the general quad (ADR-097). A right-triangle inscribed stays Thales-fixed (different `kind`). Now the shape genuinely varies (∠BAD ranges ~35–68° across seeds) and nothing is falsely forced.

**Bug 2 — degenerate / duplicate angles.** Because E lies on line AB, from A the rays to B and to E are the SAME ray, so ∠DAB and ∠DAE are the *same angle* (reported as a trivial "equal pair"); and ∠BAE / ∠AEB are ~0°/180° (degenerate). **Fix (detector):** at each vertex, MERGE neighbours that lie on the same ray in every sample (one representative per direction), and DROP any angle that is degenerate (~0°/180°) in any sample. The angle universe becomes the *distinct* angles between *distinct* ray directions.

**Result.** The free inscribed-triangle + tangent figure now correctly reports **nothing** (no equal sides/angles/values). The real cases (rhombus/square/equilateral) still detect their genuine relations. Locked by `relations.test.ts` ("a FREE inscribed triangle reports nothing"). **1425 tests green, build clean.** *Note: this also makes "show another configuration" actually vary an inscribed triangle's shape — a latent ADR-052 fix beyond the relations layer.*

**Amendment (same session) — a FALSE NEGATIVE: the tangent-chord angle was missed.** With the false positives gone, the operator noted ∠EDB = ∠DAB (the tangent-chord angle, a real theorem) was NOT marked. Root cause: the angle universe was built only from `pointNeighbors` (segments + polygon edges), but the tangent D→E is a drawn **`line`**, not a `segment`, so D and E were never "connected" and ∠EDB was never a candidate. Fix: `visibleLineEdges` connects the points lying on each **visible** line (a tangent's touch point + the crossing on it), used for the ANGLE universe only (segment *lengths* stay the drawn `segment`s). Now ∠DAB = ∠EDB is surfaced (verified across samples — the tangent-chord theorem). Locked by scenario `relations-layer-tangent-chord-angle`. **1426 tests green, build clean.**

**Amendment 2 (2026-06-27) — the false positives RETURNED through ADR-135's order constraint: an order-only `solve` was treated as "consumed".** *Files: `src/engine/sample.ts`, `src/engine/__tests__/relations.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`.* The operator re-tested the SAME figure (now via the two-step path `משולש ADB חסום במעגל` + `המשיק בנקודה D והמשך AB נפגשים בנקודה E`) and the forced angle numbers were BACK (51.8°, 65°, …) on a 2-DOF figure. **Root cause — Bug 1 reborn from a different direction.** ADR-136 Bug 1 un-froze the lone inscribed triangle (scalene `theta` + `free`); but ADR-135 (same day) gave the tangent∩extension `line-intersection` an `order` field → a `collinear-order [A,B,E]` constraint. Applying that order **RECRUITED** the now-`free` vertices A,D,B (plus centre O + free-radius circle) and marked each with a `solve` directive. The sampler's "samplable" predicates (`isFreeOnCircle`/`isFreeOnSegment`/`isSamplableExtension`/`isFreeOnLine`/the shape-carrier checks, and `freeDofs`) all required `solve === undefined`, so the recruited vertices were excluded → all 16 relation-samples identical → every angle "definitive" again. ADR-136's regression test built the triangle *alone*, so it never exercised the order-recruited combination. The exact ADR-052 smell: `freeDofCount` still read **2** (an order constraint removes 0 DOF, `dofRemoved`), but `freeDofs` read only `[O]`. **The principle (general):** an ORDER/REGION constraint (`angle-order`/`length-order`/`collinear-order`/`angle-acuteness`) pins a carrier into a *region*, not to a point — it does **not consume** the carrier's DOF. So a carrier whose `solve` is *only* such a constraint must stay free/samplable. **Fix:** an `isOrderOnlySolve` / `notConsumed` predicate in `sample.ts`; every "is this a free/samplable DOF?" check now accepts `solve === undefined` **OR** an order-only `solve`. `applySeed` perturbs the carrier while LEAVING the `solve` directive intact, so `evaluate` re-enforces the order from the perturbed seed — an in-region perturbation has 0 order residual, so the figure varies *within* the valid region (the triangle's ∠ADB now ranges ~35–86° across seeds while E stays beyond B, t>1, in every config). Not a special-case: it covers any figure where an order constraint recruits an otherwise-free shape DOF, and it also restores "show another configuration" variety for those figures. `freeDofCount` needed no change (already correct). Locked by `relations.test.ts` ("an order-recruited inscribed triangle is still samplable") + scenario `order-only-solve-stays-samplable` (the operator's exact two utterances). **1428 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-137 — "AB is a diameter" of an EXISTING circle whose endpoints already exist is a CONSTRAINT, never a re-creation

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-27). Operator session `ylea4zal`: "but I added `AB קוטר במעגל P` and it failed." *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts`, `src/parser/__tests__/circle-on-diameter.test.ts`, `src/parser/__tests__/diameter-cuts-segment.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`.*

**Context.** On a figure whose circle was a **circumcircle named P** (centre P a derived circumcentre, through A,B,D), `AB קוטר במעגל P` ("AB is a diameter of circle P") failed with **`'B' is already defined — it can't be redefined as something different`** → built-nothing. Diagnosed from the log: the named circle P existed and A,B already lay on it, so `circleOnDiameter` deferred (its line-1845 "the named circle EXISTS → `diameter` adds to it" guard) and the `diameter` rule fired, emitting the `diameter` command. That command's apply (`apply.ts`) re-creates the first endpoint as a fresh `on-circle` point and the second as **"the antipode of the first"** — which **redefines** the already-existing A,B and trips the ADR-009 redefinition guard. The `diameter` command only knows how to *build a new* diameter; it had no path for "the existing chord AB *is* a diameter."

**Decision.** This is the same well-worn pattern as **ADR-080** (an existing vertex declared "on circle O" becomes a membership constraint), **ADR-092** (a given diameter defines the circle), **ADR-099** (inscribing in an existing circle asserts membership), **ADR-115** (a tangency against an existing circle is a constraint): *a declaration against an existing circle / existing points is a CONSTRAINT, never a re-creation.* So when the `diameter` rule's two endpoints **already exist**, it emits **`set-collinear [A, centre, B]`** instead of the `diameter` command. Since the centre is equidistant from A and B (both on the circle), collinearity of A·centre·B forces the centre to their **midpoint** ⇒ AB passes through the centre ⇒ a diameter (and, by Thales, every other point on the circle then subtends 90°).

**Why `set-collinear` (and not, say, redefining one endpoint as the other's antipode).** `set-collinear` → `addCollinear`, which adapts to the circle's representation **without a dependency cycle**: for a **circumcircle** the centre is *derived from* A,B,(D), so A,B are free **points** — `addCollinear` finds no free on-circle carrier and falls to the numeric `driveOrCheck`, flexing the free DOFs until the (derived) circumcentre lands on line AB (a structural "make A the antipode of B *through the centre*" would be circular: A→centre→A). For a **named circle with on-circle endpoints** the centre is independent, so `addCollinear` cleanly converts a free on-circle endpoint to the other's antipode. One emission, both representations. Scope: only when BOTH endpoints already exist *and* a circle is resolved — the "A,B exist but no circle yet" case still defines a fresh circle on AB (`circleOnDiameter`, ADR-092), and "diameter DE in circle O" with NEW D,E still builds the diameter.

**Result.** `AB קוטר במעגל P/O` now makes the existing chord a genuine diameter — ∠ at the far vertex = 90° in **every** configuration, centre exactly at the midpoint of AB, no error, verifier clean — and the figure keeps its remaining freedom (the other vertices still slide). Locked by a unit test on the operator's circumcircle-named-P representation (`circle-on-diameter.test.ts`) + scenario `diameter-on-existing-chord-is-a-constraint` (the string pipeline; the inscribe auto-names the circle O on current HEAD, a representation drift from the session's circumcircle-P — noted in the scenario). The pre-fix parser test that asserted the buggy `diameter`-command output for existing endpoints was corrected. **1430 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-138 — Ambiguous named shapes: which sides are equal is a discrete, samplable VARIANT choice, not a frozen default

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-28) — **B1 + B2 BUILT.** Settled after a multi-agent review (4 code-grounded readers + a 4-lens adversarial panel) of an operator design proposal for the kite (`דלתון`). Realises the operator's "don't force the student to choose up front" rule and **subsumes [ADR-114](#adr-114)** (the isosceles-triangle soft default — now migrated onto this mechanism). Relates to [ADR-052](#adr-052) (no fixed assumptions), [ADR-110](#adr-110) (named-shape macros), [ADR-134](#adr-134)/[ADR-136](#adr-136) (the relations layer), and the FR-ALT alternatives feature.

**Build status (2026-06-28).** **B1 done** — a `shape-variant` SymbolicCommand (`src/engine/shapeVariants.ts`); the kite/isosceles parser macros emit it (`variant:0`); `replay` expands it to the base shape + the variant-selected `set-equal`s, with an explicit equality PINNING the matching variant and suppressing its duplicate (this is the operator's rule 2 + the ADR-114 behavior, generalised); a `cycleVariant` store action steps the index and "show another configuration" cycles it (the button shows even on a determined shape). **seed-0/variant-0 reproduces the historical drawing — zero regression (1437 tests green, tsc clean).** Locked by `engine/__tests__/named-shapes.test.ts` (unchanged geometry), `store/__tests__/shape-variant.test.ts` (cycling), and the parser-coverage guard. **B2 done** — the relations layer now SEES the variant: `detectRelations` was generalised to `detectRelationsAcross(constructions[])` (sample each variant config across its own seeds and pool the positions; `constructions[0]` gives the shared object universe), and `viewRelations` builds the variant alternatives (`variantConfigs`, bounded by the SUM of the variant counts). So a lone kite now reports **no forced equal-pair** (its pair holds in the drawn axis but not the other), while non-variant figures are byte-identical (one construction = the original single-config detection). `freeDofCount` needed **no change** — a discrete variant adds 0 continuous DOF, and the active pair's two equalities already give the correct shape-DOF count (a kite reads 2). **Mechanism (operator):** persisted index + cycleAlt — the variant is visible to "show another" (re-replays the facts) and now to the relations layer (which re-replays per variant); it is deliberately NOT a construction-level samplable variant.

**Context.** A named-shape macro (ADR-110) lowers a keyword + labels into canonical commands incl. `set-equal`. For an **ambiguous** shape, *which* sides are equal is unstated and there is genuine freedom:
- **Kite `ABCD`** (cyclic order) has exactly **two** valid drawings — axis AC (`AB=AD`, `CB=CD`) or axis BD (`BA=BC`, `DA=DC`).
- **Isosceles triangle `ABC`** has **three** (the apex at each vertex).

Today the kite macro emits **two HARD equalities** pinned to axis AC (`parse.ts`), silently asserting a choice the student never made — the exact [ADR-052](#adr-052) sin — and an explicit competing equality (`AB=BC`) then stacks into an over-constraint or a wrong shape. The isosceles triangle is better: one **soft** default that the `supersededSoft` pre-scan (`geoStore.ts`) drops when an explicit `set-equal` covers the same vertices — but that is scoped to the triangle and only yields to an *explicit* equality. The operator's proposal: propose a default so the figure draws immediately, let a later explicit equality override it without a conflict, and let **"show another configuration" cycle which pair is equal**.

**The decision.** Model "which sides are equal" as a **discrete VARIANT index**, free from the start, NOT a fixed-then-unfrozen default. Three coupled requirements (all three must land together — see "Why not the literal soft-default framing"):
1. **Persisted, replay-stable.** The chosen variant lives in a fact field (positions are never stored — the figure is derived by replay, so the choice must survive undo/redo in a fact). The natural form is a **stateful named-shape command** (e.g. `{type:'kite', ids, variant}`) that lowers to the selected pair's `set-equal`s, mirroring how `cycleAlt` rewrites `cmd.branch`.
2. **Sampler-visible.** `applySeed` must **enumerate the variants** (variant = a deterministic function of seed) so the THREE consumers that read the same sampling surface — `resample` ("show another"), `detectRelations` (the relations layer), and `freeDofCount` (the DOF cue) — all see the choice vary. This is the load-bearing coherence rule: anything "show another" can cycle, the relations layer must NOT report as forced.
3. **Pinned by an explicit equality.** An explicit `set-equal` on the shape selects/pins the matching variant (generalising `supersededSoft`), and the **chosen** pair stays a verifier given.

**Per-shape taxonomy (variant counts).** equilateral · rhombus · square · parallelogram · congruent/similar triangles = **0** (no affordance, equalities stay HARD); **isosceles triangle = 3**; **kite = 2**; isosceles trapezoid = **0** (legs fixed by the `AB∥CD` convention — but it shares item #2's redundancy risk when cyclic). The variant list is **declared per shape by the macro**, not inferred — the existing discrete-branch layer (`BRANCHABLE`, `step.ts`) is hard-wired to five *derived-point* kinds resolved by intersection geometry and cannot derive it.

**Why NOT the literal "soft default that yields then cycles" framing (the operator's wording, refined).** A *kept* soft equality is applied identically to a HARD one (`apply.ts` → `driveOrCheck`) and, when its carrier is **parametric** (a vertex pinned on a circle/segment), is frozen out of `applySeed` (`notConsumed=false`, `sample.ts`). So a lone *inscribed* kite would report its default pair as a **FORCED** equality and under-count its DOF — a brand-new [ADR-136](#adr-136)-class false positive — and continuous resampling can never *flip* a discrete pair anyway. A variant that is free from the start avoids the freeze by construction. (Nuance the panel caught: on a **free-quad** kite the vertices are free *points*, which stay samplable even while driven — `sample.ts` `freeDofs` first clause — so the freeze bites only the parametric/inscribed case; the variant model is correct and uniform for both, which is why it's preferred over patching the free/parametric split.)

**Why item #2 (the kite-tangent false over-constraint) is explicitly OUT of scope here.** That bug — `דלתון ABCD` + `B,C,D on circle O` + `AB,AD tangent` → `over-constrained: |AB|=|AD| cannot hold` — is a **redundant-constraint SOLVER** failure, not a default-pair problem: the two tangents force `AB=AD` geometrically with **no competing `set-equal`** for any syntactic supersede to detect. It is a **failure of [ADR-130](#adr-130) case (E)** ("a redundant constraint lends its hoarded carrier") to fire on *this* figure. **Root cause confirmed by a recruiter trace (2026-06-28), and it is NOT the `ancestors` under-recruit first suspected:** when the 2nd tangency `OD⟂AD` needs D's θ, D is double-booked by the redundant kite `AB=AD`; the recruiter's **case (B) finds a DECOY free DOF (the apex A) and recruits it**, which (1) sets `did=true` so **case (E)** (the redundant-lend that would lend D) is skipped, and (2) **consumes A**, so **case (D)** (free-the-blocker, which would re-point `AB=AD` onto A and free D) can't fire either (its only `alt` was A). So neither redundancy-resolving case runs. ADR-130's own scenario works only because *there* the failing constraint had `cand=[]` (no decoy) → `did=false` → case (E) ran. Likely fix direction: case (B)'s `did` must not skip cases (D)/(E) unless its recruitment actually resolves the over-constraint (verify, then fall through) — preserving the "free DOFs first" priority but not letting a decoy pre-empt the self-verifying redundancy cases. **A SEPARATE parser defect also surfaced in the same figure:** `נקודות B C D על מעגל שמרכזו O` ("points B,C,D on a circle centred O") parses to *just* `circle O` — the B,C,D membership is silently dropped (so C is never on the circle), because no rule handles "N existing points on a circle" and the ADR-089 dropped-label gate doesn't fire (B,C,D are existing labels, not new). Fixed separately, at the solver and the parser respectively, each with its own ADR. **Bundling a soft tag here would masquerade as the item-#2 fix while leaving the real defects untouched** — the panel was unanimous on this.

**Rejected alternative — unify "soft yields when REDUNDANT" to cover item #2 and the wrong-pair case in one rule.** Tempting (it was floated in the design conversation) but unsound: redundancy can only be judged by the solver (is the residual already ~0 under the rest of the system?), and `supersededSoft` runs at parse/replay time *before any coordinates exist*. A "drop-when-redundant" rule therefore collapses into the case-(E) solver fix and gains nothing for the genuinely *syntactic* wrong-pair case. Keep the two layers separate: syntactic supersede (wrong-pair) at the store; solver redundancy-lend (item #2) in `recruitFreeDofs`.

**Guards the implementation must honour (don't-break list).**
- **Atomic axis.** A kite needs BOTH pairs to be a kite, so its two equalities move as ONE unit (the variant), never two independently-droppable softs — the isosceles "drop one, stay a valid triangle" degradation does not transfer.
- **`supersededSoft` is too coarse for 4-vertex shapes** — its `{a,b,c,d}`-containment test would let *any* equality among the four kite vertices (even a restated same pair, or a diagonal) drop the default; it must become **pair-specific** before any quad uses it.
- **Verifier coverage.** A dropped/overridden default is a no-op not pushed to `applied`; the **chosen** pair must still be verified, so the figure can never go green while having silently stopped being a kite.
- **"Show another" dead-button.** A variant-flip must be exempt from `resample`'s `shapeDiffers` gate (axis AC vs BD can be similarity-equivalent for a symmetric kite), and the dual `resample()`+`cycleAlt()` press path reconciled.
- **Determinism/stability.** seed-0's variant must be deterministic and stable across unrelated edits (the first-class stability regression — the figure must not jump axes).

**Scope (operator, 2026-06-28).** The isosceles triangle is migrated off its ADR-114 soft default onto the SAME variant mechanism **in this release** — "part of the release to ensure the solution works for all cases and not a patch." So the mechanism is built once and proven on both the kite (2 variants) and the isosceles triangle (3 variants) together; ADR-114's triangle-only soft default is subsumed, not left as a parallel path.

**Open questions (for build time).** How `freeDofCount` should count a discrete variant (a binary choice is not a continuous DOF — likely 0, with the variant surfaced only to the sampler); whether non-convex/crossed labelings prune a variant (let `resample`'s convexity guard reject an impossible axis, falling back to a general quad with a notice rather than emitting an impossible equality).

## ADR-139 — A DECOY free-DOF recruit must not pre-empt the self-verifying redundancy cases: verify-then-fall-through in `recruitFreeDofs`

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-28). Diagnosed by a recruiter trace while working item #2 of the [ADR-138](#adr-138) kite design (operator session `5anuc529`). *Files: `src/engine/step.ts`; locked end-to-end by scenario `kite-tangents-redundant-equality-not-over-constrained`.* Generalises [ADR-130](#adr-130) (case (E), the redundant-carrier lend).

**Context.** `recruitFreeDofs` (the failure-path recruiter) tries cases in priority order: **(B)** recruit a genuinely-free reachable DOF; **(D)** free-the-blocker (re-point a claiming constraint to its alternative ref); **(C)** R7 steal from an over-subscribed carrier; **(E)** redundant-carrier lend ([ADR-130](#adr-130), self-verifying). Cases (B)/(D) set a `did` flag whose `continue` skips (C)/(E); case (C)'s steal also `continue`s. The intent: prefer the cheapest resolution.

**The bug (traced, not guessed).** On `דלתון ABCD` + `B,C,D on circle O` + `AB,AD tangent`, the 2nd tangency `OD⟂AD` needs D's θ, but D is **double-booked** by the redundant kite `AB=AD`. Case (B) finds a **DECOY** free ancestor of the tangency — the apex `A` — and recruits it. That decoy (1) sets `did=true`, so case (E)'s lend (which would free D) is **skipped**, and (2) **consumes A**, the only `alt` case (D) had to re-point `AB=AD` and free D — so case (D) can't fire either. Both redundancy-resolving cases are starved by a recruit that *didn't actually resolve the over-constraint*. (ADR-130's own scenario works only because *there* the failing constraint had `cand=[]` → `did=false` → case (E) ran. A decoy free ancestor is the difference.) A second instance of the same flaw: case (C) sees the now-2-carrier tangency as "over-subscribed" and does a **degenerate self-steal** (re-points one of K's own carriers back to K — a no-op) that also `continue`s and pre-empts (E).

**Decision.** A `did`/steal `continue` only earns its skip when the recruitment **actually makes the whole system valid**. Gate every intermediate `continue` on a verify: `if (did && evaluate({objects, [...constraints]}).ok) continue;` after (B)/(D), and the same after (C)'s steal. When the recruit was a decoy, fall through to the next case — ultimately to (E), which is self-verifying (a lend is accepted only if `evaluate` passes), so it can **never rescue a genuinely-impossible figure**; it only recovers a real configuration the cheaper heuristics missed.

**Why it is safe.** It preserves the existing "free DOFs first" priority (a recruit that DOES resolve still skips, identically to before) and adds at most one `evaluate` per recruited constraint, on the already-failing path only (recruitFreeDofs runs only after `evaluate` already failed once). It can only *add* rescue attempts, never remove a previously-working resolution — confirmed by the full suite. **1430 tests green, build clean, no regression.**

**Limit (the figure that exposed this is NOT fully fixed — see [ADR-140](#adr-140) + the parked note).** This fix makes case (E) *reachable* for the kite-tangent figure, but the figure needs two more things to actually build: the driven-point-on-circle conversion ([ADR-140](#adr-140)), and — beyond both — a joint-solver convergence the engine does not currently achieve for the fully-membership figure (it solves at **0 of 24 seeds**). The operator's *exact* input builds *only because a parser defect leaves C off the circle* (thinning the coupling enough to converge). Both the parser membership-drop and the solver-convergence gap are **parked** (see the 2026-06-28 session-log entry); this ADR locks the recruiter half, which is correct and general on its own.

## ADR-140 — Converting a constraint-DRIVEN free point to on-circle must PRESERVE its `solve` (else the conversion rolls back)

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-28). Same investigation as [ADR-139](#adr-139). *Files: `src/engine/apply.ts`, `src/engine/__tests__/driven-point-on-circle.test.ts`.* Amends [ADR-080](#adr-080) (declaring an existing free vertex "on circle O" makes it slide on the circle).

**Context.** ADR-080 case (c2): a non-pinned free vertex declared "on circle O" is converted to an `on-circle` point so it genuinely lies on the circle (CD becomes a real chord, the verifier's "C not on circle" is satisfied). The conversion **replaced** the object with a fresh `{kind:'on-circle', free:true}` — **dropping any `solve` directive** the vertex carried.

**The bug.** A named-shape vertex can already DRIVE a constraint: in `דלתון ABCD`, the kite's `AB=AD` is assigned the carrier **D** (and `CB=CD` → C) when D,C are free points. Declaring "B,C,D on circle O" then converts them — but dropping D's `solve` leaves `AB=AD` with **no carrier**, so the conversion's `evaluate` fails (`|AB|=|AD| cannot hold`) and the whole `point-on-circle` fact is rolled back (keep-prior-on-error). Net: **a constraint-driven point can never reach the circle** — it silently reverts to a free point off the circle. (This is why `CB=CD`/`AB=AD` kite vertices stayed adrift in item #2.)

**Decision.** Case (c2) **carries the `solve` over** to the converted on-circle point: `{kind:'on-circle', …, free:true, ...(solve ? {solve} : {})}`. D then still drives `AB=AD`, now via its on-circle θ (it slides on the circle to keep |AD|=|AB|), so the conversion's `evaluate` succeeds and D stays on the circle. An on-circle point legitimately carries a `solve` (that is how a driven on-circle vertex already works), so this is representation-preserving, not a new mode.

**Why it is safe.** A free vertex with *no* `solve` is unaffected (the spread `...({})` adds nothing) — every existing chord/inscribed-quad path is byte-identical. Only a *driven* vertex (previously un-convertible, silently reverting) changes behaviour, and strictly for the better. **1430 tests green, build clean, no regression.**

**Limit.** Same as [ADR-139](#adr-139): this lets C,D reach the circle, but the fully-membership kite-tangent figure still does not converge in the joint solver (0/24 seeds) — a parked solver-convergence gap. With both fixes in, the operator's exact input no longer over-constrains; the residual (C off the circle in that specific input) is the parked parser defect (a).

## ADR-141 — Equality-recruited parametric carriers are SAMPLED (perturbed while keeping their `solve`), so the relations layer stops reporting false "definite" values

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-28) — Stage C of the [ADR-138](#adr-138) dev plan, but an independent fix (item #1 of the two "open items"). The deeper sibling of [ADR-136](#adr-136) Am.2. *Files: `src/engine/sample.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`, `src/store/__tests__/dof-radius.test.ts`.*

**Context.** The "view relations" layer (`detectRelations`) and "show another configuration" (`resample`) both sample a figure via `applySeed`, which perturbs only the carriers a `notConsumed` predicate allows — `solve === undefined` OR an order-only `solve` ([ADR-136](#adr-136) Am.2). An **equality**-driven parametric carrier (an on-circle θ / on-segment t whose `solve.constraint` is an `equal`) was therefore FROZEN. **Confirmed bug** (operator 2026-06-27; proven this session by an engine-free variety trace): on `משולש ABC חסום במעגל` · tangent∩extension `E` · `AD` · `DB` · `F on AB` · `DE=EF` · `DF` · `DF=DB`, the layer printed **11 definite angle values** on an under-determined figure — yet ∠A(B,D) ranges **0.5°–114°** across valid configs while both equalities hold, so the angles are NOT forced. Root cause: the two equalities removed 2 DOF but the joint solver RECRUITED ~6 carriers (A,B,D,F + the centre/circle); the residual (recruited > removed) freedom hid in the **frozen** carriers, so every sample was identical and every angle read "definitive" (the exact [ADR-052](#adr-052) smell — `freeDofCount` 2 but `freeDofs` [O,C]). ADR-136 Am.2 fixed only the order-only case (0 DOF removed); an equality removes 1 DOF and IS partially consuming, so it needs a different treatment.

**Decision.** `applySeed` now perturbs a **driven** parametric carrier (on-circle θ / on-segment t with a consuming, non-order `solve`) — about its **current** value, KEEPING the `solve` — under **two gates**:
1. the figure is genuinely **under-determined** (`freeDofCount(c) > 0`); and
2. the carrier's constraint is **OVER-recruited** (`carrierCount > dofRemoved` — more carriers than the DOF it removes).

`evaluate` then re-solves from the perturbed start: an over-recruited carrier reaches a genuinely different valid config (the regulariser re-anchors to the perturbed seed), while a fully-consumed one snaps back. This **mirrors the driven-FREE-POINT perturbation** already in `applySeed` (a 2-DOF point under one scalar constraint keeps residual freedom), extended to the 1-DOF parametric carriers.

**Why both gates + a SMALL perturbation.** Without gate (1), a figure rigid up to similarity would still be perturbed — but its "over-recruited" carriers are **coupled-solve artefacts** (e.g. an angle-ratio's joint carriers), not freedom, so perturbing them only flips to a different discrete root. Without gate (2), a **fully-consumed** carrier (1 carrier, 1 DOF) is determined; perturbing it does nothing useful. And the perturbation is a SMALL in-basin jitter (±0.3 rad / ±0.25 t) about the current value — a WIDE spin would jump a consumed carrier to a **different root** (the mirror config of an inscribed `|AB|=|AC|`), spuriously reading as "another configuration". **It cannot introduce a false NEGATIVE:** re-solving stays in the valid-config space, so a genuinely-forced relation (true in EVERY valid drawing) holds in every sample.

**A finding (and a corrected test).** The `dof-radius` suite used `inscribed AB=AC` + `∠BAC = 2∠CAD` as a "shape-determined" example asserting `resample → false`. That figure is genuinely **UNDER-determined** (`freeDofCount` 1; ∠BAC ranges ~39°–67° across valid configs) — the old assertion held ONLY because the equality-recruited carriers were frozen (this very bug). The operator's original report behind that test ("5 DOF but every view is the same") was itself this frozen-carrier bug; ADR-141 is its proper root fix (sample the hidden DOF) rather than the prior symptom fix (report "no other configuration"). The example was replaced with a genuinely-rigid figure (a square).

**Result.** The `DF=DB` figure reports **0 forced angles** (was 11); determined figures (square 4×90°, equilateral 3×60°) still report their genuine values (no false negative); `freeDofCount` unchanged. Locked by scenario `equality-recruitment-not-forced` (the operator's exact 8-utterance sequence). **Full suite green, build clean.**

## ADR-142 — A SHARED-ENDPOINT extension's side is inferred from the circle, not the letter order (a reversed "המשך BD" vs "DB" the geometry disambiguates)

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-28). Operator session `1dugj1cw` (bagrut Q4, two intersecting circles + tangent-secants). *Files: `src/engine/verify.ts`, `src/store/geoStore.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`.* Refines the directional-extension family ([ADR-054](#adr-054)/[ADR-098](#adr-098)/[ADR-124](#adr-124)).

**Context.** `extend-onto-circle` ("המשך a·b onto `circle` at id") is DIRECTIONAL — the new point lies beyond the 2nd letter `b` (ADR-054). The bagrut figure has **F beyond B** (order D→B→F, F on the left circle), so it should read `המשך DB`; the operator wrote `המשך BD`, which the parser reads as **beyond D**. That side is **geometrically impossible**: D lies on a *tangent* to the target circle (so D is always OUTSIDE it), and line BD can only re-cross the circle behind B — never beyond D. So `firstSatisfyingSeed` (which requires EVERY extension to reach beyond its `b`) could satisfy **no** seed, the whole figure fell back to seed 0, and the *other* extension E drifted too (both flagged amber). The typo of one letter cascaded into a wholly-wrong, confusingly-flagged figure — and the operator had built the same problem correctly before.

**The geometric insight.** In the **SHARED-ENDPOINT** case (a line endpoint already lies on the target circle — `applyCommand` case (1)), the line meets the circle at that endpoint AND at exactly **ONE other point**, so the extension point is **UNIQUE**. Its side is then *forced by the geometry*, not by the BD/DB letter order — a reversed `BD`/`DB` describes the SAME crossing. By contrast the NEITHER-on-circle case (a driven free on-circle θ) has TWO crossings and the order genuinely SELECTS the far one — there the direction is a real constraint.

**Decision.** For a shared-endpoint `extend-onto-circle` (either `a` or `b` is on the circle — tested via `circleMembers` in the seed-gate, via the resolved-circle distance in the verifier), accept the new point on **EITHER extension** (beyond `a` OR beyond `b`); flag/reject only a point genuinely **BETWEEN** a and b. A neither-on-circle extension stays **strict** (must be beyond `b`). Applied symmetrically to **both** consumers of the direction: `extensionsClear` (the seed-gate used by `firstSatisfyingSeed`/`meetsRequirements`/`autoResolve`) and the givens-verifier.

**Why this is the right scope (not a blanket relaxation).** The strict directionality stays where it MATTERS — the driven case, where the figure can flex to put the point on either side and the student's chosen side is a genuine given. It relaxes ONLY where the side is geometrically forced (one crossing), so a reversed-letter typo "just works" and never cascades, while a real wrong-side driven figure is still caught. The circle disambiguates exactly the ambiguity the student's letter order tried (and failed) to.

**Result.** The operator's *exact typo'd input* now builds **clean** — F at the unique crossing (beyond B), E beyond A, **zero violations** — because once F is accepted, the seed search finds a config where E reaches its far side too (the cascade is gone). Locked by scenario `extension-onto-circle-side-inferred-from-circle` (the operator's exact 6-utterance sequence, reversed `BD` and all). **Full suite green, build clean.**

## ADR-143 — A CHORD of one circle tangent to ANOTHER ("מיתר AD במעגל P משיק למעגל O") is a tangent-chord construct, never mutual circle-tangency
