**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-28). Operator session `vk346px4` (two intersecting circles O,P; chord CB tangent to P at B; then "the chord AD in circle P tangent to circle O at A"). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`.*

**Context.** After two intersecting circles and a tangent chord CB, the operator typed `המיתר AD במעגל P משיק למעגל O בנקודה A` ("the chord AD **in** circle P is tangent to circle O at A"). The intended figure: D a new point on circle P, the chord AD drawn, and AD tangent to circle O at the shared point A (radius OA ⟂ AD). Instead the step parsed to a **single** `circles-tangent` between circle-P and circle-O — **point D and the chord AD were dropped entirely**, and it asserted the two circles are tangent to *each other*, contradicting the opening "two circles intersect". The step showed green ✓ while nothing new appeared on the canvas (a "no-error ≠ correct" case the verifier didn't catch because the emitted command was internally consistent — just not what was asked).

**Root cause.** `circlesTangent` fires on any "two `מעגל X` tokens + a `משיק` keyword". But here one of the two circle mentions — `במעגל P` — is the chord's **host** ("the chord AD *in* circle P"), not a second tangent circle. The rule can't tell a host-circle qualifier from a tangency target, grabs both as the tangent pair, and throws the chord away. Compounding it, the deterministic parser had **no tangent-chord construct at all** — the symmetric earlier step ("chord CB tangent to circle P at B") only worked because it was out-of-grammar and escalated to the LLM; this one didn't escalate only because `circlesTangent` wrongly claimed it.

**Decision.** A new `tangentChord` rule, ordered **before** `circlesTangent` (and `chord`). It splits the utterance at the tangent keyword: the chord + its **host** circle precede it (`circleCenter(before)`), the **tangency** circle + touch point follow (`circleCenter(after)`, point via `…at/בנקודה Z`). It requires two *different* named circles and that the touch point Z be one of the chord's own endpoints, then emits both endpoints `point-on-circle` the **host** circle, the touch point `point-on-circle` the **target** circle (idempotent at a shared intersection — `pointOnCircle` already recognises a `circle-circle` point as on both), `set-perpendicular(target-centre, Z, end0, end1)` (radius ⟂ chord ⇒ tangent at Z), and the chord `segment`. Plus a `chord`/`מיתר` **guard on `circlesTangent`**: a chord phrasing can NEVER be mutual tangency, so even a near-miss of `tangentChord`'s shape escalates to the LLM rather than silently mis-firing as mutual tangency.

**Why this scope (not a patch).** The same "two circle mentions + tangent" class breaks for *any* chord-of-X-tangent-to-Y phrasing, not just this figure; the new rule covers the class and the guard closes the fallthrough. The fix lives at the layer the defect originates (rule recognition + ordering), per the root-cause rule.

**Result.** The operator's exact 4-step sequence now builds the intended figure — D created on circle P (|PD| = |PA|), the chord AD drawn, ∠OAD = 90° (tangent at A), **zero violations**. Locked by scenario `chord-tangent-to-other-circle-at-endpoint`. **Full suite green (1445), build clean.**

## ADR-144 — Two TANGENT circles carry FREE radii, and tangency is a constraint over them (|OP| = r1±r2), not a pinned centre distance

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-28). Operator session `23vqi9u8` ("שני מעגלים משיקים מבחוץ", then `OM=`/`OP=`). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`circlesTangent`), `src/engine/apply.ts` (`circles-tangent`), `src/engine/step.ts` (`circlesOfPoint`/`pointParents`), `src/engine/verify.ts`, `src/i18n/locales/*`, scenarios.*

**Context.** The operator built "two circles tangent externally", then typed their own size given `OP = 4` and got **"over-constrained: |OP| = 8 cannot hold"**; `OM = 4` likewise couldn't move the touch point M (rigid at 5). The "8" is no radius — it is `|OP|`, the centre distance an external tangency forces to `r1 + r2 = 5 + 3`. The radii had been **pinned** at 5/3, so every size given contradicted a value the student never gave — a textbook [ADR-052](#adr-052) violation.

**Root cause (two layers).** (1) The deterministic parser had **no rule** for the unnamed "two circles tangent externally", so it escalated to the **LLM**, which emitted `circle … radius 5` / `radius 3` (**fixed**, `via:'length'`) + `circles-tangent`. (2) The `circles-tangent` apply path was **gated on `radius.via === 'length'`** and hard-set `|OP| = r1+r2` via a `distance` constraint, placing M at a **fixed** `t = r1/d`. With the radii pinned, `|OP|` was rigid at 8 and `|OM|` rigid at 5 — so the figure could only ever be that one size.

**Decision.** Make an unstated tangent-circle radius a **free DOF**, and tangency a **constraint** the radii flex to satisfy:
- **Parser** — `circlesTangent` now also materialises the two circles as **free-radius** circles (distinct seeds; `ifAbsent` so a *stated* "circle O radius 5" is preserved as a given) and handles the **unnamed plural** ("שני מעגלים משיקים…" / "two circles tangent…") and an **auto-named touch point** when none is given. No more LLM escalation for the common phrasing.
- **Engine** — when ≥1 radius is free, build external tangency as a `coincide` between the touch point seen from **each** circle: M = `radial-toward(c1→c2)` (the named touch, on circle 1) and a hidden `~`-witness = `radial-toward(c2→c1)` (on circle 2). `coincide(M, witness)` has residual `||OP| − (r1+r2)|`, so it **forces the external relation** and reads both free radii through the touch points. Both free radii are marked as **permanent drivers** of it (like `length-radius`/[ADR-071](#adr-071)) — the touch points carry no DOF themselves, and `recruitFreeDofs` only widens DOFs for a *step's own* new constraint, so without a permanent driver a later `OP=4` (which moves a centre) would break the build-time tangency and over-constrain. Internal tangency: the larger-seed circle is outer, witness on the inner toward M, `coincide` ⇒ `|OP| = |r1−r2|`. The centre is pre-seeded to the touching distance so the **default** figure is already exactly tangent (the solver re-engages only under a later given). Both radii stated ⇒ fall through to the **unchanged** fixed path, where `|OP|` is genuinely rigid and a contradiction is reported honestly.
- **Recruiter** — `circlesOfPoint`/`pointParents` learn `radial-toward` (→ its circle, → its `toward` centre), so the joint solver reaches the free radii/centres through the touch points.
- **Verifier** — a `circles-tangent` check (`|OP| = r1±r2`), so a dropped or contradicted tangency is caught.

**Why this scope (not a patch).** Pinning unstated radii is the same ADR-052 cardinal sin across *every* tangent-circle figure, not just this one; the fix lives where the defect originates (the radius is a DOF; tangency is a constraint over it), reusing the established free-radius driver machinery rather than special-casing the inputs. A green build was never sufficient — the over-constraint was the symptom of the pinned radii.

**Result.** "two circles tangent externally" then `OP = 4` resizes the radii (`r1+r2 = 4`, M on both circles) with **no over-constraint**; `OM = 4` sets `r1 = 4`; a *stated* pair of radii is still honoured (|OP| = 8). Across 20 "show another configuration" seeds every config stays tangent while r1 varies 2.2→7.6. Locked by scenario `two-tangent-circles-then-size-given-flexes-radii`. **Full suite green (1446), build clean.**

**Amendment 1 (renderer — the touch point's `radial-toward` kind must count as "on the circle").** The first cut was correct in the ENGINE but the figure still drew wrong on screen: after `OM = 3` the operator saw circle O drawn at its SEED size (5) with M floating *inside* it at 3, not a small circle with M on its edge. Cause: a free circle's drawn radius is recovered by the renderer (`scene.ts`) and the verifier from a point *known to be on it* — but `scene.ts`'s `pointOnCircleId` enumerated only `on-circle`/`line-circle`/`antipode`/`arc-midpoint`/`circle-circle`, NOT `radial-toward`. For two tangent circles the touch point (and the hidden witness) are the ONLY on-circle points and are BOTH `radial-toward`, so the renderer found none, failed to recover the solver-driven radius, and fell back to the seed — while the touch point itself sat at the solved radius. The engine `positions` were always right, so a positions-only test (the scenario, the unit checks) passed while the SCENE was wrong — the lesson: a free-radius render path needs a SCENE-level assertion (`SceneCircle.r`), not just positions. One-line fix: add `radial-toward` to `pointOnCircleId`. Locked by a scene-level test in `render/__tests__/lines-circles.test.tsx` ("the DRAWN radius matches a solver-driven free radius"). **Full suite green (1448), build clean.**

## ADR-145 — Relations layer: a definite VALUE supersedes its equal-arc, and a point ON a segment contributes its host-line angles (the foot's 90°)

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-28). Operator (production figure: AB diameter, D mid OB, AC chord, E on AC, DE∥BC, DE=EC, F on AB, EF⊥AB). *Files: `src/render/scene.ts` (`relationMarks`), `src/engine/relations.ts` (`onHostEdges`).* Amends [ADR-134](#adr-134).

**Context.** Two relations-layer ("show equal sides & angles") defects on one figure. (1) **∠DEC and ∠ECB "show twice as equal":** both are equal (alternate angles across DE∥BC) AND each a forced 18.4°, so the layer drew BOTH an equal-angle ARC *and* an "18.4°" VALUE label on each — the same fact twice. (2) **∠EFA not shown as 90°** though EF⊥AB: the right angle at the perpendicular foot was simply missing.

**Root cause.** (1) `relationMarks` has two independent channels — `equalAngles` → arcs, `definiteAngles` → value labels / right-angle squares — with no dedup between them, so an angle that is both equal-to-another and definite gets marked on both. (2) The relations angle universe is built from the figure's neighbour graph (segments + polygon edges + visible lines). A point that lies ON a segment — `F` (on-segment `AB`), or a perpendicular FOOT — is only graph-connected to its OFF-line neighbour (the drawn `EF` / the altitude), NEVER to the host segment's endpoints. So at `F` there is just one ray (to `E`) and no angle is enumerated; the 90° it makes with `AB` is invisible. This hit EVERY foot/altitude, not just this figure.

**Decision.** (1) **A displayed definite value supersedes the equal-arc.** `relationMarks` builds the value labels + right-angle squares first, records each shown angle's key, then draws an equal-angle arc only for angles whose value is NOT shown; a class left with < 2 such members carries no equality and is dropped (surviving classes renumber so the arc-stroke counts stay 1,2,3…). Two angles both labelled "18.4°" already read as equal; angles that are equal but FLOAT (no forced value — isosceles base angles) still get arcs, their only equality signal. (2) **A point on a segment/line contributes its host-line angles.** `onHostEdges` adds, for ANGLE enumeration only, an edge from each `on-segment`/`on-segment-solved`/`midpoint`/`foot` point to its host's two endpoints — NOT to the segment universe (no fake edge). At the endpoint the collinear ray merges with the ray to the far endpoint (rep-dedup), so no spurious angle appears there; only the genuine angles AT the on-host point are added — so ∠EFB = 90° (and every altitude foot's right angle) is now detected and drawn as the square.

**Why this scope (not a patch).** Both are general classes: (1) ANY equal-and-definite angle pair double-marked (equilateral corners, a square's 90°s), (2) ANY perpendicular foot / point-on-a-line whose host-line angle was invisible. Fixed at the layer each defect originates — the mark dedup, and the angle-graph augmentation — not on the one figure.

**Result.** The equilateral triangle now shows three "60°" with NO redundant arcs; a triangle altitude shows the right-angle square at its foot; an isosceles triangle still arcs its (floating) equal base angles. Locked by unit tests in `render/__tests__/relation-marks.test.ts` (value supersedes arc; floating equals still arc) + the engine relations tests. **Full suite green (1450), build clean.** *(Same commit: the "show equal sides & angles" button rename — `viewRelations`/`hideRelations` in both locales — operator request.)*

## ADR-146 — Production usage analytics + a password-protected admin dashboard

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-28). Operator request: "an admin page reporting how many people access the site and what they did with it." *Files: `src/debug/sessionLog.ts`, `server/http.ts` (new), `server/eventLog.ts` (new), `server/admin.ts` (new), `server/standalone.ts`, `server/parseHandler.ts`, `deploy/apache-geo-builder.conf`, `deploy/README.md`, `.env.example`.* Builds on the production-proxy architecture of [ADR-128](#adr-128).

**Context.** Production recorded almost nothing about user activity. The app is a client-side SPA, so typing an utterance never reaches the server — Apache access logs see only page loads and the occasional `/api/parse` (LLM-fallback) call. The rich session logger that already existed (`logDebug` → `POST /api/log` → `logs/debug-log.jsonl`) was **dev-only**: gated by `import.meta.env.DEV` on the client, and its sink was a **Vite dev plugin** absent from the production build. So "what they did" was unobservable in production.

**Decision.** Turn on lean production event logging and add an authenticated dashboard, entirely within the existing Node proxy (no new service, no DB — the data is a JSONL file).

- **Client (`sessionLog.ts`)** — tap the single chokepoint every user action already flows through. In **dev**, behaviour is unchanged (full verbose snapshots → the Vite plugin → `debug-log.jsonl`). In **prod**, emit one *lean* event per action: a `session` marker once per page load, then a `submit` per utterance (`{ utterance, locale, source, result }`) to `${BASE_URL}api/log` (→ `/geo-builder/api/log`). The heavy `kind:'figure'` snapshots stay dev-only. **No `App.tsx` changes** — all routing decided in `logDebug`.
- **Server sink (`eventLog.ts`)** — `POST .../api/log`: validate + normalise to lean fields (drops anything extra the client sends), **hash the client IP** (`HMAC-SHA256(IP_HASH_SALT, ip)`, 16 hex — never the raw IP), append one JSON line to `EVENTS_LOG_PATH`. Best-effort (always `204`), rate-limited, body-capped, self-rotating past 50 MB.
- **Dashboard (`admin.ts`)** — a self-contained Hebrew-RTL report over `events.jsonl` (visitor/session counts, daily traffic, parse-outcome breakdown, language split, top utterances, recent activity), inline CSS + inline SVG bars so the bundle stays one file. Auth mirrors the **isbot dashboard** UX (username/password from env → session → guard → logout) but with a **stateless signed cookie** (`geo_admin = base64(exp).HMAC(secret)`, verified timing-safe each request) — no session store for a single admin. A blank configured password leaves the dashboard locked (never authenticates).
- **Shared `http.ts`** — `clientIp` / `makeRateLimiter` / `readBody` extracted from `parseHandler.ts` so all three handlers reuse them (no duplication).
- **Apache** — proxy `/geo-builder/api/log` and `/geo-builder/admin` to `127.0.0.1:8788` alongside the existing `/api/parse` rule; the Node server matches on the path tail so it works whether the prefix is stripped or forwarded.

**Privacy.** Utterances (math text) are retained intentionally — they *are* "what they did". IPs are stored only as a salted hash, enough to count unique visitors without holding a PII identifier; rotating the salt resets that identity.

**Why this scope (not a one-off page).** The blocker was structural (no production event channel at all), so the fix adds the channel at the layer it was missing — the client chokepoint, a server sink, a shared HTTP layer — rather than scraping coarse web-server logs. The dashboard is then a pure read-only consumer of that channel.

**Result.** End-to-end verified locally against the built `proxy.mjs`: events accepted (`204`), IP persisted only as `iph`, wrong login `401`, correct login sets the signed cookie + redirects, no-cookie → login form, valid cookie → dashboard with live counts. **28 server tests** (`eventLog`, `admin` auth + `aggregate`); **full suite green (1472), build clean.** Remaining: deploy (add the env vars to the root-only `geo-proxy.env`, push `dist/` + `proxy.mjs`, add the Apache rules).

## ADR-147 — A point ON a named carrier ("E על מיתר AC") — descriptor noun tolerated, carrier-defining rules yield to point-on

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-28). Operator-reported: "E על מיתר AC" was not-understood. *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`CARRIER_NOUN`/`SEG_NOUN`/`POINT_ON_CARRIER`, `pointOnSegment`, `pointsOnSegment`, `segment`, `chord`, `withChordMembership`), `src/parser/__tests__/point-on-carrier.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts` (`point-on-chord-named-carrier`).*

**Context.** The point-on rules (`pointOnSegment`, `pointsOnSegment`) required the carrier's two endpoint labels to come **immediately** after the connector על/on: `([A-Za-z]\d*)\s+(?:on|על)\s+([A-Za-z]\d*)\s*([A-Za-z]\d*)`. A student naming the carrier — "E על **מיתר** AC" (chord), "E על **הצלע** AC" (side), "E על **הקטע** AC" (segment), "E על **האלכסון** AC" (diagonal) — wedges a descriptor noun between the connector and the labels, so the regex misses and there's no fallback → `not-handled`. ("E על הישר AC"/"line" worked only because `collinearConstraint` separately strips ישר.) Worse, **with a circle in context** the carrier-**defining** rules (`chord`, `segment`) run before the point-on rules and over-grab: they strip their own keyword, `labelRun` claims the bare "AC" run, and the **named rider point E is silently dropped** — a green build that loses the point the utterance was about.

**Decision.** One general fix at the layer the defect lives (rule routing), not a per-noun patch.
- **`CARRIER_NOUN`** — a single shared alternation of the nouns that can name a point's carrier: `chord|side|segment|diagonal|מיתר|ה?צלע|ה?קטע|ה?אלכסון`. "line"/"ישר" is deliberately excluded — an infinite-line carrier has distinct semantics owned by `collinearConstraint`.
- **`SEG_NOUN`** = an optional `(?:the )?(CARRIER_NOUN) ` group, spliced into `pointOnSegment` and `pointsOnSegment` right after the connector, so the point-on rules skip the noun and read the labels behind it.
- **`POINT_ON_CARRIER`** = `<label> (on|על) (the )?(CARRIER_NOUN)\s` — a guard added to the carrier-defining rules (`segment`, `chord`): when the utterance is a "point ON a carrier" shape, they `return null` and let the point-on rules win (which run later). This is the routing root cause: a point-on utterance must never be claimed by a carrier-definition rule.
- **`withChordMembership`** now also reads a `point-on-segment` carrier (its `a,b`), so the chord's endpoints still land on the resolved circle while the rider `id` (E) stays off it — matching the chord-endpoints-on-circle semantics of [ADR-119](#adr-119).

**Result.** "E על מיתר AC" → `point-on-segment E A C` (no circle), or `+ A,C on circle O` (circle in context); all four nouns + both languages parse; bare carrier definitions ("קטע AC", "segment AC") are unchanged. **Full suite green (1484), build clean.** Locked by `point-on-carrier.test.ts` (unit) + scenario `point-on-chord-named-carrier` (end-to-end).

## ADR-148 — Production-usage-driven parser batch (first real-traffic feedback)

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-29). The FIRST production usage log (ADR-146 analytics, `events.jsonl`) was pulled and analysed: 57 unique visitors / 286 real submissions over one ~9-hour window (100% Hebrew — a class clearly got the link). **31% of submits escalated to the LLM and ~19% failed outright.** Collapsing the double-counted parser-weak→LLM-retry pairs, the genuine grammar gaps clustered into a handful of phrasings — almost all already-supported *constructs* the deterministic grammar simply didn't *phrase-match*. *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`CARRIER_NOUN`, `pointOnSegment`/`POINT_ON_CARRIER`, `perpendicularConstraint`, `circleOnDiameter`, `altitude`, new `dividesInRatio`, new `radiusSegment`), `src/parser/__tests__/production-feedback.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts` (`bagrut-chord-diameter-perp-session`).* The dominant failing flow was one bagrut problem ~all the students typed: `AB קוטר במעגל → D אמצע הרדיוס OB → AC מיתר → E על המיתר AC → DE מקביל ל BC → ED=EC → F על AB → EF אנך ל AB`.

**Decision.** Fix at the layer the defect lives (phrase/keyword coverage), small and additive — a new rule only ever fires on input that currently returns `not-handled`, so it cannot regress a working parse. Operator directive: **no major changes, don't break anything.** Six fixes shipped:

1. **Definite-article chord `המיתר` ([#1], the single biggest cluster, 16×).** `CARRIER_NOUN` listed `מיתר` WITHOUT the optional `ה?` that `ה?צלע`/`ה?קטע`/`ה?אלכסון` all carry, so "המיתר" ("the chord") missed while bare "מיתר" matched (ADR-147 fixed only the indefinite form, and the deploy that masked this matched its behaviour). Fix: `ה?מיתר`, plus an optional descriptor (`נקודה`/`נמצא[הת]`) between the rider label and `על` in `POINT_ON_CARRIER`/`pointOnSegment` so "E נקודה על המיתר AC" / "E נמצאת על המיתר AC" also place E.
2. **Perpendicular as the NOUN `אנך` ([#5], 8×).** `perpendicularConstraint` matched `מאונך`/`⊥`/`⟂` but not the noun "EF **אנך** ל AB"; added `אנך` to the keyword + strip regexes (the `< 2 label-pairs` guard keeps the from-point foot phrasing out).
3. **`AB קוטר במעגל` defines a circle from its diameter ([#3], 9×).** `circleOnDiameter` only fired on a *given* diameter (endpoints already placed); broadened to also fire when the diameter LABELS precede the keyword ("AB קוטר") OR an UNNAMED circle is mentioned ("קוטר במעגל AB") AND no circle exists yet — while the keyword-first + NAMED-circle ADD phrasing ("diameter DE in circle O") still routes to `diameter`.
4. **Perpendicular / altitude FROM a point ([#6], 6×).** The `altitude` rule's from-apex gate required a literal hyphen (`מ-`), and the descriptor nouns (`מנקודה`/`לצלע`) broke the apex/side regexes; both now tolerated → `foot` + the segment to it. "EF אנך ל AB" (2-seg constraint) and the drawn through-line are unaffected.
5. **Divide a segment in a ratio ([#7], new `dividesInRatio` rule).** "G מחלקת את DC ביחס 1:2" / "G divides DC in ratio 1:2" / "היחס בין DG ל-GC הוא 1:2" → `point-on-segment` at `t = p/(p+q)`. Keyword-anchored on `divides`/`מחלק` or `ratio`/`יחס` + a literal `p:q`, ordered before `segment` so "הקטע DC" isn't grabbed and the divider dropped.
6. **Name/draw a radius `OB רדיוס` ([#8], new `radiusSegment` rule).** A bare radius declaration whose two labels include an existing circle's centre → rim point `on-circle` + centre→rim `segment`. Gated (no numeric, no `אמצע`/`=`/`on`) and placed after `midpoint`/`setRadius`/`circle`, so "D אמצע הרדיוס OB" (a midpoint) and "radius … = 5" (a value) are untouched.

**Deferred — `O מרכז המעגל` (name an existing circle's hidden centre, ~3×).** There is NO engine command to (re)name/reveal a circle's centre — relabelling is a STORE op (`parseRename` → `store.rename`) routed outside the construction pipeline in `App.tsx`. Naming the auto/hidden incentre would touch the rename/centre machinery + App routing — a "major change" the operator's directive excludes — for low frequency, and partly entangled with a separate "incircle on an UNNAMED shape" gap. Parked for a dedicated session, not forced here.

**Why phrase-coverage, not new capability.** The encouraging read of the log: the LLM fallback carried 38/57 out-of-grammar submits, and the gaps were `אנך`/`גובה`/`קוטר`/`רדיוס`/definite-articles on constructs the engine ALREADY supports — so each fix is a keyword/phrasing widening, not a new construct. A separate, larger UX item (re-typing an existing shape reads as "couldn't understand" — 52×) is logged in the plan, not in this batch.

**Result.** Every one of the six clusters now parses deterministically (no LLM call); the dominant student session builds a fully-valid figure (`violations: []`). Locked by `production-feedback.test.ts` (27 assertions over the exact student utterances, incl. anti-hijack guards) + the end-to-end `bagrut-chord-diameter-perp-session` scenario. **Full suite green (1512), tsc clean.**

## ADR-149 — A NAMED altitude segment keeps the foot the student named

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-29). Operator manual test: asked for **CD** to be a גובה (altitude) on a triangle; the figure built, but the segment came out **CF** — the student's foot letter `D` was silently replaced by an auto-named `F`. *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`altitude` rule), `src/parser/__tests__/phase4.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts` (`named-altitude-keeps-its-foot-name`).*

**Root cause.** The `altitude` rule derived the apex only from a "from/מ" phrase and **always auto-named the foot** via `freeLabel([apex,p,q], ['F','G','H','P'])` (→ `F`). A leading *named* altitude segment — "**CD** גובה …", where `C` is the apex/vertex and `D` the foot on the opposite side — matched no apex phrase, so it returned `not-handled` and **escalated to the LLM**, which normalised it to "altitude from C". The parser then auto-named the foot `F` and emitted `segment C F` → the canvas drew `CF`, dropping the `D` the student gave. This is an ADR-052-adjacent defect: the tool overrode an explicit student label. (ADR-148 #6 had widened the *from-point* phrasing — the hyphen and descriptor nouns — but the named-segment form was a separate, untouched gap.)

**Decision.** Teach the `altitude` rule to recognise a **leading named altitude segment** and honour the foot the student named, instead of auto-generating it. A new regex (`^ <L><L> (is the|הוא|ה)? (height|altitude|גובה)`) reads the two leading labels as `apex` (vertex) + `namedFoot`; the foot id is then `namedFoot ?? freeLabel(...)`. The opposite side / triangle resolution and the unnamed "from A" path are unchanged.

**Scoped to the height/altitude keyword only.** The leading-name branch fires *only* when the keyword is `height`/`altitude`/`גובה`. The generic perpendicular-from form is deliberately excluded: "**EF אנך ל AB**" is the ⟂ **constraint** (`set-perpendicular`, handled later by `perpendicularConstraint`), and the `altitude` rule runs *before* it in the rule order — if the named-foot branch fired on `אנך`, it would steal the constraint and fabricate a spurious foot. An altitude is never a constraint, so "CD גובה" is unambiguous and safe.

**Result.** "CD גובה ל AB" / "CD גובה במשולש ABC" / "CD is the altitude in ABC" → `foot D from C on AB` + `segment CD` (foot named `D`, no fabricated `F`); the figure builds with `D` on `AB` and `CD ⟂ AB`. The unnamed "גובה מ-A במשולש ABC" still auto-names `F`; "EF אנך ל AB" stays the ⟂ constraint. Locked by `phase4.test.ts` (5 assertions incl. the anti-hijack guard) + the end-to-end `named-altitude-keeps-its-foot-name` scenario. **Full suite green (1517), build clean.**

**Amendment (2026-06-29, after a live retest — the SECOND root cause).** A retest still produced `CF`. The debug log (session `243yyqae`) showed the operator's actual utterance was the bare **"CD גובה"** (triangle ABC already on the canvas, no side/triangle in the utterance) — and it went to the LLM (`source:"llm"` → `גובה מ-C במשולש ABC` → foot `F`). The named-segment regex above was correctly matching `CD`, but the rule then **bailed because it required the opposite side to be STATED in the utterance** — it had no `ctx` parameter and no figure-context fallback, so the most natural phrasing (the triangle is already drawn) returned not-handled and escalated. The `median` rule already derives the opposite side from context; `altitude` didn't. Fix: `altitude` now takes `ctx` and, when no triangle is stated, derives the opposite side from the figure (the two points that, with the apex, are the only points), exactly like `median`. The whole-string label scan for the compound "triangle ABC with a height from A" is preserved (the context fallback only fires when no triangle labels are in the utterance). Lesson: the named-segment regex was necessary but **not sufficient** — the real-world phrasing omits the side, so without the context fallback every bare "CD גובה" still escalated and lost the foot. Now "CD גובה" on a drawn triangle parses deterministically to `foot D` (no LLM). The `named-altitude-keeps-its-foot-name` scenario was rewritten to the operator's exact bare sequence (`משולש ABC` → `CD גובה`). **Full suite green (1533), build clean.**

## ADR-150 — Named-derived-point audit: midsegment keeps its endpoints + altitude keyword-first order

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-29). Follow-up to [ADR-149](#adr-149): the operator asked "are there other similar issues?" — so the bug *class* was audited, not just the one report. The class: **a rule auto-generates a derived point's label and silently discards a name the student supplied.** *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`isUpperLabel` helper, `altitude`, `midsegment`), `src/parser/__tests__/phase4.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts` (`named-midsegment-keeps-its-endpoint-names`, `named-altitude-keyword-first-keeps-foot`).*

**Audit method.** Enumerated every `freeLabel(...)` call site in the parser and classified each: most already honour a named form (`named ?? freeLabel`, `tp ? up(tp) : freeLabel` — circle centres, tangency points, secant/intersection points), and **median**/**angle-bisector** already read a student-named endpoint (the correct model). Two genuine siblings surfaced, plus an incomplete-coverage gap in ADR-149 itself:

1. **Midsegment discarded named endpoints (the true sibling).** "PQ קטע אמצעים לצלע BC במשולש ABC" / "PQ is the midsegment to BC …" auto-named both midpoints `M,N` (via `freeLabel`), renaming the student's `P,Q`. Fix: `midsegment` now reads a leading or keyword-first named pair and uses it for the two midpoint ids; guarded so the pair is NOT the triangle's own vertices.
2. **Altitude keyword-first order (completing ADR-149).** ADR-149 caught only the name-FIRST order ("CD גובה"). The keyword-FIRST order ("הגובה CD" / "the altitude CD") was still not-handled → escalated to the LLM → "altitude from C" → foot auto-named `F` → the original `CF` symptom. Fix: the named-segment detection now matches either word order.

**The connector-word trap (and the fix).** Allowing labels to follow the keyword introduced a misparse: a keyword-first regex `keyword \s+ (L)(L)` reads the lowercase connector word **"to"** as two single-letter labels `t,o` → `T,O` (likewise "in" → `I,N`), so the *unnamed* "the midsegment to BC …" wrongly produced endpoints `T,O`. The clean, convention-aligned discriminator is **case**: the parser's vertex labels are UPPERCASE Latin (`namesVertices = /[A-Z]/`), while connector words are lowercase. A shared `isUpperLabel` helper gates every named-segment capture (the keyword needs the `i` flag, so `[A-Z]` can't be enforced inside the regex — it's validated on the captured token instead). This eliminates the whole connector-word class, not just "to".

**Result.** Both word orders of a named altitude keep the foot; a named midsegment keeps its endpoints; the midsegment theorem holds (P=mid(AB), Q=mid(AC), PQ ∥ BC). Unnamed forms still auto-name (`F`; `M,N`), the ⟂ constraint "EF אנך ל AB" is untouched, and "height from A to BC" is not misread as a name. **Not fixed (logged, lower priority):** a foot-first letter order ("DC גובה", foot written before the vertex) still escalates — `altitude`/`median` both assume the leading letter is the apex, and Israeli textbooks write the vertex first. Locked by `phase4.test.ts` (named-altitude + named-midsegment blocks) + the two end-to-end scenarios. **Full suite green (1531), build clean.**

## ADR-151 — The incircle marks all three tangency points, not just the radius foot

**Status.** Accepted (2026-06-29). Operator (screenshot): an incircle built on an existing triangle ABC ("משולש ABC חוסם מעגל") drew only **one** tangency mark (F on a single side), while the incircle visibly touches all three sides. *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`incircle`), `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts` (`incircle-has-three-tangency-points`), `docs/test-scenarios.md`.*

**Root cause.** The general `incircle` branch builds the incentre (bisector∩bisector), then materialises a **single** ⟂ foot `F` on side AB — used only because `circle-through` needs one point to fix the radius. The other two tangency points were never created, so the figure showed one touch point where geometry has three. (The existing-circle DUAL branch — ADR-115 — already creates three touch points; only the fresh-incircle path was short.)

**Decision.** Materialise a ⟂ foot on **each** side: `F` on AB (also the circle's through-point), `G` on BC, `H` on CA. The latter two are derived 0-DOF points that land **on** the circle automatically because the incentre is equidistant from every side — no new engine construct, no extra solve, built from the existing `foot` primitive. Labels dodge the figure and each other.

**Amendment (centre default → O).** Operator: "why is the centre of the circle I and not O — the default should always be O." The incentre's auto-label preferred `I` (the textbook incentre letter); the project convention is that an **auto-assigned circle centre defaults to `O`** (matching `cornerTangentCircle` and the other circle rules). The preference list is now `['O', 'P', 'Q', 'I']` — `O` unless it is already taken (then `I` as the incentre-flavoured fallback). A student-named centre is still honoured. Tests reading the auto-label updated (`O`).

**Result.** "משולש ABC חוסם מעגל" / "circle inscribed in triangle ABC" now shows all three tangency points (each on its side, all at the inradius from the incentre). The triangle-first scenario `triangle-circumscribes-circle-is-incircle` (ADR-066) is unaffected (its `G` is still the first foot, on side DE). Locked by scenario `incircle-has-three-tangency-points`. **Full suite green (1550), build clean.**

## ADR-152 — Name/reveal an existing circle's hidden centre (`name-center`) — ADR-148 #2 resolved

**Context.** Production triage (2026-06-29, sessions `0nzwixeg`/`ea5dfjpr`): after "מרובע ABCD חסום במעגל" (a circle with a hidden auto-centre O), the student typed "O מרכז המעגל" to *name* the centre and got built-nothing. ADR-148 deferred this #2 as a "major change": no construction command names a centre, and re-creating the circle is idempotent (and would clobber the inscribed circle's radius spec, kicking its vertices off).

**Decision.** A new engine command `{ type:'name-center'; center }` flips the existing circle's `autoCenter` flag OFF (so its centre shows, FR-RN-8) WITHOUT touching the radius. The parser `nameCenter` rule (before `circle`) emits it when the named centre already belongs to a circle; with no circle it bows out so `circle` CREATES one (the opener "O מרכז המעגל"); a different existing-centre label would be a rename (a store op) and defers. `circleCenter` was made keyword-ORDER-independent (letter before/after, He/En, copula+נקודה tolerated, gated on both a centre word and a circle word). `dryRunOutcome` treats `name-center` as "produced" (a visible reveal that adds no object). The `circle` rule defers a "circle inscribed in a polygon" phrasing to `incircle`.

**Consequence.** "O מרכז המעגל" reveals an existing circle's centre (or creates one); the inscribed relations are preserved. Locked by scenario `name-existing-circle-centre` + `production-feedback.test.ts`.

## ADR-153 — Inscribed angle on the diameter (Thales)

**Context.** Operator feature request from the triage report: support "זווית היקפית נשענת על הקוטר" / "inscribed angle on the diameter".

**Decision.** Operator chose REQUIRE-an-existing-circle. The `inscribedAngleOnDiameter` rule (before `diameter`) builds, on the resolved existing circle, a diameter A–B (A on circle, B antipode) + an apex C on the circle + chords A–C, B–C, and `set-angle ∠ACB = 90`. The right angle holds automatically for any C (Thales), so set-angle 90 is a check that draws the right-angle square (the teaching point). With no circle it defers.

**Consequence.** ∠ACB = 90 holds, verifier clean. Locked by scenario `inscribed-angle-on-diameter-thales` + `production-feedback.test.ts`.

## ADR-154 — Generic incircle: any polygon, flexing a quad to tangential

**Context.** Operator feature request: generalise the incircle from triangle-only to all named shapes (original ask: `O הוא מרכז המעגל החסום בטרפז`). Principle: when a quad can adjust its sides to admit an inscribed circle, do it; if rigidly pinned and non-tangential, raise an issue.

**Decision.** The `incircle` rule now detects the polygon kind (triangle/quad/trapezoid/rhombus/square/rectangle/parallelogram) + vertex count, auto-names vertices when unlabeled, and builds: the shape command (carrying its constraints) + bisectors at two ADJACENT vertices → their meet (the incentre) + a foot on every edge + `circle-through` the first foot (inradius). The three edges incident to the two bisector vertices are auto-tangent; every OTHER edge's foot is FORCED onto the circle (`point-on-circle`), flexing the polygon's free DOFs until that side is tangent too (Pitot — the quad becomes tangential). A triangle forces no edge (all auto) → unchanged. A rigidly-pinned non-tangential quad surfaces as over-constraint (the general machinery), per the operator's principle.

**Consequence.** Triangle/quad/trapezoid/rhombus incircles all build with every touch point equidistant from the incentre (true incircle), verifier clean. Locked by scenario `incircle-of-trapezoid-flexes-tangential` + `production-feedback.test.ts`. The existing triangle existing-circle dual (ADR-115) is preserved (gated `n===3`).

## ADR-155 — Parser coverage: keyword-order circle centre + altitude-from-a-point triangle inference

**Context.** Production triage gaps. (1) "O מרכז המעגל" failed while "מרכז המעגל O" worked (see ADR-152 for the centre-naming half). (2) "גובה מנקודה D" (altitude from a vertex, no opposite side stated) failed when the figure had MORE than two other points — the rule's context fallback required the whole figure to be apex+2.

**Decision.** (1) `circleCenter` is keyword-order-independent (ADR-152). (2) The `altitude` rule, when no side is stated and the figure has >2 other points, reads the opposite side off the adjacency (`ctx.neighbors`): the apex's UNIQUE triangle (two neighbours that are also joined to each other) gives the opposite side. Apex in 2+ triangles (ambiguous) DEFERS rather than guess a side (ADR-052, no assumptions). The well-specified "גובה מנקודה D לצלע AB" was never affected.

**Consequence.** Locked by scenario `altitude-from-vertex-infers-triangle` + `production-feedback.test.ts`.

## ADR-156 — Re-entry is idempotent: a construct reuses an existing object instead of minting an auto-named duplicate

**Context.** Operator (local test): inscribing a quad in a circle several times then adding an incircle showed "O and P are on the same point" with stacked centre labels. Root cause: the design's idempotency relies on **deterministic IDs** (`poly-ABCD`, `seg-AB`) — re-issuing a shape/segment collides on the same id and is a no-op. But a circle's id derives from its **centre letter**, and an UNNAMED centre is auto-assigned with `freeLabel`, which picks a *fresh* letter each time (O, then P because O is taken, then Q…). So each re-entry of an auto-named circle construct created a NEW circle; for inscribe/circumcircle all the new centres are the same circumcentre → they coincide ("O and P same point"). The general principle: **auto-naming defeats deterministic-id idempotency.**

**Decision.** A circle-defining construct must **reuse an existing object that already satisfies its definition** rather than auto-name a new one:
- *points-on-a-circle* (inscribe / circumcircle, `inscribedPolygon` allExist branch): if the points are already all on an existing circle (`circleContaining` over `ctx.circleMembers`), reuse it — re-assert only the (deterministic) shape, create no circle. Skipped if the student named a *different* circle.
- *incircle*: its angle-bisector ids are deterministic; if both already exist (new `ctx.lines`), the incircle of that polygon was already built → re-assert the shape only, no duplicate incentre/circle.

`ParseContext` gained `lines` (existing line ids), built in `App.parseCtx` + the scenario/harness ctx builders.

**Consequence.** Re-inscribing reuses the circle (one circumcircle, not O/P/Q); re-issuing the incircle reuses it; a genuine bicentric quad (inscribe + incircle) is one circumcircle + one incircle with no coincidence. Locked by scenario `re-entry-reuses-no-duplicate-circles` + `production-feedback.test.ts`. **Not addressed here (separate, error-message layer):** a fully-idempotent re-entry that now produces nothing still escalates to the "couldn't build" path instead of a friendly "already drawn" — that's the App.submit messaging the parallel session owns.

**Amendment (re-entry messaging — done).** The follow-ups noted above are now built. (1) A clean re-entry that produces nothing NEW (no new label introduced) shows a friendly **"already drawn"** note instead of escalating to the LLM "couldn't build". (2) A cleanly-parsed command the engine can't satisfy against the current figure (dry-run **error**, non-deferrable — e.g. asking an existing trapezoid to become a square → "'C' is already defined") now surfaces the **specific, humanized reason** ("…contradicts an earlier given", "C is already defined — edit/delete the earlier step") rather than escalating to the generic "produced nothing" (the LLM can't fix a geometric contradiction). Locked by `re-entry-noop-message` + `contradiction-message` in the App.submit-faithful suite. _(A deeper option — treating a shape declared on EXISTING points as a CONSTRAINT that reshapes/over-constrains, so "square ABCD" on a trapezoid flexes or gives a true over-constraint — is left as a future enhancement.)_

## ADR-157 — A named shape is immutable once drawn: no morphing into a different shape

**Context.** Operator: "if someone created a trapezoid, two sides are parallel and the other two are not — you cannot turn a trapezoid into a square or a rectangle, even if the user asks. That would be a mistake; we don't need that capability. Give them the error message." (Documenting the intended rule for future cases.)

**Decision (principle).** A named shape (trapezoid / parallelogram / rectangle / rhombus / square / quadrilateral / triangle …) carries **defining constraints that ARE its identity**. Once its vertices are drawn, re-declaring the SAME vertices as a **different, incompatible** shape is a CONTRADICTION and is **refused with a clear error** — it is NOT silently morphed, and we deliberately do **not** offer a "turn shape X into shape Y" capability. To change a shape, the student **edits or deletes the earlier step** (the message says so). This is the correct, intended outcome — a *missing* "morph" feature is not a gap.

**Why.** A trapezoid means exactly one pair of parallel sides; a square/rectangle adds a second parallel pair + right angles/equal sides. Forcing those onto the trapezoid's points contradicts what was already stated. Silently reshaping it would violate the figure the student declared (the same cardinal sin as a fixed default, [ADR-052](#adr-052)).

**Mechanism (how it works today).** A shape command builds its vertices; when those vertices already exist, the engine refuses to redefine them (`'C' is already defined — it can't be redefined as something different`). App.submit surfaces this as the specific humanized conflict message ([ADR-156](#adr-156) amendment), not a generic "produced nothing". Verified: `trapezoid ABCD` then `square`/`rectangle`/`rhombus`/`parallelogram ABCD` all refuse. Locked by scenario `shape-cannot-morph-into-another`.

**Scope / non-goal.** This also blocks a *compatible specialisation* (e.g. rectangle → square) by the same redefinition guard; supporting "declare a shape on existing points as an additional CONSTRAINT that specialises/reshapes" is a deliberate **non-goal** unless a future need arises — and even then, an *incompatible* morph (trapezoid → square) must still be refused per this ADR.

## ADR-158 — Segment-length inequality `DC > AB`: a parser rule for an engine capability that already existed

**Context.** Operator session `ei99765k`: an inscribed trapezoid (`טרפז ABCD חסום במעגל`) always drew `|AB|` longer than `|DC|`, and the natural way to flip it — `DC>AB` — escalated to the LLM and came back **not-understood**. The engine has had a `length-order` constraint and a `set-length-order` command since [ADR-039](#adr-039); only the *parser* couldn't read a direct two-letter segment comparison. The single-letter `measureOrder` rule (`α<β`) handled an ordering between two *named measures*, but `DC` / `AB` are segment references, not variables — so the inequality had no rule.

**Decision.** Add a `lengthOrder` parser rule (after `measureOrder`) that reads a comparison whose two sides are each a two-letter segment: the symbolic forms `DC>AB`, `AB<DC`, `|DC| ≥ |AB|`, and the word forms `DC גדול מ-AB` / `DC longer than AB` (and `קטן` / `shorter` / `smaller`). It lowers to `set-length-order` with the **shorter** segment recorded first, and — like the ∥/⟂ rules ([FR-IN-7](04-functional-requirements.md)) — also DRAWS both segments (idempotent). The two-letter sides disambiguate it cleanly from `measureOrder` (single-letter measures), so `x<y` still parses as a named-measure ordering.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect was a *missing keyword/rule at the parse boundary*, not a missing engine capability — the joint solver already reshapes the figure into the satisfying region for an order constraint (a soft, 0-DOF region constraint, [ADR-039](#adr-039)). The fix is general across every segment pair and both phrasings/locales, not special-cased to the trapezoid that exposed it. It also clears the "AB is always bigger than DC" complaint: that was never a fixed default ([ADR-052](#adr-052)) — the trapezoid's parallel sides are free DOFs — it simply had no way to be *told* which side is longer until now. Locked by scenario `trapezoid-dc-greater-than-ab` + parser tests in `phase4.test.ts`.

## ADR-159 — `submit` paints the "thinking" spinner BEFORE its synchronous solve (a frozen UI with no feedback)

**Context.** Operator (same trapezoid session): typing an impossible inequality like `AD>BC` on a cyclic trapezoid (legs are equal, so it can't hold) took 3–4 seconds to come back with the contradiction, **with no indication the system was working** — the UI just froze. The "show another configuration" path already paints a busy state first (an inline double-rAF added for the same complaint), but `submit` did not: it set `thinking` only around the *LLM* call, while the heavy work — the synchronous `dryRunOutcome` (and the commit replay) — ran **before** that, on the main thread. A React state set is only painted on the next frame, so a blocking synchronous solve in the same tick means the spinner never appears.

**Decision.** `submit` now sets `thinking` true and `await`s a `nextPaint()` (two animation frames — React commits, the browser paints) at the **top of the geometry path** (right after the instant swap/rename/merge store ops), before `parse`/`dryRunOutcome`. The spinner therefore shows from the moment Submit is pressed until the answer, across the dry-run, the commit, and the LLM call. It is cleared on every synchronous exit (conflict / already-drawn / not-understood); the commit paths hand off to `resolveAfterCommit`, which owns the spinner through any auto-resolve search and now also clears it on its already-satisfied early return. The premature `setThinking(false)` right after the LLM `await` was removed so the spinner survives the post-LLM dry-run/commit.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The class of bug is "any synchronous solve in `submit` freezes the UI with no feedback," not just the one impossible `AD>BC` that exposed it — so the busy state is painted once at the entry of the whole geometry path, covering every heavy site (dry-run, commit replay, LLM), rather than wrapping the single reported call. It reuses the exact double-rAF "paint-first" technique the resample and `resolveAfterCommit` paths already rely on, factored into a shared `nextPaint()` helper. UI-only (no engine/parser change); build clean. (The 3–4 s solve time for an impossible order constraint is a separate, untouched perf matter — the ask was feedback, not speed.)

## ADR-160 — Out-of-scope classifier: tailored messages + a dashboard split between "real gaps" and "no need to implement"

**Context.** The operator, reviewing failed inputs, noted that many "not understood" cases are things the tool **deliberately doesn't do** — e.g. `זוויות מתחלפות` (alternate angles), which is an angle *relationship* the tool surfaces once a figure is drawn (Phase 6), not a construction to type. Two problems: (1) the student got the same flat "couldn't read that" as for a genuine gap, learning nothing about what to do instead; (2) the admin dashboard lumped these into one `not-understood` bucket, so deliberate non-features inflated the count of "real gaps we need to build."

**Decision.** A small bilingual **out-of-scope classifier** (`src/parser/scope.ts`, `classifyOutOfScope`) runs in `App.submit` **after both the grammar AND the LLM fallback fail to build** (the operator chose "try the LLM first, then the message"). It recognises four categories — `angle-relation` (named angle/theorem relationships), `proof` (`הוכח`/prove), `compute` (`חשב`/calculate/find the value), and `unrelated` (free text with no geometric signal at all) — and returns a tailored, pedagogical message (`input.scope.<category>`, e.g. "that's a relationship the tool highlights once you draw the figure — not something to type") plus an analytics tag `scope:<category>` (event `source:'scope'`). An input with real geometric content but no category match stays a genuine `not-understood` gap.

The dashboard (`server/admin.ts`) gives `out-of-scope` its own outcome bucket (never mixed with `not-understood`), two headline cards — **"פערים אמיתיים (לטיפול)"** (real gaps to implement = the `not-understood` count) and **"מחוץ לתחום (לא נדרש)"** (out-of-scope) — and a sub-category breakdown panel so the operator sees *which* out-of-scope concepts students type.

**Why this is the right shape, not a patch.** The categories are a single, operator-editable lexicon (add a pattern to extend it), not a special-case for the one reported phrase — and the classifier is deliberately conservative (it must never steal a real construction gap; locked by tests asserting `null` for tangents/secants/intersections/`find the midpoint`). It changes **no** engine/parser geometry behaviour — purely the failure-path message + the analytics tag. Hebrew has no regex `\b`, so Hebrew stems are matched bare and the "geometric signal" test for `unrelated` is case-sensitive for labels (a lowercase greeting isn't read as a point label). Locked by `src/parser/__tests__/scope.test.ts` (24) + `server/__tests__/admin.test.ts` (bucket separation + sub-category breakdown).

**Amendment (drill-down).** The **"פערים אמיתיים (לטיפול)"** and **"מחוץ לתחום (לא נדרש)"** cards are now CLICKABLE: clicking adds `?view=gaps` / `?view=scope` (toggle) to the dashboard URL and opens a panel listing the distinct utterances behind that count — grouped, counted, most-frequent-first, with locale + last-seen — so the operator sees exactly *what to build next* (or what's being typed that we don't need). The drill reads the already-`filterEvents`-filtered events, so it **respects the active date/release filter** automatically; the filter form carries a hidden `view` input and the preset chips preserve it, so changing the date re-filters the open list in place. Pure server-side dashboard addition (`aggregate` gains `gapUtterances`/`scopeUtterances`; `Filter` gains `view`) — no SPA/analytics-schema change, so it works on the existing `events.jsonl`. Locked by the `drill-down` tests in `server/__tests__/admin.test.ts`.

## ADR-161 — Shape-detection badges: on-press, sampled, linking out to the geometry book

**Context.** As a student builds, named shapes *emerge* — a typed `דלתון ABCD`, or a general quad that accumulated constraints have forced into a kite, or an isosceles triangle. The operator wants the tool to **detect which named shapes the figure geometrically contains** and surface each as a clickable **badge** whose popup **links to that shape's page in the geometry book** on the same site (`themathbible.com/bagrut/5-yehidot/571/geometry/<slug>`), so the student is one click from the definition/properties/theorems. This is the near-term, concrete realization of the deferred [FR-REF-1](02-requirements.md); it is **not** the theorem layer (Phase 6) and **not** the "view relations" layer ([ADR-134](#adr-134)) — it is a lighter "what shapes are here, and where do I read about them."

**Decision.** A new, purely-additive feature mirroring the "view relations" plumbing end-to-end:
- **Engine** `src/engine/detectShapes.ts` (`detectShapes`/`detectShapesAcross`) — a pure detector that **samples the figure across its free DOFs** (the same `evaluate(applySeed(c,s))` path the relations layer uses, with its own self-contained sampler so `relations.ts` is untouched) and classifies each `Polygon`/`Circle` by properties that hold in **every** sample. A type is reported only when **forced**: a quad is the *most-specific* of square→rectangle/rhombus→parallelogram→kite→isosceles/right-trapezoid→trapezoid; a triangle is the most-specific equal-sides type (equilateral/isosceles/general) **plus** `right-triangle` when a right angle is forced; a non-hidden circle → `circle`. Forced-across-samples is what makes detection **emergent** (a constrained general quad IS a kite) yet **truthful** (a quad that's square only in the current drawing is not reported square).
- **Map** `src/shapes/shapeCatalog.ts` — the single source of truth `ShapeType → book slug` (versioned with the app; names/definitions live in i18n under `shapes.name.*`/`shapes.def.*`).
- **Store** — a `shapes` slice with the **same facts-keyed cache contract** as `relations` (auto-invalidates on any fact change, survives "show another configuration", excluded from undo) + `detectShapes`/`clearShapes`.
- **UI** — a "detect shapes" on-press toggle beside "view relations"; when on, a row of badges (localized name + vertex label); clicking a badge opens a `Modal` with the name, a one-line definition, and a prominent "open in the geometry book ↗" link (new tab).

**Why on-press (not automatic).** Auto-surfacing an *emergent* shape ("this quad is secretly a kite") reveals a derived truth that can clue the solution — the same boundary that keeps "view relations" opt-in (Pedagogy §5.1). A button keeps the student in control and also avoids re-sampling on every keystroke.

**Why this is additive, not a change to existing behavior.** All logic is in new files; the three existing-file edits only *add* — a new store slice, a new button/badges/popup, a new `shapes` i18n group — with no existing action, selector, parser, or render path altered. `relations.ts`, the engine reducers, `parse.ts`, and the renderer are not touched. Locked by `src/engine/__tests__/detectShapes.test.ts` (classification + the emergent-kite case + the negatives: free quad ≠ named quad, rhombus ≠ square) and `src/store/__tests__/shapes-slice.test.ts` (cache/clear). **Out of scope (later):** theorem surfacing in the popup (Phase 6), n>4 polygons (no book page yet). **1645 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-162 — Detect IMPLICIT geometry: a shared edge universe for equal-segments + emergent shapes

**Context.** Right after the shape badges shipped ([ADR-161](#adr-161)) the operator found the deeper bug they really meant: **detection only ever considered DECLARED objects**, so anything a student sees *implicitly on the page* was invisible. Two reports, one root cause: (1) `טרפז ABCD חסום במעגל` → `E על AB` → `ED מקביל ל BC` makes a **parallelogram EBCD** (sides `EB`=part of `AB`, `BC`, `CD`, `DE`) with **no `polygon` object**, so the shape detector never saw it; (2) with `AB` a diameter through centre `O`, the radii **`OA`/`OB`** are the two halves of `AB`, but "view relations" never marked them equal because its equal-**segment** universe was `pointNeighbors` (drawn segments + polygon edges) only. The equal-**angle** universe already did the right thing — it adds `visibleLineEdges` + `onHostEdges` (on-segment/midpoint/foot ↔ host endpoints) to `pointNeighbors`.

**Decision.** Introduce one shared **implicit edge universe** — `figureEdges(c)` in `relations.ts` = `pointNeighbors` + `onHostEdges` + `visibleLineEdges`, canonicalised/deduped — and feed it to BOTH layers:
- **Equal segments** (`detectRelations`): the segment universe is now `figureEdges(c0)` instead of `pointNeighbors` only, so an on-host split like `OA`/`OB` (the halves of a diameter through its midpoint `O`) is detected equal. The "equal in every sample" gate, dedup, `RelationsResult` shape, and the tick renderer (which places ticks purely by position lookup) are all unchanged; only the candidate edge set grows.
- **Emergent shapes** (`detectShapes`): enumerate triangle (3-cycle) and quadrilateral (4-cycle) cycles over `figureEdges`, classify each with the existing `classifyQuad`/`classifyTriangle`, require the polygon be **simple & non-degenerate in every sample** (a shoelace-area + bowtie-cross test), and — **conservatively** — keep an emergent cycle only if it is a NAMED special type (a generic quad classifies to null; a generic emergent triangle is dropped). Declared-polygon classification is unchanged; emergent cycles are additive and deduped against declarations by `(type, vertex-set)`. A perf guard skips emergent enumeration above 16 graph vertices.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The reported symptoms (missing parallelogram, missing radii equality) are two faces of ONE flaw — the universe was built from declarations, not from what is visibly drawn — so the fix is the shared `figureEdges` definition both layers (and, already, angles) use, not a special case for the one figure. Forced-across-samples still gates every relation, so the broader universe surfaces only *genuinely* implicit truths (e.g. on the operator's figure it also correctly finds the isosceles triangle `ADE`, since `EBCD` ∥-gram ⇒ `DE=BC` and the iso-trapezoid ⇒ `AD=BC` ⇒ `AD=DE`), never coincidences. This DOES change existing "view relations" behaviour (more equal-segment ticks may appear) — the operator's explicit ask. Locked by `relations.test.ts` (the diameter `OA=OB` class), `detectShapes.test.ts` (emergent parallelogram from the operator's figure + a conservative-no-generic-triangle negative), and scenario `emergent-parallelogram-between-segments` (the exact operator sequence). **Out of scope:** generic radii `O–P` for arbitrary on-circle points (too noisy; the diameter case is covered by the on-host split), n>4 emergent polygons. **1653 tests green, build clean.**

**Amendment (badge interaction — [ADR-161](#adr-161) FR-SH-3).** A user expects a badge that names an on-canvas shape to *show* it; the link is the higher-value payload but not the expected gesture. Resolved as both, without conflict: **hovering** a badge highlights its shape on the figure (its vertices + the drawn edge segments whose endpoints are all shape vertices — reusing the existing `highlight: Set<Id>` canvas mechanism, so ~free), and **clicking** opens a small **inline card** (name + definition + book link) *below the badges* instead of the original full-screen `Modal` — so the highlighted figure stays visible while the link is shown (the modal had been the only thing forcing an either/or). UI-only and additive; no engine/detector change. The `EB`-style side of an emergent shape that is a sub-piece of a longer segment is not its own segment object so that single edge isn't lit, but its endpoints are — an acceptable v1 cue. Build clean.

## ADR-163 — A "right triangle"'s right-angle vertex is an unstated default that yields to an explicit angle

**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-30)

**Context.** The operator entered `ABC משולש ישר זוית` then `זווית ABC = 90`, and the second step was refused: `over-constrained: ∠ABC = 90° cannot hold`. The `right-triangle` construct ([apply.ts](../src/engine/apply.ts)) pins the right angle at the **last** named vertex *structurally* — A and C are free, B is built `perp-offset` ⟂ to `CA` at C, so `∠C = 90°` for any A,C (a rigid construction, not a constraint). When the student then states the right angle is at a *different* vertex, that explicit `set-angle = 90` collides with the structural `∠C = 90` (two right angles in one triangle is impossible) and is rejected. The student can only work around it by renaming or reordering the letters (`ABC` → `ACB`).

**Decision.** WHICH vertex carries the right angle in a bare "right triangle ABC" is **unstated**, so per [ADR-052](#adr-052) it is a *default*, not a given — and like the [ADR-114](#adr-114) soft isosceles equal-pair, it must **yield to an explicit statement**. A position-independent **pre-scan in `replay`** ([geoStore.ts](../src/store/geoStore.ts)) collects every enabled explicit `set-angle` of 90°, and for each `right-triangle` fact whose vertex set contains such a vertex (and it isn't already last), **reorders the triangle's ids so that vertex is last** — the structural right-angle position. The explicit `∠ABC = 90` then lands on a vertex that is *already* 90° and applies as a **passing check** rather than a conflict. Works whether the angle is typed before or after the triangle (it's a pre-scan, like the ADR-114 soft-drop and ADR-138 variant-pin scans it sits beside).

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect is the same class ADR-052/ADR-114 already name — a magnitude/position the question never fixed was silently pinned — so the fix reuses that pattern (a default that defers to the student's statement) rather than special-casing the one utterance. It re-seats the right angle for *any* of the three vertices and any entry order, and changes nothing when the student doesn't state an angle (lone "right triangle ABC" still draws the right angle at C) or states it on the default vertex (no-op reorder). Locked by scenario `right-triangle-explicit-angle-reseats-right-vertex` (the exact operator sequence). **1655 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-164 — A single-vertex angle ("∠B = 90") resolves its arms when unambiguous, else asks for three letters

**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-30)

**Context.** Stating an angle required all three letters (`∠ABC = 90`, vertex = middle). A student naturally writes `∠B = 90` / `זווית B = 90`, which fell through the grammar to the LLM — wasteful and unreliable for an in-grammar intent. The acuteness rule ([ADR-108](#adr-108)) already resolves a single-vertex angle's two arms from the figure (`ctx.neighbors`), but only when the vertex has exactly two edges; the value-based `angle` rule did not. The operator asked: support `∠B = 90`, but **only** when there is exactly one angle at B; if B has several edges (several possible angles), don't guess — tell the student to name all three letters.

**Decision.** The `angle` rule gains a single-vertex branch: for a clean `∠<V> = <number>` (exactly one label besides the value), resolve the arms from `ctx.neighbors[V]`.
- **Exactly two edges at V** → emit `set-angle` with those two arms (and draw them), identical to the three-letter form.
- **Any other count** (more = ambiguous; fewer = no arms to use) → return a new **clarification** result `{ ok:false, reason:'ambiguous-angle', vertex }`, surfaced by the app as "there's more than one angle at V — name all three letters" and logged `ambiguous-angle:<V>`. This is a THIRD `ParseResult` variant alongside `not-handled`; rules signal it via a `Clarify` return, and crucially it does **not** escalate to the LLM (a phrasing the grammar fully understands but that is genuinely ambiguous must be disambiguated by the student, not guessed).

The three-letter form is unchanged and still parses regardless of `neighbors`. The branch is gated to a single clean label so compounds still fall through to the LLM.

**Consequences.** `∠B = 90` on a triangle vertex now works directly (and composes with [ADR-163](#adr-163): the explicit angle re-seats a right triangle's right angle). The clarification channel is reusable for other "understood but ambiguous" inputs. Locked by `parser/__tests__/single-vertex-angle.test.ts` (build at 2 edges; ambiguous at >2 and at 0; three-letter form intact) and scenario `single-vertex-angle-on-triangle-vertex`. **1661 tests green, build clean.**

**Amendment (2026-06-30).** The first cut of [ADR-163](#adr-163) reseated the *geometry* but not the right-angle MARK: `angleMarkFor` drew the right-triangle's knee at the original `ids[2]` (the un-reseated last vertex), so after `∠ABC = 90` the figure showed a knee at C (now 38.7°) *and* one at B — the operator's "weird image" (two knees). Fixed: `replay` builds the right-triangle's angle mark from the reseated ids, so a single knee sits at the actual right-angle vertex B (and dedups with the explicit `set-angle` mark). Locked by an added assertion in `right-triangle-explicit-angle-reseats-right-vertex` (exactly one knee, at B).

## ADR-165 — A constraint that morphs a named shape is ALLOWED but flagged amber (it doesn't refuse)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-30)

**Context.** `טרפז ישר זווית ABCD` (a right trapezoid, angles 90/63/117/90) then `זווית ABC = 90` silently produced a **rectangle** (90/90/90/90): with ∠A and ∠D already 90, forcing ∠B = 90 makes the legs parallel, so the declared trapezoid is no longer one. [ADR-157](#adr-157) ("a named shape is immutable — refuse a morph") guards only *re-declaring a different shape WORD* on existing vertices; a **constraint** that reshapes the figure ([ADR-033](#adr-033) — shapes carry their true DOF) slips past it, and the result was shown as a clean green. (This predates the ADR-163/164 angle work — the three-letter `∠ABC = 90` morphs it too; that work just made the operator hit it.) Operator decision: **allow but flag amber** — the figure is geometrically valid (don't refuse it), but the student must be told the declared shape is gone.

**Decision.** The givens verifier (`verify.ts`, [ADR-053](#adr-053)) gains a shape-identity check: a declared `trapezoid` asserts the identity "**exactly one** pair of opposite sides is parallel" (its legs must not be parallel). If BOTH opposite-side pairs are parallel within ~1° in the final coordinates, raise a `figure.v.trapezoidMorph` violation — surfaced through the existing amber/violations channel ("ABCD was declared a trapezoid but both pairs of opposite sides are now parallel — edit/delete the trapezoid step"). A genuine trapezoid (incl. right/isosceles) keeps its legs clearly non-parallel, so it never false-fires.

**Scope / why amber not refuse.** Per the operator's choice this is a non-blocking cue, consistent with the verifier's role (green = VERIFIED, amber = built-but-doesn't-match-its-givens). Scoped to the **trapezoid family** — the clearest, operator-reported morph and the one with a crisp identity inequality. A *general* "any constraint that turns shape X into a more-specific shape Y" detector (e.g. parallelogram → rectangle, where Y *is* an X) was the larger alternative and is deliberately **not** built here; if other morphs prove confusing in practice, extend the same per-shape identity check. Locked by scenario `trapezoid-constraint-morph-flags-amber` (the exact operator sequence, `expectViolations`). **1662 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-166 — Two SEGMENTS that meet must meet ON the segments, not on the continuation (+ apex reflection as an explorable DOF)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-30)

**Context.** Bagrut Q9 (operator session `doykqc2m`): a rectangle `ABCD` with equilateral triangles `AED`, `BCF` on the two vertical sides, then `AE ו BF נפגשים בנקודה G` and `DE ו CF נפגשים בנקודה H` (prove `EGFH` is a rhombus). The figure built clean (no error) but was the **mirror** of the textbook: the triangle apexes `E`,`F` were sampled pointing **outward** (away from each other, outside the rectangle), so segments `AE`,`BF` diverge and never cross — and `line-line-intersection` computes the **infinite-line** crossing, which landed on the **backward continuation** behind `A` and `B` (param ≈ −1.02 on both segments). Operator: *"when we say two segments intersect, it needs to be ON the segments, not the continuation."*

Two root causes, both addressed (a narrow "require within" patch alone is insufficient — the correct configuration must also be *reachable*):
1. **No on-segment requirement.** A plain `line-line-intersection` had no rule that the crossing lie within both segments; the infinite-line point was accepted silently and passed `meetsRequirements`/the verifier.
2. **The apex side wasn't reachable.** Which side of the base an equilateral/isosceles apex sits is an *unstated discrete DOF* ([ADR-052](#adr-052)). The continuous sampler ([ADR-018](#adr-018)) flips it only by luck (~2% of seeds; first good seed 62), and the auto-resolver searches 40 — so even with requirement #1 the inward config was never *found*.

**Decision.**
- **Parser** flags a `line-line-intersection` `onSeg` when the utterance names a plain segment meet — **no** `המשך`/extension and **no** `הישר`/`line`/`ray` (those opt into a crossing allowed off the drawn segments). The flag is *utterance-level*: any extension/infinite word drops it, so a deliberately-extended figure (e.g. `המשך CA ו BD נפגשים בנקודה G`, where the operator accepted `G` beyond `D`) is unchanged. Carried onto the engine object (`apply.ts`).
- **Requirement** `intersectionsWithinSegments` (store) — every `onSeg` crossing's param ∈ [0.02, 0.98] on both operands — added to `meetsRequirements` and the resolvers. The **verifier** (`verify.ts`) raises an amber `figure.v.meetOnSegment` (looser tolerance: only a crossing genuinely off the segment, param <−0.02 or >1.02) so an unresolvable figure is honestly flagged rather than shown clean.
- **Apex reflection as an explorable discrete DOF.** A free point tied to ≥2 anchors by an equality/distance (`reflectableFreePoints`) has a mirror solution the numeric solver won't reach from its seed. We encode the reflection choice in the **high bits of the seed integer** (`REFLECT_STRIDE`, `withReflectMask`): the low bits are the continuous sample (today's behaviour, byte-for-byte unchanged for every existing seed `< REFLECT_STRIDE`), the high bits are a bitmask over the reflectable points. `applyReflections` (store) evaluates once to learn the anchor positions, mirrors each masked apex's solved position across its anchor line, and re-seeds the solver to that mirror basin. `firstSatisfyingSeed`/`findValidConfig` search reflection seeds (the *targeted* mask — mirror exactly the apexes whose segments fail to reach — first, then the other subsets) over a small band of continuous seeds, so the textbook config is found in a handful of tries (~7 s behind the resolve spinner) instead of a ~200-seed sweep.

**Why this shape / alternatives rejected.** A pure "require within + widen the seed budget to ~200" was rejected: the good seeds are sparse (~2%) and a 200-seed sweep of this coupled figure is minutes. Per-operand strictness (require each non-`המשך` operand within) was rejected because an explicitly-extended utterance legitimately puts the *other* operand off its segment (the Q4-family `המשך CA ו BD`), so the rule is utterance-level. The reflection is general (any apex equidistant to two anchors), bounded (≤4 reflectable points → mask ≤15), and gated by the full `meetsRequirements` (verifier + convex + distinct), so a bad mirror is never accepted. Locked by scenario `segment-meet-lands-on-segments` (the exact operator sequence). Existing no-extension intersections (kite `N=BE∩AC` 0.92/0.91; Q4 `H=AF∩BC` 0.74/0.29) already land within, so the requirement doesn't regress them.

**Amendment (same session) — the emergent `EGFH` rhombus is now DETECTED.** Operator follow-up: "there is a מעוין that the shape detector didn't detect, probably because of the node-definition issue again" (the ADR-162 class). Three coupled causes, all fixed:
1. **Node definition.** `G`/`H` are `line-line-intersection` points that lie ON their operand segments, but `onHostEdges` (the implicit-edge universe, ADR-162) only split `on-segment`/`midpoint`/`foot` hosts — so `G` had no neighbours and the `EGFH` cycle was invisible. Fix: an `onSeg` `line-line-intersection` now splits both its operand segments (`G` ↔ `A,E,B,F`). Scoped to `onSeg` (within) crossings — an extension meet isn't a clean split.
2. **Detection sampled the wrong config.** `viewRelations`/`detectShapes` replayed at seed 0 (mask 0 = the requirement-VIOLATING outward config), so `EGFH` was degenerate in every sample. Fix: both now use `firstSatisfyingSeed` as the base (0 for any figure without a segment-meet/extension, so unchanged elsewhere).
3. **Diverged samples masked the forced shape.** The equilateral-apex solver diverges at ~2/16 seeds (coordinates ~1e8 while `evaluate` still reports `ok`), and the "forced in EVERY sample" test read those garbage configs as counterexamples. Fix: `convergedSamples` drops samples whose bbox diagonal exceeds 50× the median (a robust, scale-relative outlier filter), shared by both detection layers. With all three, `detectShapes` reports `rhombus:EGFH` (the crossings' sub-segments are equal in every valid sample). Locked by the same scenario's `check` (asserts the rhombus is detected).

---

## ADR-167 — The implicit-edge universe is GEOMETRIC, not a whitelist of point kinds

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-01)

**Context.** A deep-review request from the operator: *"we keep playing around this and fixing things but not the root cause."* Detection of shapes/relations that are **visibly on the page but never declared** (an emergent rhombus, two equal sub-segments, an isosceles triangle whose sides run through a crossing) kept missing figures, and each fix added another special case. The ADR log shows the loop directly: [ADR-162](#adr-162) introduced the shared implicit-edge universe `figureEdges = pointNeighbors + onHostEdges + visibleLineEdges`, where `onHostEdges` was a **hand-maintained whitelist of point KINDS** allowed to split their host (`on-segment`/`on-segment-solved`/`midpoint`/`foot`); [ADR-166](#adr-166) Am. then had to **add another entry** (`onSeg` `line-line-intersection`) — the operator's own note called it *"the node-definition issue, **again**."* [ADR-162](#adr-162) Am. also shipped the highlight of a sub-piece edge as a known "acceptable v1 cue." The defect: **the edge universe was derived from how each point was CONSTRUCTED, not from the geometry on screen.** Any point that lands on a drawn segment via a kind not on the list — a non-`onSeg` crossing, a `set-line` collinear point, a purely emergent coincidence like a rectangle's diagonals bisecting — is invisible as a splitter, so the emergent shapes/relations through it go undetected. The operator's principle: *"if two nodes exist and there is a line between them (not necessarily defined by the nodes), include them."*

A reproduction (rectangle `ABCD`; equilateral `BCE`,`DAF` inward; `EC ∩ DF = G`; `BE ∩ AF = H`) confirmed the diagnosis and, importantly, that the CURRENT figure already passes detection on HEAD (ADR-166's whitelist entry happens to cover this exact crossing kind) — so the fix is about the *class*, not the one figure. Instrumentation also showed the reproducible half of the report is the **sub-segment highlight** (App's `shapeHighlight` matches only stored `segment` objects, and `Figure` lights strictly by object id, so `G–C`, a slice of `EC`, is unhighlightable) — left out of scope here per the operator's steer that this fix should not touch the renderer/build.

**Decision.** Replace the construction-kind whitelist with a **geometric** split, `collinearSplits(c, samples)` in [relations.ts](../src/engine/relations.ts). A *carrier* is any drawn 1-D primitive with two endpoint ids (a `segment` or a polygon edge). A point splits a carrier iff, across the sampled configurations, it is **collinear on the infinite line in EVERY sample** (forced by the givens — never a coincidence of one drawing) **AND lands within the drawn span in at least one valid config** (so it is a genuine sub-segment, not a pure-extension phantom). Each carrier then emits **every pair** among {its endpoints} ∪ {its interior points}, so both the whole segment and every sub-segment (`E–G`, `G–C`) are first-class edges. `figureEdges` becomes `pointNeighbors + collinearSplits + visibleLineEdges` and now takes `samples`; the equal-**segment** universe, the equal-**angle** adjacency, and the emergent-shape cycle graph are all built from this single set. `onHostEdges` is deleted. `visibleLineEdges` stays as-is (a drawn line's on-points are structural membership, already all-pairs — no whitelist problem there).

**Why collinear-in-every-sample but within-span-in-SOME.** The separation of concerns is the crux and the reason the first attempt regressed [ADR-166](#adr-166). *Collinearity* of a constructed/emergent point with its carrier is FORCED (it holds in every valid drawing), so requiring it in every sample cleanly rejects a coincidental alignment of one drawing. *Within-span*, however, is **not** forced for a segment-meet: the sampler ([ADR-018](#adr-018)/[ADR-166](#adr-166) reflection DOF) also visits mirror configs where the crossing `G` sits beyond an endpoint (`t` ∈ [0.74, 1.62] across converged samples for the Q9 figure), even though the requirement-satisfying config has it interior. Requiring within-span in every sample dropped the split and un-detected the rhombus (a real regression caught by the ADR-166 scenario). The fix mirrors the old whitelist's virtue — the edge universe stays **topological**; whether the resulting cycle is a FORCED shape is decided **downstream** by the classifier's existing "holds in every sample" gate — while removing its vice (dependence on the point's kind).

**Why this is the root fix, not another patch.** The whitelist could never be complete — every new construct that places a point on a line needed registering, which is exactly the loop ADR-162 → ADR-166 → "again." The geometric rule is closed under all point kinds at once: an intersection (onSeg or not), a foot, a midpoint, a collinear-constrained point, or an emergent coincidence all split the carrier they land on, with no per-kind code. Forced-across-samples still gates every reported relation/shape, so the broader universe surfaces only genuine implicit truths, never coincidences. **Out of scope (unchanged):** the sub-segment highlight (renderer-side; a separate opt-in), drawn `line` carriers (already handled by `visibleLineEdges`), n>4 emergent polygons.

**Consequences / tests.** Pure detection-layer change; `scene.ts`/`Figure.tsx`/`App.tsx` untouched.
