Locked by: `collinear-splits.test.ts` (the split is kind-independent for a plain free point; a one-sample coincidence does NOT split; an endpoint-coincident point does NOT split), scenario `emergent-shapes-through-crossings` (the operator's exact 5-utterance figure — ABH, CDG, and rhombus EGFH all detected, plus the AH=BH=CG=DG and EG=EH=FG=FH equal-segment classes), and the pre-existing `segment-meet-lands-on-segments` (ADR-166 rhombus) which the within-every-sample first attempt regressed and the final rule restores. Supersedes the `onHostEdges` mechanism of [ADR-162](#adr-162) (its equal-radii `OA=OB` and emergent-parallelogram cases now come from the geometric split). **1667 tests green, build clean.**

**Amendment (renderer — the operator then opted into the highlight, and raised the clutter problem).** Two renderer additions, on top of the engine fix:
1. **Sub-segment highlight.** App's `shapeHighlight` now emits the shape's boundary as point-PAIRS (`shapeHighlightEdges`, consecutive vertices) instead of matching stored `segment` objects; `Figure` gained a `highlightEdges` prop that strokes each pair between its endpoints' (oriented) positions. So an edge that is only a portion of a longer drawn segment (`G–C` ⊂ `EC`, no object of its own) lights up — the fix for "CDG's segments not highlighted correctly." `transform.ts` gained `toWorld` (the inverse of `toScreen`). Locked by a `phase2.test.tsx` render assertion.
2. **Hover-to-focus for "view relations" (the clutter fix).** A rich figure marked with every equal-length tick + equal-angle arc at once is unreadable and mis-read (counting 1-vs-4 ticks in a dense centre). Rather than paint it all, the relations layer is now **hover-driven**: the resting figure is clean, and pointing at a side/angle on the CANVAS reveals ONLY its equality class (`relationAt` picks the class under the cursor — a segment by perpendicular distance, an angle by pointing into its wedge near the vertex; `relationsForPick` narrows the `RelationsResult` to that class; the hovered length class also gets accent strokes on its members). Direct manipulation, no chip to hunt for; a one-line hint tells the student to hover. The pure pickers are unit-tested (`relation-marks.test.ts`); the pointer wiring lives in `Figure`. Engine untouched.
3. **Corner value drawn once (double-label fix).** Hovering the emergent rhombus showed `60° 60°` at each of its `60°` corners: the corner's angle is forced-`60°` under two IDs — `∠AFD` and `∠GFH` — because `H` lies on ray `FA` and `G` on ray `FD`, so the cross-sample angle universe enumerates them as two angles even though they are one wedge. `relationMarks` now keys a definite-angle value by its **wedge** (vertex + the two ray DIRECTIONS from the drawn positions) instead of by point IDs, so the second is deduped and the equal-arc suppression is wedge-based too. Operator-reported on the working hover feature. Locked by a `relation-marks.test.ts` case (`∠AFD == ∠GFH ⇒ one "60°"`). **1672 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-168 — One PRODUCTION `submit` per user submission (the dashboard's double-row fix)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-01)

**Context.** The operator, reading the admin **usage dashboard** ("פעילות אחרונה" / recent activity), saw a construction they'd entered themselves — `F ו E נמצאות על הצלע AB של מקבילית ABCD` — appear as **two rows with the same timestamp**: one tagged `נותח (LLM)` (`llm-built`) and one `חלקי / נשמט` (`weak`). Their read was exactly right: *"first one is from the engine sending to LLM and the other is the LLM succeeding, but only the LLM success should appear."* The debug log confirms the pattern generally — an utterance that the grammar parses only partially logs `parser … weak:*` and then, ~2 s later, `llm …` for the same text.

**Root cause.** `logDebug({kind:'input', …})` is used for **two different purposes** that collide on one code path. It is both (a) the DEV debug-trace step — every meaningful thing that happened, so a session can be reconstructed — and (b) the PROD analytics event — one `submit` per user action, appended to `events.jsonl` and aggregated by the dashboard. For every submission except one, `handleSubmit` logs exactly one `kind:'input'` event and returns. The exception is the escalation path ([App.tsx](../src/App.tsx)): when the grammar parses **partially** (a dropped new label) or **builds nothing** (`weak`), it logs a `weak` step and then **falls through** to the LLM, which logs the submission's **final** outcome (`llm-built` / `not-understood` / `out-of-scope`). Both are `kind:'input'`, so [sessionLog.ts](../src/debug/sessionLog.ts)'s PROD branch emitted a `submit` for **both** — double-counting the utterance and painting a phantom `weak` row beside its real outcome. The `weak` bucket in the dashboard was therefore *always* an intermediate double-count (a `weak` step is never a final outcome — it unconditionally escalates); the true escalation rate is already the `llmFallbacks` count.

**Decision.** One user submission → one analytics `submit`, the **final** one. The two `weak` `logDebug` calls are tagged `intermediate: true`; `logDebug`'s PROD branch skips flagged events. Factored the decision into a **pure** `analyticsSubmit(event)` that returns the lean submit payload or `null` (dropping non-`input` kinds *and* `intermediate` steps), so the "one submit per submission" rule is unit-testable without `import.meta.env`/`fetch`. **DEV is untouched** — the full debug trace still records the `weak` step (it returns before the PROD branch), so session reconstruction keeps the escalation detail; only the PROD analytics sink drops it.

**Why this is the root fix, not a dashboard patch.** The symptom is two rows in `aggregate`, so the tempting patch is to dedup at aggregation time (collapse a `weak`+`llm` pair by sid+utterance+near-timestamp). That is fragile (timestamp windows, which pairs belong together) and leaves `events.jsonl` — the source of truth every stat reads (`submits`, outcome breakdown, top utterances, recent) — carrying phantom rows. Fixing at the **emission** layer means the log itself only ever holds real user submissions, so *all* downstream numbers are correct with no per-consumer dedup. The defect is conceptual — an intermediate diagnostic step masquerading as a user action — so the fix is to stop emitting it as one.

**Consequences / tests.** Client-logging change only; no engine/parser/renderer touch, no ADR-supersession. Locked by `src/debug/__tests__/sessionLog.test.ts` (a `figure` snapshot → no submit; a final parser/LLM step → one submit; an `intermediate` weak step → none; the weak→LLM pair → exactly one submit, the LLM's). **Historical note:** `events.jsonl` rows written *before* this build still carry the old duplicates — the fix prevents new ones, it does not rewrite the past; the release filter (`rel=`) separates pre-/post-fix data. **1677 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-169 — A trapezoid's height drops to the OPPOSITE PARALLEL BASE (altitude inference generalised past the triangle)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-01)

**Context.** Operator report (session `sub2ys2a`): on a right trapezoid `טרפז ABCD ישר זווית`, the utterance `CE גובה בטרפז` ("CE is the height in the trapezoid") escalated to the LLM and returned **not-understood**, even though the same construct works on a triangle (`ABC משולש` → `CD גובה` → `foot(D, from C, a A, b B)` + `segment CD`). The operator: *"I have גובה בטרפז which I think we should have covered — it works in a triangle."*

**Root cause.** The `altitude` rule ([parse.ts](../src/parser/parse.ts)) parses the apex + (optional) named foot fine, but resolves the **opposite side** with triangle-only logic: an explicit "to BC", else a triangle named in the utterance, else the two-other-points fallback, else — the general case — the apex's *unique enclosing triangle* read off `ctx.neighbors` (two neighbours of the apex that are themselves joined). In trapezoid `ABCD` (edges AB·BC·CD·DA, so AB ∥ DC by the engine's build), the apex C's neighbours are **B and D — a diagonal, not an edge**, so no triangle closes and the rule returns `null` → LLM → not-understood. The rule simply had no notion of a *height in a quadrilateral*.

**Decision.** A height/altitude from a vertex drops to the **opposite parallel base**. The parser gains a figure-derived hint, `ParseContext.parallels` — the figure's **vertex-disjoint parallel edge-pairs** (a trapezoid's two bases `[['A','B'],['D','C']]`), computed by a new pure engine helper `parallelEdgePairs(construction, positions)` over the drawn segments/polygon edges (parallelism holds structurally for a trapezoid, so one resolved snapshot suffices). This is the same category of derived hint the parser already consumes — `neighbors`, `circleMembers` — not new geometry knowledge in the grammar. In the `altitude` rule, when no explicit side is given, `oppositeParallelBase(apex, ctx.parallels)` runs **before** the triangle inference: among the parallel pairs, it takes the partner edge of a pair whose *other* edge carries the apex. **Exactly one** such base ⇒ use it (the trapezoid height — foot on that base, `CE ⟂ AB`); **zero** (a triangle, whose `parallels` are empty — so it never interferes — or a leg-only apex) or **several** (a parallelogram's two parallel pairs → two valid heights) ⇒ null, and the rule falls through to the existing triangle logic or defers, per ADR-052 (no guessing when ambiguous).

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect is that "opposite side" was hard-wired to the triangle case; the fix supplies the *general* target-resolution (opposite parallel base) and routes the trapezoid — and any future quad whose apex sits on a base with a unique parallel partner — through it, with the triangle path untouched (its empty `parallels` short-circuit the new branch). The special-case alternative — a keyword hack that maps "trapezoid + height" to "foot on the 1st–2nd vertices" — would assume the student labelled ABCD in canonical order (an unstated given, exactly what ADR-052 forbids) and would not generalise. Threading `parallels` also leaves the door open for other parallel-aware constructs (midsegment-of-a-trapezoid, etc.) to reuse it.

**Consequences / tests.** Parser + one engine helper + context plumbing (App.tsx `parseCtx`, tests' `ctxOf`); no change to the engine's evaluation or the renderer. Locked by scenario `altitude-in-trapezoid-drops-to-opposite-base` (the operator's exact `טרפז ABCD ישר זווית` · `CE גובה בטרפז` — E on line AB, CE ⟂ AB, all steps verified) plus `phase4.test.ts` unit cases (named `CE גובה בטרפז` → foot on AB not the leg AD; unnamed `גובה מ-A בטרפז` → auto-foot on DC; a parallelogram's two parallel pairs → not-handled/defer). The triangle altitude cases are unchanged (empty `parallels`). **1681 tests green, build clean.**

## ADR-170 — Structural shadow-detection guard for the first-match parser (hardening plan A1 / PAR-11)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** The 2026-07-02 multi-area review (see [15-hardening-plan.md](15-hardening-plan.md)) identified *silent mis-parse* as the parser's systemic risk: `parse()` is first-match-wins over the ordered `RULES` array, and an earlier, coarser rule can CLAIM a fragment a later, more-specific rule should own — returning a partial command array that commits silently (the escalation tripwire `droppedNewLabels` only fires on a *new* dropped label, so any mis-parse reusing existing labels is invisible). Every historical instance is the same shape (ADR-119 parallel-chords, ADR-077, ADR-166's parser half) and each was found only by an operator session. Rule ordering was defended solely by hand-written cases; there was no structural guard against a NEW shadow introduced by a keyword edit or a new rule.

**Decision.** Export `RULES` (test-only) and add a shadow-matrix guard ([src/parser/__tests__/shadow-matrix.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/shadow-matrix.test.ts)) that runs EVERY rule against a corpus (the supported `COMMAND_CATALOG` examples, he+en) without stopping at the first match, and per utterance records the `winner` (the rule `parse()` uses) and `shadowedBy` (later rules returning a DIVERGENT array). Three checks: (1) the winner rule per catalog utterance is snapshot-pinned; (2) the divergent later-claimers (candidate shadows) are snapshot-pinned; (3) every supported catalog utterance is claimed by *some* deterministic rule (none silently escalate). A `known shadow-prone probes` block snapshots the CURRENT behaviour of the twelve review-verified Phase-C targets so each fix flips one entry visibly. The analysis runs the same `normalizeUtterance` the rules see (extracted from `parse` for this — it is now the single normalization site, forward-compatible with PAR-7's maqaf/bidi work).

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The Phase-C parser fixes (PAR-1..8) each correct one shadow; this guard prevents the *class* from silently re-emerging — a future edit that changes a winner or creates a divergent claimer produces a reviewable snapshot diff in CI, turning "one session → one ADR" into a gated invariant. Zero runtime cost (`RULES`/`normalizeUtterance` exports are inert for `parse()`).

**Consequences / tests.** New test file (4 tests) + `RULES`/`normalizeUtterance` exports + the extracted `normalizeUtterance`. No behavioural change to `parse()`. The snapshots document — as evidence — every current shadow (e.g. `chord AB = 6` → winner `chord`, shadowed by `distanceConstraint`; `הקוטר AB מאונך למיתר CD` → winner `perpendicularConstraint`, shadowed by `diameter`+`chord`). **507 parser tests green (26 files), `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-171 — One shared figure→parser context builder (retire the drifting mirrors) (hardening plan A3 / TST-2)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** The figure→parser context (which circles/points/members/neighbours/parallels/lines the grammar may consult) was re-implemented three times: App's `parseCtx` ([App.tsx](../src/App.tsx)), the scenario harness's `ctxOf` ([scenarios.test.ts](../src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts)), and the production-triage harness's `ctxFrom` ([replaySession.ts](../src/validation/replaySession.ts)). The copies drifted: `ctxFrom` was **missing `parallels`** (added to the other two by ADR-169), so the triage harness resolved no trapezoid opposite-base and classified every `CE גובה בטרפז`-style utterance as a `coverage-gap` — a FALSE gap in the exact tool built to find real coverage gaps and drive the parser worklist. Found by the 2026-07-02 review.

**Decision.** Extract one pure `buildParseCtx(construction, positions)` ([src/parser/context.ts](../src/parser/context.ts)), exported from `@/parser`, and route all three call sites through it. The App's `parseCtx` is now a one-line delegation; `ctxOf`/`ctxFrom` likewise. Any future context field is added once and reaches production, scenarios, and triage together.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** Re-adding `parallels` to `ctxFrom` alone would fix this instance and leave the drift *mechanism* — three hand-maintained copies of one contract — intact for the next field. Collapsing to a single source of truth removes the class. (This is the same "one source of truth" move as `carrierOf` for point-kind classification.)

**Consequences / tests.** New `context.ts` + `buildParseCtx`/`ParseContext` exports; ~24 lines of mirrors deleted across App/scenarios/replaySession; unused engine imports pruned from the two consumers. A regression test in [replaySession.test.ts](../src/validation/__tests__/replaySession.test.ts) asserts the triage harness now classifies `טרפז ABCD ישר זווית` · `CE גובה בטרפז` as parsed/committed, not a coverage-gap. Behaviour-preserving for App + scenarios (existing suites unchanged). **`tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-172 — Seed-sweep oracle: every displayable config must honour the scenario check (hardening plan A2 / TST-1)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** The 2026-07-02 review's top testing finding: scenario tests validate at ONE seed (the app's default, `firstSatisfyingSeed`), yet the dominant historical escape class is *wrong-configuration-at-another-seed* — a figure that builds clean but is geometrically wrong in some OTHER valid draw the student reaches via "show another configuration" (ADR-085/098/127/166 all shipped past seed-0 suites). The universal oracle that would catch this — "every SAMPLED config satisfies the givens" — was never run across seeds. (The review's literal sketch, "`meetsRequirements(s)` false OR violations empty", turned out TAUTOLOGICAL: `meetsRequirements` already requires `violations.length === 0 && lastError === null` — so it can never fail. The real, non-tautological oracle is below.)

**Decision.** A seed-sweep block in [scenarios.test.ts](../src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts) re-runs each scenario's OWN geometric `check` — the independent oracle that already exists — at EVERY seed the app would actually DISPLAY (`meetsRequirements` true), for seeds `0..N-1` (default N=3; deep pass via `SEED_SWEEP_MULT`). Scope is principled: only FREE-DOF scenarios are swept (a determined figure is seed-invariant); heavy figures are pre-skipped (`SEED_SWEEP_HEAVY`) or auto-skipped over a per-replay `THRESHOLD_MS` — both LOGGED, never silently dropped (repo rule). A `SEED_SWEEP_EXEMPT` map (one legible list, id → reason) excludes scenarios whose check asserts a CONFIG-SPECIFIC value (a free radius, an unstated extension distance, an arc position, a size-dependent separation / convex gap) that legitimately varies across displayable configs.

**Finding (reassuring).** Across **103 free-DOF scenarios × 6 seeds**, every geometric INVARIANT held — the eight "failures" were all config-specific check assertions (default-seed numbers), not correctness violations. So the engine is already seed-robust on its invariants; this oracle's ongoing value is REGRESSION protection (a future change that introduces seed-fragility fails CI) plus a documented exemption worklist. `SCENARIOS`/`factsOf` are exported (test-only) and the fact-building split out of `run` so both drive the identical pipeline.

**Consequences / tests.** Default shallow pass ~44s (was ~231s at N=6). New describe block; no source/behaviour change to the engine or store. **1 test, 103 scenarios swept, green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-173 — Pin the givens-verifier incidence tolerance ladder (hardening plan A4 / TST-6)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** The review flagged that the verifier's on-circle/incidence tolerance (`onCircleTol = max(0.05, 2%·r)`, [verify.ts](../src/engine/verify.ts)) is ~100× looser than the solver's own accept tolerance (`max(1e-6, 2e-4·scale)`, [solve.ts](../src/engine/solve.ts)). On the under-determined figures ONLY the verifier guards, so a point can drift visibly and still read "green (verified)". Nothing pinned the ladder — a future "loosen to stop false ambers" edit could silently take 2% → 10%.

**Decision.** A pinning test ([verify-tolerance.test.ts](../src/engine/__tests__/verify-tolerance.test.ts)): build a verified on-circle figure, then assert the boundary — a point displaced by HALF the tolerance stays green, one displaced by TWICE it is flagged. Widening the ladder makes the 2×-displaced case stop flagging → the test fails, forcing an explicit, reviewed change. (This pins the CURRENT ladder; whether to TIGHTEN the verifier toward the solver's tolerance is a separate future decision — the pin makes any such change deliberate.)

**Consequences / tests.** Test-only; no behaviour change. **3 tests green; `tsc -b` clean.** (A5 replay-count perf canary is deferred to pair with the E-phase store replay-memoization source change; A6 scenario-doc parity is now done — see ADR-174.)

## ADR-174 — Scenario-doc parity guard + backfill the drifted index (hardening plan A6 / TST-7)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** The repo's standing rule makes [docs/test-scenarios.md](../docs/test-scenarios.md) the operator's human-readable regression audit trail — one entry per end-to-end scenario. The review found it had **drifted 34 scenarios behind** the code (`SCENARIOS` in [scenarios.test.ts](../src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts)): those tests ran and passed, but weren't indexed, so the audit trail under-reported coverage. Nothing enforced parity.

**Decision.** (1) BACKFILL the 34 missing entries — generated faithfully from each scenario's own `title`/`steps`/`guards` (a throwaway generator, then removed), appended under a dated "Backfilled" note so the newest-first ordering of existing entries is preserved. (2) Add a permanent parity test: every `SCENARIOS` id must appear as a backticked token in the doc, else CI fails with the missing ids. The id regex is `[A-Za-z0-9-]+` (some ids embed uppercase point labels, e.g. `two-circles-meet-at-A-and-B` — a lowercase-only regex silently missed them, a bug the test caught on itself during development).

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** Backfilling alone would re-drift on the next scenario. The parity guard makes the standing rule *enforced* rather than relying on discipline — the index can no longer fall behind the code without a red test.

**Consequences / tests.** Doc grows by 34 entries (98 → 132 `###`); one new test; `SCENARIOS`/`factsOf`/`Step`/`Scenario` exported (test-only). No source/behaviour change. **Parity test green (0 unindexed ids); `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-175 — Rate-limit / visitor-hash IP: trust the LAST X-Forwarded-For hop (hardening plan B1 / SEC-1)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** The security review's top server finding. [`clientIp`](../server/http.ts) fed the per-IP rate limiter ([parseHandler.ts](../server/parseHandler.ts)) and the dashboard's hashed unique-visitor id ([eventLog.ts](../server/eventLog.ts)) from `X-Forwarded-For.split(',')[0]` — the FIRST entry. But the production topology is client → Apache (`mod_proxy_http`, `ProxyPass`) → Node on loopback, and `mod_proxy_http` **appends** the connecting peer to any client-sent XFF. So the header is `<client-forgeable …>, <real client as Apache saw it>` and the first entry is fully attacker-controlled.

**Attack (this deployment).** A student sends a fresh random first XFF value per request → each lands in its own limiter bucket → the 30/min cap never trips → unbounded Haiku calls on prepaid credit; the same spoof forges/inflates the dashboard's per-visitor hash. This silently defeated the ONLY implemented cost throttle.

**Decision.** Trust the **last** hop (the peer Apache appended = the real client), via a `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` env (default 1 = just Apache) taken from the END of the chain — raise it only if another TRUSTED proxy (a CDN) sits in front of Apache. Drop the `X-Real-IP` fallback entirely (SEC-8: Apache doesn't set it here, so any value is 100% client-supplied). Dev (no proxy, loopback-bound) still falls back to the socket address.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** It encodes the actual trust boundary — "how many proxies in front are trustworthy" — instead of blindly trusting a header position a client controls. `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` makes the assumption explicit, configurable, and testable, so a future topology change (CDN) is a one-line env, not a re-think.

**Consequences / tests.** [server/__tests__/http.test.ts](../server/__tests__/http.test.ts) (7 tests): last-hop chosen; a rotating fake first value maps to ONE bucket; single-entry used directly; `X-Real-IP` not trusted; socket fallback; `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=2`; array/short-chain clamp. Deploy README updated. **49 server tests green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-176 — Admin dashboard is FAIL-CLOSED; cookie secret never derived from a default (hardening plan B3 / SEC-3)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** [standalone.ts](../server/standalone.ts) derived the admin session-cookie secret as `ADMIN_COOKIE_SECRET || ipSalt`, and `ipSalt` itself fell back to the committed constant `'geo-builder-default-salt'`. Meanwhile the dashboard guard ([admin.ts](../server/admin.ts) `handleAdmin`) authenticated on `validCookie(...)` alone — it never checked whether admin was actually configured. So an attacker could compute a valid session cookie under the known default secret and read the dashboard through the public `/geo-builder/admin` proxy — **even with a blank `ADMIN_PASSWORD`**, which `standalone.ts` warned was "effectively locked". The login path was locked; the cookie path was not.

**Decision.** Fail closed. (1) `handleAdmin` computes `secure = username && password && cookieSecret` all non-empty; **both** the login (`ok = secure && …`) AND the dashboard guard (`authed = secure && validCookie(…)`) require it — a forged cookie is ignored when admin isn't securely configured. (2) `standalone.ts` no longer derives the cookie secret from `ipSalt`; an unset secret — or one left at the committed default — becomes empty, which the `secure` gate treats as "disabled". The `/api/parse` proxy is unaffected (only `/admin` fails closed).

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** Re-adding a config check at the guard alone would leave the default-secret derivation as a latent bypass; removing the derivation alone would leave the guard trusting any validly-signed cookie. Both halves close the actual hole: "not securely configured ⇒ no authentication, by any path." The secret is now its own required input, so a misconfigured deploy is safe-by-default rather than silently world-readable.

**Consequences / tests.** [admin.test.ts](../server/__tests__/admin.test.ts) adds two SEC-3 cases (a well-formed cookie rejected when the server secret is unset; login refused 401 without a secret even with correct creds); existing auth tests unchanged. Deploy README notes `ADMIN_COOKIE_SECRET` is required + dedicated. **51 server tests green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-177 — Global daily cost ceiling on the LLM proxy, with a distinct "service busy" message (hardening plan B2 / SEC-2)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** The proxy spends prepaid Anthropic credit on every Haiku call. NFR-SE-2 / ADR-023 specified a cost gate; none was built — the only throttle was the per-IP rate limit (30/min), which is bypassable across IPs and over time, so a bot flooding `/api/parse` with random input could run up the bill. Operator steer: a **global ceiling** (not a per-class access code — a code in the SPA bundle is only a speed-bump and adds student friction); most important is a **clear message** when it's hit (not "couldn't understand", which blames the student) and the ability to **track how often** it happens (expected only for bots, not real users).

**Decision.** A hard cap on total Haiku dispatches per UTC day — `LLM_DAILY_MAX` (default **500** ≈ ~$1.25/day worst-case at ~$0.0025/call — set to 500 per the operator on 2026-07-02, "track this as the app gains or doesn't momentum"; was 1000), read per-request so it's tunable without a rebuild, counted in-process (a restart resets it — fine for a cost backstop; the Anthropic Console spend limit + prepaid credit is the absolute backstop). Checked AFTER validation (junk never burns quota) and BEFORE the SDK call. Over the cap → a DISTINCT `429 { error: 'daily-limit' }` (separate from the per-IP `rate-limited`); the client (`llm.ts`) returns an empty outcome tagged `busy`, and the App shows `input.serviceBusy` (He/En) and tags the analytics `source:'limit', result:'daily-limit'|'rate-limited'`. Tracking: a server log line per block (`journalctl -u geo-proxy | grep 'daily limit'`) covers ALL traffic incl. bots; the analytics tag surfaces real-user hits in the dashboard.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** It caps the actual cost variable (total calls/day) rather than only per-IP rate, so a distributed flood is bounded too. A subtlety fixed in review: `Number(env) || 1000` treats a configured `0` as unset (0 is falsy) — parsed explicitly so `LLM_DAILY_MAX=0` can hard-disable the LLM. The throttle is surfaced as its own client signal so a rate-limited student never sees a "you did something wrong" message.

**Consequences / tests.** [parseHandler.test.ts](../server/__tests__/parseHandler.test.ts): `LLM_DAILY_MAX=0` → first dispatch blocked with `{error:'daily-limit'}` (before the SDK). [llm.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/llm.test.ts): a 429 returns `busy: 'daily-limit'`/`'rate-limited'` (unparseable body → `rate-limited`), with empty `built`. i18n `input.serviceBusy` (he/en); deploy README documents `LLM_DAILY_MAX` + the grep. **65 server+llm tests green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-178 — Server robustness: bounded rate-limiter, upstream timeout/concurrency, admin-login throttle (hardening plan B4 / SEC-4/5/6)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** Three medium server findings from the review. SEC-4: `makeRateLimiter`'s bucket `Map` never evicted stale keys → unbounded growth (a spoofed-IP flood pre-SEC-1, or just many clients over time, → OOM). SEC-5: `client.messages.create` ran with the SDK's multi-minute default timeout + auto-retries and no concurrency cap → a slow/hung upstream held sockets and multiplied spend; a burst could tie up the event loop. SEC-6: the admin login POST wasn't rate-limited (the compare is constant-time, but online brute-force ran at full speed).

**Decision.** (SEC-4) `makeRateLimiter` sweeps keys with no hit within the window, at most once per window; `now` is injectable and the returned limiter exposes `size()` for a deterministic eviction test. (SEC-5) the Anthropic client is constructed with `timeout: 15_000, maxRetries: 0`, and an in-process `inFlight` counter caps concurrency (`LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT`, default 6) — over it a transient `429 rate-limited` (client shows "busy"), checked after the daily ceiling but before counting a dispatch. (SEC-6) a 10/min/IP limiter on the login POST → 429 when exceeded.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** Each closes the actual failure mode (unbounded memory, hung/looping upstream, unthrottled guessing) rather than masking a symptom; all three reuse the one shared limiter/IP helpers so behaviour stays consistent.

**Consequences / tests.** http.test.ts (eviction + still-limits-in-window), parseHandler.test.ts (`LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT=0` → 429 rate-limited before the SDK), admin.test.ts (11th login from one IP → 429; `mockReq` now assigns a unique IP per call so the module-level login limiter doesn't leak across tests). **59 server tests green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-179 — Usage-event retention + a privacy note for a minors' tool (hardening plan B5 / SEC-7)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** `events.jsonl` retained student utterances + hashed IPs indefinitely (rotation was size-only, 50 MB). For a tool aimed at high-schoolers there was no age bound and no written data policy. The verbose **debug** log (full figure snapshots, `logs/debug-log.jsonl`) was suspected of leaking student work to a personal cloud.

**Decision.** Add age-based retention: `pruneOldEvents(text, cutoffMs)` (pure — drops dated events past the cutoff, KEEPS undated/malformed lines so a bad line never loses data) applied at most once per UTC day when `EVENTS_RETENTION_DAYS` is set (unset → keep-all, no behaviour change). Confirmed the full-snapshot sink (`logProxy.ts`) is a **Vite dev plugin only** — production (`standalone.ts`) never mounts it, so production stores only lean, hashed events. Documented what's stored + the retention knob + an operator action: keep the dev `logs/` folder out of personal-cloud sync (the `conflicted copy` files are the tell).

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The privacy risk is *unbounded retention* + *dev logs on personal cloud*; retention bounds the first at the source, and confirming/documenting the dev-only sink + the sync-exclusion addresses the second where it actually lives (the dev machine, not the server).

**Consequences / tests.** eventLog.test.ts adds three `pruneOldEvents` cases (old dropped / recent+undated+malformed kept / all-old → empty, no stray blank line). Deploy README gains `EVENTS_RETENTION_DAYS` + a "Data & privacy" note. **59 server tests green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-180 — Deploy durability (Plesk GUI directives) + systemd hardening (hardening plan B6 / SEC-9)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** The deploy guide led with appending the ProxyPass lines directly to `vhost_ssl.conf` — the documented Plesk-regeneration footgun (a later SSL renew / "Repair" regenerates the file and drops hand-added lines, 404-ing the proxied routes while the static app looks fine). The systemd unit had only `NoNewPrivileges`/`PrivateTmp`/`ProtectSystem=full`.

**Decision.** Make the durable **Plesk GUI** method ("Additional directives for HTTPS", stored in Plesk's DB → survives regeneration) the PRIMARY instruction; the direct-file append is the clearly-caveated fallback. Tighten the unit: `ProtectSystem=strict` + `ReadWritePaths=/var/www/geo-proxy` (only the events-log dir is writable), `ProtectHome=true` (hides /home + /root, incl. any personal-cloud folder, from the process), `PrivateDevices=true`. The env file stays 600 root:root (systemd reads it as root before dropping to www-data).

**Consequences / tests.** Docs + unit file only (no code). `ReadWritePaths` is required for `events.jsonl` writes once `ProtectSystem=strict` is on — verify the events log still appends after deploy. Also added MD031 to `.markdownlint.jsonc` (deploy guide packs env/code blocks against list items). **No code change; server tests unaffected.**

## ADR-181 — Orthography normalization at the parse boundary: maqaf + invisible bidi controls (hardening plan C1 / PAR-7)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** The 2026-07-02 review found a silent-drop class from *how text is pasted*, not what it says. Word/PDF render the Hebrew hyphen as the **maqaf** `־` (U+05BE), but the grammar's connector suffix groups (`ל-?` / `ב-?` / `מ-?`) expect an ASCII `-`; and copy-paste of mixed Hebrew/Latin text drags in invisible **bidi/zero-width control chars** (LRM/RLM, isolates, ZWSP/ZWJ, BOM, ALM). Both silently break the parser's `\s*` / optional-`-` adjacency, so e.g. `נקודה E על AC ב־40%` parsed as a point-on-segment but *dropped the 40% ratio* — a wrong figure with nothing for the verifier to catch.

**Decision.** Normalize at the boundary, in the single `normalizeUtterance` (extracted in A1, run before every rule *and* the shadow-matrix guard): map `־`→`-`, then strip the invisible format chars (`U+061C`, `U+200B–200F`, `U+202A–202E`, `U+2066–2069`, `U+FEFF`). One place, whole class gone — pasted text now parses like typed text.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The alternative — adding `[־]?` and `\p{Cf}?` to ~20 individual suffix groups — would be per-rule whack-a-mole and miss the next rule. The defect is that the *input alphabet* the rules assume (ASCII punctuation, no invisibles) doesn't match pasted reality; fixing the alphabet at the boundary is the correct layer.

**Consequences / tests.** [orthography.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/orthography.test.ts) (4 tests): maqaf ratio kept (`ב־40%` → t=0.4, identical to the ASCII form); maqaf in a `ל־` connector; a bidi-wrapped utterance parses identically to clean across nine control chars; a control glued to a keyword no longer breaks the match. Shadow-matrix snapshot unchanged (winner names stable). **Parser suite green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-182 — Hebrew final-letter inflection: plural ⟂ keywords (hardening plan C2 / PAR-3)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** `מאונך` (perpendicular) and `אנך` (the noun form) end in kaf-sofit `ך`; their plurals swap it for a regular kaf — `מאונכים` / `אנכים` — a DIFFERENT Unicode code point, so the singular-only keyword sets matched none of them. The exact ADR-119 scenario in its plural flavour — `המיתרים AB ו-CD מאונכים זה לזה` ("the chords AB and CD are perpendicular to each other") — silently dropped BOTH the ⟂ relation and chord CD (the `chord` rule grabbed the first pair; the plural ⟂ keyword never matched). The team already solved this class for `חות[כך]` (חותך/נחתך) but never applied it to the אנך family.

**Decision.** A shared `מאונ[כך]|אנ[כך]` stem at every perpendicular-keyword site (the `perpendicularConstraint` detector + its keyword-strip, `perpendicularLine`, the named-line lookahead, the perp-from discriminator, `radiusSegment`'s bail guard, `SHAPE_LEFTOVER`, and the top-level ⟂ `stop` guard). `מקביל`/parallel ends in a non-final letter, so its plurals already matched — no change there. With the stem, `perpendicularConstraint` (which runs before `chord`) now claims the plural-chords utterance and emits its segments, and `withChordMembership`/`withCarrierMembership` re-asserts A,B,C,D on the circle.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect is a Hebrew-morphology blind spot in the keyword alphabet, not a single utterance — the stem covers every inflection (`מאונך`/`מאונכים`/`מאונכות`) at every site. Audited siblings: only the kaf-sofit ⟂ words have this problem (משיק/קוטר/מיתר/חוצ end in non-final letters, so their plurals already matched).

**Consequences / tests.** [perp-inflection.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/perp-inflection.test.ts) (4 tests): singular still works; plural `AB ו-CD מאונכים זה לזה` yields the ⟂ constraint over A,B,C,D; the plural-chords case keeps circle membership. Shadow-matrix probe flipped `chord`→`perpendicularConstraint` (snapshot updated). **523 parser tests green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-183 — chord bails on a relation tail (the "מיתר AB=2" drop) (hardening plan C3 / PAR-1)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** Operator-flagged: `מיתר AB=2`. The `chord`/`מיתר` rule runs before every measure rule, grabs the first label pair, and returns — silently discarding a trailing `= 2`. You got a chord with no length, and (because A,B already existed) nothing escalated. The sibling `radiusSegment` already guarded against exactly this (bail on `=`/`⊥`/`∥`), proving the guard was known-needed but never applied to `chord`.

**Decision.** `chord` returns `null` when the utterance carries a relation operator (`=`/`<`/`>`). Then `distanceConstraint`/`equalSegments` claims the length AND draws the segment (both already do — FR-IN-7), from which the `withCarrierMembership` post-pass re-asserts the endpoints on the circle. So `מיתר AB=2` → A,B on circle + segment AB + |AB|=2, the full correct set. (⟂/∥ chords need no guard here — those constraint rules already run before `chord`.)

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** It removes the half-parse at its source (a carrier-noun rule must not swallow a measure it can't represent) rather than special-casing `=2`; the same guard covers `= number`, `= CD`, and order operators, and it composes with the existing measure rules + membership post-pass instead of duplicating measure parsing inside `chord`.

**Consequences / tests.** [chord-relation.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/chord-relation.test.ts): `מיתר AB=2` / `chord AB = 6` keep the length + membership + segment; `chord AB = CD` keeps the equality + both chords on the circle; a plain `chord AB` is unaffected. **523 parser tests green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-184 — carrier-membership post-pass generalized to diameters (hardening plan C4 / PAR-4)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** ADR-119's `withChordMembership` restored on-circle membership only for CHORD-flavoured utterances. Its sibling nouns dropped membership in relational phrasings: `הקוטר AB מאונך למיתר CD` gave the ⟂ but no diameter (no collinear-through-centre), and `קוטר AB = 10` (after C3's bail) gave a distance but not a diameter.

**Decision.** Rename to `withCarrierMembership` and add a diameter branch. It fires only when a RELATIONAL / point-on winner produced the commands (a `CONSTRUCT` skip-set short-circuits it when a dedicated circle-construct rule — `chord`/`diameter`/`circleOnDiameter`/`diameterCutsSegment`/`pointOnCircle`/arc — already modelled the geometry, so it never double-adds). For a diameter-flavoured utterance it asserts the diameter's endpoints on the circle AND collinear-through-centre (so it's a real diameter, not a chord). A chord utterance still puts EVERY named segment on the circle (parallel/⟂ chords); a diameter-ONLY utterance asserts just the diameter itself, so a diameter ⟂ a NON-chord segment doesn't wrongly force that segment onto the circle. Also added the `[=<>]` bail to the `diameter` rule.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** One membership post-pass generalised across carriers, gated by the geometric shape of the winner's output, rather than a per-noun special case; the skip-set encodes the real invariant ("a construct rule already handled membership") that keeps `circleOnDiameter`/`diameterCutsSegment` untouched.

**Consequences / tests.** [chord-relation.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/chord-relation.test.ts) diameter cases: `קוטר AB=10` → A,B on circle + collinear-through-centre O + |AB|=10; `הקוטר AB מאונך למיתר CD` → A,B,C,D on circle + AB diameter + ⟂; a plain `diameter AB` keeps exactly one collinear (no double). Fixed a regression where the generalized pass over-fired on `circleOnDiameter`/`diameterCutsSegment` (the `CONSTRUCT` skip-set). **523 parser tests green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-185 — point ON a diameter/radius: dead `על` guards + carrier nouns (hardening plan C5 / PAR-5)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** `נקודה D על הרדיוס OB` silently DROPPED D, and `E על הקוטר AB` mis-parsed. Two coupled root causes:

1. **Dead `על\b` guards.** JS `\b` is a boundary between a `\w` char and a non-`\w` char; Hebrew letters aren't `\w`, so `על\b` only matches "על" glued to a Latin letter/digit — never the common "על " (space) form. The guards at `radiusSegment` and `nameCenter` that were meant to bail on an "on" phrasing therefore never fired, so `radiusSegment` (which runs before `pointOnSegment`) grabbed the two-letter run and dropped the rider point.
2. **`קוטר`/`רדיוס` absent from `CARRIER_NOUN`.** `pointOnSegment`'s optional `SEG_NOUN` couldn't eat "הקוטר"/"הרדיוס", so its labels didn't align and it missed; and the `diameter` rule (also before `pointOnSegment`) claimed the utterance.

**Decision.**
- Replace `על\b` with `על(?=\s|$)` (a real word-tail lookahead) at both guard sites — `radiusSegment` now bails on a point-ON phrasing and defers to `pointOnSegment`.
- Add `diameter|radius|ה?קוטר|ה?רדיוס` to `CARRIER_NOUN` (the diameter IS segment AB; the radius IS segment O·rim — a point on either is a point on that segment).
- Add the `POINT_ON_CARRIER` guard to the `diameter` rule so `E על הקוטר AB` defers to `pointOnSegment`.
- Extend the `withCarrierMembership` post-pass to RADIUS: a radius carrier's rim point (the non-centre end of a centre→rim segment/point-on) is asserted on the circle. Diameter membership (endpoints on circle + collinear-through-centre) is reused from PAR-4; the centre-touching-pair exclusion keeps the centre off the circle.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The `\b`→lookahead correction fixes an entire class of dead Hebrew-word guards, not one utterance; folding diameter/radius into the shared `CARRIER_NOUN` + membership post-pass means every point-on rule (`pointOnSegment`, `pointsOnSegment`, `pointsOnSegments`) inherits the carriers at once, and the geometry (endpoints/rim on the circle) is asserted centrally rather than duplicated per rule.

**Consequences / tests.** [carrier-on.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/carrier-on.test.ts) (4): `E על הקוטר AB` → E on segment AB + A,B on circle + collinear-through-centre O; `נקודה D על הרדיוס OB` → D on segment OB + rim B on circle (centre O excluded); a bare `OB רדיוס` still routes to `radiusSegment`. Shadow-matrix probes flipped `radiusSegment`→`pointOnSegment` and `diameter`→`pointOnSegment` (snapshot updated). **Full suite: 1728 passed / 2 skipped; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-186 — multi-statement splitter for comma-joined givens (hardening plan C6 / PAR-2)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** Two independent givens in one line silently dropped the earlier one: `AB = 4, BC = 6` kept only `BC = 6` (`distanceConstraint` anchors its value to `$`, so it claims only the trailing clause — ADR-024/026), and `זווית ABC = 40, זווית DEF = 60` kept only the first angle (`angle` reads the first number + first label triple). No rule assembled the pieces; the dropped given produced a wrong figure with no error.

**Decision.** A `multiStatement` rule (right after `compoundSuchThat`) splits on a top-level separator (`,` `;` `וגם` `and`) and parses each piece, **all-or-nothing**. It splits ONLY when **every** piece (a) carries a relation OPERATOR (`= < > ⟂ ∥ ≅ ~` or a ⟂/∥/≅/~ word — deliberately NOT bare `שווה`, so "משולש שווה שוקיים" isosceles isn't read as an equality) AND (b) parses on its own. Any unreadable piece ⇒ no split ⇒ falls through to the existing rules / LLM. `angle` additionally bails when it sees two+ angle keywords (defence in depth, so a two-angle line escalates rather than half-parses if it ever reaches `angle` unsplit).

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The half-parse is structural — many relation rules are single-clause by construction. A pre-pass that decomposes a givens list into independent single-clause parses fixes the whole class (distance, angle, ⟂, ∥, …) at once, rather than teaching each rule to loop. The relation-operator gate + all-or-nothing parse gate keep construction utterances that happen to carry commas ("circle through A, B, C", "F, G, H on AB, AC, CB") untouched — they lack a top-level relation operator, so the splitter declines.

**Consequences / tests.** [multi-statement.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/multi-statement.test.ts) (8): both distances/angles kept for `,`/`and`; three-given lists; mixed `⟂`+`∥`; and the safety cases (N-points-on-N-segments and circumcircle-through are NOT mangled; a lone `AB = 4` is unaffected). Shadow-matrix probes flipped `distanceConstraint`→`multiStatement` and `angle`→`multiStatement` (snapshot updated). **Full suite: 1736 passed / 2 skipped; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-187 — plural carrier nouns for N-points-on-N-segments (hardening plan C7 / PAR-8)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** `pointsOnSegments` (ADR-076: N points placed pairwise on N segments) reads UPPERCASE labels only and ignores the noun word, so `F, G, H on sides AB, AC, CB` / `... על הצלעות ...` always worked. But when the PLURAL carrier noun contains a `segment`-rule keyword — "segments" ⊃ "segment", "הקטעים" ⊃ "קטע", "diagonals" ⊃ "diagonal" — the `segment` DEFINITION rule (which runs before `pointsOnSegments`) fired, and its `POINT_ON_CARRIER` bail guard was singular-only, so it didn't recognise the plural and defer. It grabbed the first two-label run and dropped F,G,H — building a lone `segment AB`.

**Decision.** Pluralise `CARRIER_NOUN`: `chords?|sides?|segments?|diagonals?|diameters?|radius|ה?מיתר(?:ים)?|ה?צלע(?:ות)?|ה?קטע(?:ים)?|ה?אלכסו(?:ן|נים)|ה?קוטר(?:ים)?|ה?רדיוס`. Now `POINT_ON_CARRIER` matches "H on segments AB" / "H על הקטעים AB", so `segment` (and `chord`) defer and the strictly-more-specific `pointsOnSegments` claims the list. (The Hebrew `אלכסון` ends in a final nun; its plural `אלכסונים` uses a regular nun — encoded as `ה?אלכסו(?:ן|נים)` so both forms match.)

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect was a singular-only guard, not a single utterance — pluralising the shared `CARRIER_NOUN` fixes the guard for every rule that consults it (`segment`, `chord`, `SEG_NOUN` in all three point-on rules) at once, rather than hoisting one rule or special-casing "segments". Chose the guard fix over re-ordering `pointsOnSegments` above `segment` so the semantic invariant ("a point-ON-carrier phrasing is not a carrier definition") is expressed where it belongs.

**Consequences / tests.** [plural-carrier.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/plural-carrier.test.ts) (7, he+en, plural + singular no-regression incl. the final-nun `האלכסון`); end-to-end scenario `plural-segment-noun-points-on-sides`. Shadow-matrix probe flipped `segment`→`pointsOnSegments` (snapshot updated). **Full suite: 1743 passed / 2 skipped; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-188 — area-reference dedupe for an S-leading polygon (hardening plan C8 / PAR-6)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** `areaReferences` collects every "area of a polygon" reference — verbose (`שטח [ה<shape>] ABC` / `area of ABC`) and compact (`SABC`). A `seen` Set was declared to let the compact scan skip positions the verbose scan already claimed, but it was never populated. So a verbose polygon whose FIRST vertex is "S" was re-read by the compact scan as marker-S + polygon "ABC": `שטח מרובע SABC הוא 20` produced TWO refs — `[S,A,B,C]` (correct) and a phantom `[A,B,C]` — which the downstream logic turned into a bogus `set-area-ratio {SABC : ABC = 20}` that drove the solver into nonsense. "S" is in the auto-label pools, so a student hits this without ever choosing S.

**Decision.** Populate `seen` with the string position of a verbose polygon's FIRST vertex when it is "S", so the compact scan's existing `!seen.has(m.index)` guard skips the phantom. Scoped to a first vertex of "S" (the only letter the compact marker can be), so non-S verbose polygons and genuine compact refs are untouched.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** It activates the dedup mechanism the function was already designed around (the dead `seen` Set) at the exact overlap it was meant to cover, rather than special-casing the `שטח … SABC` string — a genuine two-ref ratio (`SABC = 4 SNCE`), a compact area (`SABC = 20`, S = marker), and a verbose non-S area (`שטח מרובע ABCD`) all keep working because each has a distinct, non-overlapping marker position.

**Consequences / tests.** [area-sabc.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/area-sabc.test.ts) (5): the S-leading verbose forms give a single `measure-area [S,A,B,C]` (no ratio); compact `SABC`, verbose `ABCD`, and the two-ref ratio `SABC = 4 SNCE` are unchanged. No shadow-matrix change (a helper, not a rule). **Full suite: 1749 passed / 2 skipped; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-189 — structured-id-aware rename/swap (hardening plan C9 / PAR-9)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** `renameInCommand` rewrote a field only on a whole-field single-letter match (`v === from`), so a point letter EMBEDDED in a structured id — `circle-O`, `bis-XYZ`, `tan-O`, `sec-EO`, `line-XY`, `par-T-AB`, `chord-AB` — survived a rename of that letter. But the `center` field WAS rewritten and `hiddenCircles` WAS remapped (`circle-${F}`→`circle-${T}`), so renaming O→M produced a circle with `id: circle-O` yet `center: M` — a desync: a hidden circle popped back (its object id no longer matched the remapped `hiddenCircles` entry), and deterministic-id idempotency broke (a later "circle M" resolves to `circle-M`, a DIFFERENT id → a phantom duplicate construction). Reproduced at the store level before fixing (the plan flagged it as reasoned-not-executed): `rename('O','M')` left `{id:'circle-O', center:'M'}` and a stale `circle:'circle-O'` reference.

**Decision.** A `relabelId(v, from, to)` helper rewrites every WHOLE point label `from`→`to` inside a string — a bare id ("O") OR a label embedded in a structured id — guarded so a label is matched only at its start and not mid-label: `(?<![A-Za-z])${from}(?!\d)` (a bare "O" ≠ the "O" of "O1"; structured-id prefixes are lowercase, so their letters never match). `renameInCommand` now runs every string field (and array element) through it. Swap (which is three `renameInCommand` passes through a `\0` sentinel) and merge inherit the fix for free.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** It replaces the exact-field equality with the correct label-boundary rewrite, so EVERY structured id (present and future) stays consistent with its point letters under rename/swap/merge — rather than enumerating the id prefixes to patch. The multi-char-label guard (`(?!\d)`, `(?<![A-Za-z])`) is the same label grammar the rest of the parser uses. **Deferred (separate ADR, noted in the plan):** decoupling circle identity from the centre letter (opaque id + centre lookup) to unlock concentric circles — a larger change, out of this step's scope.

**Consequences / tests.** [structured-id-rename.test.ts](../src/store/__tests__/structured-id-rename.test.ts) (6): rename rewrites `circle-O`/`bis-`/`tan-`/`sec-` embedded letters + the centre + references; a hidden circle stays hidden (no pop-back); idempotency restored; `O1` untouched when renaming `O`; swap exchanges `circle-O`↔`circle-P`. **Full suite: 1755 passed / 2 skipped; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-190 — LLM-fallback contract tests + subscripted cross-step context (hardening plan C10 / PAR-10 + TST-3)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** The LLM never emits engine JSON — it emits canonical command STRINGS the deterministic parser re-reads (`llm.ts`). Four untested contracts could silently break the fallback: (1) the prompt's ~15 few-shot step strings were a hand-maintained list with no parse round-trip; (2) the catalog guard asserted only `parse(x).ok`, missing a shadow that flips a line to the WRONG rule while still `.ok`; (3) 23 scenarios injected pre-parsed `{llm: AnyCommand[]}` and never exercised the real re-parse of the canonical strings; (4) `absorb` filtered accumulated points with `/^[A-Z]$/`, so a subscripted `O1`/`O2` from an earlier LLM step never entered the running context and a later step that referenced it degraded.

**Decision.**
- **(a)** Extracted the few-shot examples into an exported `PROMPT_EXAMPLES` (rendered back into the prompt), with a contract test that re-parses every `steps[i]` under the example's assumed context — a drifted example (a form the prompt teaches but the parser can't read) now fails.
- **(b)** Added a catalog contract test that pins the `{example → command types}` map for every supported entry (He + En) as a snapshot — a rule shadow that flips a catalog line to the wrong type while staying `.ok` breaks the snapshot for review (the shadow-matrix model, extended to the whole catalog; chosen over a hand-annotated `expectType` because it covers every entry with no annotation drift). The explicit no-`not-handled` assertion keeps the old `.ok` guarantee.
- **(c)** Extended the scenario `Step` type to accept `{ llm: string[] }` (canonical lines re-parsed with `ctxOf`, incrementally, exactly as `llmParse` does) alongside the legacy `{ llm: AnyCommand[] }`. Migrated the 14 single-line canonical forms (segments, point-on-circle, line∩line, extension, arc-ratio) to strings so a parser change that breaks them is now caught. The multi-command LLM decompositions of typo'd / out-of-grammar inputs (8 blocks) are kept as pre-baked commands — they have no single clean re-parsing canonical string (e.g. "AB קוטר במעגל" can't resolve a circle standalone), which is exactly what the legacy form is for.
- **(d)** `absorb` (and the prompt's "single capital letters" line) now use `/^[A-Z]\d*$/`, so subscripted labels carry across LLM steps.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** Each part turns an implicit contract into a tested one at the boundary where the LLM output meets the deterministic parser — the prompt examples, the catalog vocabulary, the scenario re-parse path, and the cross-step context — rather than fixing one drifted string. The snapshot and the `{llm: string[]}` re-parse make future parser changes self-report their blast radius on the LLM surface.

**Consequences / tests.** [llm-contract.test.ts](../src/parser/__tests__/llm-contract.test.ts) (17: every PROMPT_EXAMPLES step parses; the catalog type snapshot; subscripted `absorb`). `factsOf` re-parses `{llm: string[]}` scenarios; 14 scenarios migrated. **Full suite: 1772 passed / 2 skipped; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-191 — an utterance is ATOMIC: a group with a hard-failed fact draws nothing (its scaffolding is dropped)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** One utterance lowers to a GROUP of engine commands sharing a `group` id. A perpendicular/parallel/equal given draws its operand segments too (FR-IN-7): "`EF ו BC מאונכים`" → `[segment EF, segment BC, set-perpendicular(E,F,B,C)]`. `replay` folded each fact independently: on a square ABCD with E on AB and F on DC, the ⟂ is geometrically impossible (EF spans bottom→top, so it can never be perpendicular to the vertical BC), so `set-perpendicular` HARD-failed — a "can't place F …" message was shown — but the two scaffolding `segment` facts had already committed, so **seg-EF was still drawn** (operator session `8twmmb5r`: "it gave a message but still drew the line — it should not"). The auto-drawn segments are scaffolding for a relation; if the relation is a genuine contradiction, they must not survive on their own.

**Decision.** A group is atomic. After the in-order build + ADR-104 deferral + pending classification, POISON any group that has BOTH a hard-failed fact AND a succeeded one, then **rebuild** the construction with the whole poisoned group blocked (every member carries the group's genuine error). A blocked fact is neither applied nor measured; only its owned points are claimed, so a genuine dependent of a point that group alone introduced still cascades honestly. Rebuild rather than delete-objects because a segment SHARED with an earlier shape (seg-BC of the square) must stay drawn by that shape — skipping the group re-creates it from the square, not the utterance.

**Scope / what it does NOT touch.** Only fires when the figure is NOT pending: a deferrable constraint that is merely under-determined (ADR-104 — "CE⟂AB" before its sizes) keeps its scaffolding and resolves later. A lone failed fact (a single-command group) is unaffected — blocking it changes nothing, since a failed fact adds no objects anyway. So the poisoning is a no-op except on the exact class it targets: a multi-command utterance whose relation is a hard contradiction.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect was structural — `replay` treated a group's facts as independent, so ANY multi-command utterance (⟂/∥/=, and inscribed-shape macros) could leave partial scaffolding on a hard failure. Atomicity at the group boundary fixes the whole class, not the one ⟂ input. The pending carve-out preserves ADR-104 order-independence intact.

**Consequences / tests.** `replay`'s build loop is wrapped in an inner `runBuild(forced)` (run at most twice — once clean, once with poisoned groups blocked); classification extracted to `classify`. Scenario [`impossible-perpendicular-drops-its-segment`](../src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts) locks the operator's exact 4-step sequence (message set, no seg-EF, square + seg-BC intact, no verifier violation). The ADR-104 pending-vs-contradiction scenarios still pass (the carve-out). **Full store + scenario suite green; `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-192 — a segment ratio `DF:FC = 1:2` (and its `= FC/2` lowering) is a proportion, never a silent equality

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** On a square ABCD with E on AB and F on CD, the operator typed `DF:FC=1:2` (session `o2m8f0w8`). The keyword-free colon form had **no deterministic rule** — `dividesInRatio` only matches the keyworded phrasings (`divides`/`מחלק`/`ratio`/`יחס`) — so the utterance escalated to the LLM, which correctly returned `DF = FC/2`. But `DF = FC/2` then hit `equalSegments`, whose regex matched the `DF = FC` **prefix** and silently dropped the trailing `/2`, emitting `set-equal(D,F,F,C)` — a plain `|DF| = |FC|`. Green status, no error, wrong geometry: the figure asserted a 1:1 equality where the student stated a 1:2 ratio. This is exactly the ADR-024/026 silent-half-parse class (a measure rule grabbing a fragment of a larger ratio expression), which the code already guards against elsewhere via `SEG_RATIO_LHS`, but the *divided RHS* form slipped through because no rule owned it.

**Decision.** Two root fixes at the parser boundary, covering the whole class rather than the one utterance:
- **(A) `ratioConstraint` reads a trailing divisor.** `DF = FC/2` → `set-ratio(D,F,F,C, k=½)`. The RHS grammar gains an optional `/d`; the coefficient math generalises to `|m·AB| = |n·CD/d| ⇒ k = n/(m·d)`. A new `SEG_DIV_RHS` guard makes `equalSegments` bail on any `= CD/d` RHS (defence-in-depth, so a future rule reorder can't reintroduce the drop — same discipline as `SEG_RATIO_LHS` on `distanceConstraint`).
- **(B) A new `segmentRatioColon` rule** parses the bare `seg:seg = p:q` colon form deterministically → `set-ratio(a,b,c,d, k=p/q)`, offline, so it never escalates. Like its `/`-form sibling `segmentRatio`, it emits a *constraint* that drives the shared/free point (it references existing endpoints, it does not create them — the `divides`-keyword form remains the one that creates a divider point).

Both `DF:FC=1:2` and `DF = FC/2` now emit the identical `set-ratio(D,F,F,C, k=½)`, driving F's free DOF on CD so `|DF| = ½·|FC|`.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect was two structural gaps, not one bad input: (A) a whole RHS *shape* (`seg/coef`) had no owner and was being fragment-parsed; (B) a whole utterance *shape* (`seg:seg = p:q`) had no deterministic rule and leaned on the LLM, whose reasonable output then tripped gap (A). Fixing the grammar/guard covers every segment ratio in either notation, not the reported figure alone.

**Consequences / tests.** Scenario [`segment-ratio-colon-drives-division-point`](../src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts) locks the operator's exact 4-step sequence (`|FC|/|DF| ≈ 2`, every step ok). Existing `ratioConstraint`/`equalSegments`/`segmentRatio` tests unchanged (backward-compatible: no trailing divisor ⇒ `d=1`). **Full parser + scenario + engine suite green (1464 tests); `tsc -b` clean.**

## ADR-193 — `evaluate` verifies DRIVEN constraints too: an unsatisfiable driven system is over-constrained, not a silently-accepted best-effort

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** Square ABCD, F on CD, `DF:FC=1:4` (pins F at t=0.8), E on AB, then `FE ⟂ BC` (session `vpt763yn`). `FE ⟂ BC` is geometrically impossible: F rides the top edge, E the bottom edge, BC is vertical, so `FE·BC` is a constant −25 with zero gradient — no assignment of the carriers satisfies it. The operator reported two bugs: (1) **F moved off its ratio position**, (2) **the drawn line came out parallel to BC**, not perpendicular. Both from one defect. `driveOrCheck` makes E drive the ⟂ and leaves F driving the ratio (both `on-segment-solved`); neither is pushed as a *check* constraint (only `concyclic`/`length-radius` are). `resolveDriven` → `resolveMixedCarriers` then tries to satisfy `{ratio, ⟂}` jointly, can't (the ⟂ is impossible), and its final fallback `return solveFor(carriers, false).result` **discards the `ok=false`** — returning a best-effort placement where the Tikhonov regulariser has pulled F,E back to their seed midpoints (so the ratio is broken too and FE is vertical ≡ ∥ BC). `setCarrierVals` clears the solve directives, so the driven ratio/⟂ are now neither drivers nor checks; `evaluateCore`'s final loop only checks `c.constraints`, finds nothing wrong, and returns **`ok:true`** on a figure violating both. Only the separate givens-verifier (ADR-053) caught it — as amber — after F had already been dragged off.

**Decision.** `evaluate` re-verifies every DRIVEN constraint at the resolved positions, the same `isSatisfied` gate `evaluateCore` already applies to the check-constraints. `drivenConstraintsOf(c)` gathers each carrier's constraint (an `on-segment-solved`'s `.constraint`, or any object's `.solve.constraint`) from the ORIGINAL construction before `resolveDriven` clears the directives; after `evaluateCore(resolveDriven(c))` succeeds, any driven constraint that fails `isSatisfied` makes `evaluate` return `ok:false` (`over-constrained: … cannot hold`). The message names the whole CONFLICT SET (all driven constraints failing `isSatisfied`, joined by "and") — because when a joint solve can't satisfy an impossible constraint it drags its co-drivers off too, so several read violated, and the tiny regulariser (λ=1e-3) means a genuinely-*satisfiable* driven constraint is still driven to ~0 residual and passes the gate; only the real conflict fails it. (Picking one member by residual is biased — a ratio's relative residual is unbounded while ∥/⟂ is capped at 1.)

With this, the impossible ⟂ hard-fails; the store keeps the prior figure (F stays at its ratio position t=0.8, F=(1,5)); ADR-191 group-atomicity drops the FE scaffolding (seg-EF not drawn); the message reads `|DF| = 0.25·|FC| and FE ⟂ BC cannot hold`. Both reported bugs are fixed by the one change.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect was structural: `evaluate`'s "green" meant "the CHECK constraints hold and the solver returned *some* placement," silently trusting that the driven solve found a root. That trust is false whenever a driven system has no solution (an impossible relation, a genuine over-constraint through a driven carrier) — a whole class, not this one figure. Verifying driven constraints makes `evaluate`'s contract honest ("green ⟺ every constraint holds, driven or checked") and is consistent with `solutionAccepted`, which already uses the same gate — a solve it accepted passes here unchanged; only a best-effort it rejected (and that used to leak through) is now caught. Fixing it at the recruiter or per-solver would have to be repeated for each driven path (`resolveMixedCarriers`, `resolveFreeDriven`, the single-carrier root find); the `evaluate` boundary covers them all.

**Scope / what it does NOT touch.** A satisfiable driven figure is byte-identical (its driven constraints hold ⇒ the re-check passes). An under-determined/pending constraint already fails `evaluate` and is handled by the ADR-104 deferral / recruiter — that path is unchanged; this only adds failures for driven systems that genuinely can't hold. `evaluate` is the top-level entry; the inner solver cost/accept loops call `evaluateCore` (with `skipConstraints`) directly, so the re-check adds no cost inside the optimisation, only once per top-level evaluate.

**Consequences / tests.** Scenario [`impossible-perp-does-not-clobber-ratio-pinned-point`](../src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts) locks the operator's exact 5-step sequence (F stays at ratio t=0.8, over-constrained message names the ⟂, no seg-EF, square intact, no verifier violation). **Full suite green; `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.**

## ADR-194 — a plain on-segment point stays WITHIN its segment (t∈[0,1]); the joint solver can't slide it onto the extension

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** Square ABCD, E on AB, F on DC with `DF:FC=1:10`, then `EF ∥ BC` (session `wdrfq1wf`). The parallel IS satisfiable in-segment — E slides on AB to match F's x, both at t=1/11 — but the figure came back with E and F at **t=−1/9, OUTSIDE their segments, on the extension beyond A and D**, so the student's "E on AB" and "F on DC" were both silently violated (green build, `violations:[]`; operator: "E on AB is violated as well as F on DC"). Root cause: the DISTANCE-based ratio `|DF| = 0.1·|FC|` has TWO roots — the internal division t=1/11 AND the external division t=−1/9 (both give |DF|:|FC| = 1:10) — and the multi-carrier joint solver (`resolveMixedCarriers`) landed on the external one. Its writer `setCarrierVals` HARD-clamped an EXTENSION on-segment point to t≥1.02 (ADR-105) but wrote a PLAIN on-segment point's t **unclamped** (the comment even said so), so the unbounded Nelder–Mead/coordinate search was free to slide a point declared "on the segment" off onto its line/extension to satisfy a constraint. (The single-carrier 1-D path was already safe — `drivenRoots` searches the bounded range `[0,1]` — so only the joint path leaked.)

**Decision.** A plain (non-extension) on-segment point lives ON the segment BETWEEN its endpoints — t∈[0,1] BY DEFINITION. Clamp it there in `setCarrierVals` (mirroring the extension clamp already present): `t: o.extension ? Math.max(v[0],1.02) : Math.min(1, Math.max(0, v[0]))`. `setCarrierVals` feeds both the cost landscape (via `place`) and the final write, so out-of-segment placements score at the clamped boundary (where the internal-root constraint isn't satisfied) and the search must move the figure's OTHER DOFs — landing the internal root t=1/11. E and F now sit inside their segments with `DF:FC=1:10` and `EF ∥ BC` both holding.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The bug is the segment-membership invariant, not this one figure: ANY distance/ratio/equal constraint that has both an internal and an external root, driving an on-segment carrier through the joint solver, could slide the point off its segment. Enforcing t∈[0,1] at the single place that writes an on-segment param fixes the whole class. It also completes the ADR-105 pair — the extension point is pinned OUTSIDE (t≥1.02), the plain point is now pinned INSIDE (t∈[0,1]); each stays where its declaration puts it. Sibling of ADR-193 (same session's earlier figure): there the later constraint was genuinely impossible (⟂ unsatisfiable at every t) so the step hard-fails; here it is satisfiable and the fix is to pick the in-segment root — the two are complementary, and ADR-193 is unaffected (clamping doesn't make a constant-residual ⟂ satisfiable).

**Scope / what it does NOT touch.** Extension on-segment points (t≥1.02) and the single-carrier root-find (already bounded) are unchanged; on-circle/on-line/shape-scalar carriers are unchanged. Only a plain on-segment param written by the multi-carrier joint solver is now bounded — which is exactly the definition of "on the segment," so a figure that previously relied on it leaving [0,1] was already geometrically wrong.

**Consequences / tests.** Scenario [`on-segment-point-stays-within-its-segment`](../src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts) locks the operator's exact 4-step sequence (E within AB, F within DC, `DF:FC≈1:10`, `EF ∥ BC`). **Full suite green (no regressions from the clamp); `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.**

## ADR-195 — the givens verifier is the backstop for on-segment membership (a sibling-bug audit of ADR-193/194)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** After ADR-193/194 the operator asked to not just fix the reported figures but "scan to see if similar areas would have similar bugs." Two read-only audits of the engine looked for siblings of the two classes: (193) a solver returns a best-effort placement while discarding an unsatisfiability signal; (194) a driven DOF leaves its geometric domain / a dual-root constraint picks the wrong branch. Findings: **(a)** the ADR-193 top-level `evaluate` re-check already GENERALISES — it re-verifies every driven-carrier kind (`drivenConstraintsOf` gathers from every `.solve`/`on-segment-solved`), so the other best-effort-discarding spots (`resolveFreeDriven`, `resolveMixedCarriers`, the single-carrier no-root path) are all caught by it; no new fix needed there. **(b)** the other bounded-carrier writes in `setCarrierVals` (on-circle θ, rotated angle) are PERIODIC/continuous domains — any value is a valid position, not an escape; the one-sided perp-offset/scaled-offset clamps are a possible over-restriction, not a silent escape, and have no reproducing figure — left untouched (no speculative patch). **(c)** the real systemic gap: the givens verifier (`verify.ts`) checked on-CIRCLE membership but had **NO on-SEGMENT membership check** — so a point declared "on segment AB" that landed off it (t∉[0,1]) by ANY path was silently green. This is exactly the backstop that would have caught ADR-194 independently of the clamp. **(d)** adding that check surfaced a latent MODELLING bug: the external-secant rule created the outside point `E` at `t:1.3` but **omitted `extension:true`** ([parse.ts](../src/parser/parse.ts)) — so `E` was a "plain on-segment point" living at t=1.3, contradicting its own meaning ("E on AB" vs "E on the *extension* of AB" — the operator's own framing). The clamp never touched it (E is undriven, fixed t), but the verifier rightly flagged the mismatch.

**Decision.**
- **Verifier backstop.** `checkGivens` now re-derives `point-on-segment` membership and checks the final coordinates: a PLAIN point must be collinear AND within `[0,1]` (tol); an EXTENSION point (t>1) must lie beyond the second endpoint. Loose tolerance (a point just past an endpoint isn't flagged). This is the general net for the whole "a point slid off its object" class, independent of which solver path caused it — the on-circle analogue that was already there. New i18n key `figure.v.onSegment` (+ reuse of `orderBeyond` for the extension case).
- **Operative-definition guard.** Only a point's LAST defining command is checked. A point declared on a segment/extension and then REDEFINED by a later command that OUTPUTS it ("E על המשך AC" then "E על מעגל P", which supersedes the placement) is verified against its real definition (the on-circle check), not the stale on-segment one. A CONSTRAINT that merely references the point (a ratio/∥ driving it — the ADR-194 case) does NOT count as a redefinition, so a genuinely-drifted driven point is still caught.
- **Secant modelling fix.** The external-secant rule now emits `E` with `extension: true` — correctly "E on the extension of BA beyond A," matching the ADR-105 semantics and passing the new verifier check.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The audit's product is a general SAFETY NET plus one true modelling correction, not per-figure spot fixes. The verifier backstop makes "green ⇒ every stated membership actually holds" true for segments as it already was for circles, so any future path (a new solver, a new constraint kind) that drifts an on-segment point off is caught for free. The secant fix removes a real "plain point living outside its segment" inconsistency the operator's own distinction (on-AB vs on-extension-of-AB) demands.

**Consequences / tests.** `verify.test.ts` gains an "on-segment membership" block (valid in-segment + valid beyond-b pass; a plain point dragged to t>1 or t<0 is flagged `onSegment`; an extension point fallen between the endpoints is flagged `orderBeyond`; a superseded on-segment command is NOT flagged). The 4 external-secant scenarios and the `redefine-existing-point-onto-circle` scenario stay green (secant `extension:true` + the operative-definition guard). **Full suite green (1776); `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.**

## ADR-196 — a midsegment named AFTER the triangle resolves its triangle from the figure

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** Operator session `z5dkmbla`: `משולש ABC` then, in a later step, `GE קטע אמצעים מקביל ל AB` ("GE is a midsegment parallel to AB"). The `midsegment` rule ([parse.ts](../src/parser/parse.ts), ADR-110/ADR-150) required the triangle to be NAMED in the SAME utterance (`/(?:triangle|משולש)\s*ABC/`). With no "משולש ABC" in this utterance `triM` was null, the rule bailed, and the utterance fell through to `parallelConstraint` — becoming a **plain parallel segment** (`segment GE`, `segment AB`, `set-parallel GE∥AB`) with **no midpoints**. So G and E were free points, the triangle's sides carried no equal halves, and "view relations" (`detectRelations`) correctly found nothing to show — the operator's report "no equal side and not equal angles are shown." The engine's relations layer was never at fault; the construct simply never built as a midsegment. This directly contradicts the app's primary interaction (CLAUDE.md: "building the figure up one step at a time") — a construct that only works when the whole context is packed into one utterance can't survive incremental building.

**Decision.** `midsegment` resolves the triangle from the FIGURE when it isn't named in-utterance: the apex is the unique vertex adjacent to BOTH base endpoints (`ctx.neighbors`), so the base + the figure determine the triangle. The rule restructures to require only the base match; the triangle is `triM` (named) OR `[apex, base[0], base[1]]` (inferred, when exactly one common neighbour exists — 0 or ≥2 ⇒ fall through rather than guess). Everything downstream (named endpoints, midpoint + segment emission, triangle-already-present skip) is unchanged. `GE קטע אמצעים מקביל ל AB` now decomposes to `midpoint(C,A)=G`, `midpoint(C,B)=E`, `segment GE`, so the equal halves (AG=CG, BE=CE) and the corresponding parallel angles are ground truths and surface in the relations layer.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect is a general one — a context-dependent construct that only read its context from the current utterance — not a one-figure quirk. The fix uses the SAME context-inference channel (`ctx.neighbors`) that `altitude` (via `ctx.parallels`) and the single-vertex angle already use, so it's consistent with how the parser resolves figure-relative references generally; any incrementally-declared midsegment now works, not just the reported one.

**Consequences / tests.** New end-to-end scenario `incremental-midsegment-resolves-triangle-from-figure` (the operator's exact 2-step sequence; asserts the two midpoints, GE∥AB, and the equal halves + corresponding angles surfacing via `detectRelations`). Parser/named-shapes suites unchanged (the in-utterance named form still parses). **Full suite green (1782); `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.**

## ADR-197 — Right-isosceles triangle is ONE composed shape badge, not an isosceles + right pair

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** Operator report (screenshot): a square ABCD with area 16 and its diagonal AC drawn surfaced each half-triangle (ABC, ACD) as **two** shape-detection badges — `משולש שווה שוקיים` (isosceles) **and** `משולש ישר זווית` (right) — where the operator expected a single `משולש ישר זווית ושווה שוקיים` (right isosceles triangle). Root cause in `classifyTriangle` ([detectShapes.ts](../src/engine/detectShapes.ts)): it modelled the equal-sides axis (equilateral/isosceles/general) and the right-angle axis as orthogonal and pushed a **separate badge per axis**, so any forced right-isosceles triangle double-badged (and a scalene *right* triangle badged `triangle` + `right-triangle` too).

**Decision.** `right-isosceles-triangle` becomes its own `ShapeType`, mirroring the existing precedent where `isosceles-trapezoid` / `right-trapezoid` are each first-class combined types. `classifyTriangle` now returns the **single most-specific** type, composing the two axes: equilateral → `equilateral-triangle` (never right); isosceles ∧ right → `right-isosceles-triangle`; isosceles → `isosceles-triangle`; right → `right-triangle`; else `triangle`. The two call sites (declared polygon + emergent cycle) collapse from a `for … of` over an array to one `add`. i18n gains `shapes.name/def.right-isosceles-triangle` in both locales; `TYPE_ORDER` places it between equilateral and isosceles. There is **no dedicated geometry-book page** for a right isosceles triangle (confirmed against the `…/571/geometry` index), so its `SHAPE_BOOK_SLUG` points at the **right-triangle** page `meshulash-yashar-zavit` (operator's choice — a right-and-isosceles triangle reads there).

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect is the two-axis composition model, not the one reported figure — so the fix changes how *every* triangle is classified (a scalene right triangle now surfaces a single `right-triangle` badge instead of the redundant `triangle` + `right-triangle` pair), removing the double-badging as a class rather than special-casing the square-diagonal case. It follows the established combined-type pattern already used for trapezoids.

**Consequences / tests.** `detectShapes.test.ts` updated (scalene-right → single `right-triangle`, no plain `triangle`; new right-isosceles case from a square diagonal).
