New end-to-end scenario `square-diagonal-right-isosceles` replays the operator's exact `ריבוע ABCD` · `שטח ABCD הוא 16` · `AC` and asserts one `right-isosceles-triangle` badge on {A,B,C} and {A,C,D} with no isosceles/right split; indexed in [test-scenarios.md](test-scenarios.md). Full suite green; `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.

## ADR-198 — Emergent-quad detection rejects a STRAIGHT (collinear) vertex, not only a zero-area cycle

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** Operator report (screenshot): a square ABCD with **both** diagonals AC, BD drawn (meeting at their crossing E) surfaced spurious `דלתון` (kite) badges — ABED, ABCE, ADCE, BCDE — where there are no kites. Root cause in emergent-quad detection ([detectShapes.ts](../src/engine/detectShapes.ts)): the "is this a genuine polygon" gate `isSimpleEverywhere` rejected only **zero-area** cycles (shoelace) and bowtie orderings. A cycle like **A-B-E-D** has E lying exactly on diagonal BD, so B,E,D are collinear — it is really triangle ABD with a redundant fourth vertex, yet its shoelace area equals triangle ABD's (non-zero), so it passed the gate and `classifyQuad` read the straight B-E-D corner as a kite vertex (two sides + two half-diagonals ⇒ two adjacent equal pairs). Every diagonal-crossing point plants exactly this degeneracy on both diagonals.

**Decision.** `isSimpleEverywhere` now also rejects a cycle with a **straight vertex** — a corner whose two incident edges are collinear (`hasStraightVertex`: normalised cross product of the two edge vectors ≈ 0, or a coincident consecutive vertex) — in any sample. Such a cycle is a lower-order polygon, not a genuine n-gon, so it must not be classified. The check uses the same `angleTol` the classifiers use (now threaded into `isSimpleEverywhere`).

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The defect is a **general** gap in the degeneracy gate — the shoelace-area test cannot see a single collinear vertex on an edge — not a quirk of this one figure. ANY figure with a point on a polygon edge (a diagonal crossing, an on-segment point, a foot) could spawn these phantom quads; the straight-vertex gate closes the whole class at the gate every emergent cycle already passes through. It is conservative and correct: a genuine simple polygon never has a 180° interior angle, so no real emergent shape is lost — verified by the surviving emergent scenarios (the EGFH rhombus of ADR-166/167 has no straight vertex).

**Consequences / tests.** `detectShapes.test.ts` gains a case (square + both diagonals ⇒ no `kite:*`, while the declared `square:ABCD` and the eight right-isosceles triangles survive). New end-to-end scenario `square-both-diagonals-no-phantom-kites` replays the operator's exact `ריבוע ABCD` · `AC` · `BD` · `E = חיתוך AC ו-BD`; indexed in [test-scenarios.md](test-scenarios.md). Full suite green; `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.

## ADR-199 — a base-less midsegment ("EG קטע אמצעים" with E on a side) is a 2-variant construct, cyclable

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** Operator session `n6zuhw65`: `משולש ABC` → `E על AC` (E free on side AC) → `EG קטע אמצעים`, with NO parallel base named. The `midsegment` rule ([parse.ts](../src/parser/parse.ts)) required a base (either "…in triangle ABC" or the [ADR-196](#adr-196) figure-resolved base), so with none it bailed and the utterance fell through to the plain-segment rule → a bare `segment E-G` with G an undefined free point ("EG was not drawn correctly"). A midsegment (קטע אמצעים) joins two MIDPOINTS, so E must be the midpoint of AC and G the midpoint of one of the two OTHER sides — AB (⇒ EG ∥ CB) or CB (⇒ EG ∥ AB). WHICH side is genuinely unstated ([ADR-052](#adr-052)), so — per the operator — it must be a cyclable alternative ("G should have been placed on either side CB or AB with ability to alternate between them"), not a fixed default.

**Decision.** The parser gains a `midsegmentBaseless` branch (fired when no base matches): it reads the named endpoint pair, resolves which endpoint (`E`) already rides a triangle side from a new `ctx.onSegment` hint (`E → [A,C]`, derived in `buildParseCtx` from the figure's `on-segment` objects — the same category of figure-derived hint as `neighbors`/`parallels`), resolves the triangle's third vertex `R` as the unique common neighbour of the side's endpoints (`ctx.neighbors`), and requires the other endpoint (`G`) to be fresh. It emits a `shape-variant` of a new `midsegment` shape carrying `ids = [P,Q,R,E,G]`. `expandShapeVariant` dispatches midsegment to `expandMidsegment`: `set-equal(P,E,E,Q)` pins E to the midpoint of PQ (driving the existing free on-segment point, "shapes carry their true DOF" — [ADR-033](#adr-033)), `midpoint(G, …)` places G on PR (variant 0) or QR (variant 1), and `segment(E,G)` draws it. `VARIANT_COUNT.midsegment = 2`, so the store's `cycleVariant` / "show another configuration" (and `variantConfigs` sampling for relations/shape detection) treat it exactly like a kite's axis or an isosceles apex.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The construct — "a midsegment whose second endpoint's host side is unstated" — is a genuine 2-configuration ambiguity, so it is modelled with the engine's existing discrete-alternative mechanism (`shape-variant`, generalised from equal-pair-only to a dispatched expansion) rather than by defaulting G to one side (which would silently assert an unstated given, the ADR-052 cardinal sin) or emitting a bare segment. E's midpoint pinning is definitional (a midsegment joins midpoints), not a heuristic. Reuses the same variant/cycle plumbing kite/isosceles use, so "show another configuration", relations sampling, and DOF accounting all work with no per-construct wiring.

**Consequences / tests.** New scenario `baseless-midsegment-places-G-on-a-side-and-alternates` (the operator's exact 3-step sequence; asserts E is the midpoint of AC, G is the midpoint of AB or CB, EG ∥ the opposite side, and variant 1 flips G to the other side). `expandShapeVariant` refactored to dispatch by shape (kite/isosceles path byte-identical). The base-named and [ADR-196](#adr-196) figure-resolved forms are unchanged (a base still routes to the original path). **Full suite green (1787); `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.**

**Amendment (2026-07-04, session `tg6s9dnp`) — an anchor endpoint may be an EXISTING midpoint, not only a free on-segment point.** Operator ("I now have M and N somehow"): `טרפז ABCD חסום במעגל` → `AC` → `E אמצע AD` (E = the midpoint of AD) → `EF קטע אמצעים במשולש DCA`. `midsegmentBaseless` only recognised a **free on-segment** anchor (via `ctx.onSegment`); E here is a **derived `midpoint`**, so the branch returned null → the whole rule escalated to the LLM, which "normalised" the utterance to `קטע האמצעים לצלע CA במשולש DCA`, **dropping the student's labels EF**, so the unnamed path auto-minted midpoints **M and N** (with N a redundant duplicate of the existing E). Root cause: the anchor-resolution universe was too narrow — a midpoint sitting on a triangle side is just as valid an anchor as a free rider. Fix: a new figure-derived hint `ctx.midpointOf` (each `midpoint` object → the segment `[a,b]` it bisects, built in `buildParseCtx` beside `onSegment`); `midsegmentBaseless` resolves each endpoint's host side from `onSegment` **or** `midpointOf` (a shared `anchor()` helper), and rejects a "fresh" endpoint that is itself an anchor. E is reused (the variant's `set-equal(P,E,E,Q)` pin is definitionally satisfied by the existing midpoint — a check, no DOF recruited) and only F is minted (midpoint of one of the two other sides, still the cyclable variant). No M/N, labels honoured. Locked by scenario `named-midsegment-reuses-existing-midpoint-endpoint` (the operator's exact 4-step sequence). Full suite green; `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.

## ADR-200 — one exhaustive `objectParents` for the dependency walk (retire `evaluate`'s hand-scraped `PT_FIELDS`)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02) · Hardening plan [Phase D / D1 / ENG-1](15-hardening-plan.md)

**Context.** `evaluate`'s coupled-solve detector ([evaluate.ts](../src/engine/evaluate.ts) `resolveDriven`) walks the object→references graph to decide whether an `on-segment-solved` point is part of a dependency cycle (each such point needs another's position → the topological evaluator deadlocks and must promote the pair to the numeric joint solver — [ADR-045](#adr-045)). It walked the graph with `PT_FIELDS`, a hand-maintained string list of point-id field names scraped off each object (`typeof o[f] === 'string'`). That list **silently dropped edges**: it lacked `to` (perp-offset / rotated / scaled-offset / arc-midpoint), `toward` (radial-toward), `line`/`line1`/`line2` (line-circle / on-line / line-intersection), and `circle1`/`circle2` (circle-circle), and — because line/circle refs live nested under `.spec`/`.radius` — it never chased a line's or circle's defining points at all. So a solved point coupled to another **through** such an edge went undetected → it stayed closed-form → `evaluate` errored **"unresolved dependencies"** instead of routing it numerically. This is the same silent-drop anti-pattern the point-kind whitelist ([ADR-043](#adr-043)) was built to prevent, but here with no exhaustiveness guard: a newly-added object kind's references were simply invisible.

**Decision.** Add `objectParents(o: GeoObject): Id[]` to [types.ts](../src/engine/types.ts) — an **exhaustive `switch` over every `GeoObject` kind** (points, segment, polygon, line-via-spec, circle-via-radius-spec, arc) returning every object id it directly references, with a trailing `const _exhaustive: never = o` so a new kind is a **compile error** until its references are declared. `dependsOn` now walks with `objectParents`, chasing through line/circle intermediaries. `PT_FIELDS` is deleted.

**Why a NEW function, not "reuse `pointParents`" (the plan's first phrasing).** `pointParents` (step.ts) is a point-only DOF-walk *policy*: it deliberately stops at on-circle / line-mediated carriers (returns `[]`) so the free-DOF recruiter treats them as leaves. Reusing it would have fixed `to`/`toward` but still returned `[]` for the line∩circle-mediated case the plan itself names — and modifying it to chase circles would perturb the recruiter (ADR-103/113). The two encode genuinely different graph policies, so cycle detection gets its own complete walker; `pointParents` is left byte-identical. The remaining duplication is intentional and documented (a curated policy vs. the exhaustive structural truth), not a silent second list.

**Consequences / tests.** New engine test `src/engine/__tests__/object-parents.test.ts`: (1) asserts `objectParents` includes each previously-dropped edge (`to`/`toward`/`line`/`circle1,circle2`) and chases a line spec; (2) an end-to-end **reproduction** — a solved-on-segment point E coupled to a `perp-offset` P through P's `to:E` edge (|E→P|=5 ⇒ t=0.3) now resolves (`evaluate.ok`), and was confirmed to error under the restored old `PT_FIELDS`. No behaviour change for any existing figure (more-complete detection only ever promotes a genuinely-coupled pair to the numeric path, which is correctness-preserving). **Full suite green (1789); `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.**

## ADR-201 — `evaluate` publishes solved radii; the renderer stops reconstructing them (retire `pointOnCircleId`)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02) · Hardening plan [Phase D / D2 / ENG-2 + REN-6](15-hardening-plan.md)

**Context.** A `via:'free'` circle radius the solver drives is baked into `positions` (its on-circle points sit at the solved radius) but the stored circle object keeps its SEED. `resolveCircle` reads the object, so it returns the seed. The renderer ([scene.ts](../src/render/scene.ts)) therefore reverse-engineered the true radius via `pointOnCircleId` — a **six-kind whitelist** (`on-circle`/`line-circle`/`antipode`/`arc-midpoint`/`radial-toward`/`circle-circle`) picking any point known to lie on the circle, then measuring centre→point. This is the strongest "renderer is a pure consumer" violation (it re-derives a solver internal) and the same kind-whitelist anti-pattern as ADR-200 — it already bit once ([ADR-144](#adr-144): the whitelist omitted `radial-toward`, so a tangent circle whose only on-circle point is its touch point drew at the seed with the touch point floating inside it).

**Decision.** `evaluate` **already** resolves and returns `circles: Map<Id, ResolvedCircle>` (it runs `evaluateCore(resolveDriven(c))`, and `resolveDriven` bakes the solved radius into the circle object it evaluates — so the published map carries the true radius for free/driven/tangent-inner circles alike). Thread that map through: `replay` returns it on `Derived.circles`; `App` passes it to `<Figure circles=…>`; `Figure` forwards it into `buildScene(opts.circles)`. `buildScene` now takes each circle's radius from the published map (centre still from the view-oriented positions — the radius is a scalar, orientation-invariant), and `pointOnCircleId` is **deleted**. A direct `buildScene` caller that doesn't thread the map (some unit tests) falls back to the object's declared radius via `resolveCircle` — correct for a `length`/`through` radius; a free radius then draws its seed, so tests that assert a *solved* free radius supply the map (as production does).

**Why root, not patch.** The defect is that the true radius was computed by the engine but not *exposed*, forcing every consumer to reconstruct it from a hand-maintained kind list. Publishing it once at the engine boundary removes the reconstruction entirely — the renderer becomes a pure consumer (ADR-044 intent), and a new on-circle point kind can never again silently break the drawn radius. Scoped precisely: the CENTRE stays from oriented positions (so flips/rotations still track), only the radius source changed.

**Consequences / tests.** `Derived` gains `circles`; `FigureProps` gains an optional `circles`; `buildScene`'s `opts` gains `circles`. The two ADR-144 render regressions (`radius-dof.test.ts` "renderer draws the driven radius", `lines-circles.test.tsx` tangent-radius) now pass the published map (the intended path) and stay green. New store-contract test: `replay(...).circles.get('circle-O').r` equals the solved 9 while the construction object keeps its seed 5 — proving the map is the single published source. **Full suite green (1790); `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.**

## ADR-202 — a ∥/⟂ constraint on a zero-length operand is rejected up front (no solver churn → no freeze)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-02)

**Context.** Operator session `wetjqgsj` (manual test): two free-radius circles, a valid tangent `CA משיק למעגל O בנקודה A` (→ `set-perpendicular(O,A,C,A)`), then `BB משיק למעגל P בנקודה B`. The last tangent is named by a **degenerate line "BB"** — one point repeated — so the parser emitted `set-perpendicular(a:P, b:B, c:B, d:B)`. Its second operand segment `B→B` is a **zero-length vector**, so the perpendicular residual `unit(B−P)·unit(B−B)` is NaN. Nothing rejected it: `evaluate(next)` returned not-ok only after `applyStep`'s `recruitFreeDofs` chased the NaN over every free DOF (the two free radii + on-circle θs) and the joint optimizer churned — **~4.4 s per `replay`** — before reporting a bogus `over-constrained: OA ⟂ CA cannot hold` (the *valid* earlier tangent, dragged in as a co-driver). Because the store runs `replay` many times per commit (dry-run + the `firstSatisfyingSeed`/`findValidConfig` config search), 4.4 s × N **froze the UI**. Reproduced and isolated: the degenerate `set-perpendicular` alone accounts for the 4.4 s (the `B` redefinition alone is 19 ms).

**Decision.** Reject the degeneracy at the earliest engine boundary. `applyStep` gains `degenerateConstraintError(cmd)` — a cheap, id-level guard (beside the existing `circlesTangentError` early-return): a `set-perpendicular`/`set-parallel` whose operand segment has identical endpoint ids (`a===b` or `c===d`) returns a clear error and keeps the prior figure, *before any `evaluate`*. 4.4 s → ~15 ms. The message names the offending token: `⟂ needs two distinct points on each side — "BB" is a single point, not a segment`.

**Why this layer / this scope.** The root is not the "BB" typo per se but that **a direction constraint with a zero-length operand reaches the expensive solver at all** — reachable from a parser typo, the LLM, or a student typing `AA ⟂ BC`. Guarding at `applyStep` (structural, by id) fixes the whole class in one place, independent of source, and can never churn again. A ∥/⟂ is *defined* by two distinct points per segment, so the guard rejects no well-formed constraint (the valid `set-perpendicular(O,A,C,A)` of the same session passes untouched). Scoped to the operand-**segment** direction constraints (∥/⟂), which are the ones a zero-length operand turns into a NaN *direction*; a sibling degeneracy on `set-angle`'s arms (`vertex===ray`) is the same shape and a candidate for the same guard if it ever surfaces (no repro today, so not pre-emptively added — ADR-052 discipline against speculative scope). The deeper, general "any single slow replay can freeze the config-search loop" is the separate Phase E / STO-2 wall-clock-deadline item; this ADR removes the specific pathological input that triggered it.

**Consequences / tests.** New scenario `degenerate-tangent-line-fails-fast-no-freeze` (the operator's exact 6-step sequence; asserts the clear message, the prior figure kept, and the valid `OA ⟂ CA` still holding) + `src/engine/__tests__/degenerate-constraint.test.ts` (⟂ with `c===d`/`a===b` and ∥ with a zero operand rejected in <500 ms; a well-formed ⟂ still accepted). **Full suite green (1795); `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean.**

## ADR-203 — second Fable review of the hardening phases: 16 verified findings fixed at root

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-03)

**Context.** After Phases A–D of the [hardening plan](15-hardening-plan.md) landed, the operator asked for a fresh multi-agent review **of the hardening diff itself** (`6dbcc0e..26efa93`) to validate the fixes before continuing to Phase E. Eight finder angles + five verification agents ran; every candidate was **verified by execution** (parser probes at HEAD vs the base commit, store probes, an engine timing repro, a server concurrency probe) — 16 confirmed findings, several of them regressions introduced *by* the hardening fixes themselves. All fixed in one batch, each at the layer the defect originates.

**The findings and their root fixes** (IDs are the review's; tests in brackets):

- **E3 (severe — extends ADR-202).** The "no repro" sibling ADR-202 parked was **proven reachable**: `זווית ABB = 40` parses to a `set-angle` whose ray repeats its vertex → `angleDeg` NaN → recruiter/optimizer churn (~200×), and the app's config search ran **~20 s per submit, re-firing on every later utterance**. Root: the guard covered only ∥/⟂. `degenerateConstraintError` now rejects the whole **NaN-by-id class** — ∥/⟂ zero operands, the angle family (`set-angle`/`-ratio`/`-order`/`-acuteness`) with a ray === its vertex, `set-collinear`/`set-line` with a repeated point. A zero angle between *distinct* coincident rays (finite residual) is deliberately not guarded. [`degenerate-constraint.test.ts` +6]
- **E1 (extends ADR-195).** The verifier's operative-definition scan counted any command carrying an `ids` array as a REDEFINITION of every listed point — but a polygon drawn *through* an existing on-segment point only wires edges, so `triangle ABE` silently **disabled the ADR-194 on-segment backstop for E**. `lastDef` now counts only genuine outputs (`id`/`id1`/`id2`). [`verify.test.ts` +1]
- **P1 (fixes ADR-184's post-pass).** `withCarrierMembership` pinned the diameter's through-centre collinearity to `pairs[0]` — the first segment *in the utterance* — so `המיתר CD מאונך לקוטר AB` forced the **chord** through the centre (wrong figure, verifier-green). The diameter pair is now resolved from the TEXT (the pair adjacent to the noun; a lone pair; else **no guess**, per ADR-052). [`review-fixes.test.ts` P1]
- **P5 (fixes ADR-184's bail).** The post-pass bailed on line-construct *kinds* (`line-line-intersection` et al.), so `chords AC and BD meet at E` lost all four memberships (a regression vs base). A line construct now bails only when it **anchors to the circle** (references its centre — `diameterCutsSegment`'s F–O line); a chord meet that never touches the circle gets its membership restored. [`review-fixes.test.ts` P5]
- **P4/P3 (fix ADR-183's handoff).** The chord/diameter `=`-bail orphaned noun-repeated forms (`מיתר AB = מיתר CD` regressed from parse to LLM escalation): the relation rules (`equalSegments`, `lengthOrder`) now tolerate an optional **carrier noun** before each pair (`CARRIER_PRE`), and the bail itself widened to word-form relations (`שווה`/`equals`/`גדול`…, shared `CARRIER_RELATION_TAIL`) so `מיתר AB שווה למיתר CD` **escalates honestly instead of half-parsing** to a bare chord (word equality stays out of grammar per the operator's 2026-06-25 decision). [`review-fixes.test.ts` P3+P4]
- **P6 (extends ADR-186).** The multi-statement splitter had no **bare Hebrew conjunction**: `AB = 4 ו-BC = 6` silently kept only the trailing given — the exact PAR-2 class, in the app's default language. `STATEMENT_SEP` gains `ו` (hyphen/space/attached-Latin forms only, so a ו-prefixed Hebrew word never splits); the every-piece-has-a-relation + all-or-nothing gates keep constructions (`AE ו BF נפגשים`) untouched. [`review-fixes.test.ts` P6]
- **P2 (fixes ADR-186's defence-in-depth bail).** The angle rule counted the word `זווית` and the `∠` glyph as TWO angle keywords, regressing `זווית ∠ABC = 40` (word + toolbar glyph) to the LLM. The bail now counts angle **references** (`word (∠)? | ∠`). [`review-fixes.test.ts` P2]
- **P8 (completes ADR-182).** The PAR-3 inflection stem widened `perpendicularConstraint` but **not** `perpBisector`, whose singular-only gate let the plural `האנכים האמצעיים של AB ו-CD` fall through and be HIJACKED into a wrong `set-perpendicular(AB,CD)`. The gate now admits definite/plural inflections, and the plural form emits **one ⊥-bisector per named segment**. [`review-fixes.test.ts` P8]
- **P7 (completes ADR-181).** `parseRename`/`parseSwap`/`parseMerge` run BEFORE `parse()` and skipped the orthography boundary — a pasted maqaf (`החלף בין C ל־D`) broke their connector groups. All three now use `normalizeUtterance`. [`review-fixes.test.ts` P7]
- **S1 (completes ADR-189).** `relabelId`'s lookbehind could never match a label following another letter, so rename/swap left the 2nd/3rd letters of concatenated structured ids stale (`bis-ABC` under B→P) — partially-renamed ids, duplicate constructions. It now **tokenizes** (`[A-Z]\d*` runs) and replaces exact tokens; the swap sentinel falls back to a literal replace. [store `review-fixes.test.ts` S1]
- **S2.** rename/swap/merge remapped `hidden`/`segStyle`/`hiddenCircles` but not `radiusOverrides` — a dialed radius silently snapped back to seed on rename. All three now remap it. [S2]
- **S3 (completes ADR-191).** Atomic-group poisoning ran ONE rebuild round; blocking group A could make a LATER group newly mixed, leaving its sibling scaffolding half-drawn (probe-proven). The poison→rebuild now runs to a **fixpoint** (bounded by the group count; stops if a PENDING state emerges, per ADR-104). [S3]
- **M1 (completes ADR-171/190).** `llmParse`'s per-step re-parse passed only `points`/`circles`/`circleMembers` — the caller's `neighbors`/`onSegment`/`parallels`/`lines` hints were **dropped entirely** (even for step 1) and never accrued, so a decomposition like `["נקודה E על AC","EG קטע אמצעים"]` silently built a bare segment instead of the ADR-199 midsegment. The full context is now threaded and a command-level `accrueHints` grows `onSegment`/`neighbors`/`lines` per built step (mirroring `accrueMembers`). [`llm.test.ts` +1]
- **M2 (completes ADR-170).** The shadow-matrix gate shipped as `toMatchSnapshot()` — a blanket `vitest -u` silently absorbed any new shadow, defeating the gate (the plan's checked-in allowlist was never built). The divergent **shadow-pair set** is now hard-asserted against `shadow-allowlist.json` (reviewed, commented), and each Phase-C probe pins its owning rule as a hard per-probe assertion; the per-utterance snapshots remain as readable diffs only. [`shadow-matrix.test.ts`]
- **V1 (completes ADR-179).** `pruneByRetention`'s read-modify-write raced concurrent `appendFile`s — a 204-acknowledged event landing in the window was clobbered (probe: 1/30 lost). All writers now run through **one serialized queue**, and the prune swaps atomically (tmp + `rename`) so dashboard reads never see a torn file. [`eventLog.test.ts` +1]
- **V2 (completes ADR-177).** The SEC-2 `source:'limit'` analytics tag — whose whole point is operator visibility of the cost ceiling — was bucketed by `outcomeOf`'s fallback as an **edit**. It now has its own `throttled` outcome + dashboard label. [`admin.test.ts` +1]
- **i18n (conventions).** The ADR-202 rejection message (and the new degenerate-class messages) had no `humanizeError` pattern/locale keys — Hebrew students saw raw English. Three patterns + he/en keys added. [`humanize-error.test.ts` +4]

**Also noted, deliberately NOT fixed here:** the review confirmed several efficiency observations (the poisoned-group double `runBuild` per replay, `evaluate`'s per-call `drivenConstraintsOf` scan, eventLog's synchronous parse on the daily prune) — bounded costs that fold into **Phase E**'s replay-memoization/deadline work (STO-1/STO-2), not separate patches; and the `commandPointIds` single-letter guard (subscripted points unrenamable) is the already-planned **E6/STO-7**.

**Consequences.** 39 new tests across seven suites; one deliberate shadow-matrix snapshot flip (`chord AB = chord CD` → owned by `equalSegments`); no engine behaviour change for any previously-green figure (the full suite stays green). The review also fixed the PROJECT-MEMORY "NOT yet committed" drift for ADR-200–202 (committed as `26efa93`).

## ADR-204 — replay is memoized and the config search is wall-clock-bounded (Phase E: E1/STO-1, E2/STO-2, A5/TST-5)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-03) · Hardening plan [Phase E](15-hardening-plan.md)

**Context.** `replay(facts, seed, overrides)` is pure but was treated as free: one user action ran it from four layers (dry-run, commit guard, debug snapshot, render), and the config search (`firstSatisfyingSeed` / `findValidConfig` / `meetsRequirements`) re-replayed the SAME (facts, seed) pairs across its passes — on the documented heavy figures (~1.5 s/replay, ADR-123) that compounded into multi-second freezes. Separately, the debug-snapshot subscription ran a full `replay` on every store change **in production**, where `analyticsSubmit` then discarded the event; and the search loops were deadline-free on the UI thread.

**Decision.** (1) **Memoize `replay`** behind its exact signature: a `WeakMap` keyed on the facts array's identity → per-seed/overrides `Derived`. The store never mutates a facts array (every action builds a new one), but tests/harnesses legitimately `push` into one — so a hit is validated by **element-identity** (O(n) ref compares) before being served; a mutated array recomputes. The WeakMap releases a dry-run's throwaway trial arrays with the arrays themselves; the per-facts map is bounded (512). `replayStats.computes` counts real recomputes. (2) **DEV-gate the debug-snapshot subscription** in `App` (one line — also closes the SEC-7 note about prod figure payloads). (3) **Wall-clock budget** (`SEARCH_BUDGET_MS` = 2.5 s; `Infinity` under vitest so seed choices stay machine-independent) on `firstSatisfyingSeed` and `findValidConfig`: past the deadline they return what they have and the caller keeps the current figure, honestly amber, instead of freezing — the deadline path is unit-tested via an explicit budget param. The review-confirmed double-`meetsRequirements` (resolveAfterCommit → autoResolve) is now a cache hit rather than a special-cased dedup.

**Consequences / tests.** `phase-e.test.ts`: cache-hit identity, per-seed independence, the mutated-array staleness guard, budget-0 early exits; the A5 **perf canary** asserts a standard 3-step commit flow stays under a replay-count ceiling (count, not time — CI-stable), so "replay got called from one more layer" regressions fail loudly. No behavioural change for any green figure.

## ADR-205 — the submit pipeline is race-safe and cancellable; one user action = one undo entry restoring the seen view (Phase E: E3/STO-3, E4/STO-4, E5/STO-5)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-03) · Hardening plan [Phase E](15-hardening-plan.md)

**Context.** Three coupled store/App defects: (a) `submit` awaited the network then dry-ran the LLM result against the **pre-await** facts snapshot while committing onto the live list, and only the Submit button (not the example chips) was gated — concurrent submits could race; `llmParse` had no timeout/abort, so a hung proxy meant a permanent spinner. (b) A multi-command utterance committed as N separate `execute` calls → zundo recorded N entries, so one undo peeled a single command off a step whose row still showed ✓; `autoResolve`'s rewrite added another invisible entry. (c) History partialized `facts` only, while `execute` auto-advances the seed and `autoResolve`/`resample` set it — undo replayed the reverted list at a *different* seed, showing a figure the student never saw (violating the stability promise at the history layer); dialed radii also survived undo.

**Decision.** (a) **E3:** a synchronous `busyRef` gates every `submit` entry point (chips, enter, help examples); after the `await` the store is **re-read** and the dry-run runs against the current facts; `llmParse` takes an `AbortSignal`, the App arms a ~15 s timeout plus a visible **cancel** affordance next to the spinner (i18n'd), and an aborted call resolves to the "service busy" path — never a stuck spinner, never "couldn't understand" for a fault that isn't the student's. (b) **E4:** a store `executeMany(cmds, utterance)` folds the whole batch through the same per-command policy (idempotent dup, free-point move, standalone-circle resize — extracted as `foldFact`) and commits in **one `set`** (one group id, one undo entry); `resolveAfterCommit` wraps `autoResolve` in zundo `pause()/resume()` so auto-resolution merges into the triggering entry. (c) **E5:** the temporal state is now `{facts, seed}` — undo restores the view the student actually saw — and the store's `undo`/`redo` wrappers clear `radiusOverrides` (a per-drag slider value must not flood history, so it stays OUT of the partialize; it just can't outlive the state it annotated). The seed auto-advance now rides in the SAME `set` as the facts it belongs to.

**Consequences / tests.** `phase-e.test.ts` (one-undo-per-step incl. redo; single group id; seed rollback; scratchpad clearing); `llm.test.ts` (the abort resolves null and threads the signal). `App` uses `executeMany` on all three commit paths. Existing suites unchanged — `equality` still dedupes no-op sets.

## ADR-206 — subscripted-point store ops + algebraic round-trip properties over the scenario corpus (Phase E: E6/STO-6/7, E7/TST-4)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-03) · Hardening plan [Phase E](15-hardening-plan.md)

**Context.** Store ops mutate facts via JSON/string rewriting — historically the highest-density bug area (ADR-122's substring corruption; the review's S1 partial structured-id rename) — yet only example-based tests existed. And the ops' point-id guard was `/^[A-Z]$/`: a subscripted point (`O1`, which the LLM path legitimately produces and PAR-10 explicitly widened `absorb` for) could not be renamed/swapped/merged ("no-source"), and `renameSegKey` assumed 2-char endpoints so a styled `seg-O1O2` went stale.

**Decision.** **E6:** `commandPointIds` widened to whole-token `[A-Z]\d*`; `renameSegKey` tokenizes the endpoint run (same label shape `relabelId` uses) — subscripted points now rename/swap/merge like any other (merge's utterance relabel was already fixed to the token-aware `relabelUtterance` in ADR-203). **E7:** the ~130 real scenarios are the property generator (no fast-check): for a deterministic slice, (1) `swap∘swap` and (2) `rename∘rename⁻¹` are byte-identities on commands AND utterances; (3) disable-then-re-enable restores the exact figure to 1e-9; (4) permuting two trailing constraint-only sibling groups keeps the figure verifier-clean (ADR-104 order-independence on real corpora, whole-corpus scan capped at 8 qualifying figures). Each property asserts its own coverage (no silent zero-exercise pass).

**Consequences / tests.** `phase-e.test.ts` (rename `O1`→`P`, styled `seg-O1O2` tracking) + the three-property `E7` block in `scenarios.test.ts` (same-file per the C6 lesson — importing a `.test.ts` would double-register every scenario; the stale `seed-sweep.test.ts` doc pointer and dead exports there were cleaned). Suite cost ≈ +30 s, bounded and documented.

## ADR-207 — hardening Phase F: renderer/UX for the real audience (RTL, tablets, teachers' exports, a11y)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-03) · Hardening plan [Phase F](15-hardening-plan.md) · **F2 scope set by the operator: tablets, not phones** ("I'm not concerned about mobile — the UX won't be good; but we do need to think about tablets").

**Context & decisions**, one per plan item:

- **F1/REN-1 — RTL edit-menu mirror (HIGH).** The click-anchored point/segment/circle menu positioned with `insetInlineStart` — a LOGICAL inset that resolves to `right` under the Hebrew-default `dir=rtl` — using a PHYSICAL left-based click coordinate, so the menu opened mirrored, far from the clicked point. Fixed to physical `left`; the fixed toolbars keep logical insets (they're layout, correct as-is).
- **F2/REN-4 — tablet touch.** Every active pointer is tracked in a map: ONE pointer pans (as before), a second switches to **pinch-zoom about the fingers' midpoint** (the world point under the pinch centre stays under it — previously a second finger fell into the single-drag path and corrupted the pan). The hover-driven relations layer — the pedagogical headline, unreachable on touch — gains a **tap-to-toggle** path: an un-moved touch picks the equality class under the finger (wider 16 px reach for a fingertip) and toggles it; `onPointerLeave` keeps a tap-selected class visible (no hover to sustain it). **+/− zoom buttons** join the reset control as the button fallback. Layout: the sidebar's rigid 400 px becomes `min(400px, 100%)` so a portrait tablet wraps cleanly; no phone breakpoints (out of scope by the operator's call).
- **F3/REN-3 — clean export.** `svgToPng` cloned the live SVG verbatim, baking in crossing-suggestion dots, hidden-item ghosts, hover relation marks, and selection highlights. Ephemeral/interaction visuals are now tagged `data-noexport` (stripped from the export clone) and selection accents carry their base values in `data-export-*` attributes (reverted on the clone) — the exported PNG is the clean textbook figure regardless of what was selected/hovered.
- **F4/REN-5 — fit hysteresis.** The fit refit on every positions change, so one out-of-bounds point (an extension, a tangent's far crossing, a grown radius) re-scaled and shifted EVERY existing point — voiding the engine's structural stability at the view layer. New pure `keepOrRefit(prev, next, worldPts, vp)`: keep the previous transform while the content still fits (it may eat the padding down to a small margin) and the fresh fit wouldn't zoom in > 1.6× (gross shrink); refit only then. Keyed to the viewport + orientation, so a resize/rotate still re-frames.
- **F5/REN-2 — non-passive wheel.** React 18 registers `wheel` passive, so `onWheel`'s `preventDefault()` was a no-op and zooming scrolled the page. The listener is attached natively with `{ passive: false }`.
- **F6/A11Y.** `Modal` takes initial focus, traps Tab, is `aria-labelledby` its title, and restores focus to the opener (the auto-opening intro used to leave focus in the input behind it). `inputNote`/`lastError`/`pending`/violations get `role="status"`+`aria-live="polite"` so a screen-reader student hears a failed step. A broken step's reason — previously only a `title` tooltip, invisible on touch — now shows INLINE under the row when the row is selected.
- **F7/REN-7/8/9 — polish.** (REN-7) label placement is sequential and each placed label becomes an obstacle for the next, so two nearby/coincident points can't stack their letters (the forced-coincidence N=O case printed both exactly superimposed). (REN-8) the absolute world-space epsilons (`scene.ts` on-line trim 1e-5; `intersections.ts` dedupe 1e-6) are now span-relative — a figure whose free radius grew unbounded stopped recognising its own on-line points. (REN-9) the wedge dedup keys angles by a ±1.5° tolerance predicate instead of integer-rounded degrees (a hard quantization boundary mid-wedge could double-draw one corner).
- **REN-10 — DEFERRED, documented.** Memoizing the SVG body so a pan touches only the `<g transform>` requires extracting the ~400-line render body into a `React.memo` child with ~25 props — a large, risky refactor for a LOW-priority gain (pan re-render is fast in practice; tablets pinch fine). Parked with this reason; pick it up if pan latency is ever felt.

**Consequences / tests.** New `src/render/__tests__/phase-f.test.ts` (hysteresis band: keep/overflow/gross-shrink, incl. "existing points' screen positions literally unchanged"; coincident-point labels don't stack). Pointer/pinch, export stripping, and focus behaviour are DOM/browser behaviours — **the operator's manual device pass on a tablet is the acceptance step** (pinch, tap-a-side with relations on, export with a selection active, open/close the intro modal with a keyboard). Engine untouched; renderer stays a pure consumer.

## ADR-208 — Phase 6a: the live theorem-surfacing feed (help, don't reveal)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-04) · Implementation plan [Phase 6a](09-implementation-plan.md) · theorem plan [docs/16-theorems-plan.md](16-theorems-plan.md) · corpus [docs/sample questions/theorem-ground-truth.md](sample%20questions/theorem-ground-truth.md).

**Context.** Phase 6 surfaces the relevant bagrut theorems as a student builds. The pedagogy charter's headline rule is **stated-vs-derived** ("help, don't reveal"): the feed surfaces the theorems the student's STATED givens *announce* (a stated diameter announces Thales; an inscribed triangle announces the inscribed-angle theorem), and NEVER the derived "aha" theorem whose recognition IS the exercise (the similar-triangle pairing to be proven, the angle-bisector ratio to be derived). Getting that boundary wrong hands over the solution.

**Decisions.**
- **A pure, read-only spine `src/theorems/` — a sibling of `detectShapes`/`detectRelations`, the engine untouched.** `detectTheorems(input)` folds an authored `THEOREM_TABLE` (each theorem = its citable id + bilingual catalog statement + a premise-side `match(ctx)`) over a precomputed `MatchCtx`. **Match is coordinate-free** (plan §7.5): matchers read the fact list, the dependency graph, and derived symbolic hints (`circles`, `neighbors`, `tangents`) — no `replay`/`evaluate`/coordinates. That is what lets the feed run **live** (see below), unlike the sampled relations/shapes layers.
- **The no-reveal boundary is STRUCTURAL, not a runtime filter.** The forbidden derived-premise theorems (the similarity pairings 68/69/70/71, the bisector-ratio 76) are simply **not in the table** — so they cannot surface by construction. `integrity.test.ts` asserts their absence; the corpus test's `neverSurface` lists re-assert it per question.
- **Two axes tame the flood** (plan §3): **salience** — `headline` (a specific configuration the student had to state; listed individually) vs `background` (true of essentially every figure of a family; folds into one collapsed per-family row); and **tier** — `certain` (green, it applies now) vs `possible` (amber, a sparing secondary condition, e.g. the concyclic-quad inscribed-angle read). Each entry is attributed to the LATEST stated fact that completed its premise and marked `● new` when that fact is the current step.
- **Root fixes over the reported corpus cases (never patch).** (1) A stated diameter has **two lowered forms** — a `diameter` command OR a `set-collinear` through the circle centre (a chord through the centre IS a diameter); `statedDiameterFacts` recognises both, so 103/104 gate on a genuinely-stated diameter in any phrasing, never on a bare 90°. (2) A tangent has **two construction paths** — a first-class `{via:'tangent'}` line spec OR the Thales external-tangent construction (a hidden through-circle passing through the target's centre, intersected with it); `tangentPoints` fingerprints both geometrically (no id-prefix hack), so the tangent family (105/107/108/109) fires regardless of how the tangent was built.
- **The feed is LIVE and computed in the App, not the store.** Because match is coordinate-free and cheap, the App derives it with a `useMemo` over `facts`/`construction` each step — no store action or facts-keyed cache (the pattern `detectShapes` needs *because* it samples). **Emergent-shape triggers ride the "detect shapes" layer**: when that layer is on, its `DetectedShape[]` is passed in, so a purely emergent shape (an emergent rhombus between crossing segments) surfaces its theorems too (operator 2026-07-04: purely emergent shapes DO trigger).
- **UI.** A collapsible "משפטים רלוונטיים" feed in the control column (tier dots, ● new-this-step badges, background theorems folded per family), a Display-options toggle beside "show measures", and click-a-row → highlight that theorem's **premise** objects on the canvas (`triggerObjectIds`, never conclusion objects) via the existing `highlight` prop.

**Consequences / tests.** `src/theorems/__tests__/`: `integrity.test.ts` (parses `07-theorem-reference.md`, asserts every tabled theorem is byte-exact bilingual, correct type, not an appendix `O`, and the forbidden ids excluded — 118 checks); `matchers.test.ts` (per-matcher, real parse→replay→detectShapes→detectTheorems pipeline); `corpus.test.ts` — the **6a acceptance gate**: Q5–Q7 replayed step-by-step, asserting `expectSurfaced ⊆ feed` (accumulated) and `mustNotSurface ∩ feed = ∅` (neverSurface + step-gated absents) at every step. Full suite + build clean. Phase 6b (later): the B-series booklet corpus, the parallels/median/midsegment families, and — carefully gated so they stay derived-side — the similarity/bisector families as *converse recognition* prompts rather than premise announcements.

## ADR-209 — cyclic-quadrilateral / inscribed-trapezoid theorems + the parallels family (6b pulled forward); theorems grow by operator direction

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-04) · extends [ADR-208](#adr-208) · reference [07-theorem-reference.md](07-theorem-reference.md) Appendix C.

**Context.** First operator manual-test of the 6a feed (session note 2026-07-04): typing `טרפז ABCD חסום במעגל` (a trapezoid inscribed in a circle), **none** of the surfaced theorems were relevant — the feed showed only the *generic inscribed-polygon* theorems (99 inscribed-angle, 102 same-chord, + 84/91/97/98 background), because every circle matcher keyed off raw **member count**, blind to *what shape* the points form or to the trapezoid's stated parallel sides. The operator named the four theorems the configuration actually announces: cyclic-quad opposite-angles=180, co-interior angles between the parallel sides, equal-chords→equal-arcs, and "a trapezoid inscribed in a circle is isosceles".

**Decisions.**
- **Configuration-specific matchers, not member-count.** Added **#87** (cyclic quad, opposite angles sum to 180°) gated on an actual **quad command** (`quadrilateral`/4-`polygon`) whose vertices are all concyclic — so a triangle-plus-stray-4th-concyclic-point (Q5's arc-midpoint) never trips it; and **#8/#4/#6** (parallels: co-interior headline, alternate/corresponding background) gated on **stated parallels** — a `set-parallel` OR any parallel-sided shape command (trapezoid/parallelogram/rectangle/rhombus/square), the honest symbolic premise "two parallels cut by a transversal". Both are coordinate-free (facts + `circles`), so the feed stays live.
- **#94 broadened** from arc-midpoint-only to any EQUAL-CHORD evidence: an arc-midpoint, two chords of one circle stated equal (four concyclic endpoints), or an inscribed trapezoid (its legs are equal chords). Still coordinate-free — it reads a stated/structurally-forced premise, never a coincidental length match.
- **A new theorem #201 (Appendix C).** "A trapezoid inscribed in a circle is isosceles" is NOT an atomic bagrut theorem (the core list is a full 1–109; this is derivable from #87 + #8 + #40). Rather than falsely claim a 1–109 number, it lives in a new **Appendix C — cyclic-configuration corollaries** with a **200-band id** (composed teaching statements the student may *use*, kept out of the official numbering but tabled/citable). The integrity parser already accepts any `\d+`/type-P row, so no test-infra change; `TheoremDef.id`'s doc note now covers the 200 band. This is the home for future such corollaries.
- **The no-reveal boundary held to the operator's call.** Two of the four (87, 8) are clean premise announcements; the isosceles lemma (201) and 94 are the solution chain. The operator ruled 201 a legitimate teaching theorem to surface and directed pulling the parallels family forward from 6b now — so all four surface. The **forbidden derived-premise set (68/69/70/71/76) is untouched** and still structurally excluded.
- **Working mode — theorems grow by operator direction (like ADRs).** During feature debug the operator names theorems a configuration should surface; each becomes a permanent table entry (+ reference row if new), exactly as here. Recorded so it travels (PROJECT-MEMORY).

**Consequences / tests.** `matchers.test.ts` +4 (the operator's exact `טרפז ABCD חסום במעגל` surfaces {87,8,94,201}; a plain inscribed quad surfaces 87 not 201; an inscribed triangle surfaces neither; a standalone trapezoid surfaces 8 not the cyclic ones); `integrity.test.ts` now 143 checks (201 byte-checked against Appendix C). Q5–Q7 corpus **unchanged** (no quads/parallels there → new matchers dormant). Full suite **2033 green**, build clean. Open tuning knob for the operator's debug marathon: whether generic 99/102 should demote to background once a more specific cyclic-quad theorem fires (left headline for now).

## ADR-210 — a background theorem surfaces only when the figure instantiates its FULL premise configuration, not a mere precondition

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-04) · amends [ADR-208](#adr-208)/[ADR-209](#adr-209) · governs `src/theorems/table.ts`.

**Context.** Same `טרפז ABCD חסום במעגל` figure, next operator manual-test: even after ADR-209 added the configuration theorems, the feed still carried **unjustified background** — the alternate/corresponding parallels (#4/#6), the triangle-circumscribed background (#84), and the central-angle family (#92/#97/#98/#99). The operator's ruling, verbatim: *"background will show only if the shape itself justifies it. here there is no triangle and no line between the parallel lines. זוית מרכזית should appear only if the center is given."* Root cause: several matchers keyed off a **necessary precondition** (a stated parallel pair; a raw ≥N-concyclic-point count) rather than the theorem's **actual premise configuration**. A stated parallel pair is not a transversal cut; ≥3 concyclic points is not a triangle; a circle drawn without a named/used centre does not "give" the centre.

**Decision — gate each theorem on ITS OWN literal premise (three reusable, coordinate-free gates):**
- **Transversal gate (#4/#6).** The alternate/corresponding-angle relations need a line actually cutting the two parallels. `hasTransversal(ctx)` = a stated/detected **triangle** in the figure OR an explicit **`line`** object. A bare trapezoid/parallelogram (its own legs aside — the student drew no cutting line) no longer trips 4/6. The **co-interior sum (#8) is untouched** — a trapezoid leg IS its own same-side transversal, so #8 stands on the parallels alone (this is the pointed cyclic-trapezoid theorem, ADR-209).
- **Centre-given gate (#92/#97/#98/#99 — the central-angle family).** `centerGiven(ctx, circle)` = the centre is **named** (`!autoCenter`) OR **used** (`neighbors[center]` non-empty — a segment/radius drawn to it). This **mirrors the renderer's show-centre rule** (FR-RN-8, `scene.ts`) minus the display toggle, so "the theorem speaks about the centre" and "the centre is drawn" share one signal. An inscribed figure's implicit, unnamed circumscribing circle has no given centre → the central-angle theorems stay silent; a named `circle O` (Q5–Q7) keeps them. Threaded via a new `autoCenter` field on `MatchCtx.circles` (`context.ts`).
- **Triangle gate (#84).** #84 ("every **triangle** has a circumscribed circle") is gated on an actual circumscribed triangle (`circumTriangle` — some stated/detected triangle whose three vertices are concyclic), not ≥3 concyclic points. **#91 — see the amendment below** (initially kept on ≥3 members; the operator then ruled it near-useless and it was re-gated to a constructed circumcircle).

**Amendment (2026-07-04, same session) — #91 fires only for a circumcircle CONSTRUCTED through three points.** On seeing #91 ("through three non-collinear points passes one circle") surface for the inscribed trapezoid, the operator: *"this theorem should only appear in rare cases i cannot think about right now. there is no use for this in questions I remember."* #91's premise is not "≥3 points happen to be concyclic" (true of every inscribe figure, vacuously) but "three given points **determine** a circle" — the circle is **derived from** the points. That is the `circumcircle` construction (`circle through A B C`, `מעגל דרך A B C`, `circumscribed circle of triangle ABC`, `מעגל חוסם את המשולש ABC`), NOT points placed **on** a pre-existing `circle` (every `חסום במעגל` inscribe lowers to `circle` + `point-on-circle`). So #91 is now gated on a `circumcircle` command — dormant in all inscribe figures, live only for an explicit circumcircle. It stays in the table (a real bagrut theorem) for that rare case. **Q5/Q7 corpus updated** (inscribed triangles drop #91 — they place points on a stated `circle O`, no circumcircle), Q6 step 3 too.

**Consequences / tests.** The operator's `טרפז ABCD חסום במעגל` now surfaces only what it justifies — {8, 87, 94, 102, 201} — with 4/6/84/91/92/97/98/99 correctly suppressed. **Q6 ground truth updated**: step 3 (`DE is a chord`, a diameter+chord figure with **no triangle**, points on a stated circle) drops both #84 and #91 (kept #102) — the ADR-208 corpus had encoded the older member-count rule; the operator's principle makes "no triangle ⇒ no #84" and "no circumcircle ⇒ no #91" consistent across the corpus, not trapezoid special-cases. `matchers.test.ts` +5 ADR-210 cases (trapezoid suppresses 84/91/4/6/92/97/98/99 but keeps {8,87,94,201}; 4/6 return with a transversal; bare trapezoid = 8 not 4/6; a named circle restores 84/97/98/99; #91 surfaces only for a constructed circumcircle). Q5/Q7 keep 84/99 (named circles, stated triangles), drop 91. Full suite **2038 green**, build clean. **Principle to carry forward:** when a matcher looks like it keys off a precondition (a count, a lone relation), ask whether the theorem's *configuration* is actually present; a green corpus that encoded the looser rule is itself a candidate to tighten.

## ADR-211 — a special quadrilateral surfaces its own PROPERTY family (the shape justifies its theorems)

**Context.** Operator (2026-07-04, ADR-209 working mode): *"when I show a quad shape, the relevant theorems should appear. in מקבילית which I just tested they don't."* A drawn parallelogram surfaced only the generic co-interior #8 (`parallelFacts` → the parallels family) — its own defining properties (opposite sides equal, diagonals bisect, opposite angles equal, consecutive angles = 180°) never appeared, because the special-quadrilateral **property** families (07 #39/41/43/46/48/50/52/55/56) were simply never tabled. `THEOREM_TABLE`'s only quad entries were the cyclic ones (#87/#201). This is a genuine coverage gap (Phase-6b quad family), not a gating bug — the root fix is to add the family, not to patch the one shape.

**Decision.** Table the special-quadrilateral **property** theorems (type P), each folded into the existing `quad` **background** family (the `types.ts` doc already named "the parallelogram property bundle" as the canonical background fold — the design always intended it) at tier `certain`:
- **Parallelogram** — #43 (opposite sides), #46 (diagonals bisect each other), #48 (opposite angles), #50 (consecutive angles = 180°).
- **Rectangle** — #52 (diagonals equal).
- **Rhombus** — #55 (diagonals bisect the angles), #56 (diagonals perpendicular).
- **Isosceles trapezoid** — #39 (base angles equal), #41 (diagonals equal).

**Class hierarchy is the gate.** A new `quadClassPresent(ctx, kinds)` helper reports a class present when a matching shape is **stated** (a `parallelogram`/`rectangle`/`rhombus`/`square`/`trapezoid` command) **or detected** (`ctx.shapes` — constructed or purely emergent). Each family passes its own `kinds` set, and the sets encode the containment: `PARALLELOGRAM_KIND = {parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, square}`, `RECTANGLE_KIND = {rectangle, square}`, `RHOMBUS_KIND = {rhombus, square}`, `ISO_TRAP_KIND = {isosceles-trapezoid}`. So a rectangle inherits the parallelogram bundle + #52; a rhombus inherits it + #55/#56; a **square** gets all seven; a **generic** trapezoid gets none of #39/#41 (only the detected `isosceles-trapezoid` shape trips them); a triangle gets none.

**Why properties, not converses.** The "help, don't reveal" line falls exactly on the P/C split here: a property of a shape the student **drew** is help (they can use "opposite sides are equal" freely — it isn't a hidden proof step). The **converse** recognitions (07 #44/45/47/49/51/53/54/57/58/59/60/61, type C — "a quad with … is a parallelogram/rectangle/…") stay OUT of the table; those are Phase-6b converse-recognition prompts (recognise a shape FROM properties, a proof direction), consistent with keeping similarity/bisector converses out (ADR-208).

**Consequences / tests.** `מקבילית ABCD` now surfaces #8 (headline) + the folded {43,46,48,50} background bundle; rectangle/rhombus/square/isosceles-trapezoid each add their own. `matchers.test.ts` +7 cases (each shape's bundle in He + En, hierarchy inheritance, generic-trapezoid and triangle negatives); `integrity.test.ts` grows by the 9 new byte-equal statements (still the single source, 07). **2090 tests green, build clean.** **Principle:** a named shape is a first-class premise — its catalog property block is "relevant theorems the shape justifies", tabled as a background fold; only its *converse* recognitions wait for the Phase-6b gated-prompt layer.

## ADR-212 — a theorem's salience is context-dependent: drawing the diagonals promotes the diagonal-property theorems

**Context.** Operator (2026-07-04, continuing ADR-211): on a parallelogram with the **diagonals drawn** (`מקבילית ABCD` + `אלכסונים`) — *"in this case, the theorems about the diagonals should get more weight than others."* After ADR-211 all four parallelogram properties fold equally into the `quad` background bundle; but once the student puts the **diagonals** on the figure, the diagonal property (#46 "the diagonals bisect each other") is the one they're about to use — it should lead, not sit folded beside "opposite sides are equal".

**Decision.** Make salience **context-dependent**. A matcher may now return an optional `salience` on its `TheoremMatch`; `detectTheorems` uses `m.salience ?? def.salience` (the static salience stays the default). The special-quadrilateral property matchers (ADR-211) gain a `diag` flag marking the theorems ABOUT the diagonals — #46 (parallelogram), #52 (rectangle), #55/#56 (rhombus), #41 (isosceles trapezoid) — and each returns `salience: 'headline'` **iff the diagonals are actually drawn**, else stays `background`. The non-diagonal properties (#43/#48/#50/#39) are unaffected.

**"Diagonals drawn" is geometric, not a keyword.** A new `quadHasDiagonal(ctx, vertices)` reports true when a drawn segment joins a **non-adjacent** vertex pair of the quad's cyclic order — `ctx.neighbors` adjacency comes from drawn segments + polygon edges, so the four sides are always neighbours and *only* a drawn diagonal can make a non-adjacent pair adjacent. So it fires for the diagonals however they were entered (an explicit `segment AC`, the `אלכסונים` LLM lowering to `segment AC`+`segment BD`, a diagonal that arises as an intersection chord, …) — no reliance on the utterance. `quadClassPresent` now also returns the per-quad `vertexSets` so each matcher can test its own quads. One diagonal already counts (a student mid-construction).

**Consequences / tests.** `מקבילית ABCD` alone → {43,46,48,50} all background (ADR-211 unchanged); `+ segment AC + segment BD` → **#46 headline**, {43,48,50} background. A rhombus with diagonals promotes {46,55,56}; a rectangle promotes {46,52}; a square promotes {46,52,55,56}. `matchers.test.ts` +5 ADR-212 cases (salience-axis assertions: background without diagonals, headline with, single-diagonal, rhombus/rectangle hierarchy). **2090 tests green, build clean.** **Principle:** relevance ≠ premise-satisfied. Two theorems can both hold, yet the figure's *current objects* make one more useful now — the salience override is the general lever for "what's on the canvas raises what's worth saying", and the diagonal boost is its first use.

## ADR-213 — the relevant quad property theorems are MAIN (headline), not additional; diagonal weight rides attribution (amends ADR-211, ADR-212)

**Context.** Operator (2026-07-04, Turn-4, continuing ADR-211/212): *"For quads, the theorems that are relevant should appear as the main theorems and not as additional theorems, like they are today."* After ADR-211 the special-quad property bundle folded into the `quad` **background** family (the collapsed "N משפטי רקע" row), and ADR-212 promoted only the *diagonal* property to `headline` when the diagonals were drawn. The operator wants the properties of a drawn quad treated as the **main** relevant theorems, not tucked into the background fold.

**Decision.** The special-quadrilateral property theorems are now **static `salience: 'headline'`** — a drawn quad surfaces its defining properties (opposite sides/angles, diagonals, consecutive-angle sum; the rectangle/rhombus/iso-trapezoid diagonal properties by class) as main entries. This **reverses ADR-211's background-fold choice** for this family; the type-doc line naming "the parallelogram property bundle" as the canonical background fold no longer holds (kept as an example of the *mechanism*, not this family).

**Diagonal weight moves from salience to attribution (reworks ADR-212).** With every quad property already `headline`, the ADR-212 salience-flip had nothing left to flip. Instead, when the student **draws the diagonals**, a diagonal-property theorem (#46/#52/#55/#56/#41) now folds the diagonal-drawing **facts + segment objects** into its `triggerFactIds`/`triggerObjectIds`. Consequences, all from the existing ordering (no new axis): it attributes to the diagonal-drawing step, so among the quad headlines it **leads by recency**, **marks ● new** the moment the diagonals land, and **highlights the drawn diagonals** when clicked — the non-diagonal properties stay main, just below it. `quadHasDiagonal` (boolean, `neighbors`-based) is replaced by `quadDiagonals(ctx, vertices)` returning the drawing facts + `segment` object ids (a diagonal = a `segment` joining a non-adjacent pair of the cyclic vertex order).

**Reverted plumbing.** The ADR-212 context-dependent salience override (`TheoremMatch.salience?`, `detectTheorems`'s `m.salience ?? def.salience`) is **removed** — salience is static again (one source: `TheoremDef.salience`); relevance-under-what's-drawn is now expressed through attribution/recency, the axis that already existed. Cleaner: no dead field.

**Consequences / tests.** `מקבילית ABCD` → {43,46,48,50} all **headline** (main); rhombus adds {55,56} headline, rectangle adds {52}, square all seven — headline. Drawing `segment AC`+`segment BD` makes #46 (and the rhombus/rectangle diagonal properties) **● new** and rank ahead of {43,48,50}. `matchers.test.ts` ADR-212 block rewritten to assert the headline salience + attribution/ordering (isNew on the diagonal step, diagonal-theorem-before-plain ordering) instead of the old salience-flip. **2096 tests green, build clean.** **Principle:** "relevant" = MAIN. What the student drew (the quad, then its diagonals) sets which theorems are worth surfacing prominently and in what order — order via recency, not a second salience tier.

## ADR-214 — a dropped height is a right-angle premise; distance-between-parallels (#3); and a guiding-principle "concept" feed alongside theorems

**Context.** Operator (2026-07-04, Turn-5, session `tzqfaub6`): `מקבילית ABCD` → `DB` → `AC` → `DE גובה על AB` (a height from D onto AB in a parallelogram with its diagonals drawn). *"i added a height from D but no new theorem was selected. while in general it can be that an input doesn't lead to a change in theorem list, this is something to question."* The height built a geometrically-correct figure (E is the foot of the ⟂ from D to AB, ∠DEA = 90°) but the live theorem feed stayed unchanged.

**Root cause.** The feed had no premise that a `foot` satisfies. `foot` is what `גובה`/altitude lowers to (`{type:'foot',id:E,from:D,a:A,b:B}`), and its perpendicularity is *structural* (no `set-perpendicular` fact emitted). But `rightAngleFacts` — the premise for Pythagoras (#28) — recognised only `right-triangle` / a stated 90° / an explicit `set-perpendicular`, never a `foot`. So dropping a height announced nothing. Symptom-vs-root: the correct fix is not "special-case a height in a parallelogram" but "a dropped perpendicular IS a right angle, everywhere" (a whole class — heights in triangles/trapezoids, tangency feet).

**Decision (three parts, operator-directed).**
1. **`rightAngleFacts` counts a `foot`.** A dropped perpendicular creates a genuine right angle at its foot (and a right triangle with the apex), the same footing as an explicit ⟂ which already triggered #28 unconditionally. So a height anywhere now surfaces Pythagoras.
2. **#28 Pythagoras promoted `background` → `headline`** (operator: height's theorem should be MAIN, not folded into the background family).
3. **Theorem #3 added** — "The distance between two parallel lines is constant …" (byte-exact 07 statement, integrity-checked). `salience: 'headline'`, `family: 'parallels'`. Fires when a `foot`'s base edge equals one edge of a STATED parallel pair and its apex `from` sits on the opposite parallel edge — i.e. a perpendicular dropped *between* two parallels (a trapezoid base, a parallelogram side, parallel chords). Coordinate-free: a new `parallelPairs(ctx)` helper enumerates the stated parallel edge-pairs symbolically (`set-parallel` → its two edges; a trapezoid → its one base-pair; a parallelogram/rectangle/rhombus/square → both opposite-side pairs), since the engine's `parallelEdgePairs` needs coordinates.
4. **A guiding-principle "concept" feed** (`src/theorems/concepts.ts`), a SIBLING of the theorem feed. A *concept* is a problem-solving heuristic the configuration invites, NOT a bagrut theorem to cite — so concepts live outside `THEOREM_TABLE`, carry a string-slug id (no bagrut number), and are **not** sourced from [07](docs/07-theorem-reference.md) (the integrity byte-check governs theorems only). First concept `right-triangle-complementary`: "name one acute angle α and the other is 90°−α", firing off the same `rightAngleFacts` premise as #28. Shared machinery: `detectConcepts` reuses `buildMatchCtx` and a newly-extracted `makeAttributor(ctx)` (the latest-fact attribution + ●-new logic, factored out of `detectTheorems` so both feeds attribute identically). The App renders concepts in their own labelled 💡 section (`concepts.title`, He/En) under the same Display-options toggle, warm-neutral rows, informational (no click-to-highlight).

**Consequences / tests.** `מקבילית ABCD` → `DE גובה על AB` now surfaces #28 (headline, ● new on the height step) and #3 (headline, ● new), plus the α/90−α concept; a height in a triangle surfaces #28 but not #3 (no parallels); a bare parallelogram surfaces neither #3 (no dropped perpendicular) nor the concept. `matchers.test.ts` gains a Turn-5 block (feed behaviour + `detectConcepts`); the operator's exact sequence is locked as scenario `height-in-parallelogram-builds-and-surfaces-theorems`. **Principle:** a `foot` is a first-class right angle wherever it appears — and the learning feed has two lanes now, theorems (cite this) and concepts (set it up this way).

## ADR-215 — a 30-60-90 triangle is its own detected shape type, and #33/#34 surface whenever one is detected

**Context.** Operator (2026-07-04, session `x73i1cpx`): `מקבילית ABCD` → `DE גובה לצעל BC` (a height from D onto BC, foot E) → `DC=2CE`. Triangle CDE is right-angled at E with hypotenuse DC = 2·CE, so ∠DCE = 60°, ∠CDE = 30° — a **30-60-90** triangle the size given forces. Two reported gaps: (1) the special 30-60-90 **theorems** (#33 "in a right triangle with a 30° acute angle the opposite leg = ½ hypotenuse", #34 its converse) weren't surfaced; (2) the shape badge said only "CDE is a right angle", not the special 30-60-90 **type**. The operator suspected the two might be linked ("maybe it didn't detect the triangle, so we didn't show the theorem").

**Root cause.** *Two independent causes sharing the shapes layer* — not one causing the other. (a) `detectShapes.classifyTriangle` composed only an *equal-sides* axis (equilateral/isosceles) and a *right-angle* axis; it had **no angle-magnitude axis**, so a 30-60-90 collapsed to the generic `right-triangle`. (b) Theorems #33/#34 exist in [07](docs/07-theorem-reference.md) but were **never in `THEOREM_TABLE`**, so nothing could fire. The shapes layer WAS populated (the operator had "detect shapes" on — that's how they saw the right-angle badge), so the theorem matcher could have consumed it had #33/#34 existed.

**Decision (operator chose "always surface when detected").** The reveal question — in this figure the 30° is *derived* from `DC=2CE`, not stated, so surfacing #34 tells the student a conclusion from their own given — was put to the operator; they chose to surface the special-triangle theorems whenever the type is detected, treating "name the special triangle + its half-hypotenuse relation" as a study aid rather than a hidden proof step. Two parts:
1. **A `30-60-90-triangle` shape sub-type** in `detectShapes` — a right triangle with a 30° interior angle in every sample (⇒ the third is 60°; never isosceles, so it slots between `right-isosceles-triangle` and plain `right-triangle` in `TYPE_ORDER`). It has coordinates (the sampler), so it measures the angle directly; emergence is legitimate (a size given forces exactly 30°, exact to machine ε per the validation campaign). i18n name/def (He/En) + a book-slug (→ the right-triangle page) are added; `SHAPE_BOOK_SLUG` being `Record<ShapeType,…>` forces the entry at compile time.
2. **Theorems #33 (P) + #34 (C)** added to `THEOREM_TABLE`, `salience: 'headline'`, `family: 'triangle'`, byte-exact 07 statements (integrity-checked). Both fire on the SAME premise — a detected `30-60-90-triangle` (a new `special306090(ctx)` helper reads `ctx.shapes`) — so the student sees the two-way relation (30° ⟺ ½-hypotenuse leg) together. Attribution reuses the store's canonical `commandPointIds` to anchor the trigger to the latest fact touching the triangle's vertices, so #33/#34 mark ● new on the given that completes the 30-60-90 (here `DC=2CE`).

**Consequences / tests.** With "detect shapes" on, the operator's build now shows a `30-60-90 triangle CDE` badge and #33/#34 ● new on the `DC=2CE` step. A plain right triangle or a 45-45-90 right-isosceles is NOT classified 30-60-90 and surfaces neither #33 nor #34; before `DC=2CE` (parallelogram + height only) the angle isn't forced, so neither theorem fires (only #28/#3 from the height). Consistent with the emergent-quad-property theorems, the 30-60-90 theorems consume the shapes layer, so they require "detect shapes" to be on (coordinates are what distinguish 30-60-90 from a generic right triangle — keeping the theorem feed itself coordinate-free). Locked by scenario `thirty-sixty-ninety-triangle-detected-and-surfaces-33-34`, a `matchers.test.ts` block (feed behaviour), and a `detectShapes.test.ts` classification test. **Principle:** the right-angle axis carries a magnitude sub-type; a named special triangle justifies its own theorems (the operator's "study aid, not a reveal" call, extending ADR-214's shape-justifies-property stance to the triangle side).

## ADR-216 — one general `shapeClassPresent` gate for shape→theorem surfacing (triangles and quads), superseding the bespoke 30-60-90 matcher

**Context.** Operator, immediately after ADR-215: *"are these principles applied to all cases? we need architectural solutions and not case by case."* An audit of the two altitudes: **shape *classification*** (`detectShapes.classifyTriangle`/`classifyQuad`) is architectural — orthogonal forced-property axes (equal-sides, right-angle, parallel, and ADR-215's angle-magnitude) compose into a most-specific type, and 30-60-90 slotted in as one more axis test (the axis has one non-isosceles member because the bagrut names exactly one such triangle; 45-45-90 is already `right-isosceles`). But **shape→*theorem* gating** (`table.ts`) had **two parallel mechanisms**: the quad-property families (#43/46/48/50/52/55/56/39/41) rode a general, data-driven `quadClassPresent(ctx, kinds)` (add a theorem = a table row with a `kinds` set), while ADR-215's #33/#34 rode a **bespoke `special306090(ctx)`** hardcoding `'30-60-90-triangle'`. So the next special triangle/quad theorem ("equilateral → all angles 60°", "isosceles → base angles equal") would each need new code — the case-by-case smell the operator named.

**Decision.** Collapse the two into a **single general `shapeClassPresent(ctx, kinds)`** — the one shape→theorem gate for triangles and quads alike. A named class is PRESENT when a matching shape is STATED (a shape command whose declared class is in `kinds`, via a data `SHAPE_CMD_TYPE` map) OR DETECTED (`ctx.shapes` — constructed or emergent). #33/#34 become ordinary table rows keyed to `THIRTY_SIXTY_NINETY_KIND`, identical in form to every quad-property row; `special306090` and the quad-only `QUAD_CMD` are deleted. **Attribution rule (operator chose "vertex-touching anchor for all" for emergent shapes) refined to the non-regressing general form: anchor to the shape's DEFINING fact** — the stated command when the class was declared (so a plain property leads by the declaration and a diagonal-property theorem still folds in the later diagonal-drawing fact to lead by recency, ADR-212 preserved), else — for an emergent-only class (a 30-60-90 forced by `DC=2CE`, an emergent parallelogram) — the latest fact touching its vertices (so ● new lands on the forcing given rather than "always new"). The literal "vertex-touching for ALL, stated included" was implemented first and **regressed the ADR-212 diagonal lead** (drawing a side marked the properties ● new; the diagonal theorems no longer led, since every property re-anchored to the diagonal fact equally) — the 3 failing matcher tests were correct, so the rule was refined to defining-fact attribution, which satisfies both directives at once.

**Consequences / tests.** No behaviour change for quads (same surfacing set, same declaration/diagonal attribution — the quad `matchers.test.ts` blocks stay green untouched); the 30-60-90 emergent case keeps ● new on `DC=2CE`; and the mechanism is now uniform — a future special-shape property theorem is a table row keyed to a `kinds` set, never a new matcher. Full suite **2130 green**, `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean. **Principle:** when a fix adds a second mechanism that does the same job as an existing general one, unify them — and when the operator asks "is this architectural?", the honest answer names which altitude was already general (classification) and which was the case-by-case seam (theorem gating), then closes it.

## ADR-217 — Appendix (practice-only / removed-curriculum) theorems are tabled as SUPPORTING-ONLY; the structural invariant is type-`O` ⇒ `salience: 'background'`

**Context.** Operator directive: *"i want to keep A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B3 — they should never appear in the main theorems, only as supporting."* These six are Appendix theorems in [07](docs/07-theorem-reference.md): Appendix A (**A2** intersecting chords, **A3** two secants from an external point, **A4** secant-and-tangent from an external point, **A5**/**A6** the right-triangle geometric-mean/altitude-to-hypotenuse pair) — taught only as practice, **may not be cited** in the exam — and Appendix B (**B3** the line of centers of two intersecting circles ⟂-bisects their common chord) — removed from the curriculum. All carry type `O`. Until now the Phase-6a `THEOREM_TABLE` (ADR-208) accepted only types `P`/`C`, so type-`O` was *structurally barred* — the appendix power-of-a-point / geometric-mean configurations never surfaced at all, even as help.

**Decision.** Allow `type: 'O'` in the table, but encode "supporting-only, never main" as a **structural invariant rather than a per-entry convention: every `O` def MUST carry `salience: 'background'`** (so it always folds into its family's collapsed background row and can never be a headline; tier is `possible`/amber — a secondary aid). The [integrity guard](src/theorems/__tests__/integrity.test.ts) enforces it (`O ⇒ background`, asserted per def), replacing its former blanket "no `O` entry is tabled" assertion — 07 stays the byte-exact source (the guard's row parser widened to read the Appendix `A2…B3` labels alongside the numeric ids). The theorem `id` type widened to **`TheoremId = number | string`** ([types.ts](src/theorems/types.ts)): the appendix rows are keyed by their **07 label strings** (`'A2'`…`'A6'`, `'B3'`) so they never collide with the numbered 1–109 / 200-band space and read as "not a citable bagrut number" wherever they appear; `detect.ts`'s id-sort tiebreak gained an `idRank` (numbers ascending, before the alphabetic strings), and the App's `theoremSel` state + keys carry `TheoremId` (the id is an opaque key / equality check — never shown numerically or arithmetic'd, so string ids render cleanly and fold into their family row like any background entry).

**Six coordinate-free matchers** (the "help, don't reveal" spine is unchanged — these are configurations the student STATED, not derived conclusions): **A2** — a `line-line-intersection` (undirected 4-point crossing, `dir1`/`dir2` unset) whose four endpoints all lie on one circle (two chords crossing); **A3** — an external "hub" (`point-on-segment` on the *extension* of a chord whose two carrier ends are both on one circle — the parser's `secantFromExternal` shape) joined by drawn segments to ≥2 distinct on-circle **secant near-points**, *excluding tangency points* (so a secant+tangent config doesn't read as two secants); **A4** — the same external hub also adjacent to a **tangency point** of the same circle (secant + tangent); **A5**/**A6** — a `foot` dropped from a stated right-angle vertex (a `right-triangle`'s apex, or a stated 90° angle's vertex) to the hypotenuse — the geometric-mean/altitude configuration (both key on the same premise); **B3** — a `circle-circle-intersection` between two **visible** circles (or two visible circles sharing ≥2 members). *Two precision fixes discovered by probing the real parse→replay pipeline:* the A3 near-point set subtracts the circle's tangency points (else A4's secant+tangent tripped A3); and B3 gates on **non-hidden** circles (the Thales external-tangent construction emits a `circle-circle-intersection` against a *hidden auxiliary* circle — an unconditional match would fire B3 on every drawn tangent).

**Judgment calls (noted honestly).** A2 legitimately surfaces (as background) on Q6's intersecting-chords figure and A4 on Q7 — the operator's "keep as supporting" directive accepts this: they are the power-of-a-point family the configuration genuinely invites, folded and amber, never a headline. A5/A6's trigger is scoped to a *stated* right angle plus a dropped foot (not re-derived from coordinates), consistent with the coordinate-free match contract.

**Consequences / tests.** `integrity.test.ts` now asserts the `O ⇒ background` invariant per def + a subset check that A2–A6/B3 are all tabled as background; 8 new `matchers.test.ts` cases drive each appendix theorem through the full real pipeline (He + En where relevant), asserting it surfaces as `background` salience and that the A3/A4 configs stay separated and B3 doesn't trip on a tangent's aux circle. Full suite **2169 green**, `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean. **Principle:** a "never in the main list" constraint is best encoded as a structural invariant on the data model (type ⇒ salience), checked by the catalog guard — not as a discipline authors must remember per row.

## ADR-218 — a theorem's premise can be ENTAILED by the construction's circle structure, not only by a typed shape/relation (the "Entailed" discovery level)

**Context.** Operator, testing the classic **kite of two intersecting circles** (`שני מעגלים נחתכים` → `AB` → `OP` → `PA` → `PB` → `OA=OB`; debug log 2026-07-04): *"i have an isosceles triangle but no relevant theorems appear … added OA=OB and got 1 sentence but there are others … i also didnt get any kite theorems."* Diagnosis from the log (not the reported symptom): the "isosceles triangle" is **OAB/PAB** — emergent from two circles' radii, never typed — and the figure is a textbook **kite OAPB**. The feed showed only #22 (off the explicit `OA=OB` `set-equal`) plus background 97/98/B3. Two root causes: (1) the shape-evidence matchers (`isoscelesEvidence`, and there was no `kiteEvidence`) read only **typed** shape/equal facts, never the circle **structure** the construction already encodes (`ctx.circles`) — so |OA|=|OB| (both radii of circle O) and the kite (two circles sharing A,B) were invisible though *symbolically certain*; (2) the kite theorems **37/38 were not in the table at all** (a pure corpus-coverage gap — the table grew circle-heavy over Q1–Q7). The operator framed the fix: *"fix it broadly. we are chasing case by case here."*

**Decision.** Recognise a premise that is **entailed by the construction graph + symbolic hints**, coordinate-free, as first-class evidence — the same standing as a typed declaration (both are certain; neither samples coordinates). Concretely:
- `isoscelesEvidence` gains a third source (declared · detected · **entailed**): for each circle, its centre C and any two members X,Y **drawn as a triangle** (all three sides in `ctx.neighbors`) ⇒ isosceles apex C, since |CX| = |CY| = r *by the definition of a circle*. No equality need be typed.
- A new `kiteEvidence`: declared (`shape-variant 'kite'`) **or** entailed — two circles sharing two points X,Y, centres c1,c2, with the four kite **sides drawn** ⇒ kite c1–X–c2–Y (two disjoint pairs of equal adjacent sides, the kite definition; axis = the line of centres).
