- Theorems **37, 38** added to `THEOREM_TABLE` (family `kite`, type P, headline, byte-exact from 07).
- Two shared helpers: `drawnEdge` (is x–y in the neighbour graph) and `factsAmong` (the facts whose points all lie within a vertex set — for attribution/highlight of a shape *no single command names*).

**The DRAWN gate is what keeps it honest.** Entailment surfaces a theorem only when the sub-figure is **actually on the canvas** (its sides are drawn segments). A bare circle with many members does not flood #22; two circles whose kite sides aren't drawn don't surface #37/38. So this is not coordinate-coincidence detection (that stays out of Phase 6a) — it is reading a *structural certainty* the student built, gated on their having drawn it.

**This is the middle of a three-level discovery model** (the operator's "different levels of discovery" — recorded here as the frame for the next phase, only the middle level is built by this ADR): **L1 Declared** — you named the shape or stated the defining relation (current feed); **L2 Entailed** — the tool derives it coordinate-free from the construction graph + circle/neighbour/tangent hints (this ADR: radii-isosceles, two-circle kite — certain, safe, no sampling); **L3 Observed** — the tool detects it only from the *evaluated coordinates* via the sampled `detectShapes`/`detectRelations` layers (an emergent bisector, similar triangles, a concurrency) — tiered `possible`, opt-in, because it approaches "noticing for the student." The clean line: **L2 = certain structural entailment; L3 = numeric observation.** A fourth step (solution-path / "which theorem is key") stays a **non-goal** per the pedagogy charter (§3 surface-don't-solve, §7).

**Consequences / tests.** New matcher tests: entailed isosceles from radii (no equality typed) surfaces #22; a bare circle does *not* (#22 no-flood); a declared kite and a two-circle kite both surface #37/38; two circles without the kite drawn do *not*. The operator's exact sequence is locked as end-to-end scenario `two-circles-kite-surfaces-kite-and-isosceles-theorems` (asserts the kite geometry + #22/#37/#38 in the feed). Corpus `mustNotSurface` still holds. Full suite **2179 green**, `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean. **Principle:** "help, don't reveal" is a line between *derived conclusions* and *given/entailed premises* — not between *typed* and *inferred*. A construction certainty (two radii are equal) is a legitimate given even when no command spelled it out; the guardrail against revealing is the DRAWN gate + the L2/L3 (structural-vs-numeric) split, not "only surface what was typed."

## ADR-219 — levels of discovery: an on-screen dial that grades how the tool KNEW each surfaced theorem (Declared / Entailed / Observed)

**Context.** ADR-218 gave the feed a *second* way to know a premise (circle-structure entailment, e.g. two radii ⇒ isosceles) beside a typed declaration, and named a *third* (emergent, coordinate-observed). The operator then set the direction (2026-07-04): *"give the tool (user) different levels of discovery. at first level we only give theorems based on input; in a larger phase we leverage the tool's discovery to identify cases in the diagram where we see a bisector / similarity etc."* and sharpened it: *"for L3 — all kinds of things on the theorem list that will not be given in an exercise but emerge from the diagram as it's built. where would we set the level of discovery? on screen for the user to choose?"* So the three ways-of-knowing become a **student-facing control**, not an internal detail.

**Decision.** A three-level, **nested** discovery dial, chosen on screen (Display options), defaulting to the most conservative worksheet mode:
- **L1 Declared** — the premise is instantiated by a *stated fact* the student entered (a `set-equal`, a shape command, `set-angle`, a declared circle's membership). "Help from what you said."
- **L2 Entailed** — a *coordinate-free structural derivation* the student never typed (ADR-218): two radii ⇒ isosceles, two intersecting circles with the sides drawn ⇒ a kite. Certain; no coordinates.
- **L3 Observed** — only the *evaluated coordinates* reveal it: a purely-emergent detected shape / relation (an emergent special quad, the forced 30-60-90 pair). Opt-in; selecting it auto-enables the coordinate `detectShapes` layer the observed matchers read.

The levels are **nested**: the dial "show level N" surfaces every entry with `level ≤ N`. A matcher with several evidence paths reports the **strongest (lowest) level** that fired (isosceles: typed `AB=AC` → L1; radii-entailed → L2; sampled-only → L3).

**Where the level is computed.** In the **evidence helpers** (`isoscelesEvidence`, `kiteEvidence`, `shapeClassPresent`, `circumTriangle`, `triangleFacts`, `triangleVertexSets`) — the single place that already knows *which kind* of evidence fired — each returns a `level`, and its call site passes it into `match(..., level)`. The `match` helper defaults `level = 1`, so the ~100 declaration-only matchers are untouched. `detectTheorems` stays **level-complete** (it emits every match with its tag); the **App filters** (`visibleTheorems = feed.filter(e => e.level <= discoveryLevel)`). This keeps all existing tests valid (they read the complete feed) and puts the dial purely at the presentation layer.

**Control + default.** Operator choices (via AskUserQuestion): control model = a **cumulative selector** (one escalating 3-button segment in Display options, each level includes those below), default = **L1 Given-only** (the most conservative — a worksheet shows only what the student wrote). The dial is gated on the theorems toggle; picking L3 fires the same busy-painted `detectShapes()` the "detect shapes" button uses, and an effect keeps that layer live as the figure grows (a new fact clears the `facts`-keyed cache → re-detect).

**Consequence — the emergent→L3 reclassification.** Emergent special-quad properties (ADR-211/212) and the forced 30-60-90 pair (ADR-215, formerly "always surface when detected") now carry L3 → **hidden at the L1 default**; DECLARED shapes stay L1. Nothing is lost — the dial reveals them — and the default worksheet view is quieter (only typed givens announce theorems). The kite figure that motivated ADR-218 reads correctly under the dial: its #22 off the typed `OA=OB` is L1, while the radii-isosceles and kite 37/38 are L2 (revealed at level 2), and any purely-coordinate coincidence is L3.

**Tests / gate.** New `matchers.test.ts` block *discovery level (ADR-219)*: declared isosceles → L1, radii-entailed → L2, declared kite → L1, two-circle kite → L2, emergent 30-60-90 (33/34) → L3, a declared triangle's background facts (10–14) → L1, and the dial contract (the L1 filter hides the entailed isosceles but keeps the declared one; L2 reveals it). `DiscoveryLevel` added to `types.ts` (`TheoremMatch.level`, `TheoremFeedEntry.level`) + i18n `theorems.discovery.*` (He/En). Full suite **2192 green**, `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean. **Principle:** the "help, don't reveal" line (ADR-208/218) is preserved *inside each level* — L1/L2 still never surface a derived conclusion; the dial only lets the student opt into having the tool *notice* structural/observed premises for them, which is a discovery aid, not a solution.

## ADR-220 — Phase B: alternate/corresponding parallels recognised STRUCTURALLY (any drawn-edge triangle), and AA-similarity admitted as an ENTAILED (L2) help when a parallel cuts a triangle side

**Context.** Testing the discovery dial (ADR-219), the operator built a figure the worksheet-level feed under-served: `מקבילית ABCD` → `E על DC` (E on the base) → `המשך BE ו AD נפגשים בנקודה F` (BE and AD produced to meet at F). They expected two things the diagram plainly shows: (a) the alternate/corresponding-angle theorems (זויות מתחלפות וזויות מתאימות, **#4/#6**), since the parallelogram's parallel sides are cut by the transversals FB/FA; and (b) at a deeper level, **similar triangles** — △FAB with the parallel line through E cutting it is the classic Thales/AA config. Neither surfaced: #4/#6 were gated behind a KIND-whitelist "transversal" test (`hasTransversal`) that recognised only a *typed* triangle or an explicit `line` object — not the triangle FAB that exists purely as drawn edges (FA, FB + the parallelogram edge AB); and #69/#71 were **structurally excluded** from the table entirely by the ADR-208 "help, don't reveal" rule (their premise — that two triangles are *similar* — is a derived conclusion, i.e. the proof task). Operator forks (via AskUserQuestion): #4/#6 discovery level = **L1 Declared** (so it must be coordinate-free structural recognition, not the L3 `detectShapes` layer); similarity = **"L2 entailed + L3 observed"**, plus an explicit ask to add a *concept* — "אם יש ישרים מקבילים, חפשו משולשים דומים".

**Decision.**
1. **Transversal recognition becomes geometric, not a kind-whitelist** (the recurring ADR-167 fix). `hasTransversal` is replaced by `structuralTriangles(ctx)` — every 3-cycle in the coordinate-free neighbour graph (`pointNeighbors`: drawn segments + polygon edges) — wrapped by `transversalEvidence`, which reports **present + Declared (L1)** when a *typed* triangle, an explicit `line` object, OR any drawn-edge 3-cycle exists, and **Observed (L3)** when only a coordinate-`detectShapes` triangle supplies the cut. The operator's FAB is a 3-cycle ⇒ 4/6 surface at L1; a **bare** trapezoid/parallelogram is only a 4-cycle ⇒ 4/6 stay off (ADR-210 preserved), while co-interior #8 still fires on the parallels alone.
2. **#69 (AA) + #71 (the ratio consequences) are admitted to the table as ENTAILED (L2)**, relaxing ADR-208 *only* for the one configuration that *announces* the similarity coordinate-free: `similarityEvidence(ctx)` fires when a **stated** parallel pair (`parallelPairs`) has one edge that is a *side* of a triangle (typed or a 3-cycle) whose apex lies off the *other* parallel — a line parallel to one side, which structurally forces the cut-off triangle similar to the whole (AA). Never typed "similar" ⇒ L2, not a reveal. The sharper SAS/SSS *criteria* (#68/#70) and bisector-ratio (#76) stay excluded (their premise is genuinely the proof). Because the matcher is gated on a **stated parallel**, the Q5–Q7 corpus (no parallels) never trips 69/71 — `corpus.test.ts` neverSurface assertions pass unchanged.
3. **A guiding concept** (`concepts.ts`, the ADR-214 sibling feed) — `parallels-seek-similar-triangles`: "If the figure has parallel lines, look for similar triangles / אם יש ישרים מקבילים, חפשו משולשים דומים." — rides `parallelFacts`, surfacing wherever any parallel is stated. A heuristic setup move, not a bagrut theorem, so it lives outside the numbered table.

**Deferred (flagged to operator).** *General* L3-**observed** similarity for **non-parallel** configs (e.g. Q6's shared-inscribed-angle pair) needs actual coordinates/relations plumbed into the theorem spine, which is deliberately **coordinate-free** (`detectRelations` produces equal-segment/angle classes but not similar-triangle pairs, and isn't wired into `detectTheorems`). That is a larger architectural change; only the parallel-cut (coordinate-free entailed) path ships here.

**Tests / gate.** `integrity.test.ts` forbidden list `[68,69,70,71,76]` → `[68,70,76]` (and asserts 69/71 ARE tabled; the byte-equality loop auto-verifies their statements against [07](07-theorem-reference.md)). New `matchers.test.ts` block *similarity from a parallel-cut triangle + discovery levels*: the operator figure surfaces 4/6 at L1 and 69/71 at L2 and raises the concept; a bare trapezoid and a bare parallelogram surface neither 4/6 nor 69/71 (parallelogram keeps #8); a lone triangle (no parallel) keeps 69/71 silent. End-to-end scenario `parallelogram-cut-triangle-surfaces-parallels-and-similarity` locks the exact sequence (F collinear with B,E and A,D; feed ⊇ {4,6,69,71}). Full suite **2209 green**, `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean. **Principle:** "help, don't reveal" is preserved by *what* is admitted, not by a blanket ban — a similarity the construction *entails* coordinate-free is help (name the config the student can then exploit); the derived *criteria* that constitute the proof stay out.

## ADR-221 — a GENERIC triangle earns no shape badge (declutter the "detect shapes" panel)

**Context.** Operator report (2026-07-04, latest manual test): "the trapezoid and several triangles were not detected in the shapes. In general when detecting shapes, if there is nothing special about a triangle we don't need to show it (otherwise there are too many)." Investigation of the logged sessions: **trapezoid detection was never broken** — a declared `טרפז ABCD` (or an inscribed cyclic trapezoid) surfaces its `trapezoid`/`isosceles-trapezoid` badge in every logged figure, base- and store-path alike. The actionable half is the triangle flood. `detectShapes` had an inconsistency: an **emergent** generic triangle (a 3-cycle over the implicit-edge graph with no forced special property) was already dropped (`if (t !== 'triangle') add(…)`), but a **declared** generic triangle (a 3-vertex `polygon`) was *always* badged, on the old rationale "the general triangle has fundamental theorems" (former `detectShapes.test.ts` line 169). A real figure sprouts many incidental triangles — every diagonal, cevian, midsegment, and crossing makes one — so badging each plain triangle floods the panel and buries the shapes that carry a *specific* theorem (the kite, the 30-60-90, the trapezoid).

**Decision.** A generic triangle (classifies to `'triangle'` — no forced equal side, right angle, or special magnitude) earns **no badge**, whether it was declared or is emergent. The declared branch now mirrors the emergent one: `const t = classifyTriangle(…); if (t !== 'triangle') add(t, …)`. Only a forced special type still badges: `isosceles` / `equilateral` / `right` / `right-isosceles` / `30-60-90`.

**Why nothing is lost for theorems.** The Phase-6 theorem feed does **not** depend on a generic-triangle *shape* to see a triangle. `table.ts`'s `triangleVertexSets` reads typed `triangle`/`right-triangle`/3-vertex-`polygon` commands **directly from `ctx.facts`** (as Declared/L1), and `transversalEvidence` recognises a triangle structurally from drawn-edge 3-cycles (`structuralTriangles`, ADR-220) — both independent of the badge list. The badge's only unique contribution to `ctx.shapes` was a redundant `stated:false` copy of a declared triangle (already covered by the fact path) — and generic *emergent* triangles were never in `ctx.shapes` to begin with. So the triangle-family theorems still surface; only the visual badge is dropped.

**Tests / gate.** `detectShapes.test.ts` "a free (scalene) triangle gets NO badge" flips from asserting the generic badge is present to asserting it is absent (alongside the existing not-isosceles/right/equilateral checks). End-to-end scenario `generic-triangle-gets-no-badge` (`טרפז ABCD` + `משולש ABD`): the trapezoid badges, the plain declared triangle does not. Full theorem + scenario suites (497) green; `detectShapes` suite (20) green. **Principle:** a shape badge is a pointer to a *specific* named concept with its own book page — a generic triangle has none worth the panel space, so it is surfaced only through the (fact-driven) theorem feed, never as a badge.

**Follow-up (same report, the REAL miss) — a polygon whose SIDE has a point on it (`collinearMerges`).** The operator's screenshot corrected the diagnosis: they were not asking for the generic triangle ADE, they said *"there is also a trapezoid ABCE"* — a parallelogram `ABCD` with `CD` extended to `E` (`CD=DE`) and `EA` drawn. Since `AB ∥ CD` and `E` is on line `CD`, `AB ∥ CE`, so `ABCE` is a genuine trapezoid — and it was genuinely **undetected**. Root cause: the emergent-cycle edge graph (`figureEdges`) held only **atomic** edges, and the trapezoid's side `C–E` is broken by `D` (`C–D` is a parallelogram edge, `D–E` a segment), so `C` and `E` were never adjacent and the 4-cycle `A-B-C-E` could not be enumerated. This is the exact **dual** of ADR-167's `collinearSplits` (which *splits* a carrier at an interior point so sub-segments become edges) — there was no pass that *merges* a collinear chain into a through-edge. Fix: a new `collinearMerges(c, samples)` adds the through-edge `C–E` whenever a point `D` is **strictly between** `C` and `E` and the three are **collinear in every sample** (a forced contiguous straight span), run to a **fixpoint** so a chain with several interior points (`C–D–E–F` → `C–F`) merges transitively. It is wired into `detectShapes`'s enumeration adjacency only — **scoped there, not added to the shared `figureEdges`** — because a through-edge `C–E` duplicates the existing ray `C–D` in the angle universe (`E` is on ray `CD`), which would inject redundant duplicate-ray angles into the relations layer. The generic triangle `ADE` stays unbadged (the rule above); the special trapezoid `ABCE` now surfaces. Locked by scenario `emergent-trapezoid-through-a-point-on-its-side`. **Correction to the Context above:** trapezoid detection was *not* universally fine — the *declared / on-a-carrier-free* cases detect, but an **emergent trapezoid whose side carries a point** was missed until this pass.

**Second bug this uncovered — the `hasStraightVertex` degeneracy gate was mis-calibrated.** The seed-sweep oracle (which re-runs each scenario at seeds 0..N-1) then failed the new trapezoid at **base seed 2**: `detectShapes` found `C–E` and the quad was always parallel + convex, yet in ONE of its 16 internal sampler configs the trapezoid `ABCE` was drawn *thin* — a real ~0.3° corner (`sin ≈ 5e-3`) — which fell under `hasStraightVertex`'s tolerance of `sin(0.5°) ≈ 8.7e-3`, so the corner was misread as a **collinear (phantom) vertex** and `isSimpleEverywhere` rejected the whole shape. Root cause: `hasStraightVertex` (ADR-198, added to kill phantom kites where a point sits exactly on a diagonal) reused the ambient classification `angleTol` (~0.5°), which is *far* too loose for "collinear" — a phantom vertex is collinear to **solver precision (~1e-10)**, while a legitimately narrow corner can be a few milliradians. Fix: a dedicated `STRAIGHT_SIN_TOL = 1e-4` (~0.006°) for the straight-vertex test, decoupled from `angleTol` — it still catches every phantom (collinear to ~1e-10 ≪ 1e-4) while accepting a genuine thin corner (≥ ~1e-3), and matches `collinearSplits`' own on-carrier `tolPerp = 1e-4` so the two agree on "on the line." Verified: base-seed-2 detects; the phantom-kite scenarios (`square-both-diagonals-no-phantom-kites`) and `emergent-shapes-through-crossings` still reject their exactly-collinear vertices; seed-sweep green. **Lesson: a "collinear/degenerate" tolerance must be set by solver precision, NOT reused from a shape-classification angle tolerance — the two differ by ~5 orders of magnitude, and the loose value silently makes emergent detection flaky per base seed.**

## ADR-222 — the trapezoid midsegment (median) as a parser rule, resolved from the figure's parallel bases

**Context.** Operator (2026-07-04): "do we have support for קטע אמצעים בטרפז?" (the midsegment/median of a trapezoid). We did not — deterministically. The `midsegment` rule ([ADR-199](#adr-199)) was **triangle-only**: it resolved the two sides whose midpoints to join by finding the *apex* — the vertex adjacent to **both** endpoints of the named base (`ctx.neighbors`). A trapezoid's two legs do **not** meet at a point, so there is no such apex and the utterance fell through to the LLM net (and returned not-understood). This is the exact structural sibling of the trapezoid-**altitude** gap fixed by [ADR-169](#adr-169) (the apex's neighbours are a diagonal, not an edge) — and the fix reuses the same machinery.

**The geometry differs from the triangle case.** A *triangle* midsegment joins the midpoints of two sides **meeting at a vertex** (parallel to the third side, half its length). A *trapezoid* midsegment (median) joins the midpoints of the two **non-parallel legs**, is parallel to **both** bases, and its length is the **average** of the two bases `(b₁+b₂)/2`. So it is not merely a keyword gap — it needs its own resolution of *which* two segments to bisect.

**Decision.** A new `trapezoidMidsegment(s, ctx)` branch in the `midsegment` rule, tried before the triangle paths whenever no triangle is explicitly named. Two resolution modes, both decomposing to **two `midpoint`s (one per leg) + a `segment`** — all already-supported commands, so the constraint solver keeps the median parallel to the bases and **no new engine construct is introduced** (the same "named shapes are parser macros" principle as [ADR-110](#adr-110)):
1. **Incremental (the primary app flow)** — the trapezoid was drawn in an earlier step; resolve its two bases from the figure's **unique vertex-disjoint parallel edge-pair** (`ctx.parallels`, from `parallelEdgePairs` — the very hint ADR-169 added), and each leg by pairing a base-1 endpoint with its adjacent base-2 endpoint (`ctx.neighbors`). Exactly **one** parallel pair ⇒ a trapezoid; **zero** (a triangle) or **two** (a parallelogram — which base?) ⇒ return null and defer ([ADR-052](#adr-052)), never guess.
2. **Self-contained named form** — "midsegment of trapezoid ABCD" / "קטע האמצעים בטרפז ABCD" (4 labels): by the shape convention the bases are `AB ∥ DC`, so the legs are `BC` and `DA`, derived from the vertex order (no context needed) and the trapezoid built inline if absent. This makes the form discoverable in the help catalog (whose guard parses examples standalone).

Named endpoints ("EF קטע אמצעים בטרפז") are honoured exactly as the triangle rule honours them (the ADR-149 "CD→CF" bug class); otherwise the two midpoints auto-name from `M,N,…`.

**Tests / gate.** End-to-end scenario `midsegment-in-trapezoid-joins-leg-midpoints` (`טרפז ABCD` → `קטע האמצעים בטרפז`) asserts: both leg-midpoints created, each is the midpoint of a leg, the median ∥ base AB, and |median| = (|AB|+|DC|)/2 (the median theorem) — and passes the seed-sweep oracle at every displayable config (the relations are structural). Catalog example + coverage pins (both locales) added; full parser suite (595) and scenario suite green, build clean. **Principle reaffirmed:** a named special-line is resolved from the figure's *derived* structure (parallel pairs, adjacency), not hard-coded — the same derived-hint category as `neighbors`/`circleMembers`/`parallels`.

## ADR-223 — a right triangle's vertex order is SEMANTIC (right angle at the last id), so it is never cyclically rotated; a shared-hypotenuse right triangle asserts the right angle as a constraint

**Context.** Operator session `avs58sfn` (bagrut Q8): `משולש ABC ישר זוית` → `משולש ABD ישר זוית` → `AC ו BD נחתכים בנקודה E` — two right triangles sharing hypotenuse AB, their legs meeting at E. Two symptoms: (1) the knee mark was drawn at D but **∠ADB came out 52°, not 90°**; (2) **"AC and BD cannot meet."**

**Root cause (one).** `right-triangle` was listed in `DERIVED_SLOTS` (slot `[1]`), which enrols it in `normalizeShapeComposition`'s **cyclic rotation** — the mechanism that rotates a *polygon*'s vertex tuple so an existing edge lands on free base slots ([ADR-013](#adr-013)). But a right triangle is **not** rotation-invariant: its vertex order encodes *which vertex carries the right angle* (the **last** id). For `right-triangle A,B,D` with A,B already built (triangle ABC), the rotation picked `[B,D,A]` (it put the pre-existing derived-slot vertex on a free slot) — silently **moving the right angle from D to A**. The renderer still drew the knee at the last-as-typed vertex D, so ∠BAD=90 held while the *marked* ∠ADB was an arbitrary 52°. With D placed at an arbitrary angle it landed on the opposite side of AB from C, so legs AC and BD diverged and their `onSeg` crossing fell on the backward continuation → "cannot meet." (Same shape as the [ADR-166](#adr-166) segment-meet bug, but caused upstream by the rotation, not the sampler.)

**Decision.** Right-triangle composition is handled by the construct itself, never by cyclic rotation:
1. **Removed `right-triangle` from `DERIVED_SLOTS`** — its order is semantic, so `normalizeShapeComposition` leaves it as typed (right angle stays at the last id).
2. **The apply case is adaptive.** The two non-right vertices `a,b` are interchangeable hypotenuse endpoints; whichever is **fresh** becomes the derived `perp-offset` (0-DOF, exact right angle at `c`). It **swaps** `a,b` so a fresh vertex is the perp-offset even when the as-typed derived slot pre-exists.
3. **Whole hypotenuse pre-exists ⇒ a constraint, not a rebuild.** When both `a,b` already exist (the shared-hypotenuse case), no vertex is free to be the perp-offset, so the right angle at `c` is asserted as a `perpendicular` constraint (seg c→a ⟂ seg c→b) — the ADR-099/ADR-115 "declared over existing points is a constraint" family. The carrier is forced to be the **new** vertex `c` (its `solve` is set directly), **not** a pre-existing leg's shape DOF — generic `driveOrCheck` would grab triangle ABC's `perp-offset` `dist` first and reshape the *other* triangle (a stability violation). `c` slides onto the Thales circle over the fixed hypotenuse; when `c` also pre-exists it falls back to `driveOrCheck` as a pure check.
4. **The right-angle vertex is reflectable across its hypotenuse.** `reflectAnchors` ([ADR-166](#adr-166)) recognised only equality/distance/ratio; it now also treats a right angle at a **shared vertex** (`perpendicular` with `con.a===con.c`) as symmetric across the line through the two leg endpoints — reflecting `c` there gives the OTHER valid right-angle placement (the mirror Thales arc). So the sampler can flip `c` to the side where the legs actually cross.
5. **`commandConflict`** learns that a right-triangle's derived leg vertex landing on an existing point is a reinterpretation (per §3), not a redefinition conflict.

**Tests / gate.** End-to-end scenario `two-right-triangles-share-hypotenuse` (the exact operator sequence) asserts every step lands ok, **∠ACB = ∠ADB = 90°**, C and D on the same side of AB, and E within both segments — and passes the seed-sweep oracle (the two right angles are invariants; same-side + E-within are enforced by `meetsRequirements`). Full suite 2216 green, build clean. **Principle:** a construct whose vertex order carries meaning (right-angle position) must opt out of the polygon rotation machinery, and a shape stated over pre-existing points is a constraint on the new vertex, never a silent rebuild of the old geometry.

**Amendment (the "how was a 90° knee drawn on a non-90° angle?" question).** The right-angle **square (knee)** has two independent sources: a **measured** one (`relations.ts` `definiteAngles` — only marks 90° when the coordinates measure ~90° across every sample, so it cannot lie) and an **intent** one (`geoStore.ts` `angleMarkFor` — a `right-triangle` / `∠=90` / `⟂` fact places a knee at the *declared* vertex, `right:true`, without consulting the coordinates). The Q8 rotation put the *real* 90° at A while the *command-driven* knee sat on D → a 90° mark on a 52° angle. Root cause of the mark (separate from the geometry bug): the intent path trusted the declaration. **Honesty gate added:** when building the asserted `angleMarks`, a `right` mark is kept only if its vertex **actually measures within 1° of 90°** in the output coordinates; otherwise the knee is dropped (the givens verifier already flags such a figure amber — a mark must never contradict the geometry). So even if a future figure fails to realise a declared right angle (an over-constrained/amber case), no false knee is drawn. Locked by the Q8 scenario (both real right angles keep their knees) and verified against a deliberately-unrealisable declaration (right-triangle at a square corner where ∠ACB=45° → no knee).

**Amendment 2 ("some alternative options should not be shown — they leave E off its segments").** "Show another configuration" (`resample`) and the initial display (`autoResolve`/`findValidConfig`) had DIVERGED on what a *valid* config is: the initial view gated on `meetsRequirements` (builds, verifier-clean, extensions reach, **on-segment crossings within their segments**, points distinct, polygons convex), but `resample` used a weaker cluster that omitted the on-segment check and the givens-verifier check. So the first drawing kept E on both segments, yet pressing "show another" could offer a seed where C,D fall on OPPOSITE sides of AB — leaving E off its segments, i.e. E can't be where the input instructed. Fix: `resample` now accepts a sample only when it `meetsRequirements(facts, s)` **and** is shape-different (the fingerprint gate, so the view actually changes) — unifying the "displayable config" definition across the initial view and every alternative. General across the whole on-segment/extension/verifier class, not just Q8. Locked by `src/store/__tests__/resample-validity.test.ts` (30 consecutive "show another" views on the Q8 figure all keep E on-segment).

**Amendment 3 (perf — the "identify shapes button stuck" report).** Modelling the shared-hypotenuse right angle as a DRIVEN ⟂ constraint (§3) is correct but costs ~15 ms per `evaluate` (the numeric optimizer), where the old structural perp-offset was ~0.1 ms. "Detect shapes" (and "view relations") solve the figure N× per variant to find shapes FORCED across samples, so on this coupled figure that synchronous work froze the main thread for a noticeable beat — the button (disabled while computing) read as "stuck." Not an infinite hang. Fix (operator: non-blocking): `detectShapesAcross` was split into `classifyShapesFromSamples` (pure, fast) + the sampler, and the store's `detectShapes` is now ASYNC — it samples in small BATCHES, `await`-yielding to the event loop between them, so the spinner paints and the page stays responsive, then runs the pure classification. Detection OUTPUT is byte-identical (same `convergedSamples` → `classifyShapesFromSamples`); only the scheduling changed. A `facts`-changed guard drops a stale layer if a step/undo races the sampling. (The deeper option — a closed-form Thales placement so `evaluate` is cheap again — was deferred; it risks leaking a hidden diameter circle into concyclic/theorem detection, which would reveal Q8 part א.) `shapes-slice.test.ts` updated to `await` the action.

**Open decision (issue 2 — similar triangles not surfaced).** In Q8 part ב the student must PROVE △DEG ~ △CEF, so the always-on theorem feed deliberately does NOT surface it (ADR-208 "help, don't reveal"; similarity is admitted only when a STATED parallel structurally forces it — ADR-220 — which Q8 has none of). The operator's steer (2026-07-05): "we already reveal shapes to students that might not have noticed, so revealing similar triangles is not very different" — but marked UNSURE. Recommended direction (parked for an explicit decision): surface similar/congruent triangle PAIRS in the OPT-IN "detect shapes" panel (the same student-initiated reveal boundary as shapes), NOT the always-on feed — this matches the operator's reasoning without weakening the feed's no-reveal integrity. Not built yet.

## ADR-224 — similar / congruent triangle detection, surfaced as CLASSES in the opt-in "detect shapes" panel

**Context.** Operator manual test of the full bagrut Q8 figure (two right triangles sharing hypotenuse AB; legs meet at E; F, G the midpoints of EB, EA; DG and CF drawn): "angles CFE and DEG are not detected as similar." Part ב asks the student to PROVE △DEG ~ △CEF. The always-on theorem feed deliberately does NOT surface this (ADR-208 "help, don't reveal"; AA-similarity is admitted only when a STATED parallel structurally forces it — ADR-220 — which Q8 has none of). But the OPT-IN "detect shapes" panel already reveals shapes a student might not have noticed; the operator's steer (2026-07-05): "revealing that they are similar is no different than asking a student to prove they are similar — he still has to do the work." So similarity belongs in the opt-in panel, on the same student-initiated reveal boundary as the shape badges, NOT the always-on feed (whose no-reveal rule stands).

**Decision.** `detectShapes` (the sampled, opt-in layer) now also detects **similar/congruent triangle CLASSES** and returns them in `ShapesResult.similar`:
- **Candidate pool.** Every non-degenerate triangle in the figure — declared 3-vertex polygons AND emergent triangle cycles (`triangleCycles` over the implicit edge graph) — collected regardless of whether it earns a shape badge (a GENERIC triangle earns no badge but can still be similar to another). Deduped by vertex set; capped at 64 (the emergent enumeration is already gated by `adj.size ≤ 16`).
- **Forced across samples.** Two triangles are SIMILAR iff, under some vertex correspondence, their three interior angles agree (within ~1°) in EVERY sampled configuration (AA — a structural relation, never a coincidence of one drawing, the same discipline as the shape badges). CONGRUENT iff the corresponding sides also agree. As the figure's free DOF vary, similar triangles change shape TOGETHER, so the per-sample angle match with a CONSISTENT correspondence is what certifies "structurally similar."
- **Classes, not pairs.** Similarity is transitive, so the forced-similar relation partitions the triangles into cliques (union-find). Each clique of ≥2 is ONE class, its members re-ordered to correspond to the first (so "△DEG ~ △CEF" reads off positionally; the correspondence prefers fixing shared vertices, so a shared apex like E maps to itself). This is the load-bearing flood guard: a square's two diagonals give EIGHT mutually-similar right-isosceles triangles → one row of 8 members, not 28 pairs. A class is `congruent` only when every member is congruent to the reference; otherwise `similar` (the weaker statement, true of all — e.g. the square's 4 half-square + 4 quarter triangles are all similar but not all congruent).

**UI.** A "Similar / congruent triangles" section in the detect-shapes panel, one row per class ("△DEG ~ △CEF", or "≅" when congruent). Hover/click lights the member triangles on the canvas (reusing the shape-highlight machinery — vertices + edge point-pairs). Bilingual; a hint reminds the student the PROOF is still theirs.

**Engine shape.** `detectShapesAcross` was split into a pure `classifyShapesFromSamples` (which now also runs `detectSimilarClasses`) + the sampler — the same split the ADR-223-Am.3 non-blocking work introduced, so the store's chunked async `detectShapes` gets similarity for free. `ShapesResult` gains `similar: SimilarClass[]` (additive; existing `.shapes` consumers unaffected).

**Tests / gate.** Scenario `q8-similar-triangles-detected` (the operator's exact sequence) asserts the {CEF, DEG} class surfaces. Engine unit tests lock the flood guard (square + both diagonals → one 8-member `similar` class), the congruent case (a rectangle's diagonal → congruent {ABC, ACD}), and no-false-positive (a lone scalene triangle → no class). Full suite + build green. **Principle:** the opt-in panel may REVEAL relations (shapes, now similarity) a student might miss; the always-on feed still only HELPS without revealing the "aha" — two different pedagogy boundaries, held apart.

## ADR-227 — the loose end of a "DF ⟂ AB" perpendicular is a reflectable SIDE DOF, flipped AFTER the continuous sample

**Context.** Operator session `nc207foh`: a right triangle ABC, D the midpoint of the hypotenuse AB, `DF אנך ל AB` (segment DF ⟂ AB, F a new free point), then `AC ו DF נחתכים בנקודה E` (AC and DF meet at E, parsed `line-line-intersection … onSeg:true` per ADR-166). The step built with **no error**, but E landed OFF both segments — param ≈ −4.2 along DF, 1.22 along AC. The operator: *"DF should have moved so it fits the input."*

**Diagnosis.** E is the crossing of line AC with the perpendicular-to-AB-through-D — a point **fully determined by the triangle shape alone** (F's distance along the perpendicular does not move it). Landing E within *both* segments needs two independent DOFs satisfied: the triangle must flex so |CA|>|CB| (then E is within segment AC), AND F must sit on the E-side of D beyond E (then E is within segment DF). The ADR-166 machinery for this class (`intersectionsWithinSegments` + a reflection DOF searched by `firstSatisfyingSeed`) was already present — but two gaps defeated it:
1. **F was never reflectable.** `reflectAnchors` granted a reflection axis only to a *shared-vertex* right angle (`con.a===con.c===V`, the Thales apex of ADR-223). F is the loose end of a perpendicular between two DISTINCT segments (`set-perpendicular(D,F,A,B)`), so it got no anchors and `reflectableFreePoints` excluded it — its side stayed anti-correlated with the triangle (a seed sweep found tAC within-range only when tDF was negative, and vice-versa; 0/200 satisfied both).
2. **Reflecting BEFORE the sample coupled the two DOFs.** `applySeed` spins the whole free-point cluster {A,C,F} about its centroid. F reflected first → centroid shifts → the triangle (A,C about the moved centroid, B fixed) RE-SHAPES → the very shape that put E within AC is lost when F's side flips. Reflecting F *after* the sample decouples them (probe: base seeds giving |CA|>|CB| all yield E within both segments once F is mirrored post-sample). But a *global* reflect-after swap broke the ADR-166 equidistant-apex reflection (the rhombus mirror must be seeded BEFORE the spin so the solver locks onto it).

**Decision.**
- **(1) Reflection axis for a cross-segment perpendicular's loose end.** `reflectAnchors` now returns the OTHER segment's endpoints for the second endpoint of each arm of a `perpendicular` — for `set-perpendicular(a,b,c,d)`, `b`↦{c,d} and `d`↦{a,b}. Reflecting the loose end across that line flips it to the opposite perpendicular ray (an equally-valid ⟂ placement; used as a solver SEED, `evaluate` re-enforces perpendicularity on the mirrored side). The Thales shared-vertex case is unchanged.
- **(2) Split the reflection around the sample by point KIND.** A new `directionHelperFreePoints` classifies a reflectable point as a *direction helper* iff it is tied ONLY by perpendicular/parallel constraints (no equal/distance/ratio/angle, not a shared-vertex right angle) — the loose end of a ⟂/∥ arm, which defines a line direction, not a shape vertex. `replay` splits the seed's reflection mask: **apex** bits reflect BEFORE `applySeed` (unchanged — their mirror is a genuine shape alternative the spin explores around), **direction-helper** bits reflect AFTER (so the base seed sets the shape and the reflection only flips the side, without dragging the spin centroid). `mask 0` (every ordinary figure) is untouched, and an apex-only figure has no helper bits → byte-identical to pre-ADR behaviour.

**Tests / gate.** Scenario `perpendicular-helper-flips-to-reach-crossing` (the operator's exact sequence) asserts E lands within both segment AC and segment DF. The ADR-166 apex scenarios (`segment-meet-lands-on-segments`, `emergent-shapes-through-crossings`) stay green — the split preserves their reflect-before-sample path. Full suite (2223) + build green. **Principle (this class):** an unstated "which side" of a helper line is a free DOF (ADR-052) that must be EXPLORABLE, and *when* in the sample pipeline a discrete DOF is applied matters — a shape-vertex mirror seeds the solver (before), a direction-helper mirror only re-sides an already-shaped figure (after).

## ADR-228 — size givens as one family: circle circumference/area → radius, polygon perimeter as a constraint, and `O_1` subscript normalization

**Status:** accepted (2026-07-05).

**Context.** An operator typed `מעגל O_1 שהיקפו 6π` ("circle O₁ whose circumference is 6π") and observed two failures: the centre showed as **O** (the `_1` was dropped) and the radius was **not** set to 3 (circumference was unhandled). Three gaps, sharpened by the fact that Hebrew **`היקף` is one word for BOTH a circle's circumference and a polygon's perimeter**:
- **Subscript.** A point token is `[A-Za-z]\d*` (a letter + GLUED digits, so `O1`). The LaTeX-style `O_1` has an underscore, which truncated the label to `O` (the `_1` matched nothing). Only AREA markers had underscore handling (`S_{ABC}`, ADR-121).
- **Circle circumference/area.** `parseRadius` read only `radius N` / `radius R`. There was no path from a stated circumference or area to a radius, so `שהיקפו 6π` fell through the grammar to the LLM, which drew a default-radius circle.
- **Polygon perimeter.** `היקף` on a polygon (`היקף המלבן 20`) was entirely unhandled — no constraint existed. Area (ADR-118) was polygon-only and had no circle form.

The operator chose the **unified** scope: `היקף` (circumference/perimeter) and `שטח` (area) are ONE size-measure family across every shape, so no stated magnitude is silently dropped (ADR-052).

**Decision.**
- **(A) `O_1` → `O1` at the orthography boundary.** A new `normalizePointSubscript` in `normalizeUtterance` rewrites `X_1` / `X_{1}` → `X1` for every label (scoped to a letter + `_` + DIGITS, so it never touches the area marker's `S_{ABC}` uppercase-letter subscript). One fix kills the whole class, mirroring `normalizeAreaSubscript`.
- **(B) A circle's size IS its radius.** A circle sized by circumference or area lowers to a **numeric radius** — reusing the existing fixed-radius path, NOT a new engine construct. `parseRadius` gains `circleSizeRadius`: circumference `C` ⇒ `r = C/2π` (`6π` ⇒ 3); area `A` ⇒ `r = √(A/π)` (`9π` ⇒ 3). The value may carry a π factor (`6π`) or be plain, and may follow a copula (`= 6π`, `is 6π`) or sit glued after the possessive (`שהיקפו 6π`). He forms list the possessive suffix first (`שהיקפו|היקפו|היקף`) so it's consumed whole.
- **(C) Polygon perimeter as a first-class constraint — the sibling of area.** New `perimeter` / `perimeter-ratio` constraints (`polygonPerimeter` = Σ edge lengths; a length-unit measure, mirroring area's residual/scale/tolerance/verify) and `set-perimeter` / `set-perimeter-ratio` commands emitted directly by a new `perimeter` parser rule. A lone absolute perimeter pins the figure SCALE (added to `sample.ts`'s scale-pin set alongside distance/area); a ratio drives a SHAPE DOF. The rule bows out whenever the utterance names a circle (`circle`/`מעגל`) — that `היקף` is a circumference (path B). `driveOrCheck` recruits the polygon's DOFs generically via `constraintRefs`, so no new solver plumbing. Emitting `set-perimeter` directly (not through a `measure-perimeter` symbolic layer) keeps lower/store/renderer untouched.

**Limits / follow-ups.** A perimeter given with a symbolic-variable label (`היקף ABC = P`) is out of scope — the parser returns null and it escalates to the LLM (perimeter has no `measure-perimeter` symbolic layer yet). A polygon perimeter draws no on-figure label (area does, via ADR-118's centroid label); the constraint still shapes the figure and the fact list shows the utterance. Both are noted here as deliberate scope bounds, not oversights.

**Tests / gate.** `src/parser/__tests__/perimeter-circumference.test.ts` (13 cases: subscript preservation, circumference/area→radius in He/En, polygon perimeter + ratio, circle-vs-polygon disambiguation). Two end-to-end scenarios: `circle-circumference-sizes-radius` (the operator's exact `מעגל O_1 שהיקפו 6π` → centre `O1`, radius 3) and `polygon-perimeter-sizes-figure` (`משולש ABC` + `היקף ABC = 20` → perimeter exactly 20, verifier green). Catalog examples added (both parse-in-both-locales guarded). `tsc -b` clean; full suite green. **Principle:** a stated magnitude is never dropped — `היקף`/`שטח` resolve against whatever shape they name (circle → radius, polygon → constraint), the two told apart by whether a circle is named.

### ADR-228 Amendment (2026-07-05) — tangent-circles honour stated names; circumference on an EXISTING circle sets its radius; the "pi" word

Operator follow-up on the same size-givens work: building `שני מעגלים O1 ו O2 משיקים מבחוץ` ("two circles O1 and O2 tangent externally") then `היקף מעגל O1 הוא 6pi` was refused. Three root causes, all fixed:

- **Stated names dropped in the plural form.** `circlesTangent` read circle names via a per-circle `מעגל\s+(label)` regex, which the PLURAL noun `מעגלים O1 ו O2` breaks — the `ים` suffix stops the `מעגל`-then-space adjacency, so O1/O2 were never captured and the rule INVENTED `O`/`P`. Circle `O1` therefore never existed, so nothing later could reference it. Fix: when the per-circle scan finds <2 names, a plural-list pattern (`(?:circles|מעגלים)\s+(label)\s*(?:ו|and|,)\s*(label)`) captures the two names after the plural noun. The stated centres now show (not auto-hidden).
- **Circumference/area on an EXISTING circle.** A new `circleSizeExisting` rule (before `circle`) turns `היקף מעגל O1 הוא 6π` on an existing circle into `set-radius` (r = C/2π), flexing it in place — mirroring `setRadius` for a numeric "radius = 4". Without it the `circle` CREATION rule re-emitted a `circle` command for the same id, which `addObj` ignores (keeps the first definition), silently dropping the size — the operator's "it won't let me set the circumference." A NEW circle sized this way still flows through `circle`. (New shadow pair `circleSizeExisting → circle`, added to `shadow-allowlist.json` alongside the sibling `setRadius → circle` / `nameCenter → circle`.)
- **The "pi" word.** `circleSizeRadius`'s value reader accepted only the glyph `π`, so a typed `6pi` was read as plain 6 (r ≈ 0.95, not 3). `GREEK_WORDS` deliberately omits `pi` (it collides with a segment "PI"), but immediately after a circumference/area keyword + number the context is unambiguous, so `(π|pi)` is accepted there.

**Verified NOT bugs (investigated on the report's "fixed shape" wording):** after `set-radius` pins O1, the free radius of O2 is driven to keep the pair tangent — the engine's PUBLISHED resolved-circle map (what the renderer draws) shows O1 r=3, O2 r=5.6, `|centres| = r1+r2` — geometrically correct; and "show another configuration" DOES vary the radii (it's gated on `freeDofs`, which is non-empty).

**Am.2 — the DOF cue for tangent circles (operator-authorised follow-up).** `freeDofCount` reported **0** ("✓ fully determined") for two tangent circles — the "fixed shape" impression — though the radius RATIO is one genuine shape DOF (the operator confirmed the target is **1**: two radii are movable, but uniform scaling is the gauge the cue excludes, leaving the ratio). Diagnosis corrected a mistaken first reading: `rawMovableDof` ALREADY counts a free-radius circle as 1 (via `carrierOf` → `{shape,1}`, ADR-051), so the count was off by exactly 1 for a SINGLE reason — the tangency `coincide` was counted as removing **2**. But that coincide joins two `radial-toward` witnesses that sit on the shared centre AXIS by construction, so its cross-axis component is identically 0: it is ONE scalar equation (`|O1O2| = r1±r2`), not a 2-DOF point-pin. Fix: `dofRemoved` takes the object map and counts a coincide between two `radial-toward` points as 1 (an ordinary-point coincide still removes 2). `radial-toward` exists ONLY in the tangency device (external + internal-unequal), so the rule is exact and general for the class, with no reach into other figures. Now: lone circle **0**, two tangent circles **1**, two tangent + one absolute radius **1**, square **0**, inscribed triangle **2** (all verified; only the tangent-circle class moved). Locked by a `dof-radius.test.ts` block + a DOF assertion on the scenario.

**Tests / gate.** Unit block in `perimeter-circumference.test.ts` (plural-name capture He/En, prefixed form still works, circumference→set-radius on an existing circle with the "pi" word, creation on a fresh figure). Scenario `tangent-circles-named-then-circumference` replays the operator's exact two utterances → circles keep names O1/O2, O1 radius 3, pair stays externally tangent (asserted on the published circle map). Shadow-allowlist updated deliberately. Full suite + build green.

### ADR-228 Amendment 3 (2026-07-05) — a size given on the SECOND tangent circle must not orphan the tangency; area-on-a-bare-circle-label

Operator follow-up (same tangent-circles figure): after `היקף מעגל O1 הוא 6π` (O1→r3), giving `שטח מעגל O2 הוא 81π` (O2→r9, area ⇒ r=√(A/π)) **over-constrained** — `M coincides with ~touch-M cannot hold` — and, because the operator had renamed the touch point M→E, the message said `E coincides with ~touch-E`, which read as "an error when changing M to E." Both reported symptoms are ONE root bug (the rename itself works — verified).

- **Root cause.** The free-radius tangency ([circles-tangent], ADR-052) is a `coincide` of two `radial-toward` witnesses (residual `||O1O2| − (r1+r2)|`), driven by whichever circle radius is FREE. `set-radius` pins a radius to `via:'length'`; pinning the SECOND radius leaves the coincide with NO carrier (both radii fixed) — so it over-constrains, though a free **centre** can still satisfy it (move a centre to the touch distance). `recruitFreeDofs` doesn't rescue it: it recruits only for a step's OWN new constraint, and `set-radius` adds none.
- **Fix.** `set-radius`, when it pins a radius that was driving a tangency `coincide` and no circle in that tangency keeps a free radius, recruits a free, unpinned CENTRE as the coincide's carrier (`keepTangencyDriven`). The tangency then re-solves by MOVING a centre. Scoped exactly to the tangency device (a coincide of two `radial-toward` operands, both circles now fixed-radius); ordinary point coincidences and the one-radius-free case are untouched. Now O1 r=3, O2 r=9, `|O1O2| = 12` (still externally tangent), no error.
- **Also (parser).** `circleSizeExisting` now resolves a **bare** known-circle label — `שטח O2 הוא 81π` (area of circle O2, no "מעגל" word) sets its radius, mirroring how `setRadius` resolves a bare circle label. The label scan is UPPERCASE-only (`[A-Z]\d*`) so it can't grab a stray letter from a lowercase keyword (`perimeter **o**f …` must not resolve circle O — that false shadow was caught by the shadow-matrix and fixed). A polygon area (`שטח ABC`, claimed earlier by the `area` rule) and a non-circle label are unaffected.

**Answered in passing (the operator's parallel question):** drawing a segment between a centre and a point — writing `O1E` (or `O1 E`) — already works; it parses to `segment O1–E` and using the centre in a segment reveals it (FR-RN-8). No change needed.

**Tests / gate.** Scenario `tangent-circles-both-radii-pinned-by-size` (the operator's exact three utterances → O1 r=3, O2 r=9, stays tangent). Unit block in `perimeter-circumference.test.ts` (area→set-radius on an existing circle with/without "מעגל"; bare non-circle label bows out; polygon area unaffected). Shadow-matrix snapshot updated (only the intended additions; no new shadow pair — the uppercase-label fix removed the `perimeter → circleSizeExisting` false positive). Full suite + build green.

### ADR-228 Amendment 4 (2026-07-05) — a line through two on-circle points that "passes through the centres" must not collapse them onto the tangency point

Operator (same tangent-circles figure): `A על מעגל O1`, `B על מעגל O2`, then `AB עובר דרך מרכזי המעגלים` ("AB passes through the centres of the circles") placed **A and B both onto E**, the tangency point, with no warning. Root causes:

- **The utterance didn't parse** (no rule for "line through two on-circle points crosses both centres") → it escalated to the LLM, whose interpretation collapsed A and B. E is the degenerate attractor: the external tangency point lies on the centre line AND on both circles, so a plain collinearity drives each on-circle point to the nearest centre-line intersection, which can be E for both.
- **The right reading is ORDERED.** For the segment/line A–B to pass through BOTH centres, A must be beyond O1 and B beyond O2 (the diameter ends), i.e. A, O1, O2, B in order — which forces A and B to the FAR intersections, distinct.

**Fix.** A new `lineThroughCenters` rule fires only when the two endpoints lie on DISTINCT circles (via `ctx.circleMembers`, so "the centres" resolves unambiguously) and emits `set-line [A, centreOfA, centreOfB, B]` + draws the segment. The order pairs each endpoint with its own circle's centre (A adjacent to circle-of-A), so A and B land at the far ends — verified |AB|=24, |AE|=6=2·r1, |BE|=18=2·r2, all distinct, A–O1–O2–B collinear. This realises the operator's "find a different option when points would coincide" principle (ADR-123) **structurally**, via the order, rather than relying on the sampler to dodge the collision.

**On the "I should have gotten a warning."** For a DEFAULT/avoidable collision the correct behaviour is to AVOID it silently (find the distinct config), not warn — which now happens. A warning (`coincidences`, ADR-123) is reserved for a FORCED coincidence the figure can't avoid; that machinery is unchanged and still fires there. (Notably, even a plain unordered collinearity resolves A and B to distinct points here — the exact all-on-E collapse depended on the specific LLM output, which the deterministic parse now bypasses.)

**Am.4 (cont.) — more phrasings for the ordered centre-line.** The operator tried several natural forms that all failed before landing on the one that worked. Now all reach the same ordered `set-line [A, O1, O2, B]`: (1) `AB עובר דרך O1 ו O2` — names the centres explicitly (`lineThroughCenters` accepts the centre WORD or both centre LABELS after "through"); (2) `A-O1-O2-B` / `ישר A-O1-O2-B` — a DASH-separated ordered collinear list (new `dashCollinear` rule: 3+ distinct labels joined by dashes ⇒ set-line + the spanning segment; a 2-label `A-B` stays a segment).

**Tests / gate.** Scenario `line-through-both-centres-avoids-tangency-point` (the operator's exact six utterances → A, B, E distinct, A–O1–O2–B collinear, radii 3 & 9). Parse block in `line-through-center-and-secant.test.ts` (He + En, order pairs each endpoint with its own circle, and the singular "line through THE centre" with non-circle endpoints does not fire). Shadow-matrix clean (the rule needs distinct-circle membership, so it claims no catalog utterance). Full suite + build green.

### ADR-228 Amendment 5 (2026-07-05) — NAMED tangent points on an existing circle (bagrut Q11); the `בנקודות` Hebrew-suffix bug; and a documented coupled-solve limit

The operator uploaded the book (bagrut Q11): "הקטעים AB ו-BC משיקים למעגל O2 בנקודות D ו-C … הקטע AC עובר דרך מרכזי המעגלים." So the tangent points are **D and C** (both on O2), B is the external apex, and the centre-line is **A–C**. The operator's earlier `CB ו CA` was a mis-transcription; the real figure never puts A on O2 (A stays on O1).

- **Root cause 1 — named tangent points ignored.** `cornerTangentCircle`'s existing-circle path used the ARM endpoints (A, C) as the tangent points, forcing each onto O2. For "AB tangent at D" the tangent point is D (on O2) and A is just the far end of the tangent LINE — so forcing A onto O2 contradicts "A on O1." Fix: read the named tangency points and, per arm, put the NAMED point on O2 with radius ⟂ the side and `set-collinear(T, vertex, arm)` so the tangent point lies on the side; the arm endpoint is untouched. When no points are named (the ADR-115 kite) the tangent point defaults to the arm tip — unchanged.
- **Root cause 2 — the `בנקודות` regex.** The at-points matcher was `בנקוד\w*`, but JS `\w` excludes Hebrew, so it couldn't consume the "ות" plural suffix and the following `\s+` failed — the named points were silently dropped (both here and in the new-circle path). Fixed to `בנקוד(?:ות|ה|ים)?`.
- **Now correct at the parse layer:** `AB ו BC משיקים למעגל O2 בנקודות D ו C` → D on O2 (not A), radius O2–D ⟂ BA, D collinear B–A, tangent at C via O2–C ⟂ BC; A left on O1. D is placed.

**Documented limitation (not yet solved).** The FULL figure still reports over-constrained (`O2C ⟂ BC cannot hold`): the apex **B** must satisfy TWO tangency conditions simultaneously (BA tangent at D AND BC tangent at C), which — combined with the pinned circles-tangency at E and the centre-line — is a coupled nonlinear system the greedy `driveOrCheck` + `recruitFreeDofs` can't jointly solve (B gets driven for one tangency; the other fails as a check). The figure is geometrically valid; a robust build needs either a stronger joint solver or a DETERMINISTIC construction (A, C are known ⇒ D = tangent-from-A via Thales, tangent line at C, B = their intersection). Scoped to the operator rather than built speculatively — it's a meaningful, config-specific construction.

**Tests / gate.** Parse block in `corner-circle-and-ratio.test.ts` (named points → D on O2, A untouched; C's membership not duplicated). Existing corner-tangent scenarios (kite `corner-tangent-on-existing-circle`, `arc-ratio-and-implicit-tangent-q4`) stay green — the no-named-points path is unchanged. Full suite + build green.

### ADR-228 Amendment 6 (2026-07-05) — a "try a different order / wording / smaller steps" hint on build-error messages

Design decision (operator): a bagrut book often DESCRIBES what the student sees in the diagram rather than how to construct it (e.g. Q11's "AB and BC are tangent to O2 at D and C"), so a single complex line may parse yet not build. Two ways to help: escalate to the LLM, or nudge the student to decompose. **Escalation was ruled out on cost:** the LLM only runs when the deterministic parser FAILS (there a different decomposition has genuine hope); a parsed-but-unsolvable input already has its canonical form, so the LLM would re-emit the same command — pure spend for no hope (the existing App.submit design, now explicitly affirmed). So the chosen aid is a **guidance message**.

**Change (UI only, zero engine/parser risk):** a shared `errors.retryHint` ("try a different order — enter the givens first —, reword it, or build it in a few smaller steps", He+En) is appended to every humanized BUILD error at the DISPLAY layer via a small `explainError` helper — the input note for a parsed-but-unsatisfiable step, the persistent error banner, and the broken-step tooltip. `humanizeError` itself stays a pure mapping (its unit test is untouched), so the hint rides on top of the dozen specific reasons (over-constrained, circles-don't-meet, same-spot, cannot-place, degenerate, …). The parse-failure notes (`notUnderstood`/`producedNothing`) already carried their own wording guidance and were left as-is. "Different order" is genuinely actionable here — the ADR-104 deferral means entering the givens before the constraint often builds what the reverse order can't.

**Gate.** Locale key parity verified; `humanize-error.test.ts` green (mapping unchanged); `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean; full suite green.

## ADR-229 — freeze-and-co-drive: a failing constraint consumes the SPARE DOF of an already-claimed free point, over a frozen base

**Status:** accepted (2026-07-05). **Operator directive:** "I don't understand why this is not solvable. we had complex cases before… solve this by the root cause without damaging anything else." *Files: `src/engine/types.ts` (SolveDirective.also), `src/engine/evaluate.ts` (fold `also` into both joint costs; export `resolveDriven`), `src/engine/step.ts` (recruiter case (F) + valid-early-exit), `src/parser/parse.ts` (copula-less circle-size value), tests.*

**Context (bagrut Q11, the third session on this figure).** Two tangent circles (r1=3, r2=9), A on O1, C on O2, the centre line A–O1–O2–C, two tangents from B touching O2 at C and D, then **"A נמצא על המשך BD"**. The figure is fully determined — closed form: |AC|=24, |AD|=12 (tangent from A), |BC|=18, |AB|=30 — yet the engine reported `over-constrained: A, B, D collinear cannot hold`. Root cause, precisely: **the one-constraint-per-carrier model**. B (a free point, 2 DOF) is claimed by ONE tangency (⟂ at the fixed C), which pins it only to a 1-D manifold — *sliding along the tangent line is a spare DOF* the collinear constraint could consume, but no recruiter case could express "one point, two conditions". A naive co-drive (tried and instrumented) fails for a second root reason: the joint solver re-optimises **every** driven carrier together, so adding K to the soup destabilises satisfied subsystems far from K (the circles' tangency at E broke — `M coincides with ~touch-M`).

**Decision — three pieces, all failure-path-only and self-verifying:**
1. **`SolveDirective.also`** — a carrier may co-drive EXTRA constraints beyond its primary one; both joint solvers (`resolveFreeDriven`, `resolveMixedCarriers`) fold `also` into their cost. Absent ⇒ byte-identical behaviour.
2. **Recruiter case (F), freeze-and-co-drive** (after (B)–(E) all fail): (a) **bake** the current valid solution — `resolveDriven` writes every driven carrier's solved params and clears directives (its normal output form); (b) **re-drive only the carriers K references**, restoring each one's ORIGINAL constraint from a pre-mutation snapshot (case (C)'s steal mutates even when its verification fails) and adding K via `also` on the free-point host; (c) everything else stays **frozen** at its solved position, so its constraints hold by construction and the sub-solve is small (here: A(θ) + B(x,y) + D(θ) = 4 DOF against 4 equalities). (d) **Multi-start host seeds** — the co-driven solution can be a figure-span away (B sat near the tangency point; the valid B is ~17 units along the tangent line), beyond the regularised solver's local basin, so the host is retried from a deterministic compass ring scaled to the figure extent (17 seeds); every candidate is fully verified, so a wrong basin is simply rejected.
3. **Valid-early-exit in `recruitFreeDofs`** — once the system evaluates fully valid, STOP processing the remaining new constraints: the exploratory cases mutate the carrier assignment even when their verification fails, and (observed) the sibling `collinear-order`'s failed experiments were UNDOING the just-found (F) solution.

**Why this is the root fix, not a patch.** The gap was structural (a whole class: "an apex tied by one relation must additionally satisfy a second"), and the fix is expressed at the carrier-model level, not per-figure. It composes: the frozen-base idea also prevents the (long-standing) big-soup instability for any future co-drive. Self-verification is the safety envelope — (F) runs only where today = guaranteed failure, and commits only a configuration the full evaluator accepts, so it can convert failures to successes but never the reverse.

**Also (parser).** `היקף מעגל O1 6π` / `שטח מעגל O2 81π` — the value reader accepted a number only right after the keyword or after a copula, so the copula-less named form fell to the LLM (the operator typed it twice). A third pattern (`circle-word? + ONE label + number`) reads it deterministically.

**Tests / gate.** Scenario `two-tangents-apex-collinear-with-pinned-point` (the operator's exact 8 utterances → all green, closed-form values |AB|=30/|BC|=18/|AD|=12 asserted, A-B-D collinear, D on O2). Copula-less parse tests. Full suite + build green (the early-exit and (F) fire only on today-failing paths). Perf: the Q11 replay is ~4.7 s (multi-start NM on the failure path) — acceptable for a hard figure; noted as a future optimisation target.

## ADR-230 — a size given on a circle's RADIUS drives the radius, never the free centre (busy-tangency-radius case)

**Status:** accepted (2026-07-05). **Operator:** "check why the diagram in test failed" (session `gzswxmq3`, from the dev debug log). *Files: `src/engine/apply.ts` (`radiusCircleForDistance`, `pointLiesOnCircle`, `applyRadiusGiven` extracted from `set-radius`, `keepTangencyDriven` guard), tests.*

**Context.** Two circles O1,O2 tangent externally at M; the student states `O1M=9` and `O2M=16` — M is the touch point, so `|O1M|` and `|O2M|` ARE the two radii (a `radial-toward` point sits ON its circle); then "from N two tangents to O1 at M and B". The final tangent step reported `over-constrained: |O1M| = 9 cannot hold` and the second tangent came out non-perpendicular (a broken figure). Verified constructible analytically (O1 at origin r=9, O2 at (25,0) r=16, M=(9,0); the tangent-at-M line is x=9; any N=(9,h), h≠0 has a valid second tangent point), so the verdict was a false negative.

**Root cause.** A `set-distance |centre·P|` where P lies on the circle is a size given on the RADIUS, not a positional constraint. But `driveOrCheck` had no case for it: the radial point M is not a movable carrier, and the circle's free radius was UNAVAILABLE (already `solve`-driving the tangency `coincide` — the ADR-071/circles-tangent device), so it fell through to its last resort and drove the free CENTRE O1 — which can never change `|O1M|` (≡ r1). That injected a spurious, useless centre DOF for EACH size given, so the step-40 tangent solve became a 6-DOF coupled system (2 free centres + N + B) that the numeric solver could only settle in compromise basins (it silently traded off `|O1M|=9`, landing at |O1M|≈6.9). The two circle centres being re-driven every step — the real DOF bloat — is the same "re-solving satisfied subsystems" smell ADR-229 froze in its own path.

**Decision.** In `set-distance`, detect when `|a·b|` is really a circle's radius — one endpoint is the centre, the other lies on that circle (structurally, or coincident via a `coincide` with a structural on-circle point, so the tangency witness `~touch-M` on the OTHER circle is caught too) — AND the radius is `via:'free'` with a solve directive (BUSY driving the tangency). Route that to `applyRadiusGiven` (shared with `set-radius`): pin the radius to `via:'length'` and hand the orphaned tangency coincide to a free CENTRE via `keepTangencyDriven`. That helper's guard is loosened to recruit a centre as soon as ANY tangency radius is pinned (not only the last): once one radius is fixed, the remaining free radius alone can satisfy `|O1O2| = r1±r2` only if the fixed centre gap already exceeds it — usually false at the build-time seed — so the gap must become a DOF.

**Why narrow to a BUSY free radius.** An AVAILABLE free radius must stay a flexible DOF: two INTERSECTING circles (`circle-circle-intersection` at A,B) with `|OC|=9` need the radius to grow *as a driven DOF* while circle-P and the centres adapt so the circles still meet — pinning it to a fixed length makes the seed geometry invalid and `circle-circle-intersection` hard-fails before the solve. So the fix fires only where the generic recruiter genuinely can't reach the radius (it's occupied by the coincide); every other radius given flows through the unchanged `driveOrCheck` + `recruitFreeDofs` path.

**Root fix, not a patch.** The defect is a missing carrier-selection case (distance-to-a-radial-point = radius), fixed at the routing layer for the whole class, not the one figure; the intersecting-circles guard proves it's scoped to the actually-broken condition. `set-radius` now shares the exact radius-application logic (`applyRadiusGiven`), so the `through`/`free`/`length` + tangency-handoff behaviour can't drift between the two entry points.

**Tests / gate.** Scenario `tangent-circle-size-given-drives-radius-not-centre` (the operator's exact 4 utterances → all steps ok, |O1M|=9, |O2M|=16, both tangents genuinely ⟂). The three `radius-dof.test.ts` intersecting-circles cases stay green (the narrow guard leaves them on the flexible path). Full suite (2267) + `tsc -b`/`vite build` clean.

## ADR-231 — the design-rules doctrine + the review fixes: existing-id lowering (M1), carrier-ownership re-home & order-independence (M2), shared budgeted sampling (M3)

**Status:** accepted (2026-07-06). **Operator directive:** "fix the issues you discovered in your initial review and this one… write the design rules that will prevent [a future assistant] from patching and solving specific cases in the future… be a senior designer dictating how to treat issues." *Files: `docs/17-design-rules.md` (NEW — the doctrine, linked from CLAUDE.md with operator authority), `src/engine/step.ts` (reinterpreters widened + conflict-branch recruit + staged case-(B) + (F) directive restore + orphan re-home), `src/engine/apply.ts` (`addCollinearOrder` extracted, set-distance radius reroute keeps the stated distance on record), `src/engine/evaluate.ts` (evaluate purity memo, `solutionAccepted` carrier-degeneracy guard, hidden-helper describe), `src/engine/sample.ts` (slot-free ⟂ reflection anchors, `solve.also` scanned), `src/store/geoStore.ts` (structural deferrable predicate, HOIST pass, shared budgeted sample core, resample budget), `src/parser/parse.ts` (perimeter semantic split), tests + scenarios.*

**Context.** A full review (operator-commissioned, 2026-07-06) found the recent solver ADRs (228–230) accumulating special-case routing, two probe-verified correctness holes on HEAD, and measured pathological costs (one "view relations" press = ~45 s on the ADR-123 figure, ~85% spent in failing solves that were then discarded). The same morning the operator's prod session `fn34ptei` hit `'O' is already defined` from BOTH directions on the same figure — the fifth reported member of one class (ADR-075/099/115/119/124 each fixed one). The root diagnosis, per class:

- **M1 (existing-id).** The general mechanism EXISTED (ADR-028 `reinterpretAsConstraint`, ADR-050 `reinterpretAsCollinear`) but was gated: `על`-on-segment required the existing point to own a free param DOF; placements gave up without a free *param* ancestor; and the conflict branch never ran `recruitFreeDofs`. So derived/free/busy existing points hard-conflicted, and each parser rule kept growing its own guard.
- **M2 (ownership/order).** Entry order changed satisfiability (probed: Q11 with sizes typed LAST failed `over-constrained`, sizes-first built) because (i) the deferrable set was a hand list missing `set-radius`/`set-area`/`set-perimeter` — a late size could neither defer nor pend; (ii) a pinned radius orphaned the tangency `coincide` when `keepTangencyDriven` found no free centre, and nothing re-homed it; (iii) the ADR-229 (F) bake committed a construction whose FROZEN carriers' directives were permanently stripped, so later givens found carrier-less checks; (iv) case (B) recruited every reachable DOF at once — over-recruiting is not merely wasteful, it *changes the answer* (the minimal 4-D solve of the M1 midpoint test converges where the full 8-D marking diverges — the measured ADR-123 class).
- **M3 (sampling).** `viewRelations` and `detectShapes` ran identical `variantConfigs × firstSatisfyingSeed × 16-evaluate` loops (zero sharing); a determined figure burned 16 identical solves; `resample` was the one seed loop with NO wall-clock budget; and `applyStep` re-evaluated at every fold step what the previous step had just computed.

**Decision.**
1. **Doctrine first** — `docs/17-design-rules.md`: class-first diagnosis (state the class in one sentence, grep for siblings), seven patch tripwires, a chokepoint registry (the lists that must not silently grow: `commandConflict` carve-outs, parser existing-object guards, the recruiter case ladder, `keepTangencyDriven`/`applyRadiusGiven` routing, keyword bow-outs, sampling loops, macro defaults), the designed mechanisms M1–M4, perf rules (every search loop budgeted; failure ≤ small-multiple of success; one sampler; solver ADRs state their worst-case multiplier), and the escalation template. Linked from CLAUDE.md's NEVER-PATCH rule with operator authority.
2. **M1 repaired, not re-invented:** `reinterpretAsCollinear` lowers `על` for ANY existing GeoPoint and keeps the stated direction (within → `collinear` + order [a,P,b]; extension → [a,b,P]; `addCollinearOrder` extracted from `set-line` so both share the carrier-marking); `reinterpretAsConstraint` appends the hidden-target coincidence even with no free param carrier (the recruiter reaches shape scalars/radii/centres the param walk can't) — bare `free-point` coordinate re-placement keeps ADR-011 semantics; the conflict branch gets the SAME `recruitFreeDofs` failure path as typed constraints and, when all fails, reports the RELATION (`over-constrained … cannot hold`), never `already defined`; `describeConstraint` renders a `~`-hidden helper as "its constructed target" (no internal ids in student-facing messages). **Guard:** `solutionAccepted` adds the MOVED CARRIERS to its non-degeneracy check — without it the widened path "solved" `C = midpoint of AB` on a square by collapsing the square (the residual rewards it; refs-only checking missed it).
3. **M2:** (i) the deferrable predicate is STRUCTURAL (`set-*` ∧ introduces no points — derived from apply's own output, the ADR-043/R4 anti-drift form); (ii) an unowned `coincide` on the failure path joins the recruit list (a coincide is a placement obligation born owned — an orphan is an ownership-invariant violation; this is the general form of the free-centre handoff); (iii) the (F) bake, on success, RESTORES the frozen carriers' original directives when the restored system still evaluates valid (params kept; never worse than the frozen form); (iv) case (B) recruits MINIMAL-FIRST (the newest ref's ancestors, then the full union), each stage self-verified — bounded at 2 stages so the failure path pays ≤1 extra evaluate; (v) **the HOIST pass** — the dual of ADR-104's deferral: a still-failed pure-relation fact is re-folded at the EARLIEST position where everything it references exists (`commandObjectIds`), one depth-capped recursive re-fold, failure-path only. A relation's position is presentation, not meaning; hoist + deferral together normalize entry order from both sides. **Probed: Q11 sizes-LAST now builds to the same closed form as sizes-first (|AB|=30, |BC|=18, |AD|=12).**
4. **M3:** `evaluate` gains a WeakMap purity memo (same construction reference → same result; the fold's `evaluate(prev)` double-pay disappears; changes NO results); ONE facts-ref-keyed sample core feeds `viewRelations` AND `detectShapes` (sync + chunked-async consumers over the same memo; `detectRelationsAcross` accepts pre-collected `positions`); a DETERMINED single-variant figure samples ONCE (ADR-101: the leftover gauge DOFs can't change any detected relation); sample collection and `resample` get the standard wall-clock budget (E2 convention; tests deadline-free).
5. **Honesty (review F5/F6/F8):** the perimeter rule splits by what `היקף` references (polygon run after the keyword → polygon perimeter; alongside a circle it's a compound → `'stop'` escalation — a stated magnitude never silently drops); the ADR-230 radius reroute keeps the stated `|O1M|=9` on record as a tautological `distance` check so the measure label and verifier still see it; ⟂ reflection anchors are slot-free (all four operand slots — "FD ⟂ AB" ≡ "DF ⟂ AB") and the helper classifier reads ADR-229 `solve.also`.

**Explicitly scoped OUT (documented, operator to green-light separately):** the full F4 routing unification (one semantic predicate "this distance IS a radius" regardless of solver busy-state — today the busy/available split of ADR-230 stands, protected by the intersecting-circles guard); widening the orphan re-home beyond `coincide`; deleting `keepTangencyDriven` in favour of pure re-home; solver-internal failure early-outs (deterministic-safe forms only); the Web Worker split (docs/14 backlog — the architecture review's recommended next step, with the geoStore pure-function extraction + the `theorems→store` import inversion as prerequisites).

**Tests / gate.** New: `redefine-existing-point.test.ts` M1 class matrix (derived-point `על`, no-param-ancestor placement, restated-truth-as-check, impossible-placement honest error, no `~` leakage); scenarios `existing-point-statements-lower-to-constraints` (the operator's exact `fn34ptei` sequence — no redefinition conflicts, honest relation errors, prior figure kept), `q11-sizes-last-order-independence` (the reversed Q11 → the same closed form), `perpendicular-helper-flips-mirrored-slot` (`FD אנך ל AB`); the ADR-230 scenario extended with the measure-label assertions; the F5 escalation lock in `perimeter-circumference.test.ts`. Updated: `phase1`/`adr028-driven` conflict expectations to the honest over-constraint semantics (intent — fail + keep prior — unchanged). Full suite + `tsc -b`/build clean.

## ADR-232 — save/load a figure as a portable `.geo.json` file (FR-HS-10) + the fixtures regression net

**Status:** accepted (2026-07-06). **Operator ask:** "the ability to save a drawing and then upload it from a file… will also help me with manual testing… perhaps even allow for automatic regression testing?" *Files: `src/store/figureFile.ts` (NEW — the serializer), `src/store/geoStore.ts` (`loadFigure`), `src/App.tsx` (save/load buttons + hidden file input), `src/i18n/locales/*.json` (`file.*`), `src/store/__tests__/figure-file.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/fixtures.test.ts` (NEW — the net) + `src/__tests__/fixtures/*.geo.json`.*

**Context.** FR-HS-10 specced this from the start: because the store's ordered fact list is the single source of truth and the figure is derived by `replay(facts, seed, radiusOverrides)`, a figure file is simply those replay inputs plus a small header — no positions. The operator added the testing motive: re-entering the same bagrut figures for every manual session is waste, and a saved file is a natural regression artifact.

**Decision.**
1. **Format** (`figureFile.ts`, pure data-in/data-out, no engine import): pretty-printed JSON `{app:'geo-builder', schemaVersion:1, locale?, savedAt?, seed, radiusOverrides, facts, display?}`. Facts persist exactly `{id, utterance?, group?, cmd, enabled}` — the utterance keeps the file human-readable (and feeds the drift check below); the lowered `cmd` is what load replays, so **an LLM-escalated step never re-escalates on load** (offline, deterministic, free) and `cmd.branch` keeps the chosen alternative. The `seed` + dialed radii ride in the header so the SAVED configuration reloads, not the canonical seed-0 view (they live outside the facts — the one thing FR-HS-10's one-liner missed). `display` carries the author's styling (hidden labels, dashed segments, hidden circles, measure/centre toggles). The once-flagged branch-persistence gap (ADR-043 R2: `on-segment-solved` synthesized `branch:0` fresh) was already resolved 2026-06-17 (`branch?` on `point-on-segment`) — the round-trip test locks that a cycled G reloads at its cycled position.
2. **Load is never destructive:** `deserializeFigure` refuses gracefully (`bad-json` / `not-figure` / `newer-version` / `no-facts` → a bilingual note, never a corrupt figure; unknown fields dropped, hand-edited files tolerated — missing `enabled`/`id` default); the App smoke-replays before committing (a file that makes the derivation THROW is refused, not white-screened); `loadFigure` is ONE `set` → one zundo entry, so a single undo restores the session that was open before the load.
3. **The fixtures net** (`fixtures.test.ts`): every `src/__tests__/fixtures/*.geo.json` runs the REAL load path (raw text → `deserializeFigure` → `replay`) and asserts, with zero per-figure authoring: (a) **replays green** — no error, nothing pending, verifier clean (ADR-053 makes this strong: green = every stated relation re-derived and checked), every fact `ok`; (b) **parser drift** — each stored utterance re-parsed with its prefix figure context must lower to the SAME commands (out-of-grammar utterances skip — LLM steps are stored canonically). Promotion discipline: only figures eyeballed against the textbook image join the folder (save in the app → verify → drop the file in). Seeded with 4 corpus figures: the defining interaction (square→G on AD→∠GBA=37°), equilateral-inscribed (ADR-117), parallel-chords (ADR-119), trapezoid-altitude (ADR-169).
