**What this deliberately does NOT replace:** `scenarios.test.ts` — fixtures assert "everything that built green still builds green"; scenarios assert figure-specific behavior. They feed each other: a manual session's saved file is the reproduction a fix's scenario starts from. FR-HS-4 (auto-persist across reloads) and the built-in figure library can now reuse this serializer.

**Tests / gate.** `figure-file.test.ts` (round trip to identical coordinates, branch/seed/radii survive, refusal matrix, hand-edited tolerance, load-replaces-session + one-undo restore) + the fixtures net (4 figures × replay-green + drift). Full suite + `tsc -b`/build clean.

## ADR-233 — a tangent's external-APEX role is assigned by circle membership (semantic), not by "the label that already exists" (proxy)

**Status:** accepted (2026-07-06). **Operator report:** session `pr1y4i70` — "I tried to create a tangent on C with no success until I changed syntax." *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`tangentFromExternal`, `tangentLine`), `src/parser/__tests__/tangent-on-circle-endpoint.test.ts` (NEW), `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts` + `docs/test-scenarios.md` (`segment-tangent-at-on-circle-endpoint-new-far-end`).*

**Reproduce.** `משולש ACD` → `ACD חסום במעגל` (A, C, D on the circle) → `BA משיק למעגל`. The deterministic parser DID accept it, but `tangentFromExternal` built `midpoint ~tanmid-OA → circle-through (Thales aux on OA) → circle-circle-intersection B → segment AB`: it read A (the one label already in the figure) as the external APEX and B as a new TOUCH. Because A is ON the circle, the Thales aux-circle on diameter OA is internally tangent to the circle at A, so the intersection has the single root A and the "touch" B collapsed onto A — a zero-length degenerate "tangent". The student rephrased to `מנקודה B יוצא משיק … בנקודה A` (LLM → `מנקודה B משיק נוגע במעגל O בנקודה A`), which the engine built correctly (apex B external, touch A on the circle).

**Class.** *A tangent statement assigns the external-apex role to a named point by the PROXY "it already exists" instead of the SEMANTIC fact "it is off the circle" — so an on-circle named point is misread as the apex (degenerate), and its off-circle segment-mate is dropped.* This is tripwire §2.2 (routing by the observed state rather than the meaning) applied to role assignment, and it is the unclosed member of the ADR-081/082 family: those handled "KB tangent at K" when BOTH K and B already exist (→ a `set-perpendicular` tangency constraint); the variant with an on-circle endpoint and a NEW off-circle endpoint still fell through to the greedy external construction.

**Mechanism.** Parser role-assignment by semantic incidence — genuinely local (design-rules §5.3): not M1 (nothing is re-created at the apply boundary), nor M2/M3/M4. Two edits, both semantic:
1. `tangentFromExternal`: after resolving the apex (from an explicit "from E" OR the single-existing-label heuristic), `if (members.has(apex)) return null` — an on-circle label is the tangency point, never the source of an external tangent; defer to `tangentLine`. Membership (`ctx.circleMembers`) is the semantic fact; existence was the proxy.
2. `tangentLine` (which then draws the tangent AT the on-circle point): its marker logic previously added only a two-label "line CD" naming set and a "from E" apex, and nulled out when a named endpoint WAS the touch — so `BA`'s new endpoint B was silently dropped (§6 honesty). Replaced with one unified rule: EVERY named point on the tangent line that is not the touch and not the centre becomes a ±offset slider marker (ADR-036/084, a free DOF per ADR-052) if fresh. One code path now covers the touch's segment-mate (`BA`→B), the two definers of a named tangent line (`line CD`→C,D), and the explicit apex (`from E`→E).

**Sibling audit (grep `tangent|משיק` role assignment in `parse.ts`).** `tangentsFromExternal` (two tangents) names its apex ONLY via an explicit "from E" match — it never infers the apex from existence, so it is NOT a member of this class; left unchanged (a contradictory explicit "from ⟨on-circle point⟩" is a separate, unreported concern). `twoTangentsMeet` / `tangentLineIntersection` / `tangentMeetsOtherCircle` take their touch points from explicit "at X" clauses. The single-tangent inference in `tangentFromExternal` was the only rule assigning the apex role by the existence proxy. Log scan of the tangent-error family surfaced no other open member; the July-5 `מעגל O1 וO2 משיקים מבחוץ בנקודה E` mis-parse is a DIFFERENT class (a circle-circle-tangency phrasing grabbed by a tangent-line rule) and is filed separately, not bundled here.

**Tests / gate.** Class unit test `tangent-on-circle-endpoint.test.ts` (mirrored `BA`/`AB`, He + En, all → tangent-at-A + B a marker, no Thales `circle-circle-intersection`; a genuine external "from E … at D" still uses the Thales construction). End-to-end scenario `segment-tangent-at-on-circle-endpoint-new-far-end` (the operator's exact sequence: B placed, B ≠ A, A/C/D on one circle, BA ⟂ OA). Full suite + `tsc -b`/build clean.

## ADR-234 — a student's explicit equality that matches a shape's SOFT default is the student CHOOSING it (commit + pin), not a redundant "already drawn" no-op

**Status:** accepted (2026-07-06). **Operator report:** session `z4v1zza3` — "I said משולש שווה שוקיים but didn't say which are equal. When I pressed 'show equal length' I saw nothing equal, which is correct because we don't know what is equal at this point. But when I say AB=AC — which is to say WHICH are equal — there is an error [it says it already exists]." *Files: `src/engine/shapeVariants.ts` (`pinsSoftVariant`, NEW), `src/engine/index.ts` (re-export), `src/store/geoStore.ts` (`dryRunOutcome`), `src/engine/__tests__/pins-soft-variant.test.ts` (NEW), `src/store/__tests__/dry-run.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts` + `docs/test-scenarios.md` (`isosceles-pin-soft-pair`).*

**Reproduce.** `משולש ABC שווה שוקיים` → `shape-variant{isosceles, [A,B,C], variant 0}`; drawn OK. The isosceles bakes a SOFT default equal-pair (apex A ⇒ `|AB|=|AC|`, ADR-138) into the geometry so a figure can be shown, but the relations layer samples across all three apex variants so the pair is NOT reported as forced — matching the operator's mental model (the pair is genuinely unstated, ADR-052; "show equal length" correctly shows nothing). Then `AB=AC` → parser emits `[segment AB, segment AC, set-equal(AB,AC)]`; the two segments already exist and the `set-equal` names the SAME pair the soft default already used, so the figure doesn't move → `dryRunOutcome` returned `{produced:false, reason:'empty'}` → the input gate declared "already on the figure — nothing to add" and dropped the statement. The engine WAS enforcing `|AB|=|AC|` to machine precision the whole time (verified at every seed); the bug was purely the gate swallowing the student's specification.

**Class.** *An explicit relation the student states that COINCIDES with a shape's soft/default assumption is dropped as a redundant no-op, instead of being applied as the student's specification.* Stating which pair is equal is genuine new information — it converts the engine's SOFT guess (not reported, cyclable by "show another") into the student's PINNED choice (reported/forced, no longer cyclable) — even though the coordinates, which already drew that pair by default, do not move. This is the M4 shape (defaults yield to statements): a soft default that "yields" to an explicit statement naming the SAME thing must yield by becoming the student's stated fact, not by absorbing the statement into silence. Sibling of the `reveals`/`dataOnly` cases already in `dryRunOutcome` — a step that is semantically productive without a geometric delta.

**Mechanism.** `dryRunOutcome`'s "did this build something?" test was purely geometric (moved / grew objects·constraints·labels), plus two hand cases (`dataOnly` for `set-var`, `reveals` for `name-center`). Added a third semantic case: a `set-equal` in the new commands that NAMES an enabled `shape-variant`'s (kite / isosceles) equal-pair which no EXISTING explicit equality already asserts → `produced:true`. The predicate is the pure `pinsSoftVariant(setEqual, shapeVariants, explicitEqs)` in `shapeVariants.ts` (which owns `variantPairs`/`eqMatchesPair`): it is order-independent (canonical segment/pair keys), covers both variant shapes and all their pairs, skips the pairless `midsegment`, and excludes a pair an explicit equality already stated (so a genuine RE-statement stays a no-op via the existing path). The existing explicit equalities are gathered exactly as `replay` does (`facts` minus `shape-variant`, lowered) so the shape-variant's OWN soft pair never counts as "already stated". Cost stays off the common path — the symtab/lowering runs only when the geometric checks already read empty AND an enabled shape-variant is present.

**Effect (the operator's flow, now correct).** (1) `משולש שווה שוקיים` → drawn, "show equal length" reports nothing forced (pair unspecified). (2) `AB=AC` → COMMITS; because ADR-138 suppresses the shape-variant's own pair when an explicit equality provides it, the construction still has exactly one `|AB|=|AC|` constraint, so the figure does not move — but the explicit fact now pins variant 0 across all sampled configs. (3) "show equal length" now reports `AB=AC` as forced. The apex ANGLE remains a free DOF (ADR-052) varied by "show another"; only the equal-PAIR is now the student's.

**Sibling audit.** Grepped `dryRunOutcome` and the "produced nothing / already drawn" gate for other places a soft assumption could swallow an explicit statement. The gate is the single chokepoint (App.submit, the LLM second attempt, `replaySession`, and the App-faithful scenario harness all route through it), so the one fix covers every caller. `midsegment` is the only pairless variant and is excluded. A separate, pre-existing behavior surfaced and is FILED not fixed (out of scope): a duplicate EXPLICIT `set-equal` is not deduped by the construction, so RE-typing `AB=AC` a second time grows the constraint count and shifts the figure ~0.75 (double-weighting) rather than reading "already drawn" — a constraint-dedup concern in the engine, not this gate; the reported single-statement scenario is unaffected.

**Tests / gate.** Pure matcher `pins-soft-variant.test.ts` (both shapes, all pairs, mirrored order, already-stated exclusion, non-matching pair, pairless midsegment, empty). `dry-run.test.ts` (an equality pinning the isosceles soft default is produced with no geometric move). End-to-end `isosceles-pin-soft-pair` through the App.submit-faithful gate (the operator's exact `משולש ABC שווה שוקיים` → `AB=AC`: step 1 reports nothing forced, `AB=AC` classifies as COMMIT not noop, and afterward "show equal length" reports the pair and `|AB|=|AC|` holds). Full suite (2314) + `tsc -b`/build clean.

## ADR-235 — theorem-discovery v2 slice T1 (measure & map): the coverage disposition map, the measured fill order, the full B-series corpus gate, and the feed audit harness

**Context.** The theorem-relevance replan ([docs/18](18-theorem-relevance-plan.md), accepted decision-complete 2026-07-06) diagnosed the operator's "theorems that should appear don't appear, and the order seems random" into four structural causes (R1 coverage / R2 matcher-local evidence / R3 undesigned ranking / R4 no intent layer). Slice **T1 — measure & map** builds the bookkeeping and harnesses that make the remaining work enumerable and testable, deliberately changing **no matcher, no ranking, no engine code**.

**Built.**
1. **`src/theorems/coverage.ts` — the disposition map** (`THEOREM_COVERAGE`): every id in [07](07-theorem-reference.md) (1–109, 201, A1–A6, B1–B4 — 120 ids) carries exactly one explicit disposition — `tabled` (50 today) · `no-reveal` (68/70/76, ADR-208) · `supplemental` (A1/B1/B2/B4, the Appendix ids ADR-217 did NOT keep) · `planned` with a T2 slice tag (65 ids) · `needs-construct` (#88, a circle inscribed in a *quadrilateral*). `integrity.test.ts` gained **totality** guards: total over 07, no stray keys, and the three policy kinds are checked as *equivalences* (`tabled` ⇔ in `THEOREM_TABLE`, etc.), so the map can never drift from the table or the ADR-208/217 sets. "Absent" is now a tracked state answerable in one lookup (R1's root fix).
2. **The measured fill order** (`groundTruth.ts` + the env-gated `fill-order.test.ts` → [reports/theorem-fill-order.md](../reports/theorem-fill-order.md)): parses the 25 reviewed questions' `expectSurfaced`/`solutionUses` lists out of [theorem-ground-truth.md](sample%20questions/theorem-ground-truth.md) and ranks the absent ids by measured demand. Top of the list, confirming §4's predictions: **80** (3 expect), **15/16/17**, **24**, **101** (5 solution uses), **31**, **78**, **62**, and **23** (10 solution uses). An always-on sanity block keeps the doc parser honest; the report is an OFFLINE authoring aid only (operator ruling D3 — no runtime scores). One honest tension it surfaced: B4's ground truth lists **76** as given-announced (a *stated, drawn* bisector), but 76 stays structurally no-reveal — the T5 principles lane is its designated carrier.
3. **The B-series corpus gate** (`b-corpus.test.ts`): all **22 booklet questions** (B1–B4, B6–B23; B5 removed) wired through the REAL pipeline (parse-with-context → facts → `replay` → `detectTheorems`), authored from each question's *Givens* line only, with **membership assertions** (T1; ranking assertions arrive in T3). Four-bucket semantics per question: `expect` (tabled + firing → asserted in the final feed), **`gaps` (tabled + ground-truth-expected + NOT firing → asserted absent, so a T2 evidence fix flips the test and forces the bucket move — a documented miss can neither linger nor flip silently)**, `planned` (not tabled → asserted scheduled in the coverage map), `never` (mustNotSurface ∩ tabled with no admitted path → asserted absent from the strict L1/L2 feed at every step; questions with a *stated* parallel omit 69/71 per the ADR-220 admission). 66 tests, ~28 s.
4. **The feed audit harness** (`src/theorems/audit.ts` + `theorem-audit.test.ts`, §9.5): replays debug-log sessions and every `fixtures/*.geo.json` through `detectTheorems` step-by-step and writes the operator's bulk review sheet ([reports/theorem-audit.md](../reports/theorem-audit.md) — per step: the utterance → its ● new ids). Fixtures leg always-on (robustness); debug-log leg env-gated (`THEOREM_AUDIT_LOG`/`_OUT`/`_MAX`). This is how "I'm not happy" turns into labeled data.

**R2 evidence gaps found and documented by the wiring** (each a `gaps` entry; T2's worklist, most affect several questions): (a) **tangency at an EXISTING on-circle point** (the ADR-075/115 constraint form, `set-perpendicular`) is invisible to `tangentPoints` → the whole tangent bundle misses (B4, B9, B19); (b) **`cyclic quadrilateral` / inscribe-existing lowers to `circumcircle` + `set-concyclic`**, invisible to the 87 matcher, and ≥4 bare concyclic members don't fire 87 either despite the operator's B2c ruling (B3, B9, B13, B16, B17, B19, B21, B23); (c) **a stated line THROUGH the centre** (`the line AO cuts circle O at C and D`) carries no collinear-through-centre datum → 103 misses (B15); (d) **arc-EQUALITY** (`set-angle-ratio` via ADR-116) doesn't reach the 92 matcher (B6); (e) **kite matchers key on type `kite` only** — B14's emergent rhombus (detection verified correct by hand: the trisection given genuinely forces all four sides equal) doesn't fire 37/38 (the kite ⊃ rhombus hierarchy gap); (f) 97/98/84/91/99 miss on the named-centre `circle centered at M through B` construction (B2, B3).

**Parser findings recorded (not fixed — T1 changes no behavior):** (i) compound "the perpendicular to AB at E cuts (the extension of) BD at G" **mis-lowers** — G dropped, and the `cuts line BD at G` variant *grabs the existing D* as an on-line marker (a real mis-parse, would corrupt a figure if committed; the app's droppedNewLabels gate escalates the G-drop but NOT the D-grab form); (ii) `kite ABCD inscribed in circle O` parses but **silently drops the kite shape word** (the ADR-117 class, quad edition); (iii) **`droppedNewLabels` flags the area marker `S` as a dropped point label** whenever the S-form utterance doesn't carry a letter label into the lowered command (`S_{ABC} = 13`, `S_{ACD} = 4 S_{NCE}`) → these escalate to the LLM in prod despite parsing cleanly (ADR-121/123 forms; cost/latency, not correctness); (iv) `G on line BD` for a NEW G drops G and — replayed headlessly without the app gate — **crashes** `constraintIsPending` (`residual` on an undefined position) instead of failing gracefully.

**Consequences.** T2 (coverage fill) now has a measured priority order and an enumerated evidence worklist; every fill lands against an existing corpus assertion (flip `gaps`→`expect`, upgrade `planned`→tabled under the totality guard). The corpus stays green on today's table — the gate's exact T1 definition. Full suite green, `tsc -b` + build clean.

## ADR-236 — the four T1 wiring findings fixed at root: the ⊥/∥ cut-compound, the inscribed kite's shape word, notation markers in `droppedNewLabels`, and a new point named onto a line

**Context.** Wiring the B-series corpus (ADR-235) surfaced four parser/harness defects outside the theorem track. Operator: *"fix all now."* Each is fixed at the layer it originates (never-patch rule), locked by `src/parser/__tests__/adr-236.test.ts` (16 tests through the real parse-with-context → replay path), and the B-corpus wiring is upgraded to the natural booklet phrasings the fixes unlock.

**1. The drawn ⊥/∥ line's cut-compound mis-lowered (the D-grab).** "the perpendicular to AB at E cuts **line** BD at G" / "…cuts **the extension of** BD at G" — the cut-clause regex knew only the Hebrew fillers (`ה?קו/ה?ישר/ה?משך`), so the English forms failed to bind; the rule then fell through to the ADR-036 line-NAMING fallback, which read "line BD" as the *perpendicular's own name* and emitted `point-on-line D` — **grabbing the existing rhombus vertex D onto the perpendicular** (a silently wrong figure the `droppedNewLabels` gate does NOT catch, since D is referenced) while dropping G. Root fix: (a) the cut-clause is extracted to a shared `LINE_CUT` regex whose filler group swallows both languages (`the/line/ray/segment/extension of/extended/את/ה?קו/ה?ישר/ה?משך/ה?קטע`, repeated); (b) `parallelLine` gains the same cut compound (scaffolding ∥-line + `line-through` + `line-intersection` + the joining segment — the ⊥ rule's shape, mirrored); (c) **a cut verb aimed at a NAMED segment (`LINE_CUT_TARGET`) that the clause can't bind now returns null (escalate) instead of half-parsing** — a compound we can't fully read must build nothing — while a PRONOUN cut ("וחותך אותו בנקודה E", cuts IT = the reference segment) is exempt: that's the reposition/foot form whose through-point IS the cut (two existing scenarios, `existing-segment-perpendicular-cuts-at-new-point` / `perpendicular-cuts-at-existing-point`, caught a first blanket guard and forced this precision); (d) the ADR-036 line-NAME is read only from the text BEFORE any intersect word, so an intersection-NOUN form ("G is the intersection of … and line BD") can never feed the cut-line's letters into the naming fallback either. B2's canonical decomposition is replaced by the booklet compound.

**2. "kite ABCD inscribed in circle O" silently dropped the kite word** (the ADR-117 class, quad edition: "kite"/"דלתון" was neither a `kind` nor a `SHAPE_LEFTOVER` token — a generic inscribed quad drew, no constraint, no escalation). Root fix in `inscribedPolygon`: kite is a first-class `kind`; every branch routes the base polygon through a shared `basePlusShape` which, for a kite, emits the **`shape-variant 'kite'`** (the ADR-138 axis-cyclable/pinnable macro the standalone "kite ABCD" uses — expansion supplies the quadrilateral + the equal adjacent pairs, and an explicit `AB=AD` pins the axis with no double-drive); the fresh-build path gets a right-kite starting spread (`INSCRIBED_ANGLES.kite`, axis on the vertical diameter) with FREE vertices (ADR-052). **Follow-through in the theorem spine:** `quadFacts` (the 87/201 stated-quad reader) now also accepts a 4-id `shape-variant` — without it, honouring the kite word would have *stopped* 87 from announcing on B8. B8's corpus entry now uses the kite word and **moves 37/38 from `gaps` to `expect`** (the first T1 gap closed); catalog note updated (inscribed shapes: + kite).

**3. `droppedNewLabels` read notation markers as point labels** → needless prod LLM escalations for cleanly-parsed input: the ADR-118 area marker `S` (`S_{ABC} = 13`, `S_{ACD} = 4 S_{NCE}` — the lowered command stores no letter label, so `S` looked dropped) and the raw `O_1` subscript (the utterance reads as label `O` while the commands carry `O1`). Root fix: the guard now extracts labels from `normalizeUtterance(utterance)` — the SAME text the rules parse — and masks the glued area marker (`S` before a 3–4-label run). A bare label S (`S_{ABC} = S`) was never affected (it lands in the command); a genuinely dropped label still flags. B8's ratio step returns to the compact S-form.

**4. "G on line BD" for a NEW G emitted a constraint on a point nothing defines.** `collinearConstraint`'s "P on line QR" / "line QR passes through P" branches asserted `set-collinear` referencing P without creating it — headless replay **crashed** in `constraintIsPending` (`residual` over a missing position; the app path only survived by escalating a perfectly readable utterance). Two-layer root fix: the parser branches emit an **`ifAbsent` free point** — a new engine flag mirroring the circle command's (`apply` skips it entirely when the id exists as ANYTHING; `commandConflict` and `reinterpretAsConstraint` ignore it), so the lowering is existence-AGNOSTIC (unit/harness callers parse without a figure context; the first ctx-dependent attempt broke `collinear.test.ts`) and a new P becomes a free slider the constraint drives (2 DOF − 1, ADR-052); and `constraintIsPending` gains the general honesty guard — a constraint whose `constraintRefs` lack positions is skipped in the flex probe (never crashes, surfaces as the hard error it is). B15's corpus entry uses the natural "G on line BD".

**Consequences.** One PAR-10 snapshot updated (the on-line catalog examples now emit the leading `free-point` — the intended lowering change). Full suite green, `tsc -b` + build clean. The B-corpus stays the honest map: B8 is the first entry whose `gaps` bucket shrank through a fix, exactly the designed flow.

## ADR-237 — a size given on a similarity-gauge figure is a SCALE statement: the closed-form scale rescue (last resort on the step failure path)

**Context.** Operator: *"I loaded the diagram that failed before and it is still failing."* Session `gblq4wue` — the reloaded two-tangent-circles figure, now in its FULL bagrut form: circles O1, O2 tangent externally at M; from N a tangent pair to O1 (at M and B) AND a tangent pair to O2 (at M and A) — NM the common inner tangent; "A on the extension of BN" (the line BA is the common outer tangent through N); segment O1O2; then the size **`O2M=9`** — refused *"over-constrained: M coincides with its constructed target cannot hold"* and left deferred forever.

**Diagnosis (headless replay of the exact log facts).** The ADR-230 reroute worked as designed: `radiusCircleForDistance` matched (M lies on circle O2 through the tangency coincide), r2 was pinned to 9, the tautological distance recorded. But `keepTangencyDriven` found **no idle centre** to hand the coincide's gap to — in this richer figure O1's centre already drives the A-B-N collinearity and O2's centre a tangency ⟂ (both recruited by earlier steps) — so the coincide stayed owned by the one remaining free radius alone, which cannot widen the centre gap (r ≥ 0, and gap − 9 < 0 at the seed). The M2/ADR-231 orphan re-home doesn't apply (the coincide is owned, just unsatisfiable by its owner), and the failure-path recruiter solves only the step's NEW constraints. An attempt to co-drive the coincide on a busy centre's spare DOF (the ADR-229 `also` mechanism) attached correctly but the ~9-DOF coupled solve (both centres + r1 + N + both touch params) never converges — the needed move is spread across EVERY carrier at once.

**The insight.** The figure states no other absolute size — it is determined only **up to similarity** (the ADR-101 gauge; the ADR-118 area principle is the same fact). Its first stated length is therefore a statement about SCALE, with an exact closed-form solution: multiply every free world-unit DOF by **k = stated/measured**. Every stated relation (⟂, ∥, tangency, collinearity, equalities, ratios, angles) is scale-invariant, and holding the just-pinned `length` radius fixed while scaling is precisely what lands the new given exactly (k = 9/r2_eff makes gap = r1·k + 9 on the nose).

**Decision.** `scaleRescue` on the step failure path (`src/engine/step.ts`), strictly **after** the recruiter as the LAST resort: find the failing step's positive `distance` constraint, k = value/measured-at-prev, scale free-point coordinates, free circle radii, on-line offsets and perp-offset legs (dimensionless params — on-segment t, on-circle θ — and stated `length` radii stay), then **try-and-verify**: accept only if the full evaluation holds. Three structural guards make it safe: (1) last-resort ordering — a figure a minimal recruited solve can satisfy keeps the least-perturbation behavior (the stability principle; a first draft that ran BEFORE the recruiter broke 4 driven-solve tests by scaling whole figures the recruiter used to reshape minimally); (2) try-and-verify — any OTHER absolute given breaks under a global scale, so the evaluation rejects it and the honest error stands; (3) a pinned free point (a student-typed coordinate) disables it — the frame is fixed, scale is not a gauge there.

**The second size then closes the figure.** `O1M=16` pins the remaining radius; `applyRadiusGiven` drops its coincide directive, the coincide becomes a true ORPHAN, and the M2/ADR-231 re-home path recruits the gap — |O1M| = 16, |O2M| = 9, |O1O2| = 25 exactly, every tangency ⟂ and the A-N-B collinearity verified. `keepTangencyDriven`'s doc now records the division of labour: idle-centre handoff (ADR-230) → scale rescue (first size, all centres busy) → orphan re-home (second size).

**Tests.** Scenario `size-given-scales-similarity-gauge-figure` (the operator's exact utterance sequence + the natural second size, asserting both radii, the 25 gap, all four tangency ⟂s, and A-N-B collinearity). Full suite green, `tsc -b` + build clean.

## ADR-238 — a driven carrier must not PARK at its own constraint's collapse point (anti-collapse retry), and HOIST runs from the PENDING state

**Status.** Accepted (2026-07-06). Operator prod session `sq9lt4fj` ("I'm trying to set radius sizes and it fails"): two circles tangent at M, tangent pairs from N to EACH circle through the shared touch M, `A נמצאת על המשך BN`, then `O1M=9` (ok) / `O2M=16` (refused — "M coincides with its constructed target cannot hold", logged `deferred-constraint` forever, circle-O2's drawn radius collapsed to ~0.26). *Files: `src/engine/evaluate.ts` (`collapseBarrier`, the retry in `resolveFreeDriven` + `resolveMixedCarriers`), `src/store/geoStore.ts` (the HOIST gate), tests.*

**The class (design-rules §1).** *A driven free carrier with residual manifold slack is parked at the regularised-NEAREST point of its solution manifold even when that point is (near-)degenerate — the constraint's own collapse point — and no later mechanism can re-seed it along the manifold, so any subsequent given that needs the slack falsely over-constrains.* Here: N carries `O1M ⟂ NM`; its solution manifold is the whole ⟂ line through M, every point equally valid; the least-perturbation regulariser picks the point nearest N's seed — which is M itself (the residual's NaN hole; the joint solve craters, the recruiter dodges by consuming O2, and the "fix" settles N 0.5 from M). The wedged figure then starves/destabilises every later solve: the tangents to the SECOND circle through the same M, and finally the size givens. Traced with a throwaway instrumented recruiter: case (B) over-recruits O2 as a dodge; at the later failure (C) steal/(E) lend/(F) freeze-co-drive all fail around the wedge — the machinery was fine, the parking was the disease. **Proof of mechanism:** seeding N at the healthy closed-form spot builds BOTH entry orders perfectly with zero engine changes.

**Decision 1 — the anti-collapse barrier, retry-only.** `collapseBarrier(c, cons, carrierIds)`: a per-pair linear hinge over the referenced/carrier points (exempting pairs a `coincide` intends to merge — the same convention as `solutionAccepted`), margin 5% of the solve's local extent. It is added to the search cost **only in a RETRY pass**: both driven solvers run their plain search first (previously-green basin choices preserved bit-for-bit), and re-search with the barrier-augmented cost only when the plain result FAILED or parked near-degenerate (barrier > 0), preferring a strictly-healthier accepted result. A first draft put the barrier in the primary descent and it deflected 3 seeds of the `spelled-out-alpha-then-2alpha` sweep into the angle-ratio's spurious collapse basin (0 = 2·0) — the retry-only structure is load-bearing, not a style choice. Self-verifying: a forced coincidence (ADR-123's N=O) finds no accepted healthier result and falls back; the retry can never corrupt a figure, only recover one.

**Decision 2 — HOIST runs from the PENDING state.** With the wedge fixed, the operator's exact order still failed at `O2M=16`: every DOF the orphaned tangency could use was claimed, and the ADR-231 HOIST — built for exactly "a size given typed after the solver claimed the DOFs it should have pinned" — was gated behind `!pending`. The step classified `deferred-constraint` ("waiting for more givens") when nothing more was coming. HOIST now runs from pending too; **acceptance is unchanged** (the hoisted fold must build clean AND not pending), so a genuinely under-determined figure keeps its amber cue. ADR-104's own promise ("order shouldn't matter") is the justification: a reordering of the SAME facts building fully clean proves the figure was never waiting.

**Sibling audit.** The `keepTangencyDriven` ladder (ADR-230 idle-centre → ADR-237 scale rescue → ADR-231 orphan re-home) covers the first-size case; this session's second-size + shared-touch coupling needed no new routing — once the parking and the gate were fixed, the existing machinery solves both orders to the closed form (radii 9/16, |O1O2|=25, |NM|=|NB|=|NA|=√(r1·r2)=12). Perf (§7): the barrier retry runs only on failed/wedged results (one extra bounded search on the failure path, one extra `evaluateCore` on the success path); hoist-on-pending adds at most one bounded re-fold per replay in a pending state.

**Behavioral consequence (locked deliberately).** The retry also gives a FAILED driven solve a second, differently-shaped search — so the Q4 "CE⟂AB before sizes" case, which used to DEFER (the ADR-104 pending info state, its early coupled solve never landing), now applies CLEAN: the ⟂ is satisfied immediately on the still-flexible figure (verified to solver precision; the with-sizes completion unchanged, `q4-constraints-order-independent`). The `pending-vs-contradiction` scenario was updated to lock the better state — a satisfiable early constraint is never a red error; a rigid contradiction stays red.

**Tests.** Scenario `shared-touch-tangents-sizes-last` (the operator's exact sequence, closed form asserted); unit block in `adr-238-239.test.ts` (the wedge escapes its margin; sizes-last builds the sizes-first figure); the alpha seed-sweep guards the retry-only structure. Full suite green, `tsc -b` + build clean.

## ADR-239 — the COMMON-TANGENT construct: two touch points or at the shared touch, with a soft touch↔circle pairing that yields to explicit memberships

**Status.** Accepted (2026-07-06). Operator: "we are missing a construct of tangent to 2 circles. we need to support tangent at 2 points and tangent at intersection" (session `sq9lt4fj`: `AB משיק משותף לשני המעגלים` escalated to the LLM). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`commonTangent`, registered before `circlesTangent`), `src/engine/types.ts` (`softPair` on `point-on-circle`), `src/store/geoStore.ts` (the softPair swap pre-scan), `src/parser/catalog.ts`, tests.*

**Why it fell through.** No rule owned "common"/"משותף": the plural מעגלים + משיק matched `circlesTangent`, which re-read the utterance as MUTUAL tangency of two NEW circles (inventing O,P and dropping the tangent line) — so the LLM was the only path, unreliable and unmodeled.

**Decision.** A `commonTangent` rule (unique "משותף"/"common" trigger; before the other two-circle tangent rules, none of which checks the word). Circles: two named (creating absent ones, free radius per ADR-052) or THE two circles of the figure ("לשני המעגלים"). Two variants:
- **Two touch points** ("AB משיק משותף…"): `point-on-circle` A on circle 1 / B on circle 2 + `set-perpendicular(centre, touch, A, B)` per circle + `segment AB` — no new engine construct (the ADR-110 macro pattern).
- **At the shared touch** ("…בנקודה M", M existing — the operator's "tangent at intersection"): membership of M on BOTH circles + `set-line [O1,M,O2]` (centres collinear with the touch ⟺ common tangency there; all idempotent when the pair is already tangent at M) + a DRAWN `tangent` line at M, fresh naming letters as ±offset markers (ADR-036/233 — nothing typed is dropped). A NEW "at M" point instead lowers to `circles-tangent` + the drawn tangent (the standalone form).

**The soft pairing (M4).** "AB משיק משותף" states that AB touches both circles — never WHICH touch rides WHICH circle. The rule pairs letters↔circles in stated order and tags both memberships `softPair`; a `replay` pre-scan (the ADR-163 shape, position-independent) SWAPS the pair — the two memberships and the group's radius-⟂ centres — when an explicit untagged membership elsewhere names the opposite assignment (the operator's own next line, "tangents from N to O1 at M and B", puts B on O1). A membership confirming the default keeps it; both stated → the default stands and any genuine contradiction fails honestly. **Known scope note:** "external/internal" ("חיצוני/פנימי") select a CONFIGURATION of the same assertion — the solver lands on one and "show another configuration" explores; a side-of-line bias is a filed follow-up (no stated magnitude is dropped — the words add no length/angle).

**Tests.** Scenarios `common-tangent-two-circles` (the operator's full session shape: construct + N-tangents + sizes → pairing swapped, closed form) and `common-tangent-at-shared-touch`; softPair unit block (emission He/En, swap fires, confirmation keeps) in `adr-238-239.test.ts`; catalog examples (He+En) under the catalog-coverage guard. Full suite green, build clean.


## ADR-240 — a multi-subject membership statement asserts EVERY named point; the LLM commit path re-checks droppedNewLabels

**Status.** Accepted (2026-07-06). Operator's exported `.geo.json` (saved on the server): the step "A ו C נמצאות על המעגל" was stored with only `point-on-circle A` — C floated off the circle on every machine the file was opened on, with the row reading ✓. *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`pointOnCircle`), `src/App.tsx` (the LLM-path gate), i18n (`input.labelsDropped`), tests (`multi-point-on-circle.test.ts`, scenario `multi-point-on-circle-membership`).*

**The class (design-rules §1).** *A statement naming N subjects is parsed single-subject — the co-subjects are silently dropped.* `pointOnCircle` was documented and written as "a single inscribed point": its regex took the FIRST label before the on-word. The app-level honesty net (ADR-089 `droppedNewLabels`) DID flag C and escalated — but the LLM's canonical output is re-parsed by the SAME single-subject grammar, and the LLM commit path never re-ran the net, so the round-trip committed the identical partial lowering. Two mechanisms, both fixed:

- **Grammar:** `pointOnCircle` reads the ADR-076 uppercase-label-list subject (every `[A-Z]\d*` before the on-word; "points"/"נמצאות"/ו-joiners never read as labels; a glued pair "AB על המעגל" still defers to the chord/segment readings; a lowercase label keeps the legacy single-subject read). It also gained the sibling rules' `POINT_ON_CARRIER` defer, closing a latent member: "D על המיתר AB במעגל O" used to put D **on the circle** — it is a point on the chord (now point-on-segment + the carrier's own memberships via `withCarrierMembership`). Shadow-matrix effect: three pairs REMOVED, none added (the rule stopped divergently claiming tangent/intersection utterances).
- **The second honesty gate:** `App.submit`'s LLM path now runs `droppedNewLabels` on the LLM's combined commands before committing; a still-dropped label refuses the commit with the label NAMED (`input.labelsDropped`), keeping the text for editing. Honesty invariant (§6): a stated point now parses, escalates, or errors — it can no longer vanish through the escalation seam.

**Sibling audit.** List-subject coverage now: N-on-N-segments (ADR-076), two-on-one-segment (`pointsOnSegment`), N-on-circle (this ADR). Still single-subject: `pointOnLine` ("A on line BC") — filed, not fixed; with the second gate closed such inputs degrade to an honest refusal/escalation, never a silent partial commit.

**Tests.** `multi-point-on-circle.test.ts` (list forms He/En through parse→replay with |O·|=r asserted; carrier defer; glued-pair guard); scenario `multi-point-on-circle-membership` (the file's exact sequence). Full suite green, build clean.

## ADR-241 — an edited step re-lowers against its OWN position's prefix context; a diameter on existing points asserts membership, not just collinearity

**Status.** Accepted (2026-07-06). Operator report (screenshot session): `מעגל O` / `AB קוטר` / `BD מיתר` / `BD⊥AC` drew correctly; ✎-editing step 2 to "AC קוטר" broke the figure — A slipped off the circle, C floated far outside, every row still ✓ ("when I edit an input it doesn't really run the full engine again"). *Files: `src/App.tsx` (`commitEdit`), `src/store/geoStore.ts` (`replaceGroup`), `src/parser/parse.ts` (the `diameter` rule's ADR-137 branch), scenarios (`diameter-edit-rereads-at-position`, `diameter-on-existing-free-points`), the scenario harness's `{ edit }` step form.*

**Diagnosis.** The engine DID fully replay — the edit fed it weaker commands. Two stacked defects:

1. **The class:** *an edited step is re-lowered against the END-STATE figure context instead of the context at its own position.* `commitEdit` parsed with `parseCtx()` (the full current figure), where C already existed (created free by the LATER ⊥ step) — so the M1-style context-sensitive lowering chose the existing-endpoints constraint form, and `replaceGroup` spliced it back at position 2 where that lowering is wrong. Fix: the edit parses against the PREFIX context (facts before the edited group — exactly where the replacement replays; also what `fixtures.test.ts`'s drift check always assumed the app did). `replaceGroup` additionally gained the submit path's seed-validity search (`extensionsClear`/`intersectionsWithinSegments` → `firstSatisfyingSeed`) — edit-path parity, one undo entry.
2. **The under-assertion (the no-edit sibling, reachable on the plain submit path):** *a rule gated its constraint-lowering on label EXISTENCE where the semantics require circle MEMBERSHIP* (the ADR-233 proxy-vs-semantic lesson). "XY is a diameter" entails X,Y ∈ circle AND collinear-through-centre; the ADR-137 branch emitted only the collinearity, so `מעגל O` / `BD⊥AC` / `AC קוטר` verified green with A,C floating (the verifier checks only what the commands assert). The branch now also asserts `point-on-circle` for any existing endpoint not already a member (`ctx.circleMembers`; idempotent for real chord endpoints — the ADR-099 lowering). Sibling grep: the bare `exists(a) && exists(b)` gate pattern appears only in `diameter`.

**Filed, not fixed (the deeper class limit):** stored lowered commands are context snapshots — editing an EARLIER step still never re-lowers LATER steps' utterances (replay reruns the engine, never the parser). The ADR-242 audit surfaces exactly this on load; an in-session "re-read later steps after an edit" is a possible follow-up if it bites in practice.

**Tests.** Scenario `diameter-edit-rereads-at-position` (the operator's exact sequence incl. the ✎ edit — the harness gained an `{ edit: { step, to } }` form replicating commitEdit→replaceGroup) and `diameter-on-existing-free-points`; both assert on-circle radii, |AC| = 2r, BD ⊥ AC. Full suite green, build clean.

## ADR-242 — load-time honesty audit: a figure file's stored lowering is checked against the CURRENT parser (drift + dropped labels)

**Status.** Accepted (2026-07-06). Operator: a file saved on the server drew the same broken figure when loaded locally ("uploading a file doesn't really run through the steps… some validation should be made"). *Files: `src/store/loadAudit.ts` (new), `src/App.tsx` (`loadFigureFile`), i18n (`file.loadAudit`), `load-audit.test.ts`.*

**What load does (unchanged, by design).** A `.geo.json` stores utterance + lowered commands per fact; load replays the COMMANDS (deterministic restore: an LLM step never re-escalates, `cmd.branch` survives — ADR-232). So the file is a parser-output snapshot: a parser fix never reaches an old file, and a partial lowering (the ADR-240 file) replays broken everywhere while re-parsing IDENTICALLY — the fixtures net's drift check alone certifies such a file healthy.

**Decision.** `auditLoadedFigure(facts)` — read-only, budgeted (3 s; each step costs one prefix replay) — runs after a successful load with two probes per uttered step: **dropped** (`droppedNewLabels` over the STORED commands — a stated label the save never covered; subsumes drift for the step) and **drift** (the utterance re-parses to different commands today). Load still opens exactly as saved (never destructive, one undo); findings raise a PERSISTENT note naming the step rows and pointing at ✎ — which, since ADR-241, re-reads a step against its prefix context and IS the per-step re-lower path. The operator's actual file yields exactly `step 2 "A ו C נמצאות על המעגל" (C)`.

**Deliberately not done:** auto re-lowering on load (an old file whose utterances re-parse differently may be the student's intended figure; and bulk re-parse would re-escalate nothing but could reshape a figure silently — the student chooses per step). The fixtures net keeps its CI role; adding the `dropped` differential there is a natural follow-up.

**Tests.** `load-audit.test.ts`: the operator's file verbatim (→ the `dropped` finding), a pre-ADR-241 `set-collinear` snapshot (→ `drift`), a current-parser file (→ clean). Full suite green, build clean.

## ADR-243 — T2 coverage fill, first tranche: the concyclic evidence enrichment (87/102), medians 15–17, congruence criteria 18–21, midsegments 62–67, bisectors 75/78/80

**Context.** T2 (docs/18 §10) fills the theorem table in the measured priority order, against the assertions T1 left waiting. Operator: "let's move on to next phase." This tranche = the widest evidence fix + the top three absent families by measured demand.

**1. The concyclic evidence enrichment (the T1 worklist's widest item — 8 questions).** "Quadrilateral EABF inscribed in circle M" lowers to `circumcircle`(3 points) + `set-concyclic`(4); the 4th point was invisible to `circleMembers` (structural-by-design — the parser shares it), so 87 never saw a complete quad. Fix in the spine's OWN hint layer (`buildMatchCtx`, where `tangentPoints` lives): a `concyclic` constraint ties to the circle sharing ≥3 of its points and the rest join its members. Symbolic, zero engine change. Additionally the 87 matcher gains the operator's **B2c ruling** (ground-truth review, 2026-07-03: *"#87 surfaces GREEN whenever ≥4 points are stated on a circle — a drawn quad is NOT required"*), superseding the old quad-only gate: B9/B13/B17/B21's two-circle figures announce 87 from their stated memberships. **Corpus flips: 87 gaps→expect in B3/B9/B16/B17/B19/B21/B23, and 102 in B19** (the enrichment feeds the same-chord matcher too).

**2. Three families tabled (16 ids, statements byte-exact from 07):**
- **Medians/centroid 15/16/17** (family `triangle`): `medianFacts` — a `midpoint` fact + a drawn apex→midpoint segment with the triangle's sides drawn (the ADR-218 DRAWN gate); covers the named-median lowering AND a hand-built midpoint+segment. One median → 16 (background); ≥2 medians of ONE triangle → 15/17 (headline, the two-bisectors→80 precedent). **B3/B7: planned→expect.**
- **Congruence criteria 18/19/20/21** (family `congruence`, headline): ONE constellation matcher — stated equalities/angle-equalities distributed over two typed-or-structural triangles. A stated `△ABC ≅ △DEF` (which lowers to exactly 3 side equalities) lands as full SSS → **20 certain**; a partial constellation surfaces the SPECIFIC criterion it suggests, **amber** (2 sides + included stated angle → 18; non-included → 21; 2 angles + a side → 19). This realises the operator's own motivating example ("3 equal segments → probably congruent triangles") in the TABLE, ahead of the T5 archetype. **The no-reveal line the never-guard itself enforced: a SHARED side does NOT count toward the constellation** — a first draft auto-paired it and #20 instantly fired on B8's kite halves (△ABC/△ADC over the drawn diagonal), which is exactly ה's step; the shared side's equality is the student's own observation (B8 and B13 both treat it as the aha). New never-guards lock it: B8 +20, B13 +18, B14 +18/19, B17 +18–21.
- **Midsegments 62–67** (family `midsegment`): declared (the ADR-199/222 `shape-variant` construct, L1) or **entailed** (§7a L2: a drawn segment JOINING two STATED midpoints — hosts sharing one vertex = triangle 62/63/64; disjoint hosts whose four ends form one stated 4-gon = trapezoid 65/66/67). 62/65 headline; 63/66 background; the converses 64/67 amber background (D2). **B7: 62 planned→expect; B23: 62/63 → never** (its D,E are midpoints only EMERGENTLY — the ground truth's "a midsegment hint collapses ב").
- **Bisectors 75/78/80** (family `triangle` for now — no new i18n family key while the locale files are another session's live edit; T3's authoring pass may re-family): `bisectorStatements` — a `bisector` line spec OR the "AD bisects ∠BAC" lowering (`set-angle-ratio` k=1, shared vertex + shared arm), **excluding a shared vertex that is a circle centre** (that form is the ADR-116 arc-equality lowering — arc talk, not a stated bisector; locked by a matcher test). ≥1 → 78 headline + 75 background; ≥2 at distinct vertices of one stated triangle → 80 headline (Q2/Q4's "two bisectors → incenter"). **79 → `needs-construct`** (the equidistant-from-sides premise needs point-to-LINE distance, which has no construct); 77 (ratio-cevian converse) and 81 (incircle existence — needs the incircle-construct fingerprint) stay planned.

**3. Corpus-gate hardening (found by the fills):** the T1 wiring asserted parse-commit only, letting a FAILING build group hide — B13's "line GB meets circle O at D" group fails ("over-constrained: |GA| = |AC| cannot hold") although the figure is constructible (A the midpoint of GC), so D never exists and 87 there is a BUILD gap, not a matcher gap. The b-corpus test now asserts `lastError === null` per question, with a documented **`knownBuildIssue`** bucket pinning B13's exact message (an engine finding of the ADR-229/230 solver-routing class — filed, not fixed in T2). All other 21 questions build clean.

## ADR-244 — two CONCENTRIC circles: circle identity decouples from the centre letter; the pair macro, qualifier resolution at the parse seam, and the ambiguous-circle clarification

**Context.** Operator (2026-07-06): *"שני מעגלים בעלי מרכז משותף O gives me just one circle"* — the bagrut Q6 family (two circles, common centre O; chords of "המעגל החיצוני" and "המעגל הפנימי"). Live behaviour (log session `3k5jezuu`): the He phrase escalated to the LLM, which decomposed reasonably into TWO canonical circle steps — but the second `circle-O` command collapsed into a RESIZE of the first (the ADR-011 override), so one circle was created at r=5 and resized to 3. The En phrase was worse: the plain `circle` rule claimed "two circles with a common center O" and HALF-parsed it to one circle, silently dropping "two" (§6 honesty). And "מיתר במעגל החיצוני/הפנימי" silently attached to the one circle — the stated qualifier discarded.

**Class.** *A reference to one of several circles sharing a centre is unrepresentable, because circle identity IS the centre letter* — at three seams: id minting (`circleId(centre)` = `circle-<centre>`), reference resolution (`ParseContext.circles` = centre letters; `resolveCenter`/`circleContaining` return centre letters), and the engine hint `circleMembers` (keyed by centre letter, so a pair's member sets would merge). The engine solver/renderer were already multi-circle-clean (per-id `Circle` objects, the tangent-circles corpus); the defect was the reference model.

**Decision (operator choices 2026-07-06: roles bind at creation; max 2 per centre; radii sized by ordinary distance givens, no radius-words):**
- **A. Identity.** The first circle centred at O keeps `circle-O` (back-compat: saved `.geo.json`, every existing figure); the concentric sibling is `circle-O-2`. The ROLE (outer/inner) is a binding, not part of the id.
- **B. The pair macro** (`concentricCircles`, before `circle`): "שני מעגלים בעלי מרכז משותף O" / "two concentric circles centered at O" / "two circles with a common center O" → two `ifAbsent` free-radius circles (seeds apart) + **`set-radius-order`** binding `circle-O` = OUTER, `circle-O-2` = INNER. Binding at creation is pure GAUGE — two unnamed same-centre circles are interchangeable until first referenced — so it asserts nothing (ADR-052-clean: both radii stay free DOFs; `ifAbsent` keeps a pre-stated size and makes re-statement idempotent).
- **C. The radius-order REQUIREMENT** (never a driven constraint): `apply` marks the inner circle (`innerOf`), the givens verifier checks r(inner) < r(outer) (`figure.v.radiusOrder`), and since `meetsRequirements` already gates every displayed config on a clean verifier, the sampler / "show another configuration" skip order-violating radii with ZERO new gate machinery. A genuinely contradicted order (the student sizes the inner bigger) surfaces amber. Worst-case cost: one O(1) check per verify — no new loops, no new sampler (M3-clean).
- **D. Qualifier resolution at the parse seam** (`withConcentricResolution`, the ADR-119 post-pass pattern — the chokepoint, so EVERY circle-consuming rule gains it at once): rules keep minting the outer id; an INNER qualifier ("המעגל הפנימי/הקטן", "the inner/smaller circle" — adjacency to the circle noun required, so "נקודה חיצונית" never misreads) rewrites the refs to `circle-O-2`; no qualifier → STATED MEMBERSHIP disambiguates (all the command's known member points side with one circle); otherwise → a new **`ambiguous-circle`** clarification (the ADR-164 pattern) — never a silent pick, never an LLM guess. A third same-centre circle lands in the same gate (refused with the clarification — the max-2 scope). Sliders: a paired centre's two radius sliders are labelled outer/inner (`dof.radiusOuter/Inner`).
- **E. `circleMembers` re-keyed by circle id** (entry per circle OBJECT, centre carried) so the pair's member sets stay apart; `ParseContext.circleMembers` gains optional `id`, `ParseContext.concentric` carries the pairs (derived from `innerOf` in `buildParseCtx`, which also DEDUPES `circles` so "the circle" still resolves to the one referenceable centre); per-centre "already a member" guards union via `membersOfCenter`.

**Sibling audit (the grep for the class).** Fixed with the mechanism: the En half-parse (the macro claims it); `CARRIER_RELATION_TAIL` misreading the qualifier's comparative ("במעגל הגדול"/"the larger circle") as a length relation — excluded by adjacency to the circle noun; `llm.ts`'s per-centre members map silently OVERWRITING a pair's first entry (now unions; `concentric` threaded into LLM step re-parse); `geoStore.extensionsClear`'s per-centre member lookup (now exact by id). Verified safe unchanged: ADR-230's `radiusCircleForDistance` already routes `OA=4` per membership (`pointLiesOnCircle` per circle id — the operator's sizing path works on the pair with no change); rename/swap (`relabelId` rewrites label tokens inside structured ids, so `circle-O-2` → `circle-N-2`). Filed, not fixed: `theorems/context.ts` maps `circleMembers` entries to circle objects BY CENTRE (a concentric pair's inner entry gets the outer's object id in `MatchCtx` — a theorem-feed fidelity nit on concentric figures only, no crash; that file is another session's live edit).

**Tests.** `concentric.test.ts` (25: macro both locales + synonyms, unnamed centre, half-parse fix, idempotent re-statement, qualifier resolution across chord/on-circle/set-radius/arc rules He+En, membership disambiguation, ambiguous → clarify, different-centre untouched, verifier order check both ways + `innerOf`); scenario **`two-concentric-circles-q6`** (the operator's figure: pair → outer chord AD → inner chord BC → B,C on AD → E on outer; asserts memberships per circle, inner < outer, B,C within AD, verifier clean); catalog entry (He+En, guard-tested); `shadow-allowlist` +`concentricCircles → circle` (the coarser rule reading the same words as ONE circle is the exact bug). Full suite green (2699+25); 2-D build clean (`vite build`; `tsc -b` at the time of this change was red only on the PARALLEL session's in-flight `src3d` edits, which are not part of this change).

## ADR-245 — inscription roles are assigned by the CONTAINER MARKER (ב / "in"), not by word order; a definite unnamed shape reference binds to THE existing polygon

**Context.** Operator (2026-07-06): *"I see we don't have support for במרובע חסום מעגל"* — and the live session (`ufxrtyp2`) shows it was worse than missing: `במרובע ABCD חסום מעגל O` parsed OK and silently built the **converse** figure (quad ABCD riding circle O — every vertex `point-on-circle`, every row ✓), and `במרובע חסום מעגל`, typed right after `ABCD מרובע`, minted a **fresh** quad EFGH inscribed in a circle, ignoring the quad the student was talking about. The class is old: `במשולש ABC חסום מעגל` had built a **circumcircle** in production since 2026-06-22 (session `1dela1c9`).

**Class.** *An inscription statement's subject/container roles are decided by word ORDER, not by the grammatical container marker* — `isCircleInPolygon` tested which word came first (circle word before polygon word ⇒ incircle). Order is a proxy: Hebrew passives invert freely, and the bagrut-standard container-first form ("במרובע … חסום מעגל") flips the roles, so the parser built the exact converse of what the student said — the worst honesty failure (a wrong figure with all-green rows, the same "cardinal sin" family as ADR-052). The mirror inversion (`במעגל O חסום מרובע ABCD` → was routed to the *incircle*) and the poly-word-list gaps (`מעגל חסום בדלתון` → built a kite-ON-circle; `במקבילית` → not-handled) are members of the same class. A second class rode the same session: *a definite unnamed shape reference ("במרובע" — THE quad) mints a new auto-named shape instead of binding to the existing one* — the polygon edition of the ADR-029 implicit-circle pattern.

**Decision.**
- **A. Container-marker discrimination.** `isCircleInPolygon` now resolves the CONTAINER as the noun carrying the "in" preposition — Hebrew's ב prefix (`במשולש`, `בטרפז`, `בתוך ה…`; stacked prefixes like `שבמרובע` still carry it) or English `in/inside [a/the] <noun>` — wherever it sits in the sentence. Exactly one marked noun decides; order remains only the no-marker/both-marked fallback (`incircle of ABC` has no marker and keeps working by order). One statement = one semantics (design-rules §2.3), regardless of position.
- **B. Shared poly-word lists.** The polygon alternation is extracted to `POLY_WORDS_EN`/`POLY_WORDS_HE` (now incl. parallelogram·מקבילית, kite·דלתון, מצולע) and shared by the marker test, the order fallback, and the `circumscribes` branch — the drift between per-regex copies is what mis-routed the kite (missing word ⇒ order test failed ⇒ the converse rule claimed it).
- **C. Kite incircle.** `incircle` gains `kind === 'kite'` lowering to the ADR-138 `shape-variant` macro (the same lowering the standalone/inscribed kite uses); every kite is tangential (Pitot from the two equal adjacent pairs), so the tangency force is always satisfiable. A parallelogram incircle (was not-handled) now builds via the existing tangential flex.
- **D. Definite binding.** `ParseContext.polygons` (vertex lists, derived in `buildParseCtx`) + `existingPolygon(ctx, n)`: an inscription statement that names NO vertices binds to the existing polygon when **exactly one** n-gon is in the figure — in both `incircle` ("במרובע חסום מעגל" → the incircle of ABCD) and `inscribedPolygon` ("מרובע חסום במעגל" → ABCD becomes concyclic, the ADR-099 lowering). Zero or 2+ candidates keep the previous auto-name behaviour (ambiguity is never guessed). Named vertices always win over the binding.

**Sibling audit.** Log scan (`grep 'חסום' logs/debug-log.jsonl`, 40+ distinct phrasings): the inverted forms `במרובע ABCD חסום מעגל O` (55×), `במרובע חסום מעגל` (7×), `במשולש ABC חסום מעגל` (1dela1c9) — all converse-built, all now route to the incircle; every canonical form (`X חסום במעגל` 3000+×, `מעגל חסום בX`) verified unchanged (the marker test agrees with the old order test on all of them, by construction: the canonical forms carry the same ב marker the order implied). The active-voice branch (`חוסם`/circumscribes) shares the widened word list. Filed, not fixed: a named triangle-shape word on an *incircle* utterance ("מעגל חסום במשולש שווה שוקיים") is silently dropped (the ADR-117 class, incircle edition — pre-existing, unchanged by this fix).

**Tests.** `inverted-inscription.test.ts` (20: both locales × both directions × ordered + inverted, the kite/parallelogram siblings, binding — bind/zero/ambiguous/named-wins); scenarios **`incircle-inverted-passive-quad`** + **`incircle-definite-ref-binds-existing-quad`** (the operator's exact sequences; tangency of all four sides asserted geometrically); catalog +2 (inverted phrasing, kite incircle — guard-tested in both locales).

## ADR-244 — T2 evidence worklist closed: the radius-⟂ tangency fingerprint, line-through-centre diameters, stated arc-equality, and the kite ⊇ rhombus hierarchy

**Context.** The four evidence gaps ADR-243 left open (each a documented `gaps` assertion in the B-corpus), closed at the layer each originates.

**1. The radius-⟂ tangency fingerprint (tangentPoints path 3) — the widest item.** A tangency stated against an EXISTING point/line lowers to a radius-⟂ CONSTRAINT (ADR-075/115/233), which `tangentPoints` never read — the whole 105/107/108/109 family missed on B4/B9/B19. The fingerprint: a `perpendicular` whose one side is centre→T with T ON that circle (ENRICHED membership — B19's touch point F is a member only via its quad's `set-concyclic`, so the ADR-243 enrichment is extracted to a shared `enrichedCircleMembers`), and whose other side is the tangent line — T an endpoint of it (`from` = the far end, so two such tangencies from one point fire 108/109) or T an on-segment marker riding it (the ADR-075 "AB tangent at F" form). The ⟂ may live in the constraints list OR be EMBEDDED as a point's driving constraint (`on-segment-solved.constraint`, `solve.constraint`, `solve.also` — B19's F carries its ⟂ inside the object). **Flips: B4 +105/107/108/109, B9 +105/107, B19 +105/107.**

**2. A stated line THROUGH the centre is a stated diameter.** "the line AO cuts circle O at C and D" lowers to `line-through` + two `line-circle-intersection`s — no collinear-through-centre datum, so `statedDiameterFacts` missed it (B15's 103 gap). Now: a line-through with the centre as an endpoint + two crossings of that line with the circle = a stated diameter (attributed to the completing crossing). **Flip: B15 +103.**

**3. A stated ARC EQUALITY announces 92.** "arc CA = arc AF" lowers to equal CENTRAL angles (ADR-116: `set-angle-ratio` k=1, both vertices the centre) — exactly the correspondence #92 states, missed because the 92 matcher read only `arc-midpoint` constructs. Same ADR-210 gate (given centre). **Flip: B6 +92.** (Deliberately k=1 only; a stated arc RATIO stays for a later authoring pass.)

**4. Kite ⊇ rhombus (the hierarchy gap).** `detectShapes` classifies the MOST SPECIFIC type, so B14's forced BEGD reports as a RHOMBUS and `kiteEvidence`'s detected path (type 'kite' only) never fired 37/38. Now the kite family reads the whole kite-class (`kite | rhombus | square`) at L3 — but ONLY for EMERGENT shapes: a quad the student TYPED as rhombus/square is excluded (its own family bundle 55/56 owns it; the kite lens adds value only for the discovery). **Flip: B14 +37/38.** B19's 104 stays an honest gap (its right angle is STRUCTURAL — the right-triangle command — and `rightInscribedFacts` reads stated 90° facts only; noted for the T4 observed lane).

**Tests.** 5 new matcher locks (constraint-form tangency single + pair, line-through-centre diameter, arc-equality 92, typed-rhombus kite exclusion); 11 corpus bucket flips gaps→expect. Full suite green, `tsc -b` clean.

## ADR-246 — T3: relevance as NAMED rank bands — pointedness, subsumption, rankTrace, and the tested display cap

**Context.** Stage 3/5 of the overnight run (docs/18 §5, §9.2–9.3). R3's diagnosis: the sort was salience → recency → numeric id, "prioritized" had no design and no test. The operator's rulings bind: ballpark importance-first, discrete bands, NO percentages (D3); subsumed entries fold with a "covered by #X" label (D6).

**Decision.**
1. **`pointedness: 'pointed' | 'standard' | 'generic'`** authored on every def (a REQUIRED field — the compiler is the totality guard). Pointed = the given announces the theorem in real practice (103/104, 92/94, 105/107/108/109, 87/201, 62/65, 15/17, 18–21, 30/31, 73, 78/80, 82/85/86, 37/38, 22); generic = the family backgrounds (1/2/4/6/10–14/16/24/35/36/72/75/84/91/95/97/98, appendix); standard = the rest. The corpus-frequency sheet stays the offline calibration aid.
2. **`subsumes` edges (D6):** 87 ⊐ {99, 102} (the generic same-circle inscribed-angle pair folds once the cyclic quad is stated); 201 ⊐ {8}. Demote-not-remove: a demoted entry drops to band 5, keeps its row (muted, "מכוסה על ידי #X"), stays citable.
3. **The band sort** (in `detectTheorems`, headline-before-background unchanged): band 0 intent-aligned (reserved for T5 boosts) · 1 new+pointed · 2 new · 3 pointed · 4 standard · 5 demoted; within a band: discovery level (L1<L2<L3), `certain` before `possible`, recency, id — **the id tiebreak drops to LAST**. Band 2 above band 3 is the §5 design's KEPT "what did my last fact buy me" contract — locked by a test so a future "pointedness always wins" change is a conscious decision.
4. **`rankTrace`** on every entry (`band N (name); pointedness; L#; tier[; ● new]`) — surfaced as the row tooltip, so ranking bugs are readable the way the verifier made figure-correctness readable.
5. **`visibleFeed(entries, cap=7)`** — the FR-TH-6 display contract as a PURE shared function: ≤7 visible headline rows before the expandable "עוד משפטים שחלים" fold; bands 0–1 never capped. The App consumes it; the corpus flood budgets assert the SAME function (§9.3 — anti-flood stops being a vibe).
6. **Ranking assertions (§9.2):** the Q5–Q7 corpus gains per-step `top` (must appear within the first max(3, |top|) visible rows) on the steps where order matters pedagogically — Q5's ∠ACD=90 → 104 leads; Q6/Q7's diameters → 103/104; Q7's tangent → 105/107. The B-corpus asserts the cap corpus-wide at every final feed.

**App wiring:** the headline section renders `visibleFeed` with the fold expander; demoted rows are muted with the D6 label; the tooltip carries the rankTrace. Two i18n keys (`theorems.moreFold`, `theorems.coveredBy`).

**Tests.** `t3-ranking.test.ts` (9 locks: diameter-leads, pointedness-vs-recency, the deliberate band-2 contract, both subsumption edges incl. labels, rankTrace totality, certain-before-possible, the cap + never-cap rules); corpus `top` + flood budgets. Theorems+render suites 847 green; full 2-D suite + `tsc -b` + build clean.

The spine stays coordinate-free; an absent layer means the observed paths are simply silent — so the corpus gates (which pass no `observed`) are untouched by construction.

**Scoped out, recorded:** an EMERGENT-midsegment observation (a segment that happens to join two midpoints, never stated) needs a special-line detector that doesn't exist in the sampled layers — noted as the T4 follow-up in docs/18; forced-PARALLEL classes are likewise not a `RelationsResult` output today.

**Tests.** `t4-observed.test.ts` (7 locks, synthetic observed inputs — fast, deterministic): each path fires at L3 amber and stays silent without `observed`; a non-right forced angle and a disjoint equal-class don't misfire; the L1 view never shows an observed entry (the D4 default holds).
