## ADR-248 — T5: the PRINCIPLES lane — the operator's teacher tips, the editable catalog, and intent archetypes with band-0 boosts (the D5 pedagogy amendment)

**Context.** Stage 5/5 of the overnight run (docs/18 §6, §9.4, §10-T5). The concepts feed (ADR-214, 2 entries) becomes the first-class PRINCIPLES lane — "things I, as a teacher, can tell you: whenever something is given, or emerges from the diagram, think about something" (the operator's verbatim design elevation).

**Decision.**
1. **`src/theorems/principles.ts`** — `PRINCIPLE_TABLE` (`PrincipleDef { id, he, en, match, boosts? }`), `detectPrinciples` (same coordinate-free MatchCtx + attribution machinery), `activeBoosts`. `concepts.ts` stays as a deprecated shim (aliases), so every existing import keeps working.
2. **The operator-editable catalog** (D7): a new "עקרונות" section in [docs/10-pedagogy.md](docs/10-pedagogy.md) — one row per principle (slug | Hebrew tip | English tip). The integrity guard asserts `PRINCIPLE_TABLE` matches it **byte-for-byte, total both ways** (the 07 pattern applied to the operator's own text). Dictating a principle in a session lands it in both places, tested.
3. **Eight starter principles** — the 2 migrated concepts (right-triangle-complementary; parallels-seek-similar-triangles, now boosting 69/71/72/73) + six §6 archetypes: **congruence-hunt** (the operator's motivating example — ≥2 stated cross-triangle equalities/angle-pairs → "אולי חפיפת משולשים?", boosts 18–21/30), **bisector-setup** (boosts 75/77/78/80), **midsegment-setup** (two stated midpoints on sides sharing a vertex — hints BEFORE the joining segment exists; boosts 62–67), **thales-chain** (a stated diameter + inscribed vertices; boosts 103/104/31), **power-of-a-point** (external secant/tangent hub; appendix-supporting tip, no boosts), **median-hunt** (boosts 15/16/17/31/32).
4. **Band-0 boosts:** `DetectInput.boosts` — the App passes `activeBoosts(principleFeed)` (the union of the top **2** active principles' boosts, §6); a boosted id that FIRED lifts to band 0 ("intent-aligned"), outranking even its own demotion. Boosts never invent an entry — they only lift what fired (locked by test).
5. **The D5 pedagogy amendment** (formally revising 16 §10 B1): B1 rejected *knowing the actual question*; the operator's later ruling admits **probabilistic direction-hints from the stated givens' shape alone**. Guardrails, enforced structurally where possible: family-direction questions only (a test asserts no tip instantiates point labels), tier amber, ≤2 boosting / ≤3 visible, the no-reveal ids (68/70/76) can be pointed at by FAMILY in a tip but stay untabled and uninstantiated.
6. **App:** the 💡 section renders the principles (≤3 + overflow count); i18n `principles.title`/`principles.more`.

**Tests.** `t5-principles.test.ts` (20 locks): the catalog↔table byte guard (total both ways), the operator's 3-equalities scenario (§9.4's first gate — congruence-hunt activates, #20 lands band 0 at the top of the feed with `intent-aligned` in its rankTrace), boost-never-invents, per-archetype activations incl. the earlier-than-the-matcher midsegment hint, the anti-flood constants, and the D5 no-instantiation guard. Theorems suite 807 green; full 2-D suite + `tsc -b` + build clean.

## ADR-249 — GUI overhaul: sidebar section CARDS, progressive disclosure, one type scale, one toolbar tray

**Context.** Operator: "overhaul the GUI — reconsider each element location, what should be visible and what hidden, ensure font consistency." A fresh audit (code + live screenshots) found: the sidebar was one flat stack of ~13 blocks with no visual grouping; undo/redo/clear and the display options rendered even on an empty session; three IDENTICAL full-width purple buttons ("show another configuration" / "view relations" / "detect shapes") stacked with loose status lines floating between them; examples shown twice on the empty state and expanded forever; the ✓/✗/○ legend always present; TWO font stacks (index.css vs the `page` style) plus `ui-monospace` mixed into Hebrew UI text; a font-size zoo (10/11/12/12.5/13/14/18/20); the canvas toolbar was 7+ buttons in three inconsistent shapes; and the i18n `actions.language` key existed with NO rendered toggle.

**Decision.**
1. **`src/ui/theme.ts`** — the single source of design tokens: a fixed type scale (`fs` 11/12/13/14/16/20), a small palette (blue = act, violet = explore/insight, semantic green/amber/red), and shared control shapes (`btn.primary/accent/accentOutline/ghost/subtle/chip`, `card`, `pill`, `foldToggle`, `sectionTitle`). `index.css` sets the ONE font stack ('Segoe UI' first) inherited by form controls; **no per-element `fontFamily` anywhere** (all `ui-monospace` uses dropped — Hebrew UI text now renders in one face).
2. **Sidebar = section cards** (white, bordered) instead of the flat stack: **Build** (input + send + symbols fold + examples), **Steps**, **Explore**, **Theorems**, **Principles**; a quiet "תצוגה" fold at the bottom.
3. **Progressive disclosure:** examples are fully shown while the canvas is empty and FOLD automatically once building starts (reopenable); the ✓/✗/○ legend appears only when some row isn't a plain ✓; undo/redo/clear hide on an empty session; the display options fold (open by default — see 6).
4. **Steps card header** carries the workflow chrome: the DOF cue as a compact pill (blue "N degrees of freedom" / green "✓ fully determined" — was a loose line floating between buttons) + undo/redo/clear as small in-context utilities (they act on the step list, so they live with it).
5. **Explore card:** ONE loud violet CTA ("show another configuration") + relations/shapes as half-width quiet outline toggles that fill with their on-canvas layer colour (teal/indigo) while active; the radius sliders (ADR-051) live here too — they ARE exploration.
6. **The discovery dial moved INTO the theorems card**, directly under its title — operator (mid-overhaul): "the תצוגה part is hidden and it's important, especially the levels of discovery." The dial now lives WITH the feed it controls (never buried in settings), and the display fold defaults OPEN.
7. **Canvas toolbar = one tray** (`toolbarTray` in Figure.tsx): file pair | image pair | zoom trio inside a single rounded container with thin dividers; the transform toggle gets the same tray; all controls one height.
8. **Language toggle rendered** in the header (the dormant `actions.language` key — label names the OTHER language). New i18n keys `explore.title`, `examples.title` in both locales (key-parity test still green).

**Consequences.** Pure presentation — zero engine/store/parser changes; the renderer stays a pure consumer. All behaviour is preserved (every control still reachable); only location, visibility, and styling changed.

**Tests.** Full suite green (3180 passed / 156 files) + `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean; before/after verified in a live browser (empty state, built figure, relations+shapes layers active).

**Amendment (same day) — the theorem feed SHIPS LIVE.** Operator: "remove the fixed uncheck in prod about showing theorems." The `THEOREMS_ENABLED` dev-only gate (and its `VITE_ENABLE_THEOREMS` escape hatch) is removed: `showTheorems` defaults ON everywhere, the תצוגה checkbox is always enabled (the student's off-switch), and the discovery dial rides the theorems card (this ADR §6). This supersedes the "not shipped live yet" posture the flag encoded since Phase 6a; the docs/18 operator gates (play-and-judge the T3 order, author principles, the 6c ship pass) remain open as QUALITY follow-ups on a now-live feed.

## ADR-250 — honesty pair: a stated CARRIER is drawn, a stated NUMBER is never silently dropped

**Context.** Operator prod session `m68n76e7` (2026-07-07, the first live session after ADR-249): (1) "when I say D is on the continuation of BC, I want BD drawn; same when I say E is on AD — only ED was drawn" — the student hand-typed DA/DB/EC/BE to complete the figure; (2) "I wrote שוטח and not שטח — it was silently dropped and marked ok" — `שטח AEB גדול פי 2.25 משוטח משולש CED` was claimed by the TRIANGLE rule (first-match-wins) and committed as a bare △AEB with the row ✓; the 2.25 ratio vanished until the operator ✎-fixed the spelling.

**Classes (17-design-rules §1).**
1. *"A statement that PLACES a point via a named carrier draws only part (or none) of the carrier the student named."* The draw-the-stated-geometry convention (FR-IN-7, the midpoint/angle rules) was per-rule discipline — `pointOnExtension` drew nothing, `lineMeetsCircle` drew only the off-circle half. Sibling audit: `extend-onto-circle` (apply), the external-secant rules, and the ADR-194 tangent-secant rule already draw; the plain `pointOnSegment` family relied on the carrier already existing.
2. *"An utterance whose matching rule consumes only part of its stated content is committed as the partial meaning — stated magnitudes outside the matched span are silently dropped."* The label member of this class was closed by ADR-089 (`droppedNewLabels`); the NUMERIC member was open. Design-rules §6 names the invariant verbatim: "no stated magnitude is ever silently dropped."

**Decision.**
1. **`withCarrierSegments`** — a parse-seam post-pass (the ADR-119 chokepoint, NOT per-rule memory): every `point-on-segment` command gets its base carrier `segment a–b` ensured in the batch (before the rider; idempotent, creates missing endpoints), and an `extension` rider also gets the stated leg `segment b–id` (after it) — so "D על המשך BC" shows B—C—D. `pointOnExtension`'s existing-id branch (set-line, ADR-086) draws base+leg itself (a generic `set-line` is a LINE statement — blanket-drawing it would violate ADR-077's segment-vs-line distinction, so only the rule that KNOWS the student said המשך draws). `lineMeetsCircle` now emits BOTH halves split at the crossing (`segment onCircle–R` + `segment other–R`) — no overlapping collinear strokes.
2. **`droppedGivenNumbers(utterance, commands)`** — the numeric sibling of `droppedNewLabels`, wired at the SAME seams (App.submit grammar gate → escalate to the LLM, whose job is typos; the LLM-path honesty gate → refuse and name the value; the App-faithful scenario harness gates). "Accounted" is deliberately generous (a false account only suppresses a warning; a false drop would break a working input): command numeric payloads incl. digits inside symbolic strings, string-array lengths (regular N-gon), fraction a/b → value, percent → /100, π-sizes nπ → n/2 (circumference→radius) or √n (area→radius); label-glued subscript digits are blanked. A catalog-wide sweep asserts zero false positives on every supported example, both locales.
3. **`showTheorems` defaults OFF** (same-day operator follow-up to the ADR-249 Am. ship): the feed stays live in prod but the student opts in from תצוגה.

**What stays open (named honestly):** a dropped stated WORD-magnitude with no digits (e.g. "רבע" in a typo'd ratio) is still invisible to the guard — full leftover-span accounting across ~200 rules is the complete mechanism (ADR-024's direction) and is filed, not bundled.

**Tests.** `adr-250.test.ts` (typo flags [2.25]; corrected phrasing → `set-area-ratio` + silent guard; fraction/percent/π/N-gon/subscript accounting; catalog-wide zero-false-positive sweep; He+En extension draw; set-line branch draw; both secant halves) + scenario `m68n76e7-carrier-draw-and-typo-ratio` (the operator's verbatim sequence through the App-faithful gate, ratio ≈ 2.25 verified end-to-end).

## ADR-251 — download the question as a Word document: deterministic .docx of the verbatim givens beside the figure (FR-HS-11)

**Context.** Operator: "download the question text based on what the user entered, like a textbook — a Word doc in Hebrew where the user will see the text that builds the image and the image itself; if Hebrew RTL/bidi is a nightmare, HTML + save-as is the fallback." Today the figure exports as a PNG (FR-HS-5) or a `.geo.json` (FR-HS-10), but the *question* — the typed givens plus the figure, laid out as a printed exam problem — has no export. Operator decisions (asked one-by-one): **verbatim givens list** (not prose), **image beside the text** (textbook two-column), **a real `.docx`** generated client-side.

**Decision.**
1. **Verbatim, deterministic, no LLM.** The document lists the ENABLED steps' original utterances — one numbered line per submission group, first stated utterance per group, exactly the step list's on/off state (`src/export/questionLines.ts`). Utterance-less groups are **skipped**, never rendered as command-type joins (developer jargon isn't textbook text); every typed step carries its utterance and `.geo.json` persists it, so nothing real is lost. This is deliberately the low-tech cousin of **FR-HS-9/ADR-133** (the LLM "decompiler" prose export) and stays distinct from it.
2. **A real `.docx` via the `docx` library**, packed in the browser (`src/export/questionDoc.ts`, `Packer.toBlob`). The builder is **dynamically imported** in App so the ~368 kB library lives in its own lazy chunk — the main bundle is untouched until the button is clicked.
3. **RTL/bidi stance:** `w:bidi` on paragraphs + `w:rtl` on runs, the utterance text kept verbatim (no LRM/RLM injected) — the same Unicode bidi algorithm the browser step list already renders correctly. The flags are passed as `undefined` (never `false`) for LTR docs, so an English export carries no bidi marks at all. **List numbers are REAL Word numbering, never a literal `"1. "` prefix** — a European digit + neutral period at an RTL run boundary is the classic bidi-scramble (`.1`); Word's list number is layout chrome resolved by paragraph direction, outside the bidi text stream. Fonts: Arial (ascii/hAnsi — Latin labels, digits, ∠/⟂/°) + **David** (cs — the classic Israeli textbook Hebrew face), 12pt both scripts.
4. **Side-by-side layout = a single borderless 1×2 table** with `visuallyRightToLeft` for Hebrew (text cell renders on the RIGHT; English naturally reads text-left/image-right) — the reliable two-column recipe in OOXML. Image column: the existing clean `svgToPng` export (2× oversampled, `data-noexport` stripped) at a printed 8 cm width, height from the PNG's real aspect ratio — read from the **IHDR header bytes** (`pngDimensions`), no second async decode, node-testable.
5. **Wiring mirrors `onSaveFile`:** Figure (which owns the SVG + export cleanup) rasterises and hands the PNG blob UP via a new `onSaveQuestion(png)` prop; App pairs it with the facts, packs, and downloads `question-YYYY-MM-DD.docx` (the `figureFileName` pattern). Failures surface as the existing export ✕ flash. The button sits in the toolbar tray's export group, disabled when no enabled utterance exists. i18n: `canvas.saveQuestion` ("הורידו שאלה"/"Download question"), `questionDoc.given` ("נתון:"/"Given:").

**Consequences.** Pure export consumer — zero engine/store/parser changes. New deps: `docx` (runtime, lazy chunk), `jszip` (dev-only, the test unzips `word/document.xml` — a raw-buffer text search can't work, the XML is deflated inside the zip container). **Companion root fix (same session):** `parseGroundTruth` (theorem fill-order) now splits on `\r?\n` — a fresh git checkout on Windows (`core.autocrlf`) materializes the ground-truth `.md` with CRLF and the trailing `\r` defeated the `$`-anchored heading regex (JS `.` never matches `\r`), failing the suite on ANY fresh clone; the parser was line-ending-intolerant, not the file wrong.

**Escape hatch (not built).** If manual testing in desktop Word shows bidi scrambling on mixed Hebrew/Latin lines, the fallback is an HTML document (dir="rtl" is trivially correct) the user opens in Word and saves as .docx.

**Tests.** `src/export/__tests__/questionDoc.test.ts` — `questionLines` policies (enabled-only, group dedup, first-stated-utterance, jargon-free skip, trim, order); `pngDimensions` (IHDR parse + non-PNG refusal); the packed docx unzipped and asserted (verbatim Hebrew + ∠/° survive, `w:bidi`/`w:rtl`/`w:numPr`/`w:tbl`+`bidiVisual`/`w:drawing` present, `numbering.xml` + the PNG media part exist; the LTR doc carries none of the bidi marks). **Manual gate (operator):** open a real export in desktop Word — mixed-bidi line reads correctly, numbers on the right, figure beside the text at ~8 cm, David for Hebrew. **Gate PASSED (operator, 2026-07-10): "I confirm this works well"** — mixed He/Latin bidi renders correctly in desktop Word; the HTML escape hatch stays unbuilt.

## ADR-252 — the question export omits scaffolding steps (pure ink and helper markers state no given)

**Context.** Operator (2026-07-08): the .docx question export (ADR-251) "includes all steps that were entered, but these include some steps that are visual and not needed to understand the shape — such as marking nodes to create the line. They have no effect on the shape itself so I don't want them." Real sessions confirm the pattern: `ufxrtyp2` typed `OB`, `OD`, `OA`, `OC` (bare centre-to-vertex segments) after an incircle figure; `nro4p13n` typed `EA`; `h1nocczt` typed `O2N`, `O1N`. A textbook "נתון:" list states relations and definitions, never "draw OA" — and the drawn ink is already visible in the figure PNG sitting beside the text.

**Decision.** `questionLines` gains a **semantic scaffolding filter** (never a phrasing whitelist — the classification reads the LOWERED commands, so every phrasing in both languages inherits it):

1. **Scaffold-class step** — every enabled command in the submission group is either **pure ink** (`segment`, `line-through`: drawn strokes whose geometric content is trivially true of their endpoints) or a **value-less marker creating a NEW point** (`free-point free:true`, `point-on-segment` with no stated ratio, `point-on-circle` with no arc restriction, `point-on-line` — the ADR-036 slider markers). Anything stated stays: a ratio (`t`), typed pinned coordinates, an arc restriction (`between`), and every shape/circle/derived-point/constraint/measure command.
2. **Existing-point statements are never scaffolding** (design-rules M1): the marker kinds only qualify when their `id` is new in context — "C על DF" with C existing lowers to the same `point-on-segment` command but IS a collinearity given, and is kept.
3. **A later reference rescues a scaffold step.** A reverse pass keeps a scaffold group when a LATER KEPT group references anything it introduced — "נקודה G על AD" stays when "זווית GBA = 37" follows (the reader needs G's definition). The check cascades: a marker whose only consumer is an omitted bare segment is omitted with it (mark E, mark F, draw EF → all three omitted). Introductions are computed in context (`introducedIds` minus already-defined); references use the HOIST dependency scan `commandObjectIds` (now exported).

The filter is silent and export-only: the step list UI, replay, and `.geo.json` save are untouched — the figure still draws every step; only the exported givens text drops the lines a textbook would never print.

**Consequences.** `src/export/questionLines.ts` + one export-keyword change in `geoStore.ts`; zero engine/parser changes. The docx button's disabled state follows the filtered list (an all-scaffold figure exports nothing — nothing worth printing). **Companion environment fix (same session):** vitest's crawl EPERM'd on this machine — `dist-3d/` build output (not covered by the default `**/dist/**`) and a stale `.claude/worktrees/` repo copy contained Dropbox dehydrated placeholders; both are now in the vitest `exclude` list, and `jszip` (an ADR-251 dev dep installed on the other PC) needed `npm install` here.

**Tests.** `questionDoc.test.ts` — bare segments omitted; the marker→ink cascade; marker kept when a later given references it; a bare segment kept when its NEW endpoint is referenced later; existing-point membership kept AND keeping its carrier segment; stated ratio kept; pinned typed point kept; plus two REAL-parser end-to-end cases (the operator''s `ufxrtyp2` sequence `במרובע ABCD חסום מעגל O` + `OB/OD/OA/OC` → one line; the canonical square figure → all three lines). A fixture sweep confirmed all four saved figures keep every line (no false omissions).

## ADR-253 — default placements land in GENERAL POSITION (the one-anchor template spin)

**Context.** Operator session `ad66x493` (2026-07-08, bagrut kite figure): `AB קוטר במעגל O`, `C על המעגל`, `AC`, `AM`, `OM`, "AM חותך את OC בנקודה K" (LLM), `E על BO`, then the kite givens `OK=OE` and `MK=ME` — both refused *"cannot place E on segment BO so that |OK| = |OE|"*, on **every seed**. Trace: a bare `segment A M` creates its missing endpoint via `placeBase`, whose **one-anchor fit is a pure translation** (the fit's rotation is arbitrary and was resolved to identity), so M landed at A+(5,0) — **exactly where the diameter template had put B**, collinear with A,O,B. K = AM∩OC then collapsed onto O (|OK| = 0 exactly), making the kite constraints genuinely unsatisfiable *at that composition*. And the composition is the only one the apply gate ever judges: **the seed is applied AFTER the fold** (`applySeed` on the final construction, geoStore), so a fact that failed at apply time is already dropped before any seed moves M — `findValidConfig`'s sweep re-failed identically at every seed, and the step parked as "deferred" waiting for givens that could never come. An engine probe confirmed the class: the same constraints applied at ANY generic composition (M outside, inside, |OK| from 0.13 to 11.3) solve in milliseconds — only the exact degeneracy fails.

**Class (design-rules §1).** *A default placement of new free points may land in a measure-zero degenerate spot — coincident with an existing point, or exactly collinear through the anchor and an existing point — and default placements are the one position source with no genericity guarantee.* Every solver-produced position has escape machinery (multi-start, anti-collapse ADR-238, config search ADR-106); the raw template default had none. A degenerate default also *draws a relation the student never stated* (M shown at B; A,B,M shown collinear) — the ADR-052 cardinal sin in placement form. Deterministic siblings nobody reported: `square ABCD` + `AE` stacked E onto B; `rectangle` + `BE` put E exactly on line AB (any `X` → `XY` → `XZ` chain).

**Decision.** `placeBase` — the single chokepoint where template defaults are born — gains a **general-position guard**: with exactly ONE anchor (the case whose rotation is arbitrary), if the naive placement puts any NEW vertex within ~1.5% of the span of an existing point (the `pointsDistinct` bar) or **exactly** (1e-6·span — template arithmetic produces exact hits) on the infinite line through the anchor and an existing point, the fitted template is **spun around the anchor by golden-angle steps** (≤24) until every new vertex is generic. The identity is kept whenever it is already fine, so healthy figures place bit-identically. 0-anchor (offset-right, cannot coincide) and ≥2-anchor (frame fully pinned) cases are untouched.

**Sibling audit.** The parser's fixed-coordinate auto free-points (`{x:3,y:2}` ensure-exists ADR-236, the tangent apex `{x:6,y:0}`) are a cousin class (fixed literal defaults) — each is immediately driven/recruited by its construct, so they are left as-is and noted here. The circle-side seed (ADR-254) reuses this guard's helper (`degeneratePlacement`). **Residual limitation (filed, not fixed):** apply-time satisfiability is still judged at one composition — a *legitimately special solved* position (not a default) that hard-fails a later constraint has only the recruiter's multi-start to escape; if a real figure hits that, the fix is folding the seed into the fold (a placement-override two-pass replay), a much larger change than this session warranted.

**Consequences.** `src/engine/apply.ts` only (`spanAround` + `degeneratePlacement` + the spin in `placeBase`). The operator's exact sequence now builds green in ~3.7 s (was: permanent failure, ~35 s per failing replay). A chained bare segment (`AB` then `BC`) no longer draws a false straight continuation — the corner is honest (say `המשך`/`ישר ABC` for collinear). All 998 engine+store tests and all 184 scenarios pass unchanged.

**Tests.** `src/engine/__tests__/general-position.test.ts` (the AB+AM stack, the operator prefix, the square+AE sibling, determinism, identity-when-generic) + scenario `kite-EMKO-degenerate-default` (the operator's committed fact list end-to-end).

## ADR-254 — "M מחוץ למעגל / בתוך המעגל": a point's SIDE of a circle is a first-class statement

**Context.** Same session (`ad66x493`): the bagrut given "הנקודה M נמצאת מחוץ למעגל" was typed as `M מחוץ למעגל` and came back **not-understood** (LLM escalation — the vocabulary had only membership, `על המעגל`, so there was no canonical form to normalise into). M then entered the figure as an unconstrained endpoint of `AM` with no record it belongs outside — which is exactly the point the ADR-253 degeneracy then poisoned. The operator: "we are missing the engine instruction of putting a point inside or outside a circle."

**Class.** *A REGION statement about a point (which side of a circle it lies on) was unrepresentable* — not parseable, not recorded, not verified, not respected by sampling.

**Decision.** A new command `point-circle-side {id, circle, side: inside|outside}`, following the **ADR-244 radius-order shape** (a requirement, never a driven equality — an inequality has nothing to drive):

1. **Parser** — `pointVsCircle`: `M מחוץ למעגל [O]` / `בתוך המעגל` / `M is outside circle O` / `point M lies inside the circle`, subject lists per the ADR-076/240 convention (`M ו-N מחוץ למעגל`), the circle named or implicit (ADR-029, `resolveCenter`). Deliberately a TIGHT full match so the external-point compounds (`מנקודה E מחוץ למעגל יוצאים שני משיקים…`) keep going to their own rules. Registered in the catalog (which feeds the LLM prompt vocabulary automatically) and in `consumedCircleId` (a named-but-absent circle auto-materialises, the implicit-circle post-pass).
2. **Apply** — a NEW id becomes a **free point (2 DOF, ADR-052)** seeded on the stated side at 1.7r (outside) / 0.45r (inside), in general position via the ADR-253 helper (θ=0 — the textbook "external point to the right" — is exactly on a drawn diameter's line, so the golden spin walks off it; the centre itself is excluded from the clearance set, it anchors every candidate line). An EXISTING id is a *statement about that point* (M1, never a conflict — `commandConflict`'s structural reuse covers it): a non-pinned free point on the wrong side gets its default re-seated; anything else is left to the verifier.
3. **Verifier + sampling** — `checkGivens` re-derives the side from final coordinates (`figure.v.outsideCircle` / `insideCircle`, strict beyond the on-circle tolerance); `meetsRequirements` therefore gates the sampler and "show another configuration" to same-side configs, and a genuinely contradicted side (a determined point on the wrong side) reads amber, never silently dropped.
4. **Question export** — the command classifies as a stated GIVEN (ADR-252 `default: false` branch), so "M מחוץ למעגל" prints in the exported נתון list, as in the source question.

**Consequences.** `types.ts`, `apply.ts`, `verify.ts`, `parse.ts`, `catalog.ts`, locale keys. The DOF cue is untouched (a side constrains a region, not a DOF). With both ADRs the operator's full intended sequence — side statement included — builds and verifies green (~0.6 s), M strictly outside, kite equalities exact.

**Tests.** `src/parser/__tests__/circle-side.test.ts` (parse He/En × named/implicit × subject-list; defer with no circle; auto-materialise named; compound non-capture; engine: created outside / inside; existing-point re-seat with no conflict; contradicted side flagged) + scenario `kite-EMKO-outside-point` (the operator's full sequence) + the catalog guard.

## ADR-255 — a stated segment-meet re-seats a genuinely LOOSE endpoint so the segments actually cross

**Context.** Operator session `gaawv4fr` (2026-07-08, minutes after ADR-253/254 landed): `AB קוטר`, `C על במעגל`, `M מחוץ למעגל`, `AM חותך את CO בנדוקה K` — every row ✓, yet the drawn segments AM and CO **do not cross**: M's outside seed landed up-LEFT of the circle (the ADR-254 golden spin correctly walked off the diameter line, but the side it chose makes the stated crossing geometrically impossible from there), so K sat on the continuations. The verifier DID raise `figure.v.meetOnSegment` (amber) — but the row reads ✓, and `findValidConfig` returned null: **the seed sampler explores only a small neighbourhood of a free point's default** (a rigid cluster spin + ±0.22·span jitter), so no sampled config could carry M across the figure to where the crossing works. Operator: "AM and CO intersect is not reported as impossible, which is wrong" — and the deeper truth is that it isn't impossible at all: M is free, and half the plane satisfies the statement.

**Class (design-rules §1).** *A statement that constrains an under-determined free point's REGION (here: "these two segments cross") is recorded only as a post-hoc requirement — nothing uses it to place the point, and the config search cannot reach a far valid basin.* Same family as ADR-098 ("a free point not positioned to satisfy the input is SAMPLED to a valid placement") and ADR-254's re-seat (M1/M4: defaults yield to statements).

**Decision.** At the apply boundary (`line-line-intersection` with `onSeg`), when the current crossing lies OFF a segment (or the lines are parallel): re-seat one **genuinely loose** endpoint — a non-pinned free point with **no constraint referencing it and no solve directive** — along the ray from its fixed mate through the **midpoint of the other segment** (k-ladder 1.7/2.0/2.4/1.5/2.9), requiring the new spot to (a) be in general position (the ADR-253 helper) and (b) **keep the point's side of every resolvable circle** — so a stated `M מחוץ למעגל` survives the move (ADR-254 without new state). Candidates are ordered fewest-dependents-first (a circle-defining endpoint moves only as a last resort). The point stays a free DOF — this is a better default, not a pin. Constrained endpoints (e.g. ADR-166's equilateral apexes, which carry equal-side constraints) are **never** touched — their mechanism is the reflection DOF; a meet with no loose endpoint keeps today's honest amber.

**Consequences.** `src/engine/apply.ts` only (`reseatLooseMeetEndpoint`). The operator's figure now draws the textbook configuration at seed 0 (K within both segments, M outside, verifier clean, `meetsRequirements` true). The ADR-166 scenario is unaffected by construction (its apexes are constraint-claimed). Residual limitation (inherited from ADR-253's note, unchanged): requirements whose valid region needs a large move of a free DOF are rescued here only for the segment-meet statement family; a general "requirement-guided relocation" stage in `findValidConfig` remains the fallback design if more members of this class appear.

**Tests.** `src/engine/__tests__/meet-reseat.test.ts` (the gaawv4fr basin → crossing within both segments + circle-side preserved; a satisfied meet moves nothing; mirrored operand slots; a constrained endpoint is never moved and the amber stays) + scenario `stated-meet-relocates-loose-point` (the operator's exact 4 utterances, typos included).

## ADR-256 — detection ground truth = VALID configurations only (the sample pool honours stated requirements)

**Context.** Operator session `ntzdgqn2` (2026-07-08, the kite-EMKO figure + `MO`, `AC`, `BC/EK=5/3`): "when I ask to see equal angles I get all the correct angles except AMO, which should be like OME and is not shown; also the triangles OMK and CAK are similar and are not in the list." Both relations are **forced by the givens**: MK=ME & OK=OE ⇒ △MKO ≅ △MEO (SSS) ⇒ ∠KMO = ∠EMO (and K lies on segment AM, so ∠AMO names the same wedge); and ∠MOK = ∠KOE/2 = ∠COB/2 = ∠OCA (isosceles radii triangle) with vertical angles at K gives AA ⇒ **△OMK ~ △CAK** in every valid configuration. Reproduced on HEAD through the real store path: the equal-angle class was present (the operator's session predated ADR-255, so their M sat in the impossible basin), but the similar class was missing even on HEAD — and the tell was two angle classes ({∠BAC,∠ACK} and {∠BOM,∠KOM}) that should have been ONE.

**Class (design-rules §1).** *The detection layers' "holds in EVERY sample" ground-truth pool includes samples that violate the figure's own stated configuration requirements.* The BASE config is requirement-gated (`firstSatisfyingSeed`, ADR-166 Am.), but the 16 perturbed samples were only convergence-filtered — a seed that slides the stated meet's crossing K past segment CO's end flips ray O→K, breaking ∠KOM = ∠OCA *in that sample only*, so a relation true in every valid configuration reads "not forced" and is suppressed. Any stated requirement can be violated this way (meet-on-segment, "המשך" reach, circle-side, radius-order).

**Decision.** Gate the sample pool on the same bar the config search uses, at the M3 chokepoints: a new engine filter **`requirementSamples(c, samples)`** (sibling of `convergedSamples`, same never-below-2 fallback — a thin pool over-claims, an unfiltered one only under-claims) drops samples whose `onSeg` segment-meet crossings sit off their segments; applied in `detectRelationsAcross`, `detectShapes`' `samplePositions`, and the store's shared sample core — which additionally filters by `extensionsClear` (the facts-level "המשך reaches the far side" bar, unavailable to the engine). Verifier-derived requirements (circle-side, radius-order) are noted as a follow-up if a real figure surfaces them; their seeds are already biased valid by construction.

**Consequences.** `src/engine/relations.ts` (+ index export), `src/engine/detectShapes.ts`, `src/store/geoStore.ts` (samplingJobs). On the operator's figure the pool drops 16 → 8 valid samples and detection now reports the merged four-way class **∠BAC = ∠ACK = ∠BOM = ∠COM**, the requested **∠CAK = ∠AMO = ∠EMO**, and the merged similar class **△ACK ~ △MOE ~ △MOK** (the previous congruent pair EMO ≅ KMO folded in; kind correctly degrades to `similar`). Emergent AC ∥ MO surfaces through ∠CAK = ∠AMO. All 77 engine/store/theorems test files (1814 tests incl. the B-corpus and the ADR-166/167 detection locks) pass unchanged.

**Tests.** Store-driven scenario `[ntzdgqn2-kite-detection-honours-requirements]` (the operator's exact 10 utterances → viewRelations reports the M-wedge pair; detectShapes' similar classes contain {A,C,K}~{K,M,O}).

## ADR-257 — a congruent SUB-GROUP inside a mixed similarity class is reported alongside it

**Context.** Operator follow-up on the ADR-256 fix (same kite figure): "now it shows 3 similar triangles, but we also have OEM = OMK which is not shown." Before ADR-256 the list read `congruent: △EMO ≅ △KMO`; when △ACK joined them (correctly) into one class, `detectSimilarClasses`' class-wide kind degraded to `similar` — the design rule was "congruent only when EVERY member is congruent to the reference, else similar" — and the STRONGER statement between the two kite halves silently vanished from the display.

**Class (design-rules §1).** *A relation class that carries a stronger sub-relation among some members reports only the class-wide weakest kind — merging drops information.* (The honesty invariant, detection-display edition: a true stronger statement must not disappear because a weaker cousin joined the class.)

**Decision.** In `detectSimilarClasses`, after emitting a mixed (`similar`) class, partition its members into congruence sub-groups (union-find over pairwise congruence under the aligning correspondence — congruence is transitive within a similarity class) and emit each group of ≥2 as its own `congruent` class alongside the similar row. An all-congruent class stays one row (no duplication). The flood-guard scaling changes from "one row per class" to "one row per class + one per congruence sub-group" — still bounded by member count, never O(n²) pairs.

**Consequences.** `src/engine/detectShapes.ts` only; no UI change (the `congruent` row kind already renders). The kite figure now lists `similar: △ACK ~ △MOE ~ △MOK` AND `congruent: △EMO ≅ △KMO`. The square-two-diagonals flood-guard lock updated deliberately: its 8-triangle similar class now also reports its two true congruent sub-groups (the 4 quarter and 4 half triangles) — 3 rows, each a distinct true statement. Theorems/store/engine suites (1814) pass unchanged — no feed ripple.

**Tests.** `detectShapes.test.ts` (the square-diagonals class + sub-groups; the rectangle congruent pair unchanged) + the `[ntzdgqn2-kite-detection-honours-requirements]` scenario extended to assert the congruent △EMO ≅ △KMO row.

## ADR-258 — analytic / coordinate geometry is a deliberately out-of-scope class, refused pre-LLM

**Context.** The operator observed students typing analytic-geometry terminology into the (synthetic-construction) tool — "the y axis" and the like. That input can never build here (this tool draws figures on a free canvas; there are no axes, slopes, or line equations), yet it fell through the grammar as a plain `not-handled`, spent an LLM call, and finally landed under the generic "couldn't read that" gap — inflating the real-gap count and giving the student no useful signal. The operator asked for a message saying this isn't that tool and that a separate coordinate-geometry tool is planned.

**Class (design-rules §1).** *A whole family of input the tool deliberately does not accept must be recognised and refused with a pedagogical message + its own analytics tag — never mislabelled as a genuine construction gap, and never sent to the LLM when it provably can't build.* The existing `classifyOutOfScope` (ADR — the out-of-scope boundary: `angle-relation`/`proof`/`compute`/`unrelated`) is exactly this mechanism; analytic geometry is a new member of it.

**Decision.** Add an `analytic` category to `src/parser/scope.ts` (bilingual patterns: axes `ציר`/axis, slope `שיפוע`/slope, coordinates `קואורדינ`/`שיעורי`/coordinate, origin/`ראשית הצירים`, `מערכת צירים`/coordinate-system, line equations `משוואת הישר`/`equation of the line` + the numeric `y = …x` form, cartesian). Patterns are kept SPECIFIC — the stems appear in no supported construct, and the equation form requires BOTH `y =` and an `x` term so a length given like `AB = 4` cannot trip it. Placing a free point AT coordinates (`A = (3,5)`) stays supported — the `freePoint` grammar rule builds it, so it never reaches the classifier (which runs only on a failed parse). `App.submit` short-circuits this category **before** the LLM call (unlike the other scope categories, which run post-LLM): analytic input is an unambiguous "wrong tool", so there's no reason to spend a call — it refuses instantly with `input.scope.analytic` and the `scope:analytic` analytics tag. The admin dashboard gets a Hebrew sub-category label.

**Consequences.** `scope.ts` (new category + patterns), `App.tsx` (the pre-LLM guard), `he.json`/`en.json` (`input.scope.analytic`), `server/admin.ts` (`SCOPE_LABELS_2D.analytic`). No engine/parser-grammar change — `parse()` still returns `not-handled`; the classifier is a separate, read-only boundary. The dashboard now separates analytic requests from real construction gaps (the same operator ask that motivated the original scope classifier).

**Tests.** `src/parser/__tests__/scope.test.ts` — an analytic block (He + En: axes, slope, coordinates, line equations, origin, cartesian) and regression cases asserting `null` for coordinate free-point placement (`A = (3,5)`), length givens (`AB = 4`), and bare shapes.

## ADR-259 — a circle sized by its DIAMETER + the `עיגול` synonym

**Context.** A prod-dashboard triage (the unrecognised-input list, 2026-07-08) surfaced one loud real gap: a student typed `מעגל קוטר 10` / `מעגל בקוטר 10` / `עיגול קוטר 10` / `עיגול קוטר 10 ס"מ` five times in an hour — clearly stuck. Two defects behind it: (1) a circle can be sized by radius / circumference / area (ADR-228) but NOT by its diameter; (2) `עיגול` (the everyday Hebrew word for a circle/disk) was not recognised as a circle at all — the `circle` rule matched only `circle`/`מעגל`.

**Class (design-rules §1).** *A single magnitude-form gap (sizing by diameter) and a single vocabulary gap (a shape synonym) each belong at the ONE place their whole class is handled — the size helper and the normalization chokepoint — never as a per-rule patch.*

**Decision.** (1) **Diameter sizing** — extend `circleSizeRadius` (the helper BOTH the `circle` creation rule and `circleSizeExisting` already call) with a diameter branch: a diameter word followed directly (optionally via a copula) by a number lowers to radius = d/2. The value must follow the keyword with NO endpoint label between them, keeping it DISTINCT from the diameter-CHORD `קוטר AB` (labelled, no size) which the diameter rule owns. A stated diameter is a real magnitude ⇒ the radius is numeric/fixed (ADR-052). (2) **`עיגול` synonym** — normalise `עיגול`→`מעגל` in `normalizeUtterance` (the single boundary every rule reads), so the entire circle vocabulary (creation, sizing, chord, tangent, inscribe, semicircle…) accepts it with one change. A trailing unit (`ס"מ`) is harmless — the size is read from the number and `isDef` short-circuits the leftover check.

**Consequences.** `parse.ts` (`circleSizeRadius` diameter branch + the `עיגול` normalization + a `hasDiameter` candidate in `droppedGivenNumbers` so d/2 isn't seen as a dropped magnitude), a `catalog.ts` entry (`circle with diameter 10`). The diameter-chord form and all existing circle sizing are unchanged (snapshots additive only). Also feeds the scope keyword set (`עיגול` added to `GEO_KEYWORD`).

**Tests.** `perimeter-circumference.test.ts` — a diameter/`עיגול` block (He + En, units, the chord form stays a chord, a bare `עיגול` is free-radius); catalog-coverage + shadow-matrix snapshots updated (additive).

## ADR-260 — a failed COMPOUND utterance advises breaking it into smaller steps

**Context.** Same triage: a student typed `ריבוע Abcd, נקודה f נמצאת על צלע ab, זווית cfd 37 מעלות` — three statements (shape + point-on-side + angle) in one line — which failed to build and got the flat "couldn't read that." The operator asked that long inputs packing 2–3 instructions be told to break them apart.

**Class.** *When a failed input is structurally several statements, the most actionable message is "add them one at a time," not a generic miss* — the student both gets a smaller, far-more-parseable step AND can see which piece is the problem.

**Decision.** Add `looksCompound(utterance)` to `src/parser/scope.ts`: split on statement separators (list/clause punctuation, He/En conjunctions incl. the bare `ו` glued to a construct noun), and flag when ≥2 pieces each carry a geometry KEYWORD (a construct/relation word, NOT a bare label — so a single construction with list-commas like `circle through A, B, C` or the supported `F, G, H on AB, AC, CB` stays ONE statement and is never flagged). `App.submit` consults it ONLY on the failure path (both grammar AND LLM failed to build), before the generic message, showing `input.tooManyParts` and logging `not-understood-compound` (still a real-gap count for the dashboard, but measurable). The keyword-bearing-piece guard is what makes liberal separator splitting safe.

**Consequences.** `scope.ts` (`looksCompound` + `COMPOUND_SEP`), `parser/index.ts` (export), `App.tsx` (failure-path branch + import), `he.json`/`en.json` (`input.tooManyParts`). Read-only heuristic; never fires on a successful parse, so it can't block a working compound the grammar/LLM does handle.

**Tests.** `scope.test.ts` — a `looksCompound` block: compound (the operator example; shape+circle; multi-clause En) TRUE, and single constructions with list-commas / givens-lists FALSE.

## ADR-261 — an angle bisector from a vertex resolves its angle from the figure when the triple is omitted

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-08)

**Context.** The operator typed `משולש ABC` → `AB=AC` → `CD חוצה זוית` ("CD bisects the angle"): a line was drawn but the two half-angles at C were not equal, and a production user hit an error on the same phrasing. The deterministic parser's `bisectorPlacesPoint` resolved an angle bisector from a vertex only when the angle's three letters were spelled out (`CD חוצה זוית ACB`). With the triple omitted, the input fell through to the LLM, which drew a bare segment with no equal-angle constraint — a figure that violates its own given. A sibling from the debug log, `BD חוצה זוית במשולש ABC`, also escalated: the `triangle` rule matched the embedded `משולש ABC`, saw the `חוצה זוית` SHAPE_LEFTOVER, and returned `'stop'` (the same shadowing class median/altitude/midsegment already avoid by running before the shapes).

**Class.** *A construct whose reference is fully determined by the figure must be resolved deterministically, not dropped to the LLM.* `XY חוצה זוית` names the bisecting ray `X→Y`, so `X` is the angle vertex; its two arms are the figure's edges at `X`. This is exactly the ADR-164 single-vertex angle resolution (`∠B = 90` → arms from `ctx.neighbors`), reused for the bisector.

**Decision.** (1) `bisectorPlacesPoint` now, when no explicit triple is present, resolves the angle from `ctx.neighbors[apex]` — well-defined only when the vertex has exactly two edges (one angle); a different count returns the `ambiguous-angle` clarification (ask for the three letters) rather than guessing. Gated to an explicit "angle"/"זוית" utterance so a segment bisection (`AB חוצה את הקטע CD`) never mis-fires as an angle bisector. (2) The rule is moved ahead of the shape rules (joining median/altitude/perpBisector/midsegment) so its `…במשולש ABC` form is not shadowed by `triangle`'s `'stop'`; safe there because it defers on intersect keywords, so the bisector-∩ compounds (which require an intersect keyword) still win their inputs.

**Consequences.** `parse.ts` (`bisectorPlacesPoint` neighbour resolution + RULES reorder). Deterministic — no LLM escalation for the common bisector-from-a-vertex phrasing. The placed point `D` sits geometrically on the bisector ⇒ the two half-angles are equal by construction (and a pre-existing `D` becomes a `set-angle-ratio k=1` equality, unchanged).

**Tests.** Scenarios `bisector-from-vertex-no-triple` (∠ACD = ∠DCB after triangle+`AB=AC`) and `bisector-from-vertex-in-triangle` (the `…במשולש ABC` form) in `scenarios.test.ts`; full suite + build clean.

## ADR-262 — a polygon INSCRIBED IN A POLYGON (rhombus/rectangle/square/parallelogram in a triangle or quad)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-09)

**Context.** The operator hit the bagrut figure *מעוין חסום במשולש* — a rhombus `BDEF` inscribed in triangle `ABC` (B shared; D on AB, E on AC, F on BC) — and had to build it point-by-point because the construct did not exist. Worse, `מעוין חסום במשולש ABC` (and `מלבן חסום במשולש`, and the English forms) **silently misparsed to the triangle's incircle** — a *circle* inscribed in ABC (bisectors → incenter → foot → circle-through), with the rhombus/rectangle word dropped entirely (a §6 honesty violation). Root cause: inscription in the parser only meant polygon-in-circle (`inscribedPolygon`) or circle-in-polygon (`incircle`); `isCircleInPolygon` only checked whether the *container* was a polygon, never whether the inscribed thing was a *circle*, so `incircle` claimed the polygon-in-polygon input and its `kind` scan found `משולש` first.

**Class.** *An "X inscribed in Y" statement is a membership+shape assertion whose roles are set by the ב/"in" preposition, not by which noun is a circle* — the ADR-245 principle. Polygon-in-polygon is a first-class member of the inscription family, alongside polygon-in-circle and circle-in-polygon; none may claim another's input.

**Decision.** A general **`inscribe`** store-level command (`{shape, ids, container, containerKind, variant}`) expanded by `replay`/`lowerOne` (`src/engine/inscribe.ts`) — the ADR-110 macro pattern, **no new engine construct**:
- **Placement.** A shape vertex whose *label* is shared with the container coincides with that container vertex (same id, M1 reuse). Every other vertex becomes a free `point-on-segment` rider on a container side, laid around the boundary in the shape's cyclic order (monotone; a shared vertex anchors the walk). The expansion then emits a **`polygon`** command over the shape's vertices (the ADR-111 mechanism: draws the boundary segments + creates the polygon object from the pre-placed vertices) — without it the sides exist only as length constraints, so the figure renders no lines, `detectShapes` finds no polygon, and "show equal segments" has nothing to mark (the operator's first-test report; fixed same day). What the labels do NOT pin — the mirror **direction**, and (when there are more vertices than sides, e.g. a rectangle's "base") which side hosts the extra — is enumerated as the cyclable **`variant`** ([ADR-052](#adr-052)/design-rules M4); "show another configuration" steps it, and an explicit `point-on-segment` given on a shape vertex PINS the matching variant (the ADR-138 `explicitEqs` counterpart, `explicitOnSegs`).
- **Shape constraints.** Emitted on the placed vertices: rhombus → 4 equal sides; rectangle → 3 right angles; square → rhombus + 1 right angle; parallelogram → opposite sides equal. The constraint solver flexes the riders into shape; the givens verifier re-derives membership + the relations → "green" is VERIFIED. Determinacy falls out for free (rhombus-in-triangle 3 rider-DOF − 3 equal = 0 up to variant+similarity; rectangle-in-triangle 4 − 3 = a 1-parameter family, correctly sampled by "show another").
- **Parser** (`inscribedInPolygon`, before `incircle`/`inscribedPolygon` and the base shape rules): container = the polygon carrying ב/"in"; inner = the OTHER polygon word; a circle noun anywhere → not this rule. An inner shape we can't make determinate (bare quad / triangle) returns `'stop'` (escalate) — never a plain-shape misparse. `incircle` now also requires a circle noun (a *semantic* guard — an incircle statement is about a circle — not a keyword bow-out).
- **Variant generality.** A shared `variants.ts` (`variantCountOf`/`cyclableVariant`/`withVariant`/`variantVertices`) lets the store cycle `shape-variant` and `inscribe` uniformly, so `inscribe`'s figure-dependent variant count coexists with `shape-variant`'s static `VARIANT_COUNT` without a per-type branch in the cycling code.

**Scope (operator, 2026-07-09):** the general inscribed-polygon family; cyclable-variant placement; triangle **and** quadrilateral containers; inner shapes rhombus/rectangle/square/parallelogram.

**Consequences.** `types.ts` (+`inscribe`), `engine/inscribe.ts` + `engine/variants.ts` (new), `lower.ts`, `geoStore.ts` (replay expansion + generalized variant cycling), `parse.ts` (+`inscribedInPolygon`, `incircle` circle-noun guard), `catalog.ts` (+3). Pure/deterministic; no engine geometry change (a read-only lowering to existing commands). Known limits (filed, not blocking): a generic-quad or triangle *inner* shape escalates rather than building an under-determined membership-only figure; anchored-arc rider distribution uses the canonical even split (front-loaded extras) rather than enumerating every composition — sufficient for the corpus shapes.

**Tests.** Unit `engine/__tests__/inscribe.test.ts` (placement, variant count, expansion, pin); scenario `rhombus-inscribed-in-triangle`; parser-coverage matrix (6 parse + 2 escalate) + the catalog/shadow snapshots. Full suite green (3439+), `tsc -b` clean.

### ADR-262 Amendment 1 (2026-07-09) — three prod-test follow-ups (boundary draw, angle detection across a shared vertex, canvas fit)

Operator's live prod test of the inscribed rhombus surfaced three issues, all fixed:

1. **The boundary wasn't drawn** (no lines, not detected, no equal-segments to mark). `expandInscribe` emitted riders + length/right-angle constraints but no drawing command, so the sides existed only as constraints. Fix: the expansion now emits a `polygon` command over the shape's vertices (ADR-111 mechanism — boundary segments + polygon object from pre-placed vertices). Now drawn, detected (`detectShapes` → rhombus), and its sides reportable.

2. **`∠B = ∠CDE` (corresponding angle, DE∥AB) not surfaced, and `∠B` showed a DOUBLE arc.** Two causes: (a) `relationMarks` drew an arc per class member, and `∠ABC`/`∠DBF` are two names for the *same wedge* at the shared vertex B (F on BA, D on BC) → two stacked arcs; fixed by collapsing same-wedge members before drawing (extends the ADR-167 Am. value-dedup to equal-angle arcs). (b) The store's `viewRelations` samples across an inscribe's *variant configs*, but a rhombus's two variants are **mirror relabelings** (D↔F swap), so requiring a per-label relation to hold across them wrongly dropped forced angles like `∠CDE` at D. Fix: `variantConfigs` includes only `shape-variant` (whose variant encodes a *relation* choice — which sides are equal); an `inscribe` variant is a *placement/mirror* choice that must not gate relation detection. With inscribe excluded, `detectRelations` (which already enumerates angles over `collinearSplits` sub-edges) reports the full set — `∠ABC = ∠CDE = ∠DEF = ∠AFE` — and the shared-vertex angle appears once.

3. **First shape "too large / top nodes not visible."** The base fit (padding 48) is correct; the clip came from `keepOrRefit`'s hysteresis margin `m = min(8, padding·0.2) = 8 px`, which let a boundary vertex drift to 8 px from the edge before refitting — but a vertex's LABEL sits ~24 px beyond it, so on a canvas shrink the kept transform left the figure oversized with the apex label clipped. Fix: reserve label extent in the margin (`LABEL_MARGIN = 28`, capped at the padding), so a shrink refits before a label disappears. Stability (existing points don't jump for additions inside the band) is preserved — only the outer label-width band now forces a refit.

**Tests.** `relation-marks.test.ts` (shared-vertex class → one arc at B); `shape-variant.test.ts` (store: rhombus drawn + detected + `∠ABC`/`∠CDE` in one class); `phase-f.test.ts` (a vertex within a label width of the edge refits); `inscribe.test.ts` (a `polygon` is emitted); scenario asserts the boundary is drawn. Full suite green (3471), `tsc -b` + build clean.

## ADR-263 — a height/altitude from a vertex drops to a real SIDE, never a diagonal (and picks one when ambiguous)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-09)

**Context.** The operator built a quadrilateral (parallelogram `ABCD`) with the diagonal `BD` drawn, then asked for heights: `גובה מ A` was understood but `גובה מ B` was **refused** ("not understood"), and the named height `BE גובה` **drew onto the diagonal BD** they never asked for. Root cause in the `altitude` rule's opposite-side resolution: when the parallel-base ([ADR-169](#adr-169)) and named/context paths don't resolve, it fell back to a **neighbour-adjacency** step that triangulated the figure from `ctx.neighbors` — two of the apex's neighbours joined to each other close a triangle whose "opposite side" is that join. But a drawn **diagonal** joins two neighbours too: from `A` it found the single triangle `ABD` and dropped the foot onto **BD (a diagonal, not a side)**; from `B` it found **two** such triangles (`ABD`, `CBD`) and refused as ambiguous. So the same defect both produced the wrong base (A) and the refusal (B).

**Class.** *A height/altitude drops onto a polygon EDGE opposite the apex — a diagonal is never a base.* The neighbour-triangle heuristic conflated "two vertices joined by a segment" with "an edge of the figure," which is false the moment any diagonal (or other chord) is drawn.

**Decision.**
- The opposite side is resolved from real **polygon edges** (`oppositePolygonEdges(apex, ctx.polygons)`): edges of a polygon the apex belongs to that do **not** touch the apex. A diagonal is not a polygon edge, so this can never return one — the correctness fix.
- A triangle yields exactly one such edge (unambiguous). A **parallelogram / general quad yields several** genuine heights; per the operator's steer this now **draws one deterministically** rather than refusing — **superseding [ADR-169](#adr-169)'s parallelogram-defers** for this case. (Choosing *which* real side is a branch/alternative, not an unstated magnitude, so it doesn't violate [ADR-052](#adr-052); a future "show another" could cycle the two heights.)
- Resolution order is unchanged and safe: explicit "to BC" → trapezoid parallel base (ADR-169) → named triangle in the utterance → **polygon edge (new)** → exactly-two-other-points context (bare triangle) → neighbour adjacency **only when no polygon surrounds the apex** (loose segments ⇒ no polygon diagonal, so a join is a genuine edge).
- Secondary fix, same rule: the auto-named foot now excludes **every existing figure point** (`freeLabel([apex,p,q,...ctx.points])`), so a second altitude no longer re-picks `F` and silently **redefines** the first altitude's foot (a §6-honesty collision surfaced while tracing this).

**Consequences.** `parse.ts` only (`oppositePolygonEdges` helper + the reordered opposite-side block + the `freeLabel` fix). No engine change. `phase4.test.ts`'s old "parallelogram → not-handled" assertion is replaced by "draws one real side (never a diagonal)" plus a "no polygon ⇒ still defers" case. Trapezoid heights (parallel-base path) and triangle heights (context path) are byte-unchanged.

**Tests.** Scenario `height-from-vertex-never-drops-onto-a-diagonal` (`מקבילית ABCD` · `BD` · `גובה מ A` · `גובה מ B` · `BE גובה` — all parse, three feet with distinct labels, every foot on a real side ⟂ its base, none on BD); `phase4.test.ts` updates. Full suite green, `tsc -b` clean.

## ADR-264 — a shape declared WITH its property clause in one utterance parses deterministically; a dropped stated relation is never silent

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-09)

**Context.** The operator: "the user names a shape and then gives a property needed for the shape — `משולש ABC הוא שווה שוקיים, כלומר AC=BC`, `דלתון ABCD, AB=AD` — the second part is ignored and the user is not told and thinks all is good." This is the textbook's standard appositive form for *defining* a named shape by its equal pair (the prod log has the class since 2026-06-24: `דלתון ABCD שבו AB=AD ו CB=CD`, `ABCD דלתון - AB=AD ו BC=DC` — both LLM-escalated).

**Class (two coupled members).** (1) *A compound utterance mixing a CONSTRUCTION with its property givens is never parsed deterministically*: `multiStatement` (the existing all-or-nothing splitter, PAR-2) deliberately requires **every** piece to carry a relation operator, so the shape piece falls through; the shape rule then `'stop'`s on the leftover clause (correct honesty), and the whole line escalates to the LLM. (2) *On that path, a dropped relation between existing points is invisible*: the two honesty gates watch **new labels** (ADR-089) and **numbers** (ADR-250) — an equality like `AC=BC` whose letters all already appear on the shape trips neither, so an LLM decomposition that lost the clause **committed silently as success**. (For the isosceles this is not even cosmetic: the macro's soft default `|AB|=|AC|` (ADR-114) then silently substitutes for the student's stated `AC=BC`.)

**Decision.**
- **Clause fallback (`splitStatements`), inside `parse`, LAST-RESORT.** Runs only after every whole-utterance rule failed (never shadows a rule that owns a comma/connective compound — `circle through A, B, C`, ADR-076 lists, `multiStatement` itself are all untouched). Splits on the `multiStatement` separators **plus the apposition connectives** (`כלומר`/`שבו`/`כאשר`, a spaced dash, En `that is`/`i.e.`/`where`/`in which`/`meaning`/`namely`) and parses each piece **all-or-nothing** — any unreadable piece and the whole line still escalates; a bare-label piece (a list fragment) refuses the split outright. Clause semantics = the same statements typed on separate lines (the LLM-decomposition contract, made deterministic) — so the stated pair lands as an explicit `set-equal` that **pins** the macro's soft default exactly as ADR-114/ADR-234 designed.
- **Context threads between clauses** (`augmentParseCtx`): labels → `points`, ≥3-id runs → `polygons` + ring `neighbors`, segments → `neighbors`, `center` fields → `circles`. So `מרובע ABCD, מעגל חסום במרובע` binds the incircle to THE quad (ADR-245 definite reference) and `משולש ABC, זווית B = 90` resolves the single-vertex angle (ADR-164) — the mechanism generalizes past equalities (the looksCompound example `ריבוע ABCD, נקודה F על AB, זווית CFD 37` now parses deterministically).
- **Third honesty gate (`droppedGivenRelations`)**, sibling of ADR-089/ADR-250, on **both** commit paths: a symbol-form relation given (`AB=CD`/`AB⊥CD`/`AB∥CD`, exactly two labels a side) must be carried by a `set-*` constraint referencing all its labels, or have a label *introduced* by a point-definition command (the `כך ש AB=BK` class, where the relation is baked into the definition) — else the parse is weak/refused and the student is told what wasn't captured. A bare shape command deliberately does **not** account: the student's *stated* pair must land as an explicit constraint (the ADR-234 pin), not vanish into a soft default. Word-form relations (מקביל/מאונך) stay out — they belong to rule-owned compounds that are already leftover-guarded.

**Consequences.** `parse.ts` (the extracted `runRules` + `splitStatements` + `augmentParseCtx` + `droppedGivenRelations`) and `App.tsx` (the gate wired beside its two siblings on the grammar and LLM paths). No engine change; `multiStatement` byte-unchanged. Pre-existing and deliberately untouched: a shape rule still silently drops trailing **prose** that carries no labels/numbers/symbol-relations ("דלתון ABCD, AB שווה בערך" — word-equality was ruled non-actionable, students write `AB=AD`).

**Sibling audit.** Grepped the debug log for connective forms (`שבו`/`כלומר`/`כך ש`/dash): the `כך ש` family is rule-owned (`compoundSuchThat`) and unaffected; the June-24 kite forms are now deterministic (locked in the unit test); `מעגל שבו AB קוטר`-style circle appositives ride the same fallback (the diameter clause binds via the augmented context or honestly refuses).

**Tests.** `clause-split.test.ts` (13: both locales, all four connective forms, generalization cases, all-or-nothing refusal, list-comma protection, the gate's flag/account/exempt matrix); scenarios `isosceles-appositive-stated-pair-one-line` + `kite-stated-pair-one-line` (the operator's exact utterances — stated pair holds, soft default yields, never equilateral). Full suite green, `tsc -b` clean.

### ADR-264 Am. 1 — the dropped-shape-noun guard (a lax relation rule must not swallow a bare shape declaration)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-09, same day)

**Context.** The operator's very next dev test (session `zalwhvsh`): `משולש שווה שוקיים שבו AB=AC` committed as segments `AB`, `AC` + `set-equal` — **no triangle** ("AB is equal to AC but this is not a triangle"). The ADR-264 fallback never ran because the whole-parse *succeeded*: with **no label run on the shape word**, the shape rule DEFERS (`null`, not `'stop'` — the `'stop'` path fires only for labeled shapes), and `equalSegments` matched its `AB=AC` clause anywhere in the string, silently dropping the leading declaration. The relation gate stayed quiet — the equality itself *was* accounted; what vanished was the **shape noun**. Siblings verified in the same probe: `…שבו AB=5` (distance) dropped it too, and `…שבו זווית B=40` (angle) answered a *misleading* `ambiguous-angle` clarification.

**Class.** *A LAX relation rule (equality/distance/angle/…, all matching their clause mid-string) claims a compound whose leftover still carries a shape declaration.* The labeled-shape forms were already safe (the shape rules `'stop'` on a leftover → ADR-264 splits); only the label-less bare-shape forms leaked through.

**Decision.** One guard at the winner, never per-rule (§3 chokepoint discipline): `droppedShapeNoun(s, commands, ctx)` — a stated POLYGON noun with (a) no command materializing a polygon (every polygon creator carries a ≥3-id `ids` run) and (b) no exemption — is a half-parse. Exemptions make it precise: a noun adjacent to a label run whose letters the commands or figure know is a *reference* ("קטע האמצעים PQ לצלע BC במשולש ABC"); a bare noun with polygons already on the figure is a *definite reference* ("גובה מ A במשולש"); **circle nouns are excluded** — a circle word in a relation utterance is a carrier/membership marker owned by the ADR-119 post-passes (`מיתר AB = מיתר CD` keeps working). On a trip (including a clarification that dropped the noun), `parse` tries the ADR-264 clause split as the deterministic rescue — bare `משולש שווה שוקיים` parses auto-named, the stated pair pins it (ADR-114/234), and the angle sibling resolves `∠B` from the threaded neighbors — else the WHOLE line escalates honestly. Split pieces are guarded identically.

**Tests.** `clause-split.test.ts` guard describe (operator utterance, distance + angle siblings, En mirror, carrier/reference negatives); scenario `isosceles-bare-shape-with-pair-one-line` (the exact utterance — real non-degenerate triangle drawn, |AB|=|AC| holds). Full suite green, `tsc -b` clean.

### ADR-264 Am. 2 — the trailing inscribe predicate (a lax rule must not swallow "… חוסם/חסום במעגל")

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-09)

**Context.** The Am.-1 landing left three 2-D failures on the tree (found by a cross-session check): two phase4 trapezoid-altitude tests whose STUB context omitted `polygons` (the real `buildParseCtx` always supplies a drawn trapezoid's polygon, so the bare-`בטרפז` definite-reference exemption fires in the app — the stubs were updated to match reality, zero production change), and scenario `symbolic-2alpha-drives-shape-not-the-fixed-point`, whose step 1 `משולש שווה שוקיים ABC שבו AB=AC חוסם במעגל` exposed a genuine class member. Pre-Am.-1 that line HALF-PARSED via the lax `circumcircle` rule (`חוסם`+`מעגל` cue, **no leftover guard**) to a bare circumcircle — the isosceles and the stated `AB=AC` silently dropped (the exact sin ADR-264 targets; the scenario passed only because its checks were circle-only). Post-Am.-1 the shape-noun guard correctly vetoed that winner, but the clause split's piece `AB=AC חוסם במעגל` was claimed by `equalSegments` and the inscribe clause vanished instead — a DIFFERENT half-parse (shape + pair, no circle O), and the 2α drive then tore the isosceles apart ("over-constrained: |AB| = |AC| cannot hold").

**Class.** *A TRAILING inscribe predicate (verb+circle adjacency at the end of a piece) claimed as leftover by a lax relation rule — or by the leftover-guard-less `circumcircle` rule — is silently dropped.* The circle sibling of Am. 1, which deliberately exempts circle NOUNS (carrier markers, ADR-119); the verb+noun ADJACENCY at the piece END is what distinguishes a predicate from a marker (§2.4 — narrower than a word test).

**Decision.** `droppedCirclePredicate(s, commands)` — the tail regex (He inscribe/circumscribe inflections + `במעגל`, En "inscribed in a/the circle", optionally naming the circle) with NO command touching a circle — joins the winner gate beside `droppedShapeNoun`, and `splitStatements` gains the rescue: detach the tail, parse the head as its own clause, and give the subject-less predicate its subject — **THE unique polygon of the clause context** (the ADR-245 definite-reference pattern, verb edition), by re-parsing `<polygon letters> <predicate>` through the normal rules so every inscribe semantics (named circle → per-vertex membership ADR-099, unnamed + already-on-circle → the ADR-156 idempotent no-op, fresh → circumcircle) stays owned by its rule. Uniqueness is BY CONTENT (a head clause re-declaring the figure's polygon is one subject); zero or ≥2 distinct polygons → the whole line escalates honestly. A single separator-less part is now splittable iff it carries the tail (the whole-line sibling `AB=AC חוסם במעגל` typed after the triangle exists). **Scenario ground-truth correction:** with the full parse, `∠BOC=2∠CAD ⟺ ∠BAC=∠CAD` is unsatisfiable at the seeded D (t=1.3) for EVERY apex height (with AB=AC, ∠BAC subtends the whole base while ∠CAD subtends the 0.3·BC stub), so the solver legitimately drives D's UNSTATED extension t (ADR-052; the scenario's own seed-sweep exemption said as much) — the check now asserts what the student stated: the pair holds, the ratio holds, D beyond C.

**Sibling audit.** Grepped the rules for inscribe-cue consumers: `inscribedPolygon`/`incircle`/`inscribedInPolygon`/`circumcircleMeetsSegment` all account their circle or `'stop'`; `circumcircle` is the one leftover-guard-less claimer (it caused the pre-Am.-1 half-parse; the winner gate now covers it). The ADR-156 idempotent branch (returns only the polygon — no circle command) trips the gate benignly: the split re-derives the identical idempotent lowering (locked by test). Deferred: a mid-string inscribe predicate (not at the piece end) stays rule-owned/escalates as before.

**Tests.** `clause-split.test.ts` Am.-2 describe (the scenario line full lowering He, En mirror, the whole-line existing-triangle sibling, no-subject + two-subject honesty refusals, whole-rule-owned inscribe untouched, ADR-156 idempotence); scenario `symbolic-2alpha-drives-shape-not-the-fixed-point` re-locked with the corrected ground truth (isosceles pair now asserted — it was unverifiable pre-fix). Full suite green, `tsc -b` clean.

## ADR-265

### ADR-265 — Project workflow: GitHub issues, PR-gated features, `main` as trunk, deploy tags + log, ops runbook

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-10, operator-directed: "manage this as a real project would … set up the rules so we have them as standard workflow")

**Context.** The project outgrew its informal process. A documentation audit found strong records for *decisions* (ADR logs), *changes* (CLAUDE.md current-state + PROJECT-MEMORY), and *regressions* (the scenario rule + fixtures) — but no PR concept (386 commits on `rebuild-foundation`, `main` dead at the initial commit), no issue tracker ("filed, not fixed" items scattered as ADR prose in four places, unqueryable), and no deploy record (manual `scp` from a sometimes-uncommitted working tree; log-triage silently assumes prod ≈ HEAD — the ADR-115 stale-server class, prod edition).

**Decision.** The standard operating route is **[docs/22-workflow.md](22-workflow.md)** (authoritative; summarized): (1) **every operator report/request is filed as a GitHub issue first**, labeled type (`bug`/`feature`/`debt`) + priority (`P1` prod honesty/correctness → drop everything; `P2` real input fails visibly → scheduled by log-triage demand; `P3` polish/debt → batched) + app; a bug diagnosed as a capability gap is **relabeled feature, never silently built**. (2) **Bug fixes** keep the fast loop — root cause per docs/17 + ADR + scenario, commit to `main` with `Fixes #NN`; **features always go through a PR** (`feat/<issue#>-slug`, operator plays + approves before merge). (3) **`main` is the trunk** — fast-forwarded to the `rebuild-foundation` head at adoption, `rebuild-foundation` retired; the shared Dropbox tree stays on `main`, topic branches live in worktrees (never `checkout` over another session's uncommitted work). (4) **Deploys only from committed `main`**, per **[docs/RUNBOOK.md](RUNBOOK.md)** (the consolidated two-app ops procedure), each recorded as a git tag `prod/YYYY-MM-DD[-n]` + an entry in **[docs/DEPLOY-LOG.md](DEPLOY-LOG.md)** (canonical — PROJECT-MEMORY stops accumulating deploy notes). Existing doctrine (17-design-rules, the scenario rule, the FR-sync rule, definition-of-ready) is wrapped, not replaced.

**Consequences.** "What's known-broken / queued / live?" each have one queryable answer (issues; the P-labels; the deploy log + tags). The uncommitted-tree deploy habit ends — every prod bundle is reconstructable. Costs accepted: filing overhead per report (mitigated: the assistant files via `gh` during triage), and PR latency on features (wanted — it *is* the operator gate). Seeded at adoption: labels, ~7 issues migrated from ADR "filed, not fixed" prose, tag `prod/2026-07-10` retroactively on `6168d0c`.

**Am. 1 — triage-first: a reported issue is QUEUED, never auto-fixed (2026-07-10, operator).** The first run of the route (issue #14 → PR #16) exposed a gap: the assistant filed, classified, *and immediately built* the fix. The operator's correction: while testing they raise **several** issues per pass; if the reporting session fixes immediately, they are forced to feed one issue at a time and parallel fixes overwrite each other. **The reporting session does the full triage — file, diagnose to root cause/class per docs/17, classify bug-vs-feature + priority, write a concrete fix plan into the issue — and STOPS; no implementation.** Fixing happens in dedicated fix sessions where the operator picks issues off the queue by priority. Exceptions: an explicit "fix this now", or a P1 prod-honesty emergency (announced first). Codified as [docs/22-workflow.md §2b](22-workflow.md); §3/§4 step ownership annotated accordingly.

## ADR-266

### ADR-266 — The multi-product workspace: product registry, per-product CI lanes, mechanical isolation

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-10, operator-directed; issue #13). Extends ADR-265; registry lives in [docs/22-workflow.md §9](22-workflow.md).

**Context.** The repo already hosts two products (2-D Geo Builder `src/`, 3-D Space Builder `src3d/`) under the sibling-app pattern (docs/20 §12: own entry/build/dist/prod-path, isolation by copied patterns, one shared parameterized server). Two more are planned — **analytic geometry** (the 471 4-pt + 572 5-pt questions) and **complex numbers**. Three gaps: (1) CI was one serial job running the FULL build + ~3,900-test suite for any non-docs change (~13 min), so every product paid for every other product's tests; (2) the per-product conventions (ADR log, label, status home, PR scoping) existed de facto but were written nowhere — a session had to infer which product a request relates to; (3) the isolation rule was held by convention only, and `vite.config.3d.ts` even carried an `@` → `src/` alias, so a stray `@/` import in src3d would have silently coupled the products.

**Decision.** (1) **Per-product CI lanes** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): a `changes` job classifies the push/PR diff — `src3d/`, `3d.html`, `fixtures3/`, `vite.config.3d.ts` → the 3-D lane; `src/`, `index.html` → the 2-D lane; docs paths → none; **everything else (server/, package.json, tsconfig, vite.config.ts, .github/, any uncategorized new path) → ALL lanes** — unknown-by-default is "run everything", never "skip". Each lane builds its own bundle and runs `vitest run <tree>/ server/` (the shared-server tests run in every lane; `tsc -b` covers src+src3d in both lanes, keeping the cross-product typecheck net). Lanes run in parallel; an unusable diff base (force-push/new branch) runs all lanes. Local mirrors: `npm run test:2d` / `test:3d` (+ `test:run:*`). The **full suite stays the bar before any deploy** and for shared-surface changes. (2) **The product registry** (docs/22 §9): per product — source dir, entry/build/dist, prod path, ADR log + id prefix, plan/status home, issue label, test filter, CI lane, fixtures dir — plus the *adding product N+1* recipe. Future tools decided: analytic geometry is **one product** (`src-analytic/`, `06c-decisions-analytic.md`, `ADR-AG-NNN`, label `analytic`) serving 471+572 as curriculum profiles of one engine; complex numbers separate (`src-complex/`, `06d-decisions-complex.md`, `ADR-CX-NNN`, label `complex`). (3) **Isolation made mechanical**: `server/__tests__/isolation.test.ts` scans both trees' import specifiers — src3d must not use `@/` or relative paths into `src/`, and vice versa — and runs in every CI lane; the dangerous `@` alias is removed from `vite.config.3d.ts` (a cross-product import now fails the 3-D build outright).

**Consequences.** A single-product change runs roughly a quarter of today's CI work, and lane wall-time also drops on full runs (parallel jobs); adding the analytic/complex products won't grow the common case. The conventions a session needs to route a request (which ADR log, which label, which tests) are now one lookup in docs/22 §9. Costs accepted: the classifier must be extended when a product is added (mitigated: uncategorized paths run everything, so forgetting is safe-slow, not wrong); per-lane `npm ci` duplication (~1 min each, offset by parallelism).

## ADR-267

### ADR-267 — Extension-direction semantics as a preference ladder: STRICT letter order preferred wherever achievable, the ADR-142 shared-endpoint either-side bar as the ACCEPTANCE tier — searched in ONE budget-safe interleaved sweep, honoured by every consumer

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-10, dedicated fix session; issue #19). Operator session `eew5ezi5` — re-testing the ADR-124/#6 source question (booklet 571 2025, printed p.78, Q4) with the correct NEW extension point E. *Files: `src/store/geoStore.ts`, `src/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts`.*

**Context.** Two circles meet at A,B; chord AD in P tangent to O at A; chord CB in O tangent to P at B; `המשך AC חותך את מעגל P בנקודה E` (typed with a חותר typo the LLM corrected — that path worked). Every step showed ✓, but E landed **between C and A** (t = 0.64 along C→A) instead of the book's C-A-E order, amber-flagged `orderBeyond` — the operator: "fails to create the C-A-E sequence."

**Class (docs/17 §1).** A requirement with TWO legitimate bars — a preferred strict form (the stated letter order, honoured whenever some configuration achieves it, ADR-098) and a geometric acceptance form (a shared-endpoint extension's second crossing is UNIQUE, so when NO configuration achieves the letter-order side the order carries no information and either side counts, ADR-142) — had the acceptance bar implemented as a **second full search pass behind a `relax` flag only `firstSatisfyingSeed` set**. Three coupled failures: (a) **budget starvation** — on this figure the strict side is impossible at EVERY seed (CB tangent to circle P pins C strictly outside P), so the primary strict sweep (~120 seeds × ~25 ms cold) is provably futile and the app's `SEARCH_BUDGET_MS = 2500` deadline expires before the fallback pass ever runs; (b) **consumer disagreement** — `meetsRequirements` (hence `findValidConfig`/`autoResolve`), the show-another gate, and the ADR-256 sample filter all used the STRICT form only, so even with an infinite budget `findValidConfig` REJECTED the very seed the fallback found and returned null; (c) **test/prod divergence** — the suite runs `SEARCH_BUDGET_MS = Infinity`, so every scenario reached the fallback the live app never could, and the whole starvation class was invisible to the gates.

**First attempt, reverted by its own fallout (recorded per docs/17 §2.6).** Making either-side the unconditional DEFAULT in `extensionsClear` fixed this figure but broke the ADR-098 family (`free-point-on-circle-both-extensions-reach-far-side`, its auto-advance sibling, and the seed-sweep oracle at seed 2): when the figure has free DOFs, the letter order is a genuine GIVEN that SELECTS the configuration — the search must not settle for a wrong-side config when an achievable right-side config exists. The two ADRs are not in conflict; they are a preference order.

**Decision.** The ladder, applied consistently:
1. **`extensionsClear(facts, fig, relax)`** keeps both bars: strict = the stated letter order; relax = the ADR-142 shared-endpoint either-side bar (a point genuinely BETWEEN the endpoints always fails; membership matched per circle id per ADR-244).
