**Tests / lock.** `WORKER_SEARCH_BUDGET_MS` is finite and > 2500; `searchResample`/`findValidConfig` honour an explicit `budgetMs` (an expired budget on a search-needing figure gives up, the worker budget resolves it). The exact CEFO-2 figure's base was a LOADED `.geo.json` (unlogged, #84 — same limit as ADR-295's #88), so the functional lock is the operator's play-test of the real figure; the mechanism is locked deterministically here. **Possible follow-up (not built):** surface a progress + ✕ cancel cue on `autoResolve` too (it currently shows only a busy state), so a worst-case 12 s search is cancellable like `resample`.

## ADR-297 — Anonymous promotable points: a decomposition never spends a student's letter (issue #32)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-12; feature, issue #32 → PR). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`anonId`, incircle feet + dual touch), `src/engine/relations.ts` (`isScaffoldId` adds `@`), `src/render/scene.ts` (`ScenePoint.promotable`), `src/render/Figure.tsx` (promotable dots + `onPromotePoint`), `src/store/geoStore.ts` (`promote`), `src/App.tsx` + locales; `src/store/__tests__/promote.test.ts`, scenario `incircle-feet-are-anonymous-not-namespace-hijack`.*

**Class.** A decomposition that needs an auxiliary point the student did not name (an incircle's three tangency feet, a tangent's touch point) auto-named it with a capital LETTER (`freeLabel` → `F`, `G`, `H`). That letter is then OCCUPIED: when the student reaches for it themselves — `G על המשך CA`, meaning a NEW point on CA's extension — the (correct) M1 existing-id machinery finds `G` already present and constrains the invisible incircle foot instead of creating the student's point (prod session `jsptarcl`; the same family as ADR-116's tangent-feet hijacking `E`). The bug is not in M1 — it is that the engine spent a letter on scaffolding the student never asked for. Students copy from books where these touch points usually carry NO label at all.

**Decision.** A new point state — the **anonymous promotable point**. A decomposition mints its unnamed auxiliary points with an `@`-prefixed id (`anonId('f', 'AB')` → `@f-AB`, deterministic per side so re-issuing is idempotent), which:
- **never occupies a student letter** — `@f-AB` is not `[A-Z]\d*`, so `commandPointIds` ignores it and the next student `G` is genuinely free (the bug closes as a side-effect of the representation);
- is **excluded from the detection universe** ({@link isScaffoldId} now covers `~` AND `@`) — an unnamed point is not yet a relation/shape subject;
- **renders as a clickable dot with no label** (`ScenePoint.promotable`; scene draws it instead of hiding it like `~`), reusing the crossing-dot affordance — the student sees it and can name it if the book does;
- is **promoted on click** by the store's `promote(auxId)`: assign the next free capital letter and rewrite `@f-AB → F` across every command (via the existing `renameInCommand` id-remap — the `@`-id is a literal, so only its exact occurrences change), one undo entry, next-letter default the student can later rename.

Applied in this PR to the **incircle** (fresh feet + the ADR-115 existing-circle dual touch points) — the reported case. The identical `freeLabel`-fallback pattern at the other touch/tangency sites (tangent-from-external touch points, two-circle tangency, tangent-line touch) is a mechanical **fast-follow** (the ADR-116 sibling class); the antipode/altitude-foot/centre/auto-vertex sites are deliberately NOT anonymized (they are student-facing primary objects, not touch scaffolding).

**Root cause (one sentence).** The engine assigned student capital letters to construction scaffolding, so a letter the student later typed collided with an auto-minted point instead of creating their own.

**Tests / lock.** Scenario `incircle-feet-are-anonymous-not-namespace-hijack` (the incircle + `G על המשך CA` → a fresh on-segment G, feet are `@f-*`); `promote.test.ts` (anonymous feet, promotable dots carry no label, `promote` assigns the next free letter + remaps, one undo, no-op on a real letter). Two existing incircle scenarios updated from named F/G/H to the `@f-<side>` feet.

## ADR-298 — A shared concrete-VALUE atom: radical / fraction values as stated givens (issue #77)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-12; feature, issue #77 → PR). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`NUMEXPR`/`NUMTERM`/`numexprVal`/`hasDivisor`, `measureFraction`, `parseAreaExpr` + `parseRadius` quotient branches, the radical-aware `droppedGivenNumbers` fraction span); `src/parser/__tests__/radical-fraction-values.test.ts`, scenario `radical-fraction-length-value`.*

**Class.** The parser had **no shared concrete-VALUE atom**. Each stated-value position carried its own partial regex vocabulary — `distanceConstraint` (bare number), `measureSqrt` (`coef·√rad`), `parseAreaExpr` (number / `c√n` / power / var), `parseRadius` (bare number / `nπ`) — and none represented a QUOTIENT. So a textbook length given like `BC = 35/√32` (and even a plain `BC = 35/2`) was `not-handled` and escalated to the LLM, which did not rescue it; the workaround was converting to a decimal by hand. The exact vocabulary needed — `[coef] √? n [ / √? d ]` — already existed as `RCOEF`/`RATVAL` (ADR-285) but had been unified only across the ratio-COEFFICIENT positions, never the VALUE positions. This is the ADR-285 class one seam over.

**Decision.** One shared atom `NUMEXPR` (a TERM optionally divided by a TERM, where a TERM is `[coef ·] √ number` OR a plain number — the coefficient is TIED to the √, so a bare `35` is one number, never `3 × 5`) with `numexprVal → { value, text }`; `text` is the VERBATIM typed form, load-bearing for the on-figure label (a radical fraction renders as `35/√32`, never `6.19`) and for the `droppedGivenNumbers` honesty gate. Wired into the stated-value positions, each keeping its guards + end-anchoring: a new `measureFraction` length rule (quotient-only — bare/`coef√` stay with `distanceConstraint`/`measureSqrt`, `AB = CD/2` with the ratio rule, `√2R` with the radius idiom), a quotient branch in `parseAreaExpr` (area + perimeter inherit together), and a quotient branch in `parseRadius`. Angles are deliberately excluded (a fractional-degree given is not a bagrut form; escalation stays honest). The honesty gate's fraction-span pass was made **radical-aware** to match — it now evaluates `[coef]√n / [coef]√n` spans and accounts the lowered VALUE, so a fraction RADIUS (which the circle command stores only as a number, no text) is not falsely flagged as dropping its stated numbers.

**Root cause (one sentence).** Quotient values were unrepresentable because the value grammar was duplicated and partial in every position; a shared atom exposes the existing coefficient vocabulary to the length / area / perimeter / radius RHS.

**Sibling audit.** The no-theft sweep (existing tests + new negatives) confirms `12√2`, `AB=CD`, `AB=CD/2`, `√2R`, `3x²`, `25√3`, `EB/AE=√2/2` all keep their owners; the `AB=CD/2` ratio-divisor's pre-existing `droppedGivenNumbers` flag is unchanged (verified against `main`). Out of scope, filed as noted: the 3-D app (`src3d/`) has its own value parsing with the same fragmentation — a separate issue if prod logs show demand (products never share code, docs/22 §9).

**Tests / lock.** `radical-fraction-values.test.ts` (all quotient forms × length/area/radius × He/En, no-theft, honesty gate green, angle excluded); scenario `radical-fraction-length-value` (the operator's exact «נתון: BC = 35/√32» builds with |BC| = 35/√32).

**Amendment (2026-07-12, operator review of PR #92 — the DISAMBIGUATION + rendering the first pass missed).** The operator flagged that `5√2/3` is ambiguous (root of `2/3`, or `(√2)/3`?) and that the SPEC intent — never captured in the written issue — was that the √ button produce `√()` (explicit grouping) and that the input render as formatted math. Both were genuinely missing (the flat `[coef]√n [/ √?d]` grammar had no parenthesised-radicand concept, and there was no math rendering; the MathML half is separately issue #40). Fixed in the same PR: (1) **`NUMTERM` gains a parenthesised radicand** `√(n)` / `√(n/d)` — distinct from a bare `√n` whose radicand is JUST the number so `√2/3` stays `(√2)/3` (textbook convention) while `√(2/3)` is the whole-fraction root — plus optional outer-paren term grouping `(5√2)/3`; the position gates widen from "has a divisor" to `isNewValueForm` (divisor OR parenthesised radicand, so `√(2/3)` with no top-level `/` is claimed too); the `droppedGivenNumbers` gate's value pass is made paren-radical-aware over the WHOLE value expression (one longest-match pass, no double-count of an inner `2/3`). (2) **The √ toolbar button inserts `√()`** with the caret between the parens (the `S_{}` pattern), so students produce the explicit grouping by default. (3) **`src/render/mathText.tsx`** renders the math tokens (fractions / radicals incl. `√()` / subscripts / superscripts) as **MathML** — a LIVE preview under the input (the interpretation is visible while typing: `√(2/3)` is a radical over the fraction, `√2/3` is `(√2)/3`) and in the step-list rows (issue #40). Locked by the √() cases in `radical-fraction-values.test.ts` (incl. `√(2/3) ≠ √2/3` by value) + `mathText.test.ts`. **Process note:** the requirements were missed because they were an input-UX design the operator held but the triaged issue captured only the parser grammar; when the ambiguity surfaced at `5√2/3` it should have been raised, not resolved silently by convention.
## ADR-299 — Right-angle word / glyph / homoglyph forms, normalized at the chokepoint (issue #45)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-12; feature, issue #45 → PR). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`normalizeUtterance` symbol pass + `CYRILLIC_TO_LATIN`; the `angle` rule's `ישרה`/right-angle word + lowercase-vertex handling); `src/parser/__tests__/right-angle-forms.test.ts`, scenario `right-angle-word-and-glyph-forms`.*

**Class.** A stated right angle has many surface forms a student actually types; four families all failed on HEAD (~4 distinct prod users): (1) GLYPH variants — the ∡ MEASURED-ANGLE (U+2221) and ∢ SPHERICAL-ANGLE (U+2222) glyphs, and the ⁰ SUPERSCRIPT-ZERO (U+2070) typed for degrees (`90⁰`); (2) uppercase CYRILLIC homoglyph labels (`А`/`В`/`О`… are not `[A-Za-z]`, so a pasted label silently fails every rule); (3) the WORD form `ישרה` / `right angle` instead of `= 90`; (4) a lowercase vertex (`נתון זווית d=90` — where, contrary to the issue's first read, the `נתון` prefix already worked and the real cause was the lowercase `d`, which `labelRun` resolved to `D` but the `angle` rule's UPPERCASE-only compound-guard count then read as zero labels and bailed).

**Decision.** (1)+(2) are a single SYMBOL-NORMALIZATION pass at the parse-entry chokepoint (`normalizeUtterance`, the `normalizeAreaSubscript`/`עיגול→מעגל` seam): `∡`/`∢`→`∠`, `⁰`→`°`, and the unambiguous uppercase Cyrillic look-alikes → Latin — so EVERY angle/label rule inherits the canonical glyphs at once (no per-rule patches). (3)+(4) live in the one `angle` rule: the `ישרה` / `right angle` word lowers exactly like `= 90` (the "right angle" phrase is excluded from the multi-angle reference count so it isn't read as a second angle), and the single-vertex compound-guard now counts a LONE lowercase Latin letter as a label (only when no uppercase label is present, so a lowercase filler word's letters are never miscounted) so a lowercase vertex resolves.

**Root cause (one sentence).** The parser's canonical glyph/label alphabet was narrower than what students type, and the `angle` rule's compound guard counted only uppercase labels — so a homoglyph, a superscript, a word, or a lowercase vertex each fell outside the recognized surface.

**Sibling audit.** The normalization is at the ONE boundary every rule reads (the ADR-121/228/283 chokepoint), so the ∡/° fix and the Cyrillic fix help every future angle/label rule, not just the reported ones. No-theft verified: `∠ABC = 37`, `זווית B = 90`, and a multi-angle givens list are byte-unchanged; the `נתון`-prefix path was already working. The En "right angle" phrase's double-`angle` count is neutralised only for the right-angle word (a real two-angle list still splits).

**Tests / lock.** `right-angle-forms.test.ts` (13: glyph ∡/∢/⁰, Cyrillic diameter, `ישרה`/`right angle` word in every position, lowercase vertex, + no-regression on the numeric and multi-angle forms); scenario `right-angle-word-and-glyph-forms` (the headline «∡ABC=90⁰» builds ∠ABC = 90 end-to-end).

## ADR-300 — "from an external point" accepts the abbreviated `מ-X`, not only the spelled-out `מנקודה X` (issue #96)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-12). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`secantFromExternal`, `tangentsFromExternal` external-point cue); `src/parser/__tests__/from-external-and-oncircle.test.ts`.*

Operator building bagrut 2023-קיץ-א Q4 ("a line from B cuts the circle at E and A"): `secantFromExternal`'s external-point cue matched `from`/`מנקודה`/`מהנקודה`/`מ נקודה` but NOT the very common abbreviation **`מ-B`** (from-B), so the natural utterance was not-handled and the operator built a wrong reconstruction (arc-midpoint substituting the secant). Fix: the cue gains the `מ-\s*` alternative (the diameter rules ADR-270 already had it) with a `(?![A-Za-z])` single-label guard so `מ-AB` (a segment) never misfires as "from A"; applied to `secantFromExternal` AND `tangentsFromExternal` (same cue, same class).

## ADR-301 — A point stated `על המעגל` keeps its membership through a relation clause (issue #97)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-12). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`withOnCircleMembership` post-pass + chain); `src/parser/__tests__/from-external-and-oncircle.test.ts`.*

`D על המעגל כך ש-CD מקביל ל-EA` ("D on the circle such that CD ∥ EA") lowered to `segment CD / segment EA / set-parallel` — the leading **`D על המעגל`** membership was DROPPED (the parallel rule claimed the clause), so D floated free (a green row, a silently-wrong figure — the §6 honesty class, the ADR-119 chord-membership family, "such-that" edition). Fix: a `withOnCircleMembership` post-pass (sibling of `withCarrierMembership`, but keyed on the explicit `על המעגל`/`on the circle` phrase, not a chord/diameter/radius noun) asserts `point-on-circle` for every label the utterance says is on the circle, when a circle resolves; idempotent (a point a circle-construct already placed is skipped) and PREPENDED so the point is created on the circle before the relation drives its remaining DOF. A `(?<![A-Za-z])` label guard keeps a word's last letter ("...are ON the circle") from being read as a phantom point (ADR-240 regression averted).

## ADR-302 — A tangent THROUGH an on-circle point + a DEFINITE back-reference to "the tangent" (issue #100)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-12). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`throughPointLabel` shared reader, `tangentLine` third touch source, new `theTangentMeetsCircle` rule, `circleCenter` בנקודה vocabulary, FILLER articles, `tangentLine` degenerate-pair guard); `src/parser/__tests__/issue-100.test.ts`, scenario `tangent-through-oncircle-point-then-back-reference`.*

**Class.** A tangent LINE that is (a) constructed *through a named on-circle point* with no segment naming the line and no "at" clause, and (b) then *referenced back and intersected* with another circle in a SEPARATE statement, had no lane. The 2025-bagrut two-intersecting-circles figure states exactly this: «דרך הנקודה A העבירו משיק למעגל הקטן. המשיק חותך את המעגל הגדול בנקודה K.» Both clauses were not-handled (prod, operator report 2026-07-12).

**Root cause.** (a) `tangentLine` inferred the touch only from an explicit at-clause or a named SEGMENT's on-circle endpoint — while `tangentFromExternal` already correctly DEFERRED the on-circle through-point case to it (the ADR-233 membership handoff), so the handoff had no receiving lane. (b) A definite "המשיק"/"the tangent" subject intersected with a circle matched no rule, and `lineLineIntersection` then 'stop's on the משיק keyword — so the whole parse aborted.

**Decision.** (a) A shared `throughPointLabel` reader (extracted from `orientTouchCut`); `tangentLine` gains the third touch source — a through-point that is a circle MEMBER is the touch (membership-gated per ADR-233: an off-circle through-point still routes to the external-tangent rules). (b) A new `theTangentMeetsCircle` rule — the ADR-029 implicit-reference pattern, tangent-line edition: a subject that is EXACTLY the bare definite tangent noun + cut verb resolves THE unique `tan-*` line from `ctx.lines` (0 or 2+ → defer/escalate, never guess; an existing crossing label → defer, it's an M1 statement) and lowers to `line-circle-intersection` avoiding the touch when the touch is a member of the target circle, + the drawn chord segment. Registered after `tangentMeetsOtherCircle` (whose self-declaring subject also starts «המשיק») and before `lineLineIntersection`.

**Ride-alongs (same session, §6 honesty).** `circleCenter` reads «שמרכזו בנקודה O» (the stated centre was silently dropped and an auto-named sibling minted — luck-dependent); the articles "a"/"an" join FILLER lowercase-only (the En mirror read the article as a point label, degenerating `tangentLine`'s pair to A,A → a spurious «AA» ⟂); `tangentLine` rejects a degenerate equal pair semantically.

**Sibling audit.** `twoTangentsMeet` (subject «המשיק בנקודה A והמשיק…») doesn't match the tight anchor; `tangentMeetsOtherCircle`'s single-utterance form byte-unchanged; the Hebrew-verb anchor uses `(?![A-Za-z])`, never `\b` after a Hebrew letter (the recorded ℓ trap). Not built (filed in #54's scope note): resolving "המעגל הגדול/הקטן" as a NON-concentric two-circle reference — the scenario names the circles.

**Tests / lock.** `issue-100.test.ts` (9: He/En end-to-end with exact tangency + K-on-circle asserts, defer on 0/2+ tangents, defer on existing K, no-theft ×2, both ride-alongs); scenario `tangent-through-oncircle-point-then-back-reference`.

## ADR-303 — A point's side of a POLYGON region is a first-class requirement (issue #99)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-12; feature, issue #99 → PR). *Files: `src/engine/geometry.ts` (`pointInPolygon`), `src/engine/types.ts` (`point-polygon-side`), `src/engine/apply.ts` (seed/re-seat incl. a free on-circle rider's θ), `src/engine/verify.ts` (`region-side`, `figure.v.insideRegion`/`outsideRegion`), `src/parser/parse.ts` (`REGION_TAIL` + `regionSideFallback` + the `droppedRegionSubject` honesty gate), i18n; `region-side.test.ts`, scenario `bagrut-2025-two-circles-full-figure`.*

**Class.** A point-defining (or point-referencing) statement carrying a REGION disambiguator — "הנקודה E נמצאת על מעגל O **בתוך המשולש KAO**" (2025 bagrut) — was unrepresentable: the region clause selects WHICH part of its carrier the point occupies, and no rule owned the compound, so the whole statement escalated → not-understood and VANISHED. The ADR-254 family (a point's side of a *circle*), polygon edition.

**Decision.** Same shape as ADR-254 end-to-end. A `point-polygon-side` command is the side REQUIREMENT record: the verifier re-derives it from final coordinates (strict inside with an edge margin), `meetsRequirements` gates sampling/"show another" on it, a genuinely contradicted side reads amber — never a driven equality, never dropped. Apply improves DEFAULTS only: a NEW id seeds as a free point on the stated side (golden-angle general position around the region centroid); an EXISTING non-pinned free point on the wrong side re-seats; a free ON-CIRCLE rider re-seats its starting θ to an on-circle spot inside the region (the exam case — E keeps BOTH its membership and the region). Parser: a LAST-RESORT `regionSideFallback` (runs only after runRules + splitStatements fail, so inscriptions — which parse fully — are untouched) strips the trailing region clause, parses the head normally, and attaches the region to the ONE point the head introduces; a bare head ("M בתוך המשולש ABC") attaches directly (M1 for an existing id). Region vertices must be drawn points (a reference), with ONE implicit-creation exception: an all-NEW *triangle* (the `withImplicitCircles` pattern — "E inside triangle KAO" states the triangle exists). `droppedRegionSubject` joins the dropped-given honesty family: a winning parse that eats the region utterance while dropping its subject (the bare "M בתוך המשולש ABC" → `triangle` rule) is rescued, never committed subject-less.

**Root cause (one sentence).** The region qualifier had no lane — parse dropped the statement whole; and no engine requirement could hold a point to a polygon side across sampling.

**Tests / lock.** `region-side.test.ts` (10: He/En × inside/outside, the exam's carrier+region form building E on-circle AND in-region, bare-subject rescue, M1 re-seat, contradicted-side amber, inscription no-theft ×2, unknown-vertices defer); the full-figure scenario.

## ADR-304 — Per-circle RADIUS SYMBOLS + radius relations (issue #54)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-12; feature, issue #54 → PR). *Files: `src/engine/types.ts` (`Circle.radiusSymbol`, `radius-symbol`, `set-radius-ratio`), `src/engine/apply.ts` (stamp; witness-resolve/mint + `ratio` lowering; `set-radius-order` stamps `innerOf` only for a shared centre), `src/engine/verify.ts` (`radius-ratio` against resolved radii), `src/engine/lower.ts` (`SymTab.radiusOf`, per-symbol measure coupling, legacy per-spelling fallback), `src/parser/parse.ts` (`normVar` case-preserving, `parseRadius.sym` any letter, `withRadiusSymbolBinding` post-pass, `radiusSymbolStatement`, `radiusRelation`), `src/parser/context.ts` (`radiusSymbols`), `src/store/geoStore.ts` (`dryRunOutcome` data-statement family), `src/App.tsx` (slider labels); `radius-symbols.test.ts`, scenario `bagrut-2025-two-circles-full-figure`.*

**Class.** A radius SYMBOL was a single reserved global (`RADIUS_VAR`, ADR-034/071: `normVar` folded `r → R`, `buildSymTab` bound it to "the" circle) — wrong the moment a question names TWO radii (the 2025 bagrut: big R, small r, `R > r`, `R = 1.5r`). Stated symbols were silently unbound (the letter vanished — nothing to reference), and radius relations had no construct.

**Decision.** The ADR-034 auto-bind generalized per circle. **Binding:** the letter (ANY letter, case-sensitive) stamps `Circle.radiusSymbol` via a `radius-symbol` data command — at creation through the `withRadiusSymbolBinding` post-pass (the ADR-119 chokepoint: every circle rule gains the שרדיוסו clause at once; pairing by order, unpairable counts left to the #53 honesty gate), or after the fact via `radiusSymbolStatement` ("רדיוס מעגל O הוא R" — the operator's requested form; M1, existing circle only). The radius stays a FREE DOF (a name, not a size — ADR-052); the slider shows the letter. **Relations** (`radiusRelation`, both letters must be bound — else defer, never guess): `R > r` lowers to the ADR-244 `set-radius-order` requirement (independent-circles edition — `innerOf` is now stamped only for a shared centre so two intersecting circles never read as concentric; the verifier check was always by circle id); `R = 1.5r` / `R/r = 2√7/5` lower to `set-radius-ratio`, which apply resolves to an ordinary `ratio` over (centre, on-circle-witness) pairs — a witness is any point already on the circle, else a hidden PINNED `~radw-*` rider is minted (θ fixed ⇒ 0 sampled DOF; `~` ⇒ unrendered, detection-excluded per ADR-295) — **zero new solver code** (the ADR-103 free-radius recruitment drives it). The verifier checks the ratio against the RESOLVED radii (never the witness implementation). **Measures:** `AB = √2R` couples to the BOUND circle via `SymTab.radiusOf`; an UNBOUND R/r keeps the legacy single-circle fallback per spelling, so old figures are byte-unchanged. **Honesty:** `radius-symbol`/`set-radius-order` join `dryRunOutcome`'s data-statement family (a binding/order moves no coordinates — it must commit, not read as "nothing to add", the ADR-234 class).

**Root cause (one sentence).** Radius symbols were a single-circle special case with no binding record, so a second named radius was unrepresentable and every relation over the letters had nowhere to land.

**Not built (documented follow-up).** Resolving "המעגל הגדול/הקטן" as a reference between two INDEPENDENT circles (the exam's unnamed-circle wording) — today only a CONCENTRIC pair resolves qualifiers (ADR-244); with R>r bound the size roles are knowable, so the extension is natural. Filed on issue #54's thread.

**Tests / lock.** `radius-symbols.test.ts` (14: binding forms He/En × creation/after-the-fact, any-letter, ratio product + radical quotient drive, order requirement + mirrored slots + no-concentric-marker, measure-couples-to-bound-circle vs creation order, data-statement gate, unbound defers, numeric no-theft, legacy single-circle unchanged); the full-figure scenario.

**Amendment (2026-07-12, operator play-test of PR #101 — the honesty gates false-positived on the NEW vocabulary; session `yla2d4xo`).** The parses were all correct, but the App's submit gates — which the scenario corpus (parse→replay) never exercises — rejected three of them: (1) `droppedNewLabels` read the BOUND radius letter in «R > r» / «R=1.5r» as a dropped point label (`weak:dropped:R` → needless LLM → not-understood) — the gate gains a `measureSymbols` mask fed from `ctx.radiusSymbols` at both App call sites (semantic, never an utterance-shape guess); (2) `droppedGivenVerbs` read the definite tangent back-reference («המשיק חותך…», whose lowering REFERENCES `line:"tan-A"` but contains no `tangent` command) as a dropped משיק verb — the satisfied-set gains the `"tan-` line-reference form; (3) the operator's retry phrasing «המשיק **בנקודה A** חותך…» now SELECTS the tangent by its named touch (and disambiguates the 2+ case). The reported "E placed outside the triangle" was HONEST amber: the gate refusals had forced a workaround figure (K on the small circle) in which no on-circle point can lie strictly inside △KAO — with the gates fixed the real figure builds. **Process lock:** `scenarios-props-submit-gate.test.ts` gains `[bagrut-2025-submit-gates]` — the full 11-utterance figure through App.submit's EXACT gate order (labels+symbols → numbers → relations → verbs → dry-run), so a gate false-positive on new vocabulary can never again pass the corpus while failing the app.

**Amendment 2 (2026-07-12, operator play-test round 2 — same session `yla2d4xo`; the after-the-fact bindings and «R>r» now committed, three NEW members surfaced).** (1) **The one-sentence compound** «דרך A עובר משיק למעגל O שחותך את מעגל P בנקודה K» — the touch named by the THROUGH-clause, not an at-clause, so `tangentMeetsOtherCircle`'s two-pair match missed it and `circleCircleIntersection` claimed a garbage bare re-statement (gates caught it → dead-LLM dead end). tMOC gains a single-pair + through-point branch (membership-gated per ADR-233: the through-point must be a member of the «משיק למעגל X» circle), and `circleCircleIntersection` gains the SAME tangent defer its siblings already carry (`lineMeetsCircle` bows out on משיק, `lineLineIntersection` 'stop's) — a not-handled escalates honestly instead of a gate-caught half-parse. (2) **Region-then-membership order** — «נקודה E בתוך משולש AKO» then «E על מעגל O»: the apply (c2) free→on-circle conversion jumped E to an arbitrary `nextTheta` slot, ignoring both its seat and its region requirement; the conversion now lands at the point's OWN BEARING from the centre (M1 stability — a membership statement keeps the point near where it was), which preserves the earlier region seat by default. (3) **A region/side REQUIREMENT about an existing point commits** — `point-polygon-side`/`point-circle-side` join `dryRunOutcome`'s requirement-data family (zero coordinate delta, but the record gates all future sampling — the ADR-234 class); an EXACT duplicate of an enabled fact stays a truthful no-op (deepEqual dedupe). Locked by the one-sentence-compound + membership-after-region + duplicate-noop tests (`issue-100.test.ts`, `region-side.test.ts`) and `[bagrut-2025-second-session]` — the operator's verbatim round-2 flow through the full gate order.

## ADR-305 — «המעגל הגדול/הקטן» between two INDEPENDENT circles: the size qualifier both REFERS and ASSERTS (issue #102)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-13; feature, issue #102 → PR; operator ruling: "when we say המעגל הגדול או הקטן we should translate it to a R>r like constraint"). *Files: `src/engine/types.ts` (`Circle.orderedBelow`), `src/engine/apply.ts` (`set-radius-order` stamps the pure size role for ANY pair; `innerOf` stays concentric-only), `src/parser/context.ts` (`radiusOrder`, `circleSizes` — visible circles only), `src/parser/parse.ts` (`resolveSizeQualifier` pre-pass at the parse boundary + the creation-adjective seed split in `circle`); `size-qualifier.test.ts`, scenario `bagrut-2025-verbatim-unnamed-circles`.*

**Class.** The 2025 bagrut never names its circles — «מעגל גדול שרדיוסו R», «מעגל קטן שמרכזו בנקודה O ורדיוסו r», then «המעגל הגדול/הקטן» throughout — and a size-qualified DEFINITE reference between two independent circles had no lane (only a CONCENTRIC pair resolved qualifiers, ADR-244), so every such reference dead-ended at the LLM.

**Decision (per the ruling).** The qualifier is INFORMATION, not just a pointer: (1) **resolve** each definite «המעגל הגדול/הקטן» / "the big/small circle" to a concrete circle — from the RECORDED roles when they exist (`set-radius-order` now stamps `Circle.orderedBelow` for any pair, concentric or not, which `ctx.radiusOrder` reads back), else the FIRST use ASSIGNS them from the currently-drawn sizes (`ctx.circleSizes` — the M4 soft default, what the student is looking at; hidden/scaffold circles excluded); and (2) **assert** — an assigning use appends the locking `set-radius-order`, the R>r-like requirement, so sampling/"show another" can never swap which circle is the big one and a later contradicting size reads amber. Implemented as a ctx-aware REWRITE at the one parse boundary (the ADR-119/244 chokepoint — every circle-consuming rule gains the reference at once; both qualifiers in one utterance each rewrite, one assert). Scope guards: exactly TWO visible circles (0/1/3+ keep existing behavior/escalate); a concentric pair keeps its ADR-244 path; the INDEFINITE creation adjective («מעגל גדול שרדיוסו R» — no ה on the adjective) is a creation, whose adjective now shapes the STARTING radius only (`קטן`/small seeds 0.72×, the `twoCirclesMeet` split — sizes stay free DOFs per ADR-052), so the default drawing matches the words and the first assignment reads the intended circle.

**Root cause (one sentence).** The size qualifier carried both a reference and a relation, and the grammar had a lane for neither outside the concentric special case.

**Not built (noted).** Inferring the order from a recorded `set-radius-ratio` (k>1) without an explicit order; a 3+-circle qualifier clarification.

**Tests / lock.** `size-qualifier.test.ts` (8: first-use assign+assert, second-use consistency without a duplicate assert, recorded-roles-win-over-drawn-sizes, both-qualifiers-one-utterance, En mirror, indefinite-creation seed split, 1/3-circle defers, concentric untouched); scenario `bagrut-2025-verbatim-unnamed-circles` — the exam in its published wording, end-to-end.

## ADR-306 — Name an auto-assigned circle centre after the fact (issue #112)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-13; issue #112). *Files: `src/parser/context.ts` (`autoCenters`), `src/parser/parse.ts` (`ParseContext.autoCenters`, `parseNameCenter`), `src/store/geoStore.ts` (`nameCentre` action), `src/App.tsx` (interception + hook); `src/store/__tests__/name-centre.test.ts`.*

**Class.** A student draws an UNNAMED circle — the system auto-picks a hidden centre letter (O). Later they want to name/refer to it ("circle P"), but there was NO path to name an auto-assigned centre after the fact: «מרכז המעגל הוא P» / "the centre of the circle is P" / "circle P" all minted a SECOND circle (circle-P), and once a stray circle existed, further attempts hit "already exists". The student can't rename by the hidden letter either (they can't see it's O). Operator report 2026-07-13 (raised twice — the general form of the size-qualifier resize bug).

**Root cause.** The `nameCenter` parser rule only REVEALS a centre when the named letter already IS that circle's centre; a FRESH letter fell through to the `circle` creation rule. Renaming the hidden centre is a store-level operation (rewrite the letter across every fact), which no rule reaches — and a plain rename would also leave the centre hidden (`autoCenter` unchanged).

**Decision.** The rename/swap/merge pattern, centre edition: `parseNameCenter(utterance, ctx)` (intercepted by App.submit BEFORE the parser, so the `circle` rule can't mint circle-P) resolves the naming statement to `{from: hiddenCentre, to: freshLetter}` and calls the new store action `nameCentre`, which RENAMES `from`→`to` across every fact (the shared `renameInCommand`/`relabelId` id-remap already rewrites `circle-O`→`circle-P` and `center:O`→P) AND reveals it (drops `autoCenter` on the just-named circle so it shows, FR-RN-8) — one `set`, one undo entry, never a second circle. The source centre comes from `ctx.autoCenters` (the sole auto-named centre — the one they drew); with none auto but one named centre, a fresh target re-letters it. Ambiguous (0 or ≥2 auto-centres) or a taken target → defer to the parser (existing behaviour). The reveal-with-the-same-existing-letter case stays with the `nameCenter` rule.

**Tests / lock.** `name-centre.test.ts` (9): He/En/label-first rename+reveal to one circle, subscript label, single undo, reveal-existing no-theft, ambiguous defer, taken-letter refusal, re-letter a named centre. **Follow-up (noted on #112):** a bare «circle P» / «מעגל P» after an unnamed circle is deliberately NOT treated as a rename (too ambiguous with wanting a second circle) — the explicit «centre … is P» forms are the naming path.

## ADR-307 — A definite plural circle reference «המעגלים» binds the two existing circles (issue #111)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-13; issue #111). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`definiteTwoCircles`, `twoCirclesMeet` existing-circles branch); `src/parser/__tests__/definite-two-circles.test.ts`, scenario `intersection-of-the-circles-binds-existing`.*

**Class.** With two circles already drawn, «A נקודות חיתוך בין המעגלים» / «A היא נקודת החיתוך של המעגלים» ("A, the intersection of the circles") **invented a THIRD circle** and intersected the first with it, ignoring the second (operator report 2026-07-13). Root cause: `twoCirclesMeet` and `circleCircleIntersection` resolve their circles only from NAMED «מעגל X» tokens; a DEFINITE PLURAL reference names none, so `twoCirclesMeet`'s "draw two intersecting circles" opener fired and minted fresh circles (auto-naming Q because the existing centre letter P was taken). The ADR-029 implicit-reference pattern («the circle» → the one circle) was missing for the two-circle plural.

**Decision.** `definiteTwoCircles(s, ctx)` — when the figure holds exactly TWO circles and the utterance refers to them by a definite plural («(שני) המעגלים» / «the (two) circles») with NO circle letters — returns those two EXISTING circle ids. `twoCirclesMeet` gains an early branch: bind those circles and emit only the crossing point(s) the student named (one → branch 0; two → the other crossing, `avoid` the first) — never a new circle. A NAMED reference («מעגל O ומעגל P») still routes to `circleCircleIntersection`; the OPENER («שני מעגלים נחתכים» with no circles yet) still creates both; 0/1/3+ circles → the resolver bows out (never binds an arbitrary pair).

**Tests / lock.** `definite-two-circles.test.ts` (7): He/En definite-plural binds the existing two, two named crossings, opener no-theft, named-two-circle no-theft, the ≠2-circles guard; scenario `intersection-of-the-circles-binds-existing`.

## ADR-308 — «M אמצע OK» on an existing crossing point: a collinear midpoint drives the upstream free DOF via 1-D equidistance, freeing soft-order carriers (issue #110)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-13; issue #110). *Files: `src/engine/step.ts` (`collinearByConstruction`, `driveHardOn`, the midpoint branch in `reinterpretAsConstraint`, `ancestors`/`freeCarrierAncestor` `'soft-order'` availability); `src/engine/__tests__/midpoint-of-crossing.test.ts`, scenario `extension-crossing-then-midpoint-given`.*

**Class.** A student defines M = (extension of AE) ∩ OK, then states the book given «M אמצע OK» / "M is the midpoint of OK". The restatement is the M1 class (a statement about an existing point is a constraint, not a re-creation) and `reinterpretAsConstraint` correctly fired — but it reported **over-constrained though a valid configuration exists** (closed-form: a unique E on the small circle makes line AE pass through the midpoint of OK, inside △KAO). The 2025-bagrut part-ב could not be drawn (operator report 2026-07-13).

**Root cause (two coupled defects).** (1) The soft `collinear-order` from the crossing's `onSeg2` («M within OK») had, via `addCollinearOrder`, **over-recruited the upstream free carrier E** (and O and the radii) as its driven carriers — so `freeCarrierAncestor` skipped E as "already solving" and the reinterpret found NO carrier, appending a directive-less coincide the recruiter then couldn't place. (2) The generic reinterpret builds a 2-D `coincide(M, midpoint(O,K))`, which the 1-D driven-carrier solver (`drivenRoots` over a single θ) cannot zero even when the residual is effectively 1-D — while the equivalent **1-D equidistance** |OM|=|MK| is nailed exactly.

**Decision.** A **collinear midpoint** — an existing point that is collinear-by-construction with its endpoints (`collinearByConstruction`: a `line-line-intersection` / on-segment point whose line is exactly the endpoint pair) — lowers to the well-conditioned 1-D equidistance `set-equal(a, M, M, b)` instead of the 2-D coincide, driven by the upstream free carrier. The carrier is found **past soft-order carriers**: `ancestors`/`freeCarrierAncestor` gain a `'soft-order'` availability mode that treats a carrier driven only by a SOFT ORDER (collinear-order / angle-order / length-order / angle-acuteness) as claimable — those orders ride the optimizer and own no dedicated DOF, so a HARD constraint may take the carrier. `driveHardOn` then FREES every competing soft-order carrier (they remain in `constraints` as checks) so the equidistance's single driven carrier solves alone. A non-collinear M keeps the generic coincide; an unsatisfiable midpoint still fails honestly (keep-prior).

**Root cause (one sentence).** A soft order that "rides the optimizer" had captured the upstream free DOF a later hard midpoint needed, and the midpoint was being expressed as a 2-D coincide a 1-D driven carrier can't solve.

**Sibling audit.** The `'soft-order'` availability is the general lever (any hard constraint reinterpreted onto a point whose upstream DOF a soft order captured now reaches it); the midpoint→equidistance lowering is scoped to `midpoint` (the reported construct). The broad `ancestors` change is covered by the full suite (the driveOrCheck/recruiter paths that use `freeCarrierAncestor` pass `false` and are byte-unchanged). Filed-not-fixed: `addCollinearOrder` over-recruiting many carriers for one soft order is a latent inefficiency — the availability fix neutralises its harm here; a leaner recruitment is a separate perf item if it resurfaces.

**Tests / lock.** `midpoint-of-crossing.test.ts` (2: the crossing-then-midpoint flexes the upstream carrier to |OM|=|MK|; an unsatisfiable pinned midpoint fails honestly); scenario `extension-crossing-then-midpoint-given` (the FULL 2025 exam + «M אמצע OK» — M bisects OK with E on the small circle, K on the big circle, OA⟂AK, A-E-M collinear).

## ADR-309 — The radius slider respects stated radius relations; math panels render LTR-isolated (issues #113, #26/#89)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-13; issues #113, #26, #89). *Files: `src/store/geoStore.ts` (`setRadius`), `src/App.tsx` (similar/congruent row `dir="ltr"` + `unicodeBidi: isolate`, radius-slider label `dir`); `src/store/__tests__/dof-radius.test.ts`.*

**#113 — the slider must not drag into a figure that violates a STATED given.** `setRadius` accepted any dialed value whose replay had `lastError === null`, but a `set-radius-order` (R>r) / `set-radius-ratio` is a REQUIREMENT the verifier flags (amber) while leaving `lastError` null — so the slider dragged the small circle past the big one (operator report 2026-07-13, the 2025-bagrut two-circle figure). Fix, two layers: (1) `setRadius` rejects a candidate that introduces a `radius-order`/`radius-ratio` violation (the value guard); (2) the two circles under an order share ONE common slider SCALE (min = smaller base×0.3, max = larger base×2.2), so R's thumb always sits to the RIGHT of r's on the same axis — the order is legible, not just enforced. (Two intermediate takes were superseded: per-slider ranges made the small circle's thumb sit further right than the big one's — enforced but not shown; a clamp tying the inner's max to the outer's radius fixed the drag limit but kept the ranges incomparable. The shared scale shows the order and the value guard enforces it.) Scoped to radius-relation violations — the dial directly controls them — so a pre-existing unrelated amber doesn't freeze the slider. The engine already gates resample/"show another" on the order (`meetsRequirements` includes the radius-order violation), verified by a seed sweep.

**#26/#89 — the similar/congruent triangle rows garble under RTL.** «△AMO ~ △AOE» rendered as «AMO ~ △AOE△» — the leading △ (U+25B3, bidi-neutral) and the ~/≅ separators reordered under the Hebrew `dir=rtl` document. Fix: the row is pure LTR math notation, so force `dir="ltr"` + `unicodeBidi: 'isolate'` on the button (the same class as the canvas-label LTR override). The radius-slider label (mixed «רדיוס מעגל O (R)») gets `dir={textDir(label)}` for the same reason.

**Tests / lock.** `dof-radius.test.ts` (+2): dialing the small circle above the big is rejected, a valid smaller value accepted, and dialing the big below the small is rejected. The bidi rows are a render-only change (no unit surface); confirmed against the operator's screenshot.

## ADR-310 — A radical is a RATIO COEFFICIENT via the shared `NUMEXPR` atom, not the stale `RCOEF`/`RATVAL` (issue #114)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-13; issue #114). *Files: `src/parser/parse.ts` (`ratioConstraint`, `segmentRatio`, `measureRatioK`; removed the dead `RCOEF`/`rcoefVal`/`RATVAL`/`ratvalAt`); `src/parser/__tests__/ratio-radical-coefficient.test.ts`.*

**Class.** *A stated radical value in a ratio/factor COEFFICIENT position is not parsed when written with the `√()` toolbar form* (parens around the RADICAND). Operator prod session `qderonm3` (bagrut Q5): `AC=√(3)CO` and `AC גדול פי √(3) מ CO` escalated to the LLM (which then produced a malformed figure — the root of the same session's E-on-K and area-fail symptoms), while `CK=√(63)` — a radical DISTANCE — parsed fine.

**Root cause.** The segment-ratio rules (`ratioConstraint` the `=k·seg` form, `segmentRatio` the `/`-form) and the area/perimeter-ratio helper (`measureRatioK`) built their coefficient from the older `RCOEF`/`RATVAL`/`COEF` vocabulary: `\(? √? number …\)?` — one optional paren around the WHOLE atom, so it parses `(√3)` but **not** `√(3)`. The length/area/radius/perimeter VALUE rules had already been migrated to the shared **`NUMEXPR`/`NUMTERM` atom (ADR-298 / #77)**, which carries a parenthesised-radicand group (`<prn>`) and so handles `√(3)`, `√(2/3)`, and quotient radicals — but the ratio COEFFICIENT positions were left on the stale vocabulary. A whole-class gap, not the one figure.

**Fix (root — consolidate onto the shared atom, not a carve-out).** All three ratio-coefficient positions now use `NUMEXPR('…')` + `numexprVal`. The stale `RCOEF`/`rcoefVal`/`RATVAL`/`ratvalAt` are deleted (they had no other callers). No new chokepoint entry — this REMOVES a duplicate vocabulary. No theft: `ratioConstraint` still requires two labels on each side of `=`, so `AB = √2R` (reserved radius symbol) stays with `measureSqrt` and `AB = √2` stays a concrete length (locked). **New capability:** every ratio/factor coefficient (`√(3)`, `√(2/3)`, `√35/√32`, the `/`-form value, and the Hebrew `פי k מ`) now parses in the same radical vocabulary as the length rules, in both the segment-ratio and the area/perimeter-ratio families.

**Sibling audit.** grep'd `RCOEF`/`RATVAL`/`COEF` uses: `ratioConstraint` (2), `segmentRatio` (1), `measureRatioK` (2) — all migrated. `parseAreaExpr` already used `NUMEXPR` (fine). The verbose `אורך …גדול פי …מאורך …` WRAPPER (length words + `מאורך`) is a distinct gap owned by **#105** (cross-linked), not this ADR. Locked by `ratio-radical-coefficient.test.ts` (14: the operator's forms, non-theft, the area-ratio sibling) + the Q5 end-to-end scenario.

## ADR-311 — A point-on-object rider defaults into GENERAL POSITION, off existing points (issue #115, extends ADR-253)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-13; issue #115). *Files: `src/engine/apply.ts` (`freeSegT` is position-aware); `src/engine/__tests__/rider-general-position.test.ts`.*

**Class.** *An on-object rider's default parameter is chosen without the general-position guard, so it can land on an existing point — a coincidence the student never stated (ADR-052).* Operator prod session `qderonm3`: `E על CB` defaulted onto K (the "E ו-K נפלו על אותה נקודה" notice). Deterministic repro: `ריבוע ABCD` → `M אמצע AB` → `E על AB` places E exactly on the midpoint M (|E−M| = 0).

**Root cause.** `freeSegT` (the free on-segment rider's default-`t` seeder) dodged only OTHER on-segment riders on the same segment (its `objects`-only, topological view). ADR-253's general-position machinery (which nudges TEMPLATE base placements, default directions, and meet-reseats off existing points/lines using coordinates) was never applied to the rider default. So any existing POSITIONED point lying on the segment — a midpoint, an intersection, a foot — was invisible to the seeder.

**Fix (root — extend the existing general-position guard to the rider seam).** `freeSegT` now takes the `pos` map (already threaded into `applyCommand` and used by `reseatLooseMeetEndpoint`) and, in addition to sibling riders, treats any existing point whose CURRENT position lies ON the a→b segment (perpendicular distance < 0.015·span — the ADR-253 "too close to draw" bar — and param in (0.02, 0.98)) as "taken", so the new rider seeds into the largest clear gap. The point stays a FREE DOF (a better default, not a pin): "show another configuration" still slides it, and a later constraint that FORCES a coincidence still drives `t` there (ADR-123 notice path unchanged). A clear segment is byte-unchanged — the first rider still lands at 0.5.

**Sibling audit.** The class also covers on-line and on-circle rider defaults; those seed via their own paths (`freeSegT` is the segment case, which is where the report and the deterministic repro live). Filed as follow-up if a prod case surfaces — this ADR fixes the reported (segment) member at its seam and does not grow a chokepoint list. Locked by `rider-general-position.test.ts` (E avoids a midpoint / a foot on the segment; clear-segment and two-rider-spread regressions) + the Q5 end-to-end scenario. Note: for the operator's exact Q5 figure the decisive fix was #114 (K did not land on CB once √3 parsed deterministically); #115 is the independent safety net the M-on-AB case proves.

## ADR-312 — The live math preview follows the INPUT's direction, not a hard-coded LTR (issue #118)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-13; issue #118). *Files: `src/App.tsx` (live math preview container `dir`).*

**Class.** *A mixed Hebrew+math string rendered under a forced `dir="ltr"` has its Hebrew word order reversed* — the same bidi class as ADR-309 (#26/#89, the similar/congruent rows). Operator manual test: typing `אורך הצלע AC גדול פי √(3) מהקטע CO` showed the live preview as `CO גדול פי √3 מהקטע AC אורך הצלע` (scrambled), so the preview meant to CLARIFY the radical instead confused.

**Root cause.** The live math preview (added for #77/#40 to render `35/√32` as a real fraction-with-radical) hard-coded `dir="ltr"` on its container — correct for a pure math VALUE (which is left-to-right), but `hasMath(text)` also fires on a Hebrew SENTENCE that merely contains a radical, and LTR reverses Hebrew. `MathText` itself renders `√(3)` correctly (an `<msqrt>`), so the only defect was the container direction. (The literal `√(3)` in the `<input>` box is inherent — a text input cannot render a radical; the preview is the mechanism that shows it nicely, so fixing the preview covers the "sqrt not presented nicely" report too.)

**Fix.** The container is now `dir={textDir(text)}` — a pure math value stays LTR, a Hebrew sentence renders RTL with the MathML atoms as LTR islands in place. (`unicode-bidi: plaintext` was rejected: it derives direction from the first strong char, which mislabels a Latin-first Hebrew sentence like `AC גדול פי √3 מ CO` as LTR; `textDir` keys on "any Hebrew present", the correct base.) Render-only change (no unit surface, per the ADR-309 precedent); confirmed against the operator's screenshot + the bidi logic. Filed separately: the verbose `אורך…גדול פי…מהקטע` wrapper still escalates (that's #105, the parse layer — this ADR is presentation only).
